title: Create synchronous generic SessionKernel with fake-engine transcripts
description: Turn phux-client-core into a frontend-neutral synchronous SessionKernel<E> with EngineAdapter, normalized KernelInput/Action/Effect, reusable EffectBuffer, terminal staging/published replicas, canonical geometry, stream/bootstrap sequencing, and no transport/render/layout I/O. Normalize current synthesized bootstrap through it first so work can proceed before native bindings.
design:
Boundary: extend phux-client-core; do not create a second client-core crate. Generic synchronous core, no async trait/boxing and no transport/frontend dependencies.

Core shape:
- EngineAdapter associated Live, HistoryPage/Projection, Anchor, Error.
- push_bootstrap(live, opaque chunk) -> Pending|Ready|Finished; apply_pty; import/project history; create/resolve engine anchors; format selection; borrowed render access.
- SessionKernel<E> owns terminal map, connection state, staging/published replicas, bounded HistoryCache, viewport/selection/reconnect state.
- update(KernelInput, &mut reusable EffectBuffer) emits Send, Damage, Clipboard, ScheduleTimer, ConnectionChanged, HistoryJob, Fatal. It performs no I/O/frontend callback.
- KernelInput normalizes server events, explicit-terminal user actions, transport events, timers. Layout/plugin/theme/help remain outside.

Replica invariants:
- publish only after both phux BOOTSTRAP_READY and engine internal READY agree; mismatch is corruption/resync.
- apply only matching stream/bootstrap raw seq > base_seq, contiguous; wrong/stale/gap never reaches engine.
- keep last published replica while a replacement stages; atomically swap on dual READY.
- canonical live geometry equals BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN. Physical viewport/history projection never independently resizes it.
- engine synchronous effects are queued then drained after apply to prevent reentrancy.

History/anchors:
- opaque generation-scoped engine page handles, bounded by encoded/materialized bytes.
- newest-first pull; duplicates idempotent; gaps explicit; visible/prefetch/selection pages pinned; LRU otherwise.
- ViewportAnchor Tail or Pinned(engine DocumentAnchor + row bias). Tail follows; pinned stays and unread increments.
- selection endpoints are engine anchors across History(page)/Live segments. Missing pages defer copy and emit fetch; engine defines wraps/graphemes/join boundaries.
- historical projections cache by page,target_cols,engine generation; cooperative visible+neighbor slices. Live grid is not reflowed.

Allocation: borrow frame Bytes into adapter; reuse effects/engine-effects/decode/reflow/render scratch; no durable Canvas Grid/cell model; allocate selection text only at copy completion. Move predict::overlay stdout VT emission to Ratatui shell.

Migration: fake-engine transcript kernel -> Ratatui synthesized compatibility normalization -> native adapter dual READY -> bounded history -> semantic selection -> reconnect staging -> web compatibility reducer deletion -> native host. Delete old reducers/viewport-cell selection after both frontends migrate.
acceptance_criteria: Core compiles native+wasm without Ratatui/crossterm/tokio/web-sys/DOM; deterministic fake-engine transcripts enforce dual READY, chunk/raw order, attach barrier, stale generation rejection, and exact effects without allocation-heavy async traits.
notes: Implemented on isolated phux branch feat/session-kernel and integrated into feat/native-state-sync-wave1 through 229d053f. Added synchronous generic SessionKernel/EngineAdapter, explicit replica keys and canonical geometry, staging/published atomic dual READY, exact raw sequence and tombstone gates, aggregate ATTACH_READY barrier, StateSync generation ACKs, typed reusable effects, generation-buffered Status/Job, adapter-error retirement, and wasm-safe dependencies. Independent review found/fixed ACK, error atomicity, bootstrap effect, close-removal, and generation-key defects. Validation: cargo fmt clean; phux-client-core 169 tests passed; wasm32-unknown-unknown no-default-features check clean.

title: Specify protocol 0.7 bootstrap and history cutover
description: Finalize ADR and normative L1/proto 0.7 contract: retire TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT tag 0x91 permanently; define StreamId/BootstrapId, codec sets, BEGIN/CHUNK/READY, ATTACH_READY, HISTORY_REQUEST/PAGE, tombstones, actor cut sequence, mode matrix, bounds, resize, multi-pane fairness, and federation mapping. Prefer exact libghostty v2+Raw; synthesized VT+Raw/StateSync is compatibility.
design:
Protocol target: 0.7.0 clean cutover.

Discriminants:
- C→S HISTORY_REQUEST = 0x16.
- S→C ATTACH_READY = 0x83.
- S→C BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN = 0x93, BOOTSTRAP_CHUNK = 0x94, BOOTSTRAP_READY = 0x95, HISTORY_PAGE = 0x96, BOOTSTRAP_TOMBSTONE = 0x97.
- Withdraw TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT 0x91 permanently; never reuse it.

Types:
- nonzero StreamId(u64): one logical subscription.
- nonzero BootstrapId(u64): replaceable replica generation.
- BootstrapCodec values allocated only after Ghostty version decision: SynthesizedVtV1 and exact LibghosttyCheckpointV2+.
- BootstrapCodecSet additive bits; ClientCapabilities advertises set + max_chunk_bytes + max_history_page_bytes. HELLO_OK returns selected supported bounds/profile. OutputMode remains Raw|StateSync.
- Allowed profiles: exact native+Raw preferred; synth+Raw and synth+StateSync compatibility; native+StateSync rejected CodecUnavailable.
- TombstoneReason: RawReplayOverflow, OutboundGap, Resize, RelayReconnect, ExplicitReattach, CodecFailure, Other.

Frame fields / TLV ids:
BEGIN: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, codec=4, cols=5, rows=6, output_mode=7, base_seq=8.
CHUNK: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, chunk_seq=4, payload=5.
READY: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, history_cursor=4 optional.
HISTORY_REQUEST: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, cursor=4, max_bytes=5.
HISTORY_PAGE: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, cursor=4, next_cursor=5 optional, payload=6. next_cursor=None means this payload ends the requested codec stream/FINISH.
TOMBSTONE: terminal=1, stream=2, bootstrap=3, reason=4, last_valid_seq=5.
ATTACH_READY: attach_id=1.
Append stream=4, bootstrap=5 to TERMINAL_OUTPUT; append stream=3, bootstrap=4 to FRAME_ACK. Add attach_id to ATTACH/ATTACHED.

No separate raw/bootstrap ACK gates server release: reliable ordering plus dual READY is sufficient and avoids one RTT. FRAME_ACK remains cumulative only for StateSync within (stream,bootstrap). Raw uses actor stream seq for gap/cut verification but does not ACK.

Ordering:
ATTACHED -> BEGIN for all panes in stable snapshot traversal -> round-robin bounded CHUNKs -> per-pane READY -> per-pane raw seq base_seq+1 immediately -> ATTACH_READY once all panes are READY/closed. History is client-pull and lower priority; at most one request outstanding per logical stream. Payloads are opaque engine bytes; phux never scans magic/tags/READY/FINISH.

Server cut:
actor stamps checked non-wrapping stream_seq before broadcast. Coordinator drains subscription, takes actor-turn cut, drops seq<=cut, queues bounded seq>cut, sends state through READY, then releases contiguous raw. Missing/gap/overflow/loss/resize produces TOMBSTONE before a new BEGIN. No old generation data is legal after tombstone.

Federation:
select profile per logical stream. Bijection downstream(client,stream)<->upstream(link,stream). Rewrite only phux IDs/envelope; payload/raw bytes unchanged. Distinct profiles use distinct subscriptions. Proxy history and StateSync ACK. Bounded return queues; raw overflow tombstones rather than silent try_send loss.
acceptance_criteria: Every field/discriminant/order/error is allocated; engine payload stays opaque; native+StateSync is rejected; raw native bytes are never color-rewritten; previous ADRs are explicitly superseded/constrained; implementation tasks require no semantic guesswork.
notes: Implemented on isolated branch feat/native-state-sync-wave1 through d29ff12a. ADR-0067 and normative L1/proto define the 0.7 clean cutover, explicit NativeState/SynthesizedVtRaw/SynthesizedVtStateSync profiles, actor-global inclusive cut, no raw ACK RTT, per-pane READY/global ATTACH_READY, opaque history/tombstone/federation and negotiated bounds. Protocol crate adds nonzero IDs, exact profiles/codecs/features, new discriminants/frames, required-field decoding, pre-copy negotiated limits, and permanently retires 0x91. Validation: cargo test -p phux-protocol 196 passed; docs-check 125 files/0 violations; cargo check -p phux-protocol clean; independent review findings fixed.

title: Expose incremental checkpoint handles through C and WASM ABI
description: After the Zig incremental READY/history state machines land, expose callback-free opaque capture/decoder handles, caller buffers, sized options/events, capability metadata, structured codec errors, take-terminal-at-READY, history push/abort, and exact cleanup. Use the same linear-memory ABI for native C and the standalone ghostty-vt.wasm module.
design:
Engine API direction:
- Version enum with immutable v1 and exact v2+; CheckpointId is validated READY prefix digest.
- Capture::init is the pause-sensitive operation: serialize active prefix/continuation through READY and acquire bounded stable history lease/pins/COW. Capture::next writes exactly one non-advancing-on-short-buffer opaque chunk (READY, history manifest/page, FINISH), reports metadata, and releases on abort/deinit.
- Decoder buffers at most one bounded record, accepts arbitrary fragments, reports NeedInput/Ready/HistoryBegin/HistoryPage/Finish, and consumes nothing after FINISH. take_ready transfers a stable Terminal exactly once; serialized vt_write may run between later history pushes.
- HistoryImport tracks only imported old nodes. Post-READY corruption/FINISH failure rolls back imported history and invalidates pins into it while preserving active READY state and post-READY PTY writes. Retention pressure may report retained=false rather than evict newer live output.
- Pull history lease/cursor is generation-bound, newest-to-oldest, byte/page bounded, stale/pruned explicit. Never expose Page.memory, cloneBuf, compressed-page bytes, parser structs, allocator pointers, or native padding.
- Continuation is canonical replay-safe bytes only. Tracking starts before first vt_write. Disabled/unavailable capture fails explicitly.
- C ABI uses opaque handles, sized options/events, caller buffers, exact consumed counts, structured codec errors, and no callbacks/file descriptors. Rust typestate owns handles/terminal and makes pre-READY access/wrong-terminal history application unavailable.
- Source capture leaves compressed pages compressed and does not mutate terminal presentation/cache state.
acceptance_criteria: A pure C test and WASM smoke can fragment at every byte boundary, take a usable terminal only at verified READY, vt_write between history pages, finish or abort cleanly, distinguish version/corruption/limits/OOM, and never mix a decoder with the wrong terminal.
notes: Implemented native C and standalone wasm incremental snapshot/history ABI through 8f5b178d4: opaque capture/decoder/lease/cursor/importer handles, sized metadata/events, strict bounds, exact READY/consumed semantics, ownership/OOM cleanup, honest wasm capability gating, C contract and Node smoke. Independent review clear. Native test-lib-vt passed 5327 tests (34 skipped); wasm smoke and zig fmt checks pass.
close_reason: Incremental native C/wasm checkpoint ABI implemented, hardened, reviewed, validated, and published

title: [epic] Native engine-state terminal synchronization and client-owned history
description: Build phux's next terminal substrate around exact, versioned libghostty state rather than VT-synthesized bootstrap: READY-before-history attach, raw PTY live fanout, canonical bounded server history, progressive client-owned history caches/viewports, queue tombstones and full resync, and one frontend-neutral client kernel shared by Ratatui, web, and future native UI. Preserve the invariant one PTY = one authoritative active-area geometry; independent client sizes mean projection, crop/letterbox, zoom, and deferred historical reflow, never multiple PTY winsizes. Upstream engine work stays on phall1 forks unless explicit upstream permission is granted.
design:
DECISION SUMMARY

Phux will preserve its existing distributed-terminal shape—one authoritative libghostty Terminal beside the PTY and one engine replica per client—but replace native clients' VT-synthesized bootstrap with exact, versioned libghostty checkpoint bytes. Live output remains raw PTY bytes. Historical state becomes a separate progressive, client-pull lane. Synthesized VT remains an explicitly negotiated compatibility codec for web/older-engine/agent consumers; it is not the native fidelity ceiling.

The engine owns terminal semantics and binary codecs. Phux owns connection negotiation, logical stream/bootstrap IDs, ordering/fences, resource bounds, cursor routing, tombstones, and frontend-independent policy. No cells, styles, Ghostty record tags, page layouts, parser structs, or compressed Page memory enter phux's protocol. CRC32C/BLAKE3 validation stays inside libghostty.

GEOMETRY INVARIANT

One process + one PTY = one authoritative active cell geometry and one PTY winsize. Multiple clients may have different physical surfaces, font sizes, zoom, crop/letterbox, layouts, scroll positions, cache budgets, and historical projections. They do not simultaneously turn the same live PTY into true 80x24 and 200x60 terminals. Existing server window-size policy selects the canonical geometry. Phase 1 history pages remain canonical-width. Deferred client-local historical reflow/disk paging is later engine work; it must never resize the live raw-PTY replica.

ENGINE FORMAT

Current Ghostty main already has portable field-wise snapshot records:
  envelope -> TERMINAL -> SCREEN/PAGE active suffix -> CONTINUATION -> READY(BLAKE3)
           -> HISTORY/PAGE newest-to-oldest -> FINISH(BLAKE3)

The current continuation branch changed v1 incompatibly and current v1 omits load-bearing state such as Kitty image payloads. Freeze complete-v1 bytes. Add an explicit v2 (or later) with replay-safe CONTINUATION and exact feature coverage. Native is advertised only when the engine can preserve all canonical state present in that terminal; otherwise choose synthesized compatibility before payload delivery. Raw Page.memory/cloneBuf/compression.Page bytes are process-local only and never portable.

The final engine API is incremental and callback-free:
- capture begin emits bounded prefix chunks through verified READY and returns a stable bounded history lease/cursor;
- decoder consumes arbitrary fragmentation, transfers one usable Terminal at internal READY, then applies history records newest-to-oldest while serialized vt_write continues;
- history failure after READY preserves active/live state and invalidates/rolls back only imported history;
- abort/drop frees pins/clones/handles exactly once;
- C sized structs/opaque handles and safe Rust typestate wrappers expose milestones/errors/capabilities;
- standalone ghostty-vt.wasm uses the same caller-buffer ABI.

The whole-blob C bridge is the first proven slice, not the final transport API: phall1/ghostty feat/terminal-snapshot-c-api commit e32f7169c.

PROTOCOL 0.7 CLEAN CUTOVER

Retire TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT and permanently reserve 0x91; no alias or shim. Both native and synthesized bootstrap use one generation-scoped lifecycle. Exact discriminants/fields are finalized in phux-slogic.2.1, with this semantic vocabulary:
- HELLO client codec set + limits; HELLO_OK selected codec/profile + limits.
- StreamId: one logical subscription. BootstrapId: replaceable replica generation.
- BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN {terminal, stream, bootstrap, codec, canonical cols/rows, output_mode, base_seq}
- BOOTSTRAP_CHUNK {terminal, stream, bootstrap, chunk_seq, opaque payload}
- BOOTSTRAP_READY {terminal, stream, bootstrap, optional history cursor}
- ATTACH_READY {attach_id} after all panes reached READY/closed.
- HISTORY_REQUEST {terminal, stream, bootstrap, cursor, max_bytes}
- HISTORY_PAGE {terminal, stream, bootstrap, cursor, next_cursor, opaque payload}
- BOOTSTRAP_TOMBSTONE/RESYNC_REQUIRED {old generation, reason, last valid seq}; then a new BEGIN.
- TERMINAL_OUTPUT and StateSync ACK carry stream/bootstrap identity.

Preferred profile: exact LibghosttyCheckpointV2+ + Raw. Compatibility profiles: SynthesizedVtV1 + Raw or StateSync. Native + StateSync is rejected until libghostty supplies an exact native delta. Native raw output is byte-identical and never color/image rewritten. Protocol version and engine codec version/build capabilities are independent.

CAPTURE/RAW ORDERING

TerminalActor owns checked non-wrapping u64 stream_seq and stamps every accepted raw PTY payload before broadcast. Runtime actively subscribes/drains before requesting capture. Capture runs in one actor turn and returns cut=last_stream_seq. The coordinator drops buffered seq <= cut (already represented by checkpoint), queues only seq > cut under a strict byte/count bound, sends BEGIN/CHUNK/READY, then sends cut+1, cut+2, ... exactly once. No client ACK gates raw release or adds a round trip: reliable phux frame order plus dual READY is the fence. BOOTSTRAP_ACK, if retained, is observational/resource accounting only.

Multi-pane attach sends BEGIN for all panes first, schedules bounded chunks round-robin, allows each ready pane's raw stream immediately, and sends ATTACH_READY after all pane outcomes. Large history never blocks READY, raw output, input, or another pane.

HISTORY

History is canonical, bounded, retained once by the server terminal, but replicated progressively into client-owned engine caches. One request may be outstanding per logical stream. A cursor is an opaque sequential lease token bound to bootstrap/history generation—not a byte offset and not a scroll position. The engine chooses complete payload boundaries; phux may fragment bytes but never parses them. Server clamps page bytes, prioritizes live output, and releases leases on completion/TTL/detach/tombstone. Stale/pruned cursors fail explicitly. Clients request newest pages first, prefetch older pages near a cache boundary, and own viewport/selection/search/prefetch/cache budgets. Server never stores “client is scrolled up N rows.”

RESYNC

Per stream: Absent -> Bootstrapping -> Ready -> Tombstoned -> Bootstrapping(new). Raw replay overflow, missing sequence, outbound loss, resize, relay reconnect, explicit reattach, or codec failure emits a tombstone before replacement. No old generation chunk/page/output/ACK applies afterward. Client keeps the last published replica visible while staging replacement and atomically swaps only when both phux BOOTSTRAP_READY and libghostty internal READY agree. Resize creates a new canonical generation. StateSync compatibility reference/ACK state is keyed by (client, stream, bootstrap).

CLIENT KERNEL

phux-client-core becomes a synchronous generic SessionKernel<E: EngineAdapter>, with no Ratatui, crossterm, tokio, web-sys, DOM, sockets, stdout writer, or async traits. It owns negotiation results, terminal staging/published replicas, dual READY, stream/bootstrap order, history cache, viewport/document anchors, selection/search, tombstones, reconnect state, and reusable effect buffers. It emits effects; transport/frontend shells execute them. Layout/chrome/theme/plugin policy remains outside.

EngineAdapter owns terminals/pages/tracked anchors/reflow/selection formatting and borrowed render access. The kernel stores no cells. HistoryCache stores bounded engine-owned opaque handles/materializations. ViewportAnchor is Tail or Pinned(engine document anchor); pinned views do not jump as raw/history arrives. Missing selection pages trigger fetch and deferred copy, never silent truncation. Historical projection may reflow cooperatively; live canonical geometry may not.

Migration order: fake-engine kernel -> native libghostty adapter -> bounded history/anchors -> selection/search -> reconnect staging -> Ratatui cutover -> web compatibility cutover -> native-sdk host bridge/UI -> optional native web codec. Delete duplicate Ratatui/web reducers and viewport-cell selection authority after migration.

FEDERATION

Codec/profile selection is per logical stream, not just HELLO connection. Hub maps (downstream client, stream) bijectively to satellite stream, rewrites only phux IDs/envelopes, and proxies history/ACK. Different downstream profiles use distinct upstream subscriptions. Native payload and raw bytes compare identical end-to-end; no hub transcoding. Replace return-leg try_send loss with bounded per-stream queues; overflow tombstones raw streams. Satellite reconnect tombstones all mapped generations.

ORCHESTRATION WAVES

Wave 0 (done/active): synchronize phall1 forks; whole-blob C checkpoint bridge e32f7169c; architecture issue graph.
Wave 1 (parallel): v1/v2/fidelity decision; complete whole-blob Rust wrapper; strict HELLO for every stateful constructor; protocol 0.7 ADR/spec; fake-engine SessionKernel.
Wave 2: incremental Ghostty capture/decoder/history lease; exact missing-state codec; incremental C/WASM ABI; protocol types/goldens.
Wave 3: safe Rust typestate wrappers and phux pin; actor raw sequence/cut; native kernel adapter.
Wave 4: fair runtime coordinator; pull history; tombstone replacement; HistoryCache/anchors; federation mapping.
Wave 5: Ratatui migration and web compatibility migration in parallel; native host bridge after native adapter; selection/search/reconnect.
Wave 6: production native UI; optional exact web/WASM native mode; remove obsolete TerminalSnapshot/PanesOutput::Resync paths.
Wave 7: cross-architecture compatibility, fuzz, deterministic race/fault proofs, benchmarks, browser/native/recording smoke, release soak.

VALIDATION/END STATE

Non-negotiable proof:
- READY authenticated/renderable before history; input/raw continue while history stalls.
- Arbitrary parser cut (UTF-8/CSI/OSC/APC/DCS) resumes identically.
- Every byte is in checkpoint or seq>cut raw exactly once.
- Tombstone recovery never accepts stale data and converges without blank/double content.
- Multiple physical client sizes share identical canonical live state/raw stream while local viewport/history state differs.
- Cross-language and macOS-arm64/Linux-x86_64 fixtures agree; v1 immutable, future versions explicit.
- Fuzz/malformed/OOM/drop paths have no panic/leak/unbounded allocation/partial pre-READY terminal.
- Ratatui, browser compatibility, portable recording, and real native multi-pane paths are artifact-backed.
- After warmup, raw payload fanout adds no payload copy per client; history/cache memory is formula-bounded.

Initial performance targets: 200x60 codec READY p95 <=25ms; warm UDS READY p95 <=100ms/p99<=250ms; 50k history changes READY <=10%; page import/reflow slices p95 <=4ms and <=256KiB; input-to-paint p99 <=50ms during paging; eight-client raw throughput >=90% current baseline with zero extra payload copies; local resync <=250ms. Establish pinned baselines before enforcing relative gates.

This program aims to surpass the disclosed Superlogical terminal architecture through measured exact-state fidelity plus phux's existing open protocol, browser/remote transports, federation, agent APIs, and shared frontend kernel. No “surpassed” claim is valid until these gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: A native client can attach, render exact current engine state before history finishes, type immediately, scroll/search/select locally through demand-paged history, survive dropped output via deterministic resync, and share the same client state machine as Ratatui/web; compatibility clients retain synthesized VT mode; focused fidelity, corruption, loss, performance, and end-to-end tests pass.

Native tombstones supersede new investment in phux-kztd/phux-205m but those existing beads are not mutated here. 486.3 was descoped, so phux-slogic.3 is a new replacement kernel program. nk07/h5hj.5 preserve one canonical geometry; abi/7143/549 are projection seams. Web stays synthesized compatibility until WASM parity. Recording/transport/agent work stays orthogonal. Strict HELLO gap from phux-0vp is completed by phux-slogic.2.8. Planning evidence produced by parallel TrackerReconciler, GhosttyCodecPlanner, WirePlanner, ClientKernelPlanner, and ValidationPlanner; code slice by GhosttyCAbi.

title: Wire: acknowledge idempotent atomic input operations
description: phux-mobile public-launch chaos testing found an unavoidable ambiguity at reconnect boundaries: the consumer can know that a pane was input-ready and that bytes entered its local queue, but cannot know whether the server accepted them before a WebSocket failure. Replaying may duplicate commands; not replaying may silently lose them. Define and implement a protocol-owned atomic input operation carrying a consumer operation ID, with server acknowledgment after acceptance by the pane input path and bounded deduplication across reconnect. Update the normative wire spec, changelog/version, protocol codec, server dispatch, and consumer APIs. Preserve structured key/mouse/focus semantics; do not infer delivery from terminal echo. This is a public-launch prerequisite for phux-mobile bead phux-q7e.24.
acceptance_criteria: A complete line/paste/key batch has one operation ID and is accepted atomically; the server ACKs acceptance and deduplicates retries of the same ID across reconnect; clients can classify each operation as accepted, refused, or unknown without claiming unacknowledged delivery; reconnect tests cut the socket before send, after send, and after server acceptance and prove no silent loss or duplicate PTY execution; docs/spec and docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md describe the compatibility/version behavior.
close_reason: Merged in PR #286 as f1a1306a: capability-gated atomic acknowledged input, PTY write/flush receipts, reconnect dedupe, server incarnations, bounds, tests, ADR, and normative spec.

title: Set up the release GitHub App (blocks release-please)
description:
release-please.yml (PR #215) fails closed until a GitHub App exists.

Why an App and not GITHUB_TOKEN: main's ruleset 'main automation guardrails' requires the check+test contexts with bypass_actors: [] and current_user_can_bypass: never. GitHub raises no workflow runs for GITHUB_TOKEN-triggered events, so a release PR opened with GITHUB_TOKEN would never get CI, those checks would never report, and the PR would be unmergeable BY ANYONE including the owner.

Setup:
1. Create a GitHub App on the phall1 account. Repo permissions: contents: write, pull requests: write.
2. Install it on phall1/phux.
3. Repo variable RELEASE_APP_ID = the App's numeric App ID
4. Repo secret RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY = the App's generated .pem

Both the release-please job and the sync-lockfile job use it. Do not merge PR #215 to main before this exists.
close_reason: Release GitHub App is configured: RELEASE_APP_ID and RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY are present, and release-please successfully opened PR #266.

title: Implement QUIC transport for remote satellite connections
description:
Add QUIC as a transport option for federation, replacing SSH-stdio for remote satellites.

- Quinn-based QUIC server/client
- 0-RTT connection establishment
- Connection migration for network changes
- NAT traversal via hole punching
- Certificate management (mTLS or token-based)
- Fallback to TCP when UDP is blocked

QUIC gives us streams, multiplexing, and connection migration for free. This makes satellite deployment resilient to network changes.
notes: Remote-consumer relationship: native QUIC is Phase 2 of the remote-consumer transport sequence (Phase 1 = wss+token, phux-5vsr). A native consumer reuses quinn directly (wire-identical) for connection migration and no HOL blocking; wss stays the universal fallback for blocked-UDP networks; the browser equivalent is WebTransport (phux-0wmf); NAT traversal still needs the relay (phux-yx6y). Anti-sprawl: QUIC is NOT needed when a remote consumer connects over an overlay (Tailscale/Headscale/WireGuard) — the overlay already gives reachability + encryption + roaming, so QUIC's migration win is redundant and double-encryption is overhead. Mosh-class resilience = overlay path-roaming + app-level state resume (ADR-0018 StateSync). QUIC earns its keep only on the no-overlay/relay path and for federation/satellites (this bead's driver). Treat QUIC + WebTransport + relay as one coherent no-overlay bundle.
close_reason: Completed the launch-critical QUIC remote-attach slice by adding native WebSocket/TLS fallback for UDP-blocked networks, sharing the QUIC certificate pinning trust policy, wiring phux attach --ws, adding WS/WSS transport tests, and updating remote attach docs; nix develop -c just ci passed. NAT relay/hole punching remains tracked separately in phux-yx6y per the issue notes.

title: Implement hub-and-spoke federation with real satellite support
description:
Move federation from wire reservation (v0.1) to fully working hub-and-spoke architecture.

- Hub receives frames with Satellite IDs and relays to appropriate satellite connection
- Satellite enrollment protocol (token-based or mTLS)
- Connection management: satellites reconnect on drop, hub tracks active satellites
- Error handling: UnsupportedSatelliteRoute becomes a real routing decision
- Testing: 2-3 satellite end-to-end scenario

This is the foundation of the distributed C2 architecture. Without this, tradecraft is limited to single-host operations.

title: Cancel per-pane output pumps on DETACH/session switch
description: Audit finding from phux-zh01: handle_attach spawns raw broadcast output pump tasks with spawn_local, but they are not tracked in the per-client JoinSet and have no cancellation token. DETACH removes ServerState subscriptions/consumer state but leaves the pump's broadcast receiver and out_tx clone alive. In the in-process session-switch path, old-session pane output can continue forwarding TERMINAL_OUTPUT frames to the same client after reattach. Fix by tracking output pumps per attach/session and aborting them on DETACH/switch, or routing pump sends through a subscription/session generation check.

title: PTY writer dies permanently on any io error, and its Drop injects newline+VEOF into the pane
description: spawn.rs:401-415 breaks the writer loop on ANY io::Error with no errno discrimination, no retry, no partial-write accounting. Compounding: the receiver drops (discarding up to 64 queued requests), nothing ever restarts the thread (writer_thread is only taken in shutdown_pty), and self.pty_tx stays Some so every later send hits TrySendError::Closed and is discarded at debug! level while ROUTE_INPUT keeps acking Ok -- pane looks alive, all input goes nowhere. Additionally portable-pty's Drop for UnixMasterWriter writes newline + VEOF into the master on thread exit (unix.rs:392-405), which in canonical mode commits a truncated partial line as if complete. EIO asymmetry is the realistic trigger: portable-pty maps EIO to EOF on the read half (unix.rs:94-97) but not the write half (unix.rs:407-412). Split out of phux-6b6t.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #318 (4bbe113e). Writer now classifies errno: EIO/EPIPE are routine child teardown, EINTR/EAGAIN retry under a bounded budget, only unexpected errnos end the loop and they log the partial-write count. write_all replaced by a resuming loop. portable-pty's VEOF-injecting Drop now fires on clean shutdown only (ManuallyDrop), so a failed write can no longer commit a truncated line to a canonical-mode shell. Drop sites raised to warn!/error!.

design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Verified: reload.rs:88 constructs StatusBarPainter::new(bar, Position::default()) while startup uses cfg.status.position.into() (driver.rs:4244-4246). Additional divergence found: reload composes the bar BEFORE loading plugin manifests, whereas startup runs plugin::merge_widget_contributions first (driver.rs:4233-4240) — reload appears to drop plugin-contributed status widgets; same bug class, in scope. - Client: $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/client-<pid>.log (phux-server/src/telemetry.rs:210-223); the doc comment admits "Public so a future phux subcommand can report the path" — no caller exists. Client panics are durable but unreachable.

docs/operations.md:80-84 concedes: no server status, no logs discovery verb. docs/architecture/process-model.md:24-30 flatly contradicts tui.md:558-563 about whether the state dir even exists (tui.md is right; process-model.md is stale).

Fix: (a) a `phux logs` verb (or `phux doctor --logs` section) that names every live log path and which process writes it; (b) doctor gains a check/section reporting log + state paths (doctor.rs:104-109 currently runs four checks, none mention logs); (c) every fatal client/attach error prints where the log went; (d) reconcile the two server log locations or teach service logs about both; (e) surface phux doctor in README.md and docs/QUICKSTART.md — it currently appears only in tui.md (grep-verified).
design: DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream C, 2026-08-01). Resolved: (1) canonical server log is $XDG_STATE_HOME/phux/server.log for BOTH spawn paths — auto-spawn (currently <socket_dir>/phux-server.log, server.rs:305-314) moves to the file the service unit already uses (service.rs:367, 705), via a single phux_server::telemetry::server_log_path() helper so service logs / phux logs / doctor can never disagree; startup line gains pid+version+socket. (2) phux logs is a new top-level verb: bare invocation prints the path inventory, --server/--client tail with -f/-n, --json for machines; phux service logs delegates. (3) doctor gains a logs check (doctor.rs:104-109 has four checks today, none names logs). (4) doctor and logs get surfaced in README and QUICKSTART (grep-verified zero doctor mentions today). (5) Stale process-model.md:22-34 state-dir/stderr claims fixed inside C1 (owner; stream F's F6 defers to it). Fatal-error log pointers implemented in C6 to keep the error-remedy pass in one place. Decomposed into C1, C2, C3; umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: canonical log, phux logs verb, doctor path reporting all landed.

title: Dead config keys: implement or delete defaults.shell / refresh-rate / log-filter; honor or drop the widget style promise
description:
Keys that parse, validate clean, echo back in config show, and do nothing:

- defaults.shell (schema.rs:96): consumed NOWHERE — server unconditionally uses $SHELL (phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:123,266). It is the FIRST LINE of the documented minimal config (tui.md:578) and tests/loader.rs:110 green-lights it.
- defaults.refresh-rate (tui.md:580): dead.
- defaults.log-filter: dead, undocumented, and its doc-comment claims $PHUX_LOG overrides it when PHUX_LOG is actually a log file path (main.rs:132).
- Widget `style` table: tui.md:1923-1925 promises every widget accepts style {fg,bg,bold,...}; NO factory reads it (time.rs:74-89, session_name.rs:65-99, cwd.rs:104-139, exit_status.rs, exec.rs). Opts are an open BTreeMap so it parses and renders unstyled. Only help-hints rejects unknown opts (help_hints.rs:33-38) — the inconsistency is itself a trap.
- session-name widget: tui.md:1911 documents a `format` opt that does not exist (session_name.rs:68-93 reads prefix/max-len).
- defaults.mouse works but is documented nowhere.

Fix: each key either gets implemented or deleted (with docs updated); widget opts move to closed structs or a per-factory unknown-opt warning surfaced via config check. Guiding rule: if `phux config check` says ok, the key must do something.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01) — per-key verdicts** (note: widget factories live in crates/phux-config/src/widget/widgets/, not phux-client; substance of every audit claim holds): defaults.shell (schema.rs:93-96) IMPLEMENT via a resolve_shell seam mirroring the defaults.term/apply_term precedent, threaded from the server's single config load. defaults.refresh-rate DELETE (no consumer exists; with deny_unknown_fields a stale config fails loudly with a located finding — the epic's contract). defaults.log-filter DELETE (zero consumers; its $PHUX_LOG doc claim is false — PHUX_LOG is a log-file path; filtering is RUST_LOG). defaults.mouse works — DOCUMENT in tui.md §12. Widget style table (tui.md:1927-1929 promise) IMPLEMENT UNIVERSALLY by hoisting style extraction into the registry build path (CellStyle already exists). session-name `format` opt IMPLEMENT. Widget opts CLOSE: generalize help_hints' unknown-opt rejection to every factory with did-you-mean; surface widget composition errors through config check. Decomposed into A8 (defaults truth) and A9 (widget closure + style). Umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: defaults truth (wave 3) + widget closure/style (wave 4).

title: [umbrella] Validate what parses: vocab registry, config check semantics, lenient resolver, honest error lines
description:
Everything that parses is assumed valid; three independent silent-no-op traps:

1. Typo'd action name: "x" = "kill-pain" parses (Action::Bare, schema.rs:369), passes config check, and the key does nothing — logged at tracing::debug only (input_dispatch.rs:2560-2562). The canonical 36-name list ACTION_NAMES already exists (input_dispatch.rs:1727) and is CI-enforced against the palette, but is not exposed to the validator.

2. One malformed chord disables EVERY keybinding including detach: driver.rs:3709-3716 — Resolver::new fails on first bad chord -> tracing::warn -> None -> no binding resolves. config check cannot catch it because chords are BTreeMap string keys.

3. Hooks fail open three ways (check.rs:329-334 asserts free-form hook keys are never flagged): typo'd event name ([[hooks.pane-exited]] vs real pane-exit, phux-server/src/hooks.rs:56) never fires; unknown `when` key never matches (hooks.rs:528); non-server-executable matched action consumes the event at debug level (hooks.rs:435-440). The six valid event names are consts at hooks.rs:54-64, surfaced nowhere.

Fix: teach phux config check (and resolver-build error paths) the action-name list, chord grammar, and hook event-name list; a bad chord must degrade to "this one binding is dead, loudly" not "all bindings are dead, silently". Also fix the on-screen config error (driver.rs:4259) to recommend `phux config check` instead of `phux config show`, and stop printing the fabricated 1:1 position (lib.rs:143) that check.rs:19-21 itself calls "worse than reporting none".
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Evidence verified: ACTION_NAMES at input_dispatch.rs:1726 (36 names, CI-synced); silent unhandled-action arm at input_dispatch.rs:2560-2562; Resolver::new fails whole on first bad chord and driver.rs:3709-3716 degrades to None = every binding dead including detach; unknown hook `when` key silently never matches (hooks.rs:519-530); non-`run` matched hook action consumes the event at debug! (hooks.rs:435-440); fabricated (1,1) span at lib.rs:130-131; wrong remedy `phux config show` at driver.rs:4256-4260. Architecture decision: **phux-config owns the validation vocabulary** (new crates/phux-config/src/vocab.rs). ACTION_NAMES moves INTO phux-config and is re-exported from input_dispatch.rs; hook event names move in from phux-server hooks.rs with re-exports; CI sync tests pin dispatch to vocab. No new crate, no codegen; did-you-mean is a ~25-line in-crate Levenshtein, no new dependency. Resolver policy: attach-time builds become lenient per-binding (new_lenient + diagnostics surfaced on the status bar); strict new stays for config check and reload (reload keeps all-or-nothing per tui.md:1119-1122). Decomposed into A2 (vocab), A3 (chords+actions in check), A4 (hooks in check + loud runtime warnings), A5 (lenient resolver), A6 (remedy + span honesty). Umbrella. Cross-stream: vocab is also consumed by stream F's generated action/widget/hook references (F3/F4).
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all five children (vocab, check semantics, hooks, lenient resolver, honest errors) landed across waves 1-3.

title: TUI failure surface: pane exit status, last-pane death, live reconnect indicator
description:
Three silent failure paths in the attach TUI, all evidence-verified:

1. Pane death is invisible. server_frame.rs:1169-1215 (phux-client): TerminalClosed receives exit_status, logs at tracing::info (file only), removes the PaneSlot, folds the layout. No toast, no "[exited 137]" placeholder, no status-bar line. When the last pane dies (1211-1216) the whole client exits with zero explanation — an OOM-killed shell looks like phux crashed.

2. Server crash = ~10 seconds of blank terminal. attach.rs:272 RECONNECT_DEADLINE=10s; attach.rs:335-341 prints "server restarted; re-attaching" only AFTER a successful reconnect; the alt screen is already torn down. No "reconnecting..." indicator during the window, and on failure the user gets the generic "connection closed by server before DETACHED" arm (mod.rs:2095-2097) with no log path, no doctor pointer.

3. The status-bar error_line mechanism exists (status_bar.rs:526-534) but is called for config errors only (driver.rs:4224,4251). Disconnect, reconnect-in-progress, pane death, degraded federation, take/give authority changes all have no user-facing representation.

Fix: exit-status toast + optional dead-pane placeholder; a reconnecting state that is visible while it happens; route lifecycle events through the existing error_line/toast machinery. docs/consumers/tui.md:28-40 calls the TUI the adoption wedge — the wire is the differentiator and the wire is precisely what has no failure UI.
design:
DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream B, 2026-08-01) — decomposed into B1/B2/B3; umbrella. Resolved: (1) Pane-death UX is a transient STATUS-BAR NOTICE, not a modal and not a dead-pane placeholder (placeholder rejected: layout is a shared metadata envelope — a client-local dead leaf desyncs siblings and PTY winsizes; a server-side dead leaf is a wire change out of scope). Text 'pane <label>: exited N' / 'killed (signal or unknown)'; suppressed for exit 0 and client-initiated kill-pane; 7 s newest-wins slot. (2) Last-pane death: run_* entry points return Result<AttachEnd, AttachError> (Detached | LastPaneClosed { exit_status }); the CLI prints a one-line explanation on the cooked terminal after teardown; process exit stays 0. (3) Reconnect: NO alt-screen re-entry — RawModeGuard drops on unwind (driver.rs:1258), so the 10 s wait (attach.rs:318-344) runs cooked; honest design is a live stderr countdown plus a post-reconnect status-bar notice inside the next attach (the current eprintln at attach.rs:337 is instantly alt-screened over). Failure distinguishes socket-unlinked vs timeout and names phux doctor. (4) General mechanism: StatusBarPainter gains a transient Notice slot riding the existing 1 s status_tick; persistent error_line outranks it; FrameOutcome gains notices: Vec<Notice>; first consumer is input-authority transitions. No wire changes — TERMINAL_CLOSED already carries exit_status (frame.rs:2105-2110).

FINALIZER AMENDMENT (2026-08-01): the bead's five enumerated lifecycle events must ALL map to a surface. Degraded federation was orphaned; B1 now carries it as the Notice slot's second consumer (degraded-federation transitions push a Warn notice, server_frame-tested). C5's phux status degradation line remains the CLI view, not a substitute for the in-TUI representation.

title: Server silently swallows a broken config.toml and reverts to defaults
description:
crates/phux/src/commands/server.rs:113-148 reads history-limit, cwd-inheritance, term, window-size, and the entire hook catalog via five consecutive config_loader::load().map_or_else(|_| default, ...) calls. A single typo in config.toml silently disables every configured hook and reverts scrollback/TERM/window-size policy, then the server prints its normal "listening on ..." banner. Contrast server.rs:153-158 where connector registry failure correctly aborts loudly, and the client attach path which at least prints one line (attach.rs:110-113).

Also: config is read from disk five separate times in ~35 lines, so an edit mid-startup yields a torn read.

Fix: load once, bind once. On failure, print the config-check-style error to stderr (and the server log) and state explicitly which defaults are in effect. Never revert silently.
design:
---

**Design resolution (stream A, 2026-08-01).** Audit correction: a malformed config.toml already kills the server today via the fatal connector-registry read (server.rs:153-158) with a misattributed error; the five earlier reads (server.rs:113-148) silently default and misattribute every config error to the connector registry. Resolved design: load config exactly once; a broken config is fatal at server start with the real error and the remedy `run: phux config check`, written to both stderr and the server log via tracing::error (auto-spawn nulls stdio, so the log line is the durable trace). Missing file stays fine (loader.rs:71-77 returns defaults on NotFound). Degrade-and-continue rejected: the connector security stance already makes any parse error fatal, and one load cannot scope an error to a section. Decomposed into A1 (single load + loud fatal) and A8 (defaults.shell rides A1's struct). This bead is now an umbrella.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: single child 1.1 landed (wave 1).

title: [epic] UX: it just works — never silent, one grammar, visible at the moment of need
description:
Full-surface UX audit (2026-08-01, three parallel deep audits: CLI ergonomics, config surface, onboarding/visibility) found that phux's UX foundations are genuinely excellent but exist as islands: phux doctor, phux config check, config layering with provenance, output_hygiene.rs, the broken-pipe discipline, the first-run overlay. The product-level failures are four systemic patterns, not missing features:

1. SILENCE. Errors, dead keys, typos, and pane death all no-op invisibly: server swallows a broken config.toml with zero output (server.rs:113-148); a typo'd action name logs at debug (input_dispatch.rs:2560); one malformed chord disables ALL keybindings including detach (driver.rs:3709); a dying pane discards its exit status (server_frame.rs:1169-1216); server crash = 10s blank screen (attach.rs:272-341).

2. INVISIBILITY. The good tools are never pointed to at the moment of need: doctor appears in zero READMEs/quickstarts; three different log files exist and no command or doc ever prints any path; the on-screen config error names the wrong recovery command (driver.rs:4259 says "phux config show", the diagnostic tool is "config check").

3. INCONSISTENCY. 89 invocation paths with per-command grammar: --socket copy-pasted 36 times and not global; --json on ~32 verbs with no shorthand and no error-path contract; ls/list/rm/remove alias roulette across 8 registries; two split-direction flag styles (one of which is parsed and discarded, main.rs:364); four near-duplicate concept pairs (enroll vs satellite enroll, remote vs satellite, pair vs relay pair, workspace vs worktree).

4. DOCS DRIFT. CONFIG.md says reload does not exist (it ships); tui.md promises a widget style table no factory reads; README claims scrollback search that has no action; defaults.shell is the first line of the documented minimal config and is consumed nowhere.

Design principle for every child issue: the failure path IS the product. Simplicity means one grammar, and every error names its own remedy. Builds on phux-q9wj (CLI and API surface polish, 3/4 done); supersedes its altitude.

Full audit reports preserved in the three child-issue descriptions and session transcript 3bedc523.
design:
---

**Stream G landing sequence (planning resolution, 2026-08-01).** The epic lands in dependency waves closed by stream-G integration gates: never-silent failure surface (.1-.6) gated by G2; one-grammar + host namespace (.7 .8 .12) gated by G3; help/discoverability/docs+generated reference (.9 .10 .11) gated by G4. After the grammar wave, a deprecation-alias audit test (crates/phux/tests/deprecated_aliases.rs) pins every hidden alias, its deprecation note, and its absence from help/completions, bidirectionally against the clap tree. A scripted failure-UX dogfood lands as crates/phux/tests/failure_ux_e2e.rs in the `just e2e` PR lane (per scripts/check-e2e-lanes.sh), so the new failure UX is CI-enforced, not a release ritual. Release is a release-please minor bump (0.6.0 -> 0.7.0, automatic from feat commits under bump-minor-pre-major): run scripts/release-preflight.sh, undraft the release PR to run CI, merge; then `gh release edit` prepends the UX story + deprecation table (release.yml only uploads assets, never rewrites the body). Epic close: bd close sweep, bd remember entries (vocab location, reference-generation mechanism, alias contract, failure-UX lane), vision.md remaining-work reality check. Merge protocol throughout: branch per slice, rebase + ff-only, conventional commits, `just ci` green before every merge.
notes: EXECUTION IN PROGRESS (2026-08-01, session 3bedc523): user ordered full autonomous execution to completion. Wave-by-wave workflow loop; playbook + graph at scratchpad ux-epic/ (execution-playbook.md). Wave 1 = phux-i0e8.1.1, .3.1, .3.4, .2.1 branching from origin/main 6770f366.

description: PR 316 fails CI in phux-server::hub_relay_federation::aggregated_list_merges_local_and_satellite_terminals_and_degrades. Reproduce the failure, correct the test or implementation, run relevant quality gates, update the PR branch, and enable merge queue/automerge.

title: Snapshot replay drops mouse-reporting DEC modes, breaking scroll in TUIs after attach
description: The TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT epilogue replayed bracketed paste, focus events and the alt-screen bits but never the mouse-reporting modes (9/1000/1002/1003, 1005/1006/1015/1016, 1007). The client gates wheel handling on its own libghostty mirror, so a mirror seeded from such a snapshot believes no program wants the mouse and downgrades the wheel to arrow keys. Repro: opencode in a phux pane -- scrolling moved the editor cursor instead of the message list.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #314: snapshot epilogue now replays the mouse-reporting DEC modes (9/1000/1002/1003, 1005/1006/1015/1016, 1007), and ReferenceCursorMode tracks the same bits so the per-tick diff path re-emits on a bare mouse-mode toggle.

title: Headless geometry: agents cannot set a pane size without a real PTY
description:
There is no way to set a pane's size without attaching a real terminal. phux new has no size flag, phux snapshot --rendered --cols/--rows does not persist (verified: pane stayed 80x24 after a 120x40 rendered read), and there is no phux resize verb.

This bit twice building phux rec: the demo asset is stuck at 80x24, and the non-resize regression test has to stand up a full portable-pty attach purely to obtain a pane whose size differs from the 80x24 a mistaken attach would impose -- otherwise the test resizes an 80x24 pane to 80x24 and passes vacuously.

For a project whose pitch is that agents are first-class users, agents cannot set a terminal's size. Proposed: a phux resize TARGET COLSxROWS verb and/or --cols/--rows on phux new, with the interaction against the attached-client WindowSize policy (schema.rs WindowSize::Smallest) thought through and specced -- that policy is why this is a design question and not a one-line flag.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Conformance test: the three libghostty cell projections must agree
description:
The libghostty snapshot -> RenderedFrame projection now exists three times: crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs, crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs, and crates/phux-record/src/replay.rs.

The duplication is a DELIBERATE, documented tradeoff (a shared home would force phux-core to depend on libghostty, which is worse), so this issue is not 'deduplicate them'. It is that three copies which must agree cell-for-cell have nothing enforcing it, and divergence surfaces as 'the recording does not match the screen' or 'the agent sees different cells than the human' -- the bug class nobody notices for months.

Work: a conformance test that feeds one corpus of VT bytes (SGR truecolor and palette, wide CJK plus spacer tails, combining marks, alt screen, scroll regions, DECAWM wrap, cursor states) through all three projections and asserts identical output. Where they cannot be identical, assert the difference explicitly so it is a decision rather than a drift.

Consider afterwards whether a thin phux-vt-project crate between phux-core and libghostty is worth the refactor; the test is valuable either way and is the cheap half.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Shared scripted-server test harness so fakes cannot lie about frame order
description:
Unit-test fake servers are hand-written per module, so each one encodes what its author believed the protocol does. That is the same belief that produces the bug, so the fake cannot catch it.

Evidence: 17 phux rec unit tests passed against a completely non-functional feature because the fake answered COMMAND_RESULT before the priming snapshot, while the real server does the opposite.

Work, cheapest first:
1. Extract one shared scripted_server into a test-support module, with the reference server's frame ORDER encoded once (snapshot before ack on ATTACH_TERMINAL, etc.).
2. Migrate the per-module fakes to it.
3. Consider golden frame traces: capture real server responses once into fixtures and replay them, so a fake that diverges from the reference implementation fails. Bigger lift; decide after 1 and 2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Add Connection::request so COMMAND callers cannot swallow interleaved frames
description:
Connection exposes send()/recv() only, so every COMMAND caller hand-rolls 'loop until my request_id returns'. The server legitimately interleaves: handle_attach_terminal pushes TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT before the COMMAND_RESULT ack. A caller that discards non-matching frames loses data that is never re-sent.

This is not hypothetical. It shipped as a bug in phux rec (fixed in PR #306): captures came back as a 0x0 grid with no opening screen, and all 17 unit tests passed because the scripted fake answered ack-first.

Work:
1. Add Connection::request(cmd) -> Result<(CommandResult, Vec<FrameKind>)> that returns interleaved frames instead of eating them. Callers physically cannot forget what they did not ask to drop.
2. AUDIT every existing COMMAND caller for the same swallow: GetScreen, GetTerminalState, AcquireInput, ReleaseInput, SignalTerminal, KillTerminal(s), DetachClients, PutFile, SubscribeTerminalEvents. Report which ones discard frames and whether the server can interleave on that path. This audit is the point of the issue; the helper is the easy half.
3. Migrate callers, and document the interleave contract on Connection itself.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: [epic] Seams and guardrails surfaced by the recording slice
description:
The phux rec feature (phux-e7ez, PR #306) cut across protocol, server, client, CLI, docs, and CI. That slice exposed a set of missing seams and absent guardrails. Each child is evidence-backed: something that actually bit during the build, not a speculative cleanup.

Theme: every item is a case where a silent, hard-to-notice failure is possible because a contract exists in someone's head or in prose, but nothing in the type system or CI enforces it.
close_reason: All children landed across PR #307 and #309.

title: Support managed Gas City runtime sessions
description: Add the generic Phux lifecycle behavior required by a native Gas City runtime provider: headless-created sessions must arm last-session server self-exit, and session creation must preserve explicit environment values.
acceptance_criteria: phux new can pass typed environment overrides into the seed process; a server used only through headless control exits after its last session is killed; focused tests and local CI pass.
notes: PR, protected-branch merge, semver bump, and release authorized by user.

title: [epic] Built-in session recording: phux --rec to .cast and .gif
description: Native terminal-session recording built into phux: `phux --rec <out>` on the attach path and headless `phux rec <target> -o <out>`. Exports asciinema cast v2 and an animated GIF rendered natively in Rust (no vhs/agg/ffmpeg at runtime), replaying captured VT bytes through libghostty-vt into a cell grid and rasterizing with an embedded bitmap font. title: worktree remove kills bound session before git validates removal
description: run_remove in crates/phux/src/commands/worktree.rs kills the bound session BEFORE running git worktree remove, but only pre-checks 'current' and dirty state. git also refuses: main working tree, locked worktrees, submodules. Scenario: 'phux worktree remove main' from another worktree kills the primary session, then git refuses removal — session lost, worktree still there. Fix: mark first entry from 'git worktree list --porcelain' as is_main and refuse before killing; also check locked attribute. Found by research-team review of f1a1306..b7ffd45, adversarially verified.
notes: Fixed: WorktreeInfo now carries is_main (first porcelain entry) and locked; run_remove refuses main worktree and locked worktrees BEFORE killing the session. Parser test extended.
close_reason: Closed

title: BUG: PTY input writer corrupts or dies under large paste load
description: Live phux-mobile image-upload experiments over INPUT_PASTE reproduced nondeterministic byte corruption in tiny 1.8 KiB base64 payloads (first divergence around byte 1150/1450) and the server log 'pty writer: write failed; pane input is now dead' under load. A 1.9 MiB JPEG also remained in canonical-mode ingest after 24s. ADR-0059 PutFile bypasses this path for file upload, but large interactive pastes still traverse the PTY input writer and may corrupt or permanently kill pane input. Reproduce with repeated multi-KiB trusted INPUT_PASTE / APPLY_INPUT batches against a checksum-reading fixture; fix write/flush/backpressure ownership so bytes are ordered and the writer survives transient pressure.
close_reason:
Resolved by decomposition (option A). RCA split this into three distinct defects; every part is now fixed or tracked separately.

1. 'dies under load' -> REAL BUG, fixed. Writer broke on any io::Error with no errno discrimination and never restarted, so a routine child exit permanently killed pane input. Fixed in phux-oxd7 / PR #318 (4bbe113e).

2. 'corrupts' -> WORKS AS SPECIFIED. A single INPUT_PASTE event is already atomic (one contiguous Vec, one write_all). Corruption only appears when a consumer splits ONE logical payload across MULTIPLE fire-and-forget events, and L1 SPEC section 9 explicitly makes those droppable ('a full mailbox drops the event but still acks OK'). The spec never promised cross-event delivery or ordering. ADR-0053 APPLY_INPUT (acknowledged, reconnect-safe) and ADR-0059 PutFile exist for exactly this; the original reporter, phux-mobile image upload, has already moved to PutFile. Making fire-and-forget atomic would put backpressure on the hot keystroke path -- a latency regression for phux's core purpose -- to buy correctness a different verb already provides. The defensible complaint was the SILENCE, not the semantics: both drop sites were raised to warn!/error! in PR #318.

3. 'canonical-mode ingest stuck after 24s' -> separate mechanism, tracked as phux-mjmc (P2). Empirically reproduced: MAX_CANON wedge, a hang rather than corruption.

Residual guidance gap filed separately.

title: send-keys TARGET "text" Enter does not submit in codex; Enter must be a separate call
description:
Observed while capturing codex detection fixtures. 'phux send-keys --socket S cx "prompt text" Enter' places the text in codex's composer but does NOT submit — the composer still shows the text and no turn starts. Sending 'phux send-keys --socket S cx Enter' as its own call immediately submits.

Likely the same class herdr hit (their 0.7.5 notes: 'Named agent prompts now honor live bracketed-paste mode before sending Enter'). Probable cause: the text is delivered as a paste/bracketed run and the trailing Enter is coalesced into it, so codex sees a literal newline inside the paste rather than a submit key.

Matters because it is the documented one-liner for driving an agent from a script, and it silently half-works: the text lands, so a caller sees no error and waits forever for a turn that never started. Worth an e2e test against a real agent TUI.
close_reason: Merged by PR #295 after live Codex reproduction and full local CI passed

title: Right-click context menus in the TUI (pane, window, session)
description: Right-click currently forwards to the pane or is dropped on chrome. Add anchored context menus: right-click a pane opens a pane menu, a status-bar tab or sidebar window row opens a window menu, other chrome opens a session menu. Menu commits flow through run_action like every other affordance.
notes: Shipped in PR #293 (branch feat/right-click-context-menus). ADR-0058 records the interaction model.
close_reason: Closed

title: phux doctor: one-command install diagnosis
description: Composes config check, socket-path validation, server reachability, and plugin manifest loading into one read-only verdict with three states (pass/warn/fail). Warn means 'could not verify' and does not fail the run, so a stopped server is not reported as a broken install. Every non-pass carries a next step. Goes past herdr, which documents troubleshooting in prose but ships no preflight command.

RETRACTED — false alarm on every count, verified 2026-07-25.

My earlier claim came from reading 'timeout ... exit=124' as a hang — but 124 is what timeout reports whenever it had to signal the command, which is the normal outcome for a long-running stream verb. title: Native agent-session restore: persist and replay agent resume identity across pane restart
description: A phux-launched agent may carry a provider-native resume identity. Persist that identity with exact Terminal and integration provenance, include it in workspace archives, and reconstruct the provider's safe structured argv when workspace restore recreates the pane. Provider semantics remain client/plugin-owned L3 policy; the server only transports and atomically stores bounded opaque record bytes, without interpreting native identities.
design: Use a dedicated terminal-scoped, versioned L3 restore record rather than overloading `phux.agent/v1.session` (a free-form fleet label) or plugin-global link state. The record contains exact plugin/integration ownership plus an opaque, bounded native identity. The launch client carries the encoded record in additive optional `SPAWN_TERMINAL` field 9 so the server can install it atomically in the same state transaction that creates the local Terminal; ordinary metadata GET/SET remains the durable readback surface and the server never interprets provider semantics. Create-without-attach carries the same bytes in its nonce-correlated `phux.session.create/v1` request and installs them while seeding the pane. Workspace save copies only validated records read from exact local TerminalIds and verifies the terminal set did not change across collection. Restore re-resolves a unique enabled plugin/integration owner before reconstructing structured argv. Archive format advances to schema v2 while parsing schema v1 through an explicit compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Integration templates expose a typed, validated native-session policy with a bounded identity source and structured fresh/resume argv; the placeholder occupies exactly one whole argv element, substitution never invokes a shell, and option-shaped identities are rejected.
2. `phux launch` captures a non-empty provider-native identity only from the integration's declared source and carries a bounded, versioned Terminal-scoped record atomically with the exact local `SPAWN_TERMINAL`; it never guesses from focused state or a global link.
3. `phux workspace save` collects each local pane's valid restore record into archive schema v2 and refuses an inconsistent snapshot if the local Terminal set changes during collection. Schema-v1 archives remain readable only through the explicit compatibility path; v2 fails closed for older readers.
4. `phux workspace restore` selects the archived preferred pane, re-resolves exactly one current enabled `(plugin_id, integration_id)` owner, validates provenance and bounds, uses the current integration working-directory policy, and replays the native identity as structured argv. Existing session names remain skipped without launching anything.
5. Missing records preserve non-agent restore behavior. Malformed, oversized, ambiguous-owner, unavailable-integration, option-shaped, stale, and ownership-mismatched data fail clearly before that session is spawned; there is no silent fresh-agent fallback or cross-pane/session identity reuse.
6. Protocol compatibility is additive: no new frame type/tag or protocol-version break; optional `SPAWN_TERMINAL` field 9 is ignored by older servers, and the versioned L3 metadata convention remains the durable consumer surface. Satellite spawns reject local provenance.
7. Session creation results are nonce-correlated and one-shot; failed/competing creates cannot reuse another caller's TerminalId. Provenance is installed in the same server state transaction that creates/interns the pane and is removed by normal Terminal reaping.
8. Deterministic tests cover template validation/substitution, unique owner resolution, wire compatibility, exact-Terminal atomic persistence and bounds, archive v1 compatibility/v2 round-trip, restart/replay argv, existing-session skip, stale ownership, and snapshot consistency. The real restore smoke observes resumed argv after server restart.
9. Formatting, focused tests, full `just ci`, docs checks, and required repository gates pass; review findings and CI failures are fixed before merge.
notes: Implementation complete: Terminal-scoped versioned native resume records, schema-v2 archives, current-policy argv/env/cwd reconstruction, atomic spawn provenance, owner-only bounded nonce results, batch preflight for older servers, rollback/confirmation, and stale/ambiguous ownership rejection. Validation: focused restart/replay E2E passed; focused security tests passed; just ci passed (3079/3079 tests, fmt, clippy, docs, deny). Independent correctness and security re-reviews report no remaining actionable findings.

title: watch consumers are starved of dirty/idle events unless a StateSync consumer exists
description: docs/consumers/agents.md lists dirty and idle among the events 'phux watch --json' emits, but on the current server a watch subscriber effectively never receives them: tick_emit (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/mod.rs, ~line 2957) returns early when no consumer negotiated OutputMode::StateSync, WITHOUT clearing terminal_dirty_since_tick ('dirty flag untouched' comment). maybe_emit_idle (~line 1637) requires that flag false, so idle never fires; in_output_burst latches true at the pane's first-ever output, so dirty is emitted exactly once per pane lifetime — and a watcher only sees it if subscribed before the pane's first output. The reference TUI attach client negotiates OutputMode::Raw (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs ~line 1368), so in practice no consumer opens the gate. Repro: 'phux watch --json' on a fresh pane, drive output with send-keys — bell/title_changed/pane_closed flow, dirty arrives at most once, idle never. Either tick_emit should maintain the dirty/idle bookkeeping independently of StateSync negotiation, or agents.md must stop advertising dirty/idle as generally available — any wait/watch consumer hoping to observe quiescence without polling is affected. Line numbers are as of 379cae0.
