title: Mouse input never reaches pane apps: encoder emits zero bytes without EncoderSize; scrolling dead in phux
description: User-visible: cannot scroll inside phux panes at all; worst in mouse-tracking apps (Claude Code sets ?1000h/?1002h/?1003h/?1006h — probed 2026-07-14) which never receive wheel events. Root cause chain: (1) PerTerminalMouseEncoder::encode never configures libghostty mouse EncoderSize; ghostty's encoder emits ZERO bytes for every event when cell geometry is unset (proven by probe test: click and wheel encode to empty against a full-tracking terminal; with EncoderSize set the same events encode to correct SGR). service_input then drops them at the 'encoded to zero bytes' branch — so ALL mouse input (clicks included) is silently discarded server-side, violating docs/spec/input.md §3.2 which mandates setting EncoderSize from Terminal/cell geometry. (2) The TUI client sends pane-local CELL indices in INPUT_MOUSE but spec §3.1 defines wire positions as Terminal-local surface PIXELS (cell_index x cell_size for cell-quantized clients) — must convert at the send boundary or fixed server quantization mis-lands clicks. (3) Alt-screen apps WITHOUT mouse tracking (less, vim) get a local scroll_viewport that no-ops (alt screen has no scrollback); needs xterm alternate-scroll: wheel -> arrow keys when alt screen + mode 1007 (libghostty defaults 1007 ON, probed). Primary-screen local scrollback path (input_dispatch.rs:683) is sound. Fix: server sets EncoderSize (cell_px from actor, cols/rows from terminal); client converts cells->pixels using host cell geometry (fallback 8x16 == server DEFAULT_CELL_PX); client synthesizes Up/Down INPUT_KEY x3 for alt-screen+1007 non-tracking wheel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Server does not inject PHUX_SOCKET into spawned panes; in-pane phux CLI silently hits the default server
description:
The server injects PHUX_TERMINAL_ID into every pane it spawns (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/spawn.rs:170 apply_terminal_id) so an in-pane process can 'self-target on the phux wire with zero configuration'. But it does not inject the socket it is listening on. So an in-pane 'phux <verb>' on a server bound to a non-default socket resolves default_socket_path() and talks to a DIFFERENT server.

Observed live: a pane spawned by a server on /tmp/pvfy.sock ran a bare 'phux agent set --name reviewer'; the write landed on the default-socket server's @1 -- a live pane in an unrelated session -- with no error. The pane's own server never saw it.

Zero-config self-targeting is only true on the default socket. PHUX_TERMINAL_ID names WHICH pane but not WHICH server, and the pair is what identifies a pane.

Fix: inject PHUX_SOCKET=<the server's listening socket> alongside PHUX_TERMINAL_ID at both spawn sites (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:101 and :181). Blocker: ServerState/SharedState does not currently carry the socket path (crates/phux-server/src/state/mod.rs:96), so it needs threading through seed_session_with_pty{,_and_colors} / spawn_pane_with_pty{,_and_colors} or storing on state at startup. Also update the apply_terminal_id doc comment, which currently overclaims 'zero configuration'.
close_reason: Landed on main via integration train PR #255 (rebase-merge, commits 8a4097e4..b5f72d15)

title: TUI: attention indicator + jump-to-next-attention
description:
The human half of 'pop over to it': you are working in one pane, an agent elsewhere gets blocked, you see it, you press a key, you are there. Then you press another key and you are back (which is why the '=' / last-focused bug matters).

There is more to build on here than you would expect: 'phux agent list' already infers per-pane agent state (working / blocked / idle, with a confidence score and a reason -- verified live: it correctly identified a blocked Claude in pane 22). There is already a focus-pane action addressing (window index, DFS leaf ordinal), described in the code as being 'used by the agent-fleet dashboard' (input_dispatch.rs:2029). Find that dashboard and build on it rather than beside it.
design:
Files: the action table -- actions are STRING-NAMED, not an enum: ACTION_NAMES at attach/input_dispatch.rs:1502-1534, dispatch is 'match resolved.action.as_str()' in run_action (:1548), and the palette/help metadata registry is attach/action_registry.rs:139-292. Default keybindings live in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml (prefix C-a, :82; existing pane bindings :96-116). Status bar is the natural home for the indicator -- note a recent commit already moved the status bar out of the sidebar's columns, so look at how it composes today.

Keep the jump ADVISORY (the human presses the key) unless ADR-0044's opt-in directed-focus config is on. The whole point of the ADR's focus/attention distinction is that the human stays in control of their own viewport by default.
acceptance_criteria: With an agent blocked in another pane, the status bar shows it, one keybinding jumps there, and one jumps back. Works with several agents blocked at once (cycle). Bindings documented in docs/consumers/tui.md:429-438 and defaulted in default.toml.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Attention channel: an agent raises 'I need you, at pane N'
description:
The mechanism behind 'hey, pop over to it.' Per ADR-0044, this is a notification with an actionable target -- NOT shared focus, NOT a viewport yank.

Most of this may already exist. AgentEvent::Asked ships today (ADR-0035/0036), carries {id, question, suggestions, elapsed_seconds}, is emitted both from the REPORT_ASKED command (runtime/commands.rs:2098) and from an OSC-title sentinel (terminal_actor/mod.rs:1460-1470), and the TUI ALREADY handles it (server_frame.rs:1203). 'phux ask' is already a CLI verb and 'phux_ask' is already an MCP tool. So the honest first question for this bead is: is 'agent wants attention' just Asked, or is it genuinely a different event? ADR-0044 decides; implement what it says.
design:
If a new AgentEvent tag is needed, next free is 0x0b (frame.rs:424-458). Files: the AgentEvent enum (frame.rs:1373), EVENT_TAG_* const, encode_agent_event (:3610), decode_agent_event (:3702), the proptest roundtrip + insta golden-byte snapshot (crates/phux-protocol/tests/), an emitter, and the hub relay forward path (hub/relay.rs:956-965).

TWO TRAPS:
1. There are TWO parallel event fan-out paths and they are NOT unified. Path A (SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS -> broadcast_event, runtime/client.rs:1227) carries Bell/Asked/TitleChanged. Path B (SUBSCRIBE_TERMINAL_EVENTS -> the actor's own subscriber list, terminal_actor/mod.rs:1546) carries TerminalControl. A new event must pick one, or wire both -- pick wrong and the TUI never sees it.
2. Consumers match AgentEvent non-exhaustively, so a new variant compiles everywhere and is SILENTLY IGNORED. The three places that must actually learn about it: phux-client/src/watch.rs:72, phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs:1171-1255 (the TUI), phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:412-441 (the JSON projection agents read).
NOTE: adding an AgentEvent tag IS a wire change (spec + CHANGELOG + version bump), unlike the layout work. If ADR-0044 lets us reuse Asked instead, this bead gets much cheaper -- prefer that if it is honest.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can raise attention against a pane and an attached TUI learns about it. Old clients skip an unknown tag rather than breaking (AgentEvent::Unknown, frame.rs:1481). If the wire changed: docs/spec updated, CHANGELOG appended, PROTOCOL_VERSION bumped, golden snapshots regenerated.
close_reason: Already implemented by AgentEvent::Asked across CLI, MCP, shared client, wire, and TUI attention fold; ADR-0049 selects this advisory channel without new wire.

title: MCP parity: expose the full control surface, not a subset
description:
The MCP adapter exposes 11 tools; the CLI exposes 26 verbs. MCP is missing, among others: launch (the agent launcher -- the single most important verb for this epic), spawn, signal, take/give (input lease), tag, rename, agent (identity/state inference), and the new spatial verbs from this epic (focus, split, move).

Net effect today: an LLM connected over MCP is strictly WEAKER than the same LLM shelling out to the CLI through Bash. That is backwards -- ADR-0022 says the CLI is the stable contract and MCP is 'a thin adapter over the same structured surface', so the adapter should not be a lossy subset of it.

Deliberately ONE bead, not several: every MCP tool edits the same json! catalog array (tools.rs:64-172), the same dispatch match (:184-197), AND a test asserting the EXACT ORDERED vec of tool names (:717-729). Parallel beads here are a guaranteed three-way conflict on one array. Do them all in one coherent pass.
design:
Per-tool recipe (from the anatomy inventory): catalog entry in the json! array; dispatch arm; handler fn (or its own module with schema()/call(), mirroring ask_tool.rs -- preferred for anything non-trivial, and then a mod decl in main.rs:37-42); add the name to the ORDERED test vec at :717-729; extend the required-args test at :781-823.

CRITICAL: the handler must call the SHARED phux-client fn, not re-implement the CLI's logic. The adapter has already drifted by duplicating: MCP's phux_kill (tools.rs:346) omits the CLI's per-pane KILL_TERMINAL fallback and never fetches the tag index; MCP's create_session duplicates the SESSION_CREATE_KEY metadata dance; run_nonce() is a copy-paste 'matching phux run's run_nonce'. Do not add nine more copies. Depends on the get_state de-duplication bead for the same reason.

Docs: docs/consumers/mcp.md:102 hardcodes the tool count IN PROSE ('Eleven tools') -- bump it. Add a section 3.N per tool (model: 3.7 phux_kill at :219-231). Update the name-for-name CLI mapping at :352-364.

Also fix the two known CLI/MCP divergences while you are in here (docs/consumers/mcp.md:116-121, :178-185): phux_ls returns raw wire fields (window_count/attached_client_count) where the CLI projects to windows/attached, and on run timeout MCP returns {outcome:'timed_out'} in the body where the CLI emits no JSON and exits 125. Parsers are currently not portable between the two surfaces, which defeats the point of a 'thin adapter'.
acceptance_criteria: Every CLI control verb has an MCP tool, or a documented reason it does not (attach and server are legitimately TUI/daemon-only). Handlers share phux-client fns with the CLI -- no new duplication, and the existing kill/create_session/run_nonce duplication is retired. Tool count in mcp.md prose is correct. An LLM on MCP is no longer weaker than the same LLM on Bash.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Placement on spawn and launch: put the agent's pane where the caller asked
description:
The payoff bead for the whole epic. 'phux launch claude-code --target . --split vertical --ratio 0.3' -- go get an agent, put it beside me.

Today launch/spawn have zero placement control and land the new pane by horizontally splitting whatever pane happens to have been created first in the window (see the spawn-placement bug). Fixing that bug makes the default sane; this bead makes placement explicit and callable.
design:
Depends on the spawn-placement bug fix and on layout_ops. Per the epic's thesis and that bug's design note, STRONGLY prefer keeping SPAWN_TERMINAL geometry-free on the wire and doing placement as a follow-up L3 layout write from the caller -- that keeps this epic at zero wire changes. If you conclude the wire genuinely needs placement fields, that is a spec change (docs/spec/L1.md + docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md + PROTOCOL_VERSION bump + the 5 silent '_' match arms including relay.rs:1407 route_to_satellite) and it needs its own ADR -- do not do it quietly inside this bead.

Files: crates/phux/src/commands/launch.rs and the spawn path. Note launch resolves an integration template from an enabled plugin (examples/plugins/agent-tools/ has claude-code/codex/gemini-cli) and routes the agent through an identity wrapper so the pane self-declares its phux.agent/v1 identity (ADR-0040) -- do not break that; it is what makes 'phux agent list' able to say 'pane 22 is a blocked claude'.
acceptance_criteria: phux launch claude-code --target . --split vertical lands the agent pane exactly where asked. The launched pane still self-declares its agent identity (phux agent list shows it). Same for phux spawn. e2e test.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed. Remaining dependency beads track broader/general follow-up, not this delivered scope.

title: phux-client/src/layout_ops.rs -- shared L3 layout envelope read/mutate/write
description:
THE load-bearing module of this epic. Every spatial verb (focus, split, move, swap, and placement on spawn/launch) is a wrapper over it, and both the CLI and MCP call it -- so it must land before the verb fan-out.

What it does: read phux.tui.layout/v1/<session> via GET_METADATA, decode the v2 envelope ({version, windows:[{name, root: LayoutNode, focused_terminal}], focused_window_index} -- phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs:15-17), apply a mutation to the binary split tree, re-encode, write back via SET_METADATA. The server broadcasts METADATA_CHANGED and attached clients re-render. Zero wire change.

The tree operations mostly EXIST ALREADY and must be reused, not reinvented: phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs has the envelope + set_ratio_at (:621); phux-core/src/window.rs has split/kill_pane/seed_layout/focus_direction (:281-304, a genuinely good directional-navigation walk). NOTE the phux-core copy is near-dead (the server populates Window.layout but never runs it in response to user splits -- the live tree is the client's), so read it for the algorithm and be deliberate about which crate the shared logic should live in. Also note phux-core/src/window.rs:12-23 explicitly warns 'do not reintroduce a parallel implementation' of tiling -- honor that; do not add a fourth LayoutNode.

Envelope v1 ({version, root, focus}) is still decoded for back-compat (layout/mod.rs:51-54) -- preserve that.
design: Design the mutation API around what the verbs need: focus(target), split(target, dir, ratio) -> new leaf slot, move/swap(a, b), close(target). Read-modify-write on shared metadata is a lost-update race if two writers interleave; state the concurrency story explicitly (last-write-wins is probably fine and is what the TUI does today, but SAY so rather than discovering it). Decide up front whether these live in phux-client (alongside snapshot/send_keys/run/wait/watch -- the de-facto shared surface both consumers use) or phux-client-core (where the tree types already are). Do NOT put them on the Agent facade; it is being deleted.
acceptance_criteria: One module, unit-tested against envelope fixtures (v1 and v2), that both a CLI verb and an MCP tool can call. No new LayoutNode type. No wire change.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: ADR-0049: agent-directed navigation and attention
description:
The decision that unblocks everything spatial in this epic. It must settle, in the ADR's own controlled vocabulary:

1. FOCUS STAYS CLIENT-LOCAL. Reaffirm ADR-0019 section 6. The server does not track which pane a human looks at. This ADR must not be read as reopening it.

2. ATTENTION IS A NEW, DISTINCT CONCEPT. An agent raising 'I am blocked, look at pane 7' is a notification with an actionable target, not shared focus. ADR-0019 rejected CONVERGENT focus (all clients yanked to the same pane, tmate-mirror-style); it never considered advisory attention. Name that distinction explicitly so the next reader does not think we snuck focus back in.

3. WHAT CARRIES ATTENTION? Two candidates, pick one and say why:
   (a) A new AgentEvent tag (next free is 0x0b). This is the ONLY extension seam with a real, tested forward-compat story: unknown tags decode to AgentEvent::Unknown and are skipped by old clients (frame.rs:1481). Delivery is already gated by opt-in subscription (SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS), which IS the de facto capability negotiation -- there is no ServerFeature bit mechanism, it is spec'd vapor with zero Rust. The attached TUI already subscribes server-wide (driver.rs:1821). Precedent: ADR-0035/0036 Asked did exactly this.
   (b) Reuse AgentEvent::Asked, which already ships, already carries a question + suggestions, and which the TUI ALREADY renders (server_frame.rs:1203). Cheapest possible path; the question is whether 'blocked on a question' and 'wants attention' are really the same event.

4. DIRECTED FOCUS: opt-in or not at all. If an agent can move a human's viewport, that must be config-gated (e.g. focus-follows-agent = false by default), never the default. NOTE: depending on the spike's answer, an agent may ALREADY be able to do this today by writing phux.tui.layout/v1 metadata -- if so, that is a latent capability that this ADR must either bless with a gate or explicitly close.

5. NO WIRE CHANGE FOR LAYOUT. Record the finding that split/focus/move ride L3 metadata (ADR-0019's own mechanism), so this epic does not touch docs/spec, does not bump PROTOCOL_VERSION, and does not need capability negotiation. That is a load-bearing constraint and it should be written down, because the obvious instinct (add a FOCUS_PANE command) is both a wire change AND a re-litigation of ADR-0019.
design:
Follow the strict template in docs/CONVENTIONS.md: controlled Status vocabulary, ~150-line cap. Cite ADR-0019 (the constraint), ADR-0012 (the split tree), ADR-0035/0036 (the Asked precedent), ADR-0033 (input authority -- the existing precedent for the server arbitrating between a human and an agent contending over one pane, and a good model for how the loser learns the world changed).

RECOMMENDATION going in (the ADR may overturn it, but argue against it explicitly): attention is advisory by default -- agent raises a flag, the TUI shows an indicator, the human presses a key to jump. Directed focus is opt-in config. This is ADR-0019-compatible, it is better UX than having your viewport yanked while you are mid-thought in another pane, and it degrades gracefully when nobody is attached.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0044 merged, passing just docs-check, with a Status line. Answers all five questions above. Every downstream bead in this epic can cite it instead of re-deriving the constraint.
notes: 2026-07-15: ADR number corrected after duplicate ADR-0035 audit. Drag-to-resize is now ADR-0048; client-local focus/advisory attention is ADR-0049. ADR-0049 reuses terminal-scoped AgentEvent::Asked for the evidenced blocked-question attention case, keeps directed focus default-off, and leaves layout operations on L3 metadata with no wire change.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green foundation train PR #243 (combined CI passed).

title: Every spawn hardcodes a horizontal 0.5 split of Window.active -- agent panes land in the wrong place
description:
crates/phux-core/src/registry.rs:139: new_terminal() unconditionally does w.split(t, terminal_id, SplitDir::Horizontal, 0.5) against Window.active. SplitDir::Vertical is unreachable from any spawn; there is no wire path to it. There is no window/geometry/position argument on SPAWN_TERMINAL at all (frame.rs:1958-1998 -- no window id, no direction, no ratio, no anchor).

Worse: Window.active is NEVER updated by client focus. Nothing in phux-server ever writes Session.active / Window.active except structural create/remove in phux-core::Registry plus the upgrade-blob restore. So 'the active pane being split' is effectively THE FIRST PANE EVER CREATED IN THAT WINDOW -- not the pane the human is looking at, which is client-local state the server does not have.

Consequence for this epic: 'phux launch claude-code' drops the new agent pane by splitting some arbitrary first-created pane, horizontally, at 0.5, regardless of where you are or what you asked for. This is THE bug that makes agent orchestration feel wrong today, and it is a prerequisite for placement args on spawn/launch.
design:
Do NOT fix by teaching the server about focus -- ADR-0019 section 6 killed server-tracked focus and this bead must not re-litigate it. The server has no business knowing which pane a human is looking at.

The right shape follows from the epic's key fact: layout is client-owned. So the CALLER (who does know the target) should tell spawn where to put it. Two options for the ADR/design to settle: (a) SPAWN_TERMINAL stays geometry-free and the caller does a follow-up layout metadata write to place the new pane (pure L3, no wire change -- consistent with the epic's zero-wire-change thesis); or (b) add optional placement fields to SPAWN_TERMINAL (wire change, needs spec + CHANGELOG + version bump). Strongly prefer (a). Under (a) this bead's job is to make the DEFAULT placement sane and to stop pretending Window.active means anything.

TRAP: if you do touch the Command enum, note that adding a variant breaks NOTHING at compile time outside phux-protocol -- there are 5 silent '_' fallback arms across phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs and phux-server/src/hub/relay.rs. relay.rs:1407 route_to_satellite is the one people miss, and missing it means the command silently does not route in federation.
acceptance_criteria: A pane spawned with an explicit placement lands where the caller asked. Default placement is documented and deliberate. Regression test. No re-litigation of server-side focus.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: SPIKE: does the TUI adopt a sibling's focused_terminal from a layout METADATA_CHANGED?
description:
Blocks ADR-0044. The layout envelope v2 ALREADY carries focus: {version, windows:[{name, root, focused_terminal}], focused_window_index} (phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs:15-17, LAYOUT_ENVELOPE_VERSION=2 at :49). And the client already subscribes to layout metadata and re-renders on a sibling's write (attach/server_frame.rs:894 MetadataChanged arm, gated by is_layout_key at :1334).

So the question that decides how much client work ADR-0044 needs: when client B decodes a layout blob that client A wrote, does B ADOPT the focused_terminal / focused_window_index, or does B preserve its own local focus and take only the tree?

Evidence it may NOT adopt: layout/mod.rs:311-315 says the active-window index 'is serialized as focused_window_index but a bare window switch does not broadcast it', and focus-changing actions set effects.layout_mutated + effects.set_focus but NOT effects.set_metadata (input_dispatch.rs:1846-1849), whereas resize-pane DOES set set_metadata (:1866-1867). That asymmetry is deliberate and smells like 'focus rides along in the blob but is not honored on read.'

If B DOES adopt: phux focus is a pure metadata write, near-zero client work, and directed focus is basically free (which makes the ADR's opt-in question urgent -- an agent could yank a human's view today by writing layout).
If B does NOT adopt: we need an explicit client-side opt-in path, and the ADR must specify it.
design: Method: run two attached clients on one session (phux attach in two terminals). In client A, change focus (C-a o) then force a layout broadcast (resize a divider, which DOES set_metadata). Observe whether B's focused pane moves. Then read the MetadataChanged arm at server_frame.rs:894 and the layout decode path to confirm from source. Write the answer into this bead's notes -- ADR-0044 depends on it.
acceptance_criteria: A definitive yes/no, cited to source, recorded in bd notes. If yes, also answer: can an agent writing phux.tui.layout/v1 today already move an attached human's viewport? (That is a latent capability -- and arguably a latent security/UX surprise -- either way it must be stated in the ADR.)
notes: 2026-07-15 source evidence: MetadataValue and MetadataChanged both decoded the full Workspace and replaced local state, including focused_window_index and focused_terminal, so a sibling layout write could yank a human viewport. Fixed in crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs: reconciliation now adopts topology while preserving valid local active index and per-window focus, with deterministic repair. Regression tests cover initial loads, sibling broadcasts, tombstones, topology changes, and foreign layouts. Decision recorded in ADR-0049.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green foundation train PR #243 (combined CI passed).

title: Agent workspace: programmatic layout, attention routing, and CLI/MCP parity
description:
phux ships a complete agent CONTROL surface (observe/drive/spawn/signal) and a complete human SPATIAL surface (binary split tree, focus-direction, zoom, drag-resize dividers). The two do not meet. An agent can spawn a pane and read it, but cannot place it, cannot arrange it, and cannot get the human to look at it. A human can arrange panes beautifully but has no way to be told 'the agent in pane 7 is blocked on you.'

This epic closes that seam so phux becomes a workspace an agent can orchestrate and a human can supervise: an agent launches work into a placed pane, raises a flag when it needs you, and you jump to it.

KEY ARCHITECTURAL FACT (drives the whole decomposition): the layout tree is NOT server state. It is a client-owned CBOR blob in L3 metadata under phux.tui.layout/v1/<session> (ADR-0019). Clients mutate locally, push SET_METADATA, server broadcasts METADATA_CHANGED to siblings; the server never parses it. phux rename already works exactly this way. Therefore split/focus/move can be built as L3 metadata edits with ZERO wire-protocol changes: no new frame types, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump, no capability negotiation. That last point matters because ServerFeature/AGENT_HOOKS capability bits are spec'd in docs/spec/proto.md 6.2 but have ZERO lines of Rust behind them (caps.rs ServerCapabilities has exactly one field: layers). There is no per-feature gate to build on.

THE ADR-0019 CONSTRAINT: ADR-0019 section 6 explicitly REJECTED server-tracked focus, names the exact FOCUS_CHANGED frame, and marks it 'Killed.' Convergent focus was rejected as 'a different product (a la tmate view-only mirror).' Do not re-litigate it. The resolution is a distinction ADR-0019 did not consider: FOCUS (which pane this client looks at; client-local; ADR-0019 is right) is different from ATTENTION (an agent raising a flag with an actionable target). Attention is a notification, not shared focus. phux already has the primitive: AgentEvent::Asked ships, the TUI already renders it (server_frame.rs:1203), and phux agent list already infers working/blocked/idle. Build on that. Directed focus, if we ship it at all, is opt-in config -- never the default.
design:
WAVE STRUCTURE (dependency edges are wired; run bd ready to get parallel work):

Wave 0 -- foundations, all parallel, no deps: the spike, three bugs that make agent panes misbehave today, the get_state triplication, the dead Agent facade, and the missing MCP registration doc.
Wave 1 -- ADR-0044 (blocked on the spike; blocks everything spatial).
Wave 2 -- phux-client/src/layout_ops.rs, the shared L3 layout envelope module. Load-bearing; every verb wraps it.
Wave 3 -- CLI verbs fan out in parallel (focus/split/move), each with real logic in NEW files.
Wave 3b -- ONE bead for ALL MCP tools (see conflict note).
Wave 4 -- attention routing (event + TUI indicator + opt-in directed focus).
Wave 5 -- docs, skill, worked example.

SWARM CONFLICT NOTE (read before fanning out): every new CLI verb edits three shared registry files -- crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs (the Command enum), crates/phux/src/main.rs (dispatch arm AND the curated long_about inventory), and crates/phux/src/help_inventory.rs (EXPECTED_INVENTORY, an order-sensitive pinned list). Parallel verb beads WILL conflict on those three lines each; that is a trivial rebase, and the tests command_inventory_matches_snapshot / top_level_help_lists_every_subcommand will catch a miss. By contrast, every new MCP tool edits ONE json! array in crates/phux-mcp/src/tools.rs plus a test asserting the EXACT ORDERED tool-name vec (tools.rs:717-729) -- parallel MCP beads are a guaranteed painful conflict, so all MCP tool work is deliberately ONE bead. Per CONTRIBUTING.md, fan-out uses self-managed worktrees.
acceptance_criteria: An agent (Claude, via MCP or CLI) can, in one session: launch a sub-agent into a pane placed where it asked; watch it; snapshot it; be told when it is blocked; and surface to the human a way to jump straight to that pane. The human can supervise a fleet without hand-navigating. just ci green; docs/spec untouched (no wire change); ADR-0044 landed.
close_reason: All orchestration children are closed; delivered and merged via #223, #231, #243, and #246 with green combined CI and live dogfood.

title: User rename-window must outrank agent/OSC title in tab + sidebar labels
description: Window display label resolves as agent_label.or(osc_title).unwrap_or(stored_name) (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:3608), so an explicit rename-window is invisible whenever the focused pane has a phux.agent/v1 record or any non-empty OSC 0/2 title. Root cause: WindowState.name is overloaded — it is both the auto default ("1","2") and the user's name, so the resolver cannot distinguish deliberate intent from a placeholder. Fix: split user_name: Option<String> from the auto name; user_name outranks agent record and title; agent/title remain the default when unset.
close_reason: Split WindowState.user_name (human's rename) from the auto name; label ranking is now user_name > phux.agent/v1 record > OSC title > auto name. Blank rename clears the name and restores automatic labelling (required making the rename-window prompt commit an empty buffer, which previously cancelled). Verified live in the TUI: tab strip + sidebar spaces + sidebar agents rows all honor the rename over an agent record AND an OSC title; name persists across client restart via the L3 layout blob.

title: Prevent multi-agent attach screen flicker
description: Routine agent metadata, title, lease, and attention updates currently trigger ED2 full-screen repaint transactions. Under several concurrent agents this repeatedly exposes blank or partially rebuilt frames. Make repaint transactions visually coherent and avoid destructive redraws for chrome-only updates where safe; add focused regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent chrome updates do not expose full-screen clear flicker; full-frame redraws are emitted as coherent transactions; cursor visibility remains correct; focused tests and repository CI pass.

title: Resume exit watchers so killed sessions are reaped
description: After a graceful server upgrade, rebuilt pane actors are registered without respawning their terminal-exit watchers. Killing or naturally exiting a resumed pane therefore drops the actor but leaves its pane/window/session in the authoritative registry, so phux kill reports success while phux ls and TUI pickers retain a ghost session. Return rebuilt exit receivers to the runtime, install watchers, and cover kill-after-upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: After phux upgrade, killing the only pane/session reaps it and allows the empty server to self-exit; ordinary non-upgrade lifecycle behavior remains covered.
close_reason: Restored exit watchers for every pane rebuilt after graceful upgrade and added a real upgrade/kill/reap regression test; just ci and targeted upgrade e2e pass.

title: SelectList overlays clip instead of scrolling: selection can leave the viewport
description: The command palette and every picker built on SelectList (window picker, agent fleet) build a Line for every filtered row and hand them all to a Paragraph, which clips at the modal's bottom edge. There is no scroll viewport, no offset, and no position indicator, so navigating past the last visible row moves the selection off-screen with no way to see where you are. Fix: window the rows around the selection, add a scrollbar on the modal border, and support PageUp/PageDown/Home/End and wheel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Resize pane PTYs when toggling sidebar
description: Toggling the TUI sidebar changes the painted content rectangle but does not emit TERMINAL_RESIZE for affected panes, so applications keep the old width and are clipped rather than reflowing. Reuse the zoom/SIGWINCH reflow handshake for sidebar geometry changes and validate live. Also simplify the developer install path to one ~/.cargo/bin executable plus the Homebrew fallback.
close_reason: Sidebar toggles now emit per-pane TERMINAL_RESIZE before repaint. Unit geometry and isolated PTY probe verified width changes from 100 to 80; developer path reduced to ~/.cargo/bin only and live sessions preserved through upgrade.

The cache name + the CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN secret are the only inputs the CI wiring needs. Blocks the wiring task.

comments.author: phall
comments.text:
Implemented on branch dogfood/foz-9-sidebar-parity (worktree). Sidebar now sectioned herdr-style: muted 'spaces'/'agents' headers (new sidebar_section theme slot), status-dot + bold-name window rows with dim branch sub-line, agents section with lifecycle glyph + window name + 'state - agent-name' colored by new agent_idle/working/blocked/done slots, bottom-anchored + new / = menu affordances, collapse chevron in the bottom corner (click = toggle-sidebar; agent rows click-select their window).

title: Honor synchronized-output mode across phux repaint boundaries
description: Why: Codex wraps each complete TUI redraw in DEC private mode 2026 (synchronized output). phux applies each raw TerminalOutput chunk to libghostty and immediately paints unless another frame is already buffered in the same socket wakeup; it never checks Mode::SYNC_OUTPUT. PTY coalescing is bounded/arbitrary and snapshot requests can interleave, so fast scroll and bottom-of-screen redraws expose the application's intermediate clear/scroll/paint states as flicker. Codex rust-v0.144.1 probes OSC 10 and OSC 11 for default fg/bg at startup; style::user_message_style_for returns default style when the probe is absent. phux TerminalActor installs on_pty_write and on_size but constructs libghostty Terminal with no default colors; ClientCapabilities has color depth only. No production path reads Mode::SYNC_OUTPUT, and TerminalActor PTY coalescing boundaries are arbitrary/bounded; snapshot and screen requests can interleave. title: Seed pane inherits daemon CWD, not client cwd — breaks claude --resume
description: A claude (Claude Code) session started inside a phux shell can't be resumed: 'claude --resume' from the project dir finds no history. Root cause: the seed/initial pane never sets a cwd and inherits the daemon's cwd. Claude keys its transcript at HOME/.claude/projects/<cwd-hash>/*.jsonl on the pane's actual cwd (= daemon cwd), so the transcript IS written and flushed, just under the hash of the wrong directory. The session NAME is derived from the client cwd basename, so it looks like it's in the project dir while the pane runs in the daemon dir. HOME/env inherited correctly (not the cause); data not lost, just filed under wrong project hash. Fix: client should send its real cwd (not None) for the initial attach, and resolve_create_if_missing must apply it, mirroring the split path's resolve_inherited_cwd. Likely warrants an ADR. Verified against code: resolve_create_if_missing ignores _cwd (phux-server/src/runtime/attach.rs:159, doc-comment :140-142); client sends cwd:None (phux/src/commands/attach.rs:177); seed_session_with_pty sets no .cwd() (phux-server/src/runtime/commands.rs:63-94); split path DOES honor cwd (attach.rs:496-500). Secondary (lower prio): TerminalSignal::Kill group-SIGKILLs via killpg (terminal_actor/mod.rs:1324-1344), so killing a pane while claude is foreground gives no chance to flush; clean shell-exit reaps gracefully. Reported via phux-mobile bead phux-mobile-3ru. See SEED_CWD_BUG.md.

title: Decide the agent-asked wire mechanism (new AgentEvent vs TERMINAL_EVENT vs RUN_HOOK)
description: The emission mechanism is genuinely unsettled (a real protocol decision, not readable from source). Candidates: (a) a new additive AgentEvent variant Asked{ id, question, suggestions?, ... } on the existing 0xB3 stream -- cheapest, forward-compatible; (b) implement the spec-only TERMINAL_EVENT 0xB1 frame + TerminalEventBody::USER_NOTIFICATION (OSC 9 / OSC 777) at docs/spec/L1.md:183-194; (c) implement the spec-only RUN_HOOK command (L1.md:436, tag 0x06 reserved in frame.rs:403-410) as an agent-hook dispatch point. The downstream Swift consumer already expects agentAsked(terminalID, AgentQuestion{ id, text, suggestions[], waitingSeconds }) (phux-mobile Packages/PhuxKit/Sources/PhuxProtocol/Model.swift:22-45) -- the chosen payload must carry that shape. Resolve whether OSC 9/777 are currently parsed-and-dropped (L1.md:228 "server does not forward every OSC type") or forwardable.
design: Read docs/spec/proto.md:203-213 (versioning), L1.md sec 3.3 and 5.1. Prefer the additive AgentEvent variant unless USER_NOTIFICATION/OSC reuse is clearly superior.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR is written and merged in phux choosing exactly one mechanism with rationale, defining the wire payload (fields + tags) and the minor-version bump, AND this spike FILES the downstream implementation beads (the protocol-type bead and, if 0xB1/RUN_HOOK is chosen, the frame-implementation bead) under this epic with the decided shape.

DECISION MADE + IMPLEMENTED (not yet written as a formal phux ADR): chose the additive AgentEvent::Asked variant on the 0xB3 EVENT stream (tag 0x08) over TERMINAL_EVENT/RUN_HOOK. Shipped in bdb64f6 (feat/agent-asked-wire). Remaining: write the ADR doc to close the spike formally.

title: Client pane mirror frozen at attach size: resize-grow (kill/window-enlarge) leaves freed space blank
description: phux-wurs removed the paint-path mirror resize (to fix alt-screen ghost cells on shrink), leaving safe_resize ONLY in the client's TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT arm. But the server's post-resize resync (broadcast_resync_after_resize, phux-8v1) is delivered via the raw output_tx broadcast -> TERMINAL_OUTPUT, which the client applies with vt_write WITHOUT resizing the mirror. Net: the client libghostty mirror is frozen at its attach-time size and never grows on ANY resize. Shrink looks fine (render clips mirror->rect); GROW cannot fill. Repro: stacked split (C-a "), nvim in bottom, kill top (C-a k, C-a x) -> survivor stays ~19 rows tall at top, rows 20-38 blank. Server grid is correct (snapshot shows 120x39); the client mirror is the problem. Verified via pyte independent-emulator capture of the composited client frame. Fix: deliver the resize-resync as a TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT (carries cols/rows) instead of raw TERMINAL_OUTPUT, by making the actor output broadcast carry an enum {Output(Bytes) | Resync{cols,rows,bytes}}; pumps map Resync -> FrameKind::TerminalSnapshot. Client TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT arm already resizes+resets+repaints. Keeps server-authoritative mirror dims (phux-wurs principle) and fixes the GENERAL resize-grow case, not just kill.
close_reason: Fixed in 870c679: resize resync delivered as TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT via PaneOutput::{Live,Resync} enum so the client mirror resizes to post-reflow dims. Verified via pyte (kill-survivor fills, window-grow fills, alt-screen shrink no ghost) + full nextest green (1400).

title: Graceful server upgrade: sessions survive a binary update (ADR-0032)
description:
Per ADR-0032 (Proposed). Today a binary upgrade requires 'phux kill' -> restart, which closes every PTY master and SIGHUPs the children (shells, editors, the Claude agent session) — the maintainer hit this directly (installing a fix killed the session hosting the work). tmux has the same hole; phux can close it because it ALREADY emits a replayable per-pane snapshot (vt_replay_bytes + scrollback_bytes via SnapshotSynthesizer, ADR-0013).

APPROACH (ADR-0032): graceful in-place upgrade via execve re-exec + fd inheritance + VT snapshot replay. On 'phux upgrade' the running server (1) snapshots every pane + serializes the session/window/pane tree + an fd->pane manifest into an inherited state fd; (2) clears FD_CLOEXEC on the PTY masters + the UnixListener and execve's the new binary as 'phux server --resume <fd>' (fds survive exec -> children stay alive, socket stays bound); (3) the new server adopts the fds and rebuilds each pane's Terminal by vt_write-ing its snapshot ('attach to yourself'). Clients blink-reconnect (v1); passing live client sockets for flicker-free swap is v2.

PHASES: v1 = explicit 'phux upgrade' command (the dev-iteration + agent-session win). v2 = auto-detect a newer on-disk binary after cargo install / brew upgrade (the non-dev 'just works' win) + pass client sockets for seamless. Rejected alts: kill+restart (status quo, loses sessions); separate fd-keeper daemon (cleaner crash-isolation but a permanent 2nd process + IPC seam — recorded as v2 hardening); serialize libghostty engine state (not feasible / drifts — replay the VT snapshot instead).

IMPLEMENTATION SLICES (file beads as children): (a) state-blob format (versioned — old<->new server versions straddle it) + ser/de; (b) fd manifest + CLOEXEC clearing + the --resume server mode that adopts inherited PTY masters + listener; (c) the snapshot-all-panes + quiesce (a pane mid-SPAWN / in-flight input must quiesce before snapshot); (d) the re-exec orchestration with a SAFE FALLBACK (validate the new binary via --version / dry --resume probe BEFORE committing; on failure keep serving on the old image — must never strand children); (e) client reconnect-on-swap; (f) 'phux upgrade' command + tests (incl. a child-survives-upgrade integration test: spawn a sleep/echo, upgrade, assert the same child + scrollback survived). SHARP EDGES: scrollback fidelity bounded by the snapshot (styled-scrollback still plain pending phux-q0x7); OSC8/graphics registries deferred same as attach; the state format is a maintained compatibility boundary across releases.
notes:
SCOPED (session 2026-06-10): ADR-0032 = execve re-exec + fd inheritance + VT-snapshot replay (NOT fd-keeper daemon, NOT engine serialization). HARD CONSTRAINT (not in ADR): portable_pty 0.9 exposes MasterPty::as_raw_fd() (read) but NO constructor to rebuild MasterPty/Child from an inherited fd+PID. => Approach A: on resume, bypass PtyOwned with an adopted-PTY backing wrapping File::from_raw_fd(master) + waitpid(pid); keep portable_pty for SPAWN only. ~1100-1500 LOC across ~9 files. Phases: P0 spike (open PTY, clear FD_CLOEXEC, execve, confirm child alive + bytes flow). P1 versioned state blob (phux-server/src/upgrade/{mod,blob}.rs): per-pane {core/wire ids, child_pid, master_raw_fd, dims, cell_px, term, title, cwd, vt_replay_bytes+scrollback_bytes via SnapshotSynthesizer::synthesize_with_scrollback synthesizer.rs:252} + listener fd + next_wire_id counters (registry.rs:51-54); expose raw fd+PID via a new TerminalHandle request channel (mirror ScreenRequest, terminal_actor/mod.rs:148). P2 perform_upgrade: quiesce panes, collect manifest, clear FD_CLOEXEC on masters+UnixListener (rustix), write blob to memfd/temp fd, std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::exec current_exe as 'server --resume <fd>'; PRE-COMMIT validate new binary; GATE the unconditional socket unlink (runtime/mod.rs:392-397). P3 --resume runtime: UnixListener::from_raw_fd, rebuild registry+wire maps, spawn adopted-PTY actors, vt_write snapshot into fresh Terminal (new_with_seed). P4 wire Command::Upgrade (frame.rs:824, #[non_exhaustive] => additive) + handle_command + phux upgrade CLI. P5 client blink-reconnect (ABSENT today: driver.rs:1148 breaks on Disconnected): outer reconnect loop around main_loop, distinguish detach(exit) vs server-vanished(reconnect); ATTACH already resyncs via TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT (reconnect_scenario.rs:105). RISKS: fd adoption (#1), FD_CLOEXEC miss kills a child, exec-in-place (NOT Command::spawn/fork), quiesce ordering, blob version skew, snapshot fidelity (styled scrollback plain-text). Needs manual upgrade DRILL for acceptance. Update ADR-0032 with the fd-adoption gap + cross-platform blob carrier (macOS has no memfd).
DECISION + SPIKE GREEN (session 2026-06-10): going with re-exec v1 (execve + fd inheritance + snapshot replay), framed as STAGE-1 of substrate/projection separation (NOT the end state). Custodian/fd-keeper stays the planned v2 whose real prize is CRASH-durability (surviving our own panics), which re-exec cannot give. CORRECTION to the earlier SCOPED note: the fd-adoption 'real constraint' is NOT ~1100-1500 LOC and does NOT need to bypass PtyOwned. portable_pty's MasterPty/Child are PUBLIC traits and PtyOwned already stores them as trait objects, so the adopted backing is ~250 LOC of two trait impls over (raw_fd, pid) — no portable_pty fork, no library patch, no new direct dep (Downcast is blanket-impl'd; libc already a dep). The 1100-1500 figure is the WHOLE feature; fd-adoption is its CHEAPEST slice, not the blocker. Built it as a standalone, extractable workspace crate: crates/portable-pty-adopt (AdoptedMaster/AdoptedChild; README has TODO(extract) to split to its own repo + crates.io — it fills a genuine upstream gap). TWO proofs pass (clippy -D warnings + fmt clean): (1) tests/adopt_inprocess.rs — adopt a real PTY from (raw_fd,pid) alone and drive read/write/resize/reap; (2) tests/execve_roundtrip.rs — a PTY master fd (CLOEXEC cleared) + its child survive a REAL execve of the parent, and the post-exec image re-adopts via the crate. Core ADR-0032 bet is de-risked. Remaining work is ordinary feature eng (children a-f): the genuinely hard slices are quiesce-ordering and the never-strand-a-child fallback, NOT fd adoption. title: Client incremental paint leaves stale ghost cells after a coalesced redraw burst (nvim 'fucked up')
description:
REPRODUCED + SEEN (rendered the client's actual output through pyte, an independent non-libghostty emulator, to a PNG and looked at it). Symptom: scrolling/jumping in neovim (e.g. G in a long file) under the user's real config leaves STALE 'ghost' cells on the right half of rows — fragments of the previous screen (e.g. top-of-file doc-comment text) overlapping the new content. This is the user-reported 'neovim weird and fucked up'.

LOCALIZED (evidence chain, all rendered to images):
 1. Server authoritative grid (phux snapshot --cells) = CLEAN.
 2. Client output captured from a real 'phux attach' via PTY, parsed by pyte = GHOST TEXT.
 3. After a forced full redraw (terminal resize -> server resync + render_at_full) = CLEAN again.
 => The server is right, the client's libghostty MIRROR is right (a full repaint from it is clean), pyte is honest. The corruption is in the client's INCREMENTAL paint. NOT broadcast lag (server log had no Lagged warnings during the repro). NOT the SGR-fidelity bugs fixed on main today (those were color; this is erase/stale-cell). NOT a static-attach issue (a fresh attach re-synthesizes a clean snapshot, which is why round-trip tests + static captures never saw it).

MECHANISM (leading): render_at_inner's Dirty::Partial path repaints only rows whose libghostty per-row row.dirty() bit is set (crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs:282-366). Under the phux-jhv8 frame-coalescing (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:936 coalesce_defer_flags + server_frame.rs:464 defer_paint), a burst applies all vt_writes but paints ONCE on the pane's final frame via render_at (Partial). The final partial paint misses rows that actually changed across the burst — while render_at_full (paints every row) is clean. So either libghostty's row.dirty() under-reports after a scroll/big-redraw (content-dirty-per-cell vs paint-dirty-per-absolute-position mismatch: a viewport scroll moves rows whose cells didn't 'change' but whose absolute screen position now needs repainting, and the client repaints in place rather than scrolling the outer terminal), or dirty state is lost across the coalesced batch.

FIX DIRECTIONS (need hands-on debugging): (a) when libghostty reports a scroll / Dirty implies viewport shift, force render_at_full for that pane; (b) track a per-row content signature of what was last PAINTED to the outer terminal and repaint on mismatch (decouples paint-dirty from libghostty content-dirty); (c) on a coalesced burst whose accumulated change is large, fall back to a full repaint. (a)/(c) are cheapest; (b) is most correct.

REPRO HARNESS (reusable to verify a fix): /tmp/phux-diag/cap_big.py drives 'phux attach' in a PTY, opens nvim on a long file, jumps with G; /tmp/phux-diag/render_big.py renders the captured client bytes via pyte to PNG. Server-grid cross-check: /tmp/phux-diag/render_srv.py over 'snapshot --cells --json'. Needs: pip install --break-system-packages pyte pillow.

SEVERITY: high — it's the headline visible defect for the primary use case (human in neovim). Distinct bead from phux-ahk/emdv/the SGR fixes.
notes: FIXED on main (commit 74b1a81), just ci green (1397 tests) + visually confirmed via pyte. ROOT CAUSE (workflow disproved the original scroll/dirty hypothesis — libghostty correctly re-dirties scrolled rows and render_at was faithful): the client resized its libghostty MIRROR to its own layout rect in the paint hot path (safe_resize in paint_focused_pane / paint_full_frame loop / the TerminalOutput arm). On the ALT SCREEN (neovim) libghostty resize() does NOT reflow, so a SIGWINCH repaint at the new smaller viewport_dims BEFORE the server's resized output arrived shrank a server-authored width-N mirror to width M<N, stranding the previous screen's content in columns >=M; render_at then painted the divergent mirror and (clipping only rows, never cols) never repainted M..N -> the right-side ghost that persisted through scrolling until a server resync. The 'forced full redraw heals it' clue was contaminated: a resize also triggers a TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT resync that overwrites the mirror. FIX: drop the per-paint safe_resize (mirror sized only by the server-authoritative TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT resync); add clip:(cols,rows) to render_at clamping BOTH axes to min(mirror,rect). Steady state clip==grid so Dirty::Partial perf is preserved. VERIFIED with an independent emulator (pyte, not libghostty): the attach-resize+G-jump repro that was ghost-ridden is now clean, as are pure-scroll and live-shrink. Tests added: render_at_clips_columns/rows_to_rect, paint_focused_pane_does_not_resize_server_authoritative_mirror (red->green).

title: Split+resize leaves dead space: three divergent layout algorithms
description:
Live repro: with a split, resizing the terminal leaves dead/unfilled space (reported at the bottom).

Verified structural root cause — phux has THREE different pane-rect computations that must agree but don't:
1. phux-client-core/src/layout.rs:729 fill_rects/pane_rects — used by REFLOW (compute_reflow) to decide the size to TELL the server (TERMINAL_RESIZE → TIOCSWINSZ). Subtracts dividers GLOBALLY up front: compute_reflow does content = (cols - total_h_dividers, rows - total_v_dividers), then fill_rects splits with NO per-node gap (left_w + right_w == bounds.w).
2. phux-client-core/src/multi_pane.rs:335 walk_layout/compute_layout — used by PAINT (paint_full_frame, snapshot/output arms) to decide WHERE TO DRAW. Subtracts ONE divider per split node LOCALLY: content_w = bounds.w - 1 at each interior node, recursively.
3. phux-core/src/window.rs:390 pane_rects — the SERVER's own layout (sizes PTYs / builds snapshots).

In the SIGWINCH path (driver.rs:1159-1217): prev_rects come from compute_layout (walk_layout), new_rects from compute_reflow->pane_rects (fill_rects). The diff that drives TERMINAL_RESIZE emission compares rects produced by TWO DIFFERENT algorithms. For a SINGLE split they happen to agree (both use content=dim-1, split_dim(content,ratio)); for NESTED splits the per-node-vs-global divider subtraction and split_dim float rounding diverge at different recursion depths -> the size phux tells the server to make a PTY (fill_rects) != the rect it draws into (walk_layout) -> gaps/overlap. The 'changed' detection can also miss/spurious-fire because it compares incompatible sources.

Secondary contributor (single-split case): resize is async — SIGWINCH emits TERMINAL_RESIZE then immediately paint_full_frame's the NEW geometry, but the reflowed PTY output arrives later, so a pane's libghostty mirror is briefly shorter than its new rect and render_at leaves the extra rows blank (dead space at the bottom) until the reflowed output repaints.

Also note split geometry is RATIO-based (ratio: f32 per split, recomputed via split_dim each resize) rather than tmux's authoritative integer sizes + remainder distribution — float re-derivation is inherently lossy.

FIX DIRECTION (the tmux lesson): collapse to ONE client layout algorithm with an exact-tiling invariant (sum of child sizes + dividers == parent, remainder distributed one cell at a time per tmux layout_spread_cell/layout_fix_offsets), used by BOTH reflow-emit and paint so PTY size == draw rect by construction. Add a property test: for any tree + viewport, rects tile (0,0,W,H_pane) with zero gap and zero overlap. Reconcile the server-side window.rs::pane_rects with it too. Best nailed with a live resize trace once Slice-1 observability lands.

Found during live copilot session 2026-06-05.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #55 (merged, e824f9e): unified client pane tiling — reflow/paint share multi_pane::pane_rects; exact-tiling property test added.

title: Split + re-attach renders blank panes (typable but no content)
description:
Live-session repro: re-attach to a session with a split -> all panes render blank/wiped, but input still routes to the shells (can type).

Root cause (confirmed in code):
1. crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs:279 - the TerminalSnapshot paint block is gated behind `if is_focused`. VT bytes are written to every pane's mirror (:277), but render_at (:298) only runs for the focused pane, so non-focused split panes never paint.
2. The recovery full-repaint (paint_full_frame) only fires on `layout_replaced`, which depends on the server returning a persisted layout under LAYOUT_KEY; the Attached arm seeds a single-pane bootstrap first and requests layout after (driver.rs:761-781). If layout metadata is absent/slow, the split is never reconstructed.
3. Stacked with phux-jhv8 frame-coalescing: the focused pane's snapshot paint is defer_paint-suppressed (:291) expecting a later full repaint that (per #2) never lands -> even the focused pane blanks.

Fix direction (needs care - render hot path): paint every pane's snapshot into its layout rect (the `origin` at server_frame.rs:246-255 is already computed), not just the focused one; and/or trigger an unconditional full repaint once attach snapshots land, independent of the LAYOUT_KEY metadata round-trip. Subtlety: if workspace layout isn't known yet, origin falls back to (0,0) for all panes -> they'd overlap; the fix must ensure layout is known (or defer the full repaint until it is) rather than naively ungating the per-pane render.

Found during live copilot session 2026-06-05; server was at INFO so per-pane snapshot/paint detail wasn't captured - itself motivation for the agent-observability work (self-narration + debug-on-reattach).
close_reason: Done: non-focused-pane snapshot paint present in attach/server_frame.rs (~L348) with regression tests (~L1404,L1445) guarding the focused path; split+reattach renders content.

title: Multi-pane/window re-attach wedges the client (screen freezes, Ctrl-C/detach dead); panes die as collateral
description:
USER REPORT: re-attaching to a session with multiple panes/windows -> screen freezes (no updates), client fully wedged (Ctrl-C and C-a d don't work), and the pane shells die. Single-pane re-attach is fine. Triggers on (re)attach to an EXISTING multi-pane OR multi-window session, both layouts.

NOT YET REPRODUCED headlessly: with a fast pty sink, multi-pane build + hard-detach + re-attach works (B renders + responds, panes survive, reaps delta 0). The 'code 1' pane exit also happens on NORMAL teardown kill in repro, so pane-death is likely COLLATERAL: the user force-kills the wedged terminal -> session EOF/kill -> panes reaped. PRIMARY bug = the WEDGE.

HYPOTHESIS (strong): same class as phux-jhv8 (synchronous render blocking the biased select! loop on a slow host-terminal sink), scaled by N panes. On multi-pane re-attach the server sends ATTACHED + a TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT per pane + layout metadata -> layout_replaced=true -> paint_full_frame() renders ALL panes synchronously inside the frame-processing loop (driver.rs ~891), emitting a large burst. On a real terminal that flush blocks; while blocked the select! loop never polls the stdin arm -> Ctrl-C/detach unprocessed = wedge. If the panes are also producing output, repeated full repaints keep the loop blocked = permanent wedge. A fast pty drains instantly so it never blocks locally.

SECONDARY (real but probably not the wedge cause): compute_reflow (phux-client-core/src/multi_pane.rs ~112-129) can emit degenerate w=0/h=0 rects as TERMINAL_RESIZE on re-attach; server clamps to 1x1 in terminal_actor handle_resize (cols.max(1)) so unlikely to kill the child directly, but emitting 0-dim resizes is wrong and worth fixing.

REPRO PLAN: multi-pane session with panes that continuously output, re-attach client B with a THROTTLED reader (simulate slow terminal, as in the jhv8 repro /tmp/phux_pty_capture.py SLOW_READ), then send B a detach keystroke DURING the re-attach paint and check it never responds = wedge confirmed. Suspect paths: driver.rs select! loop (paint_full_frame synchronous; biased frame arm starves stdin), and whether multi-pane makes the emitted-byte burst big enough to block. FIX direction: don't block the input loop on render (offload stdout writes / make the sink non-blocking) -- the option-2 'non-blocking sink' deferred on jhv8. Confirm with the throttled repro before fixing.
notes:
SECOND BUG (the 'still can't type after re-attach' the user hit while testing #51). DISTINCT from the render wedge: my #51 off-loop-writer fix made the prompts RENDER on re-attach, but input to the re-attached panes was still dropped. User clue: a NEW window accepted typing, existing re-attached panes did not.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via server WARN log 'client not subscribed to pane; dropping input wire_terminal_id=Local{id:3} INPUT_KEY'): ServerState::attach (state.rs ~975) subscribed the attaching client to ONLY the session's active pane. The input gate handle_terminal_input (runtime.rs ~3434) DROPS any keystroke to a pane the client isn't subscribed to. So on (re-)attach to a multi-pane session the client could only ever type into the one active pane (and after a focus move, none). Fresh panes worked because handle_spawn_terminal (runtime.rs ~1930) auto-subscribes the spawning client.

FIX (on the fix/fysb-nonblocking-stdout-sink branch, state.rs attach): subscribe the client to EVERY pane in the session (iterate session.windows -> window.panes), mirroring attach_snapshot_panes (which already snapshots all of them) and the spawn auto-subscribe. Also lets each pane's actor fan out live output to the client, so non-focused panes stay live too. VALIDATED: server 'dropping input' WARN count 0 after fix (was 5+ per keystroke); typed `echo MARKER` into the re-attached focused split pane @3 -> output appears in @3's snapshot (before: dropped).
RESOLVED. Both documented bugs were already fixed on main; this session verified and locked in the fix.

PRIMARY (re-attach wedge): fixed by #51 (8fdb4dd) off-loop writer + non-blocking stdout sink (crates/phux-client/src/attach/stdout_writer.rs). The synchronous paint-on-the-select!-loop that the hypothesis blamed no longer blocks the input arm.

SECOND (can't type into re-attached non-active panes): ServerState::attach now subscribes the attaching client to EVERY pane across the session's windows (crates/phux-server/src/state/registry.rs:412-442). This landed on main not via a dedicated phux-fysb PR but folded into the state.rs module split (f305f94) — which is why the bead was never closed. The companion commit c3643a7 on the local fix/fysb-nonblocking-stdout-sink branch (committed 07:53, after #51 merged 03:46) was the stranded original.

SECONDARY (degenerate 0-dim TERMINAL_RESIZE on reflow): now a deliberate design after phux-islu (#55) — compute_reflow tiles exactly and surfaces ReflowDiff::too_small as a WARNING; the server clamps cols/rows to 1x1. Not a bug; closed off by design, no action.

GAP CLOSED this session: the SECOND fix had only a ServerState unit test (the subscriber map) and was nearly lost in the module-split refactor. Added a wire-level regression (#59, 270f75e -> main 4fb0af1): crates/phux-server/tests/reattach_multipane_input.rs builds a two-pane cat session, drops the builder, re-attaches a fresh client, and INPUT_KEYs into the NON-active pane; a side observer reads the pane mirror via GET_SCREEN to prove the keystroke reached the PTY. Proven to bite: reverting attach to active-pane-only fails the non-active assertion. just ci + Linux PR CI + main CI all green.
close_reason: Closed

title: PTY-heavy e2e tests starve each other -> WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT flakes (attach_detach_churn quarantined)
description: Fresh-session task. attach_detach_churn_keeps_pane_alive (and latently reconnect_after_detach, already retry-pinned) fail under e2e-lane parallelism: a fresh attach's snapshot render misses WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT when PTY-backed tests compete for CPU; harness recv_framed (common/mod.rs:258 .expect) then panics with core::result::unwrap_failed. Failed 3/3 even with retries=2, so retries are insufficient. ROOT CAUSE is concurrency, not correctness (passes in isolation / at low -j). FIX: add a nextest test-group with max-threads (e.g. 1-2) covering the PTY-heavy timing-sensitive tests (stress_attach_churn::attach_detach_churn, reconnect_after_detach, likely the perf_* gates) so they don't oversubscribe, instead of retry-roulette. Then REMOVE the quarantine: drop the '-E not test(=attach_detach_churn_keeps_pane_alive)' filter in justfile e2e recipe (added under this bead id). Validate by running just e2e 5-10x green. Context: discovered while consolidating CI from 6 jobs to 2 (separate PR).
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTION (verified by flaky-e2e investigation 2026-06-06): the bead's stated root cause (CPU oversubscription; 'passes in isolation/low -j; concurrency not correctness') is FALSIFIED. attach_detach_churn_keeps_pane_alive fails DETERMINISTICALLY 3/3 in pure isolation on a fast 10+ core Mac, always ~15.0-15.8s at common/mod.rs:258 (.expect on recv timeout in ClientHandle::attach), AND also at near-creation commit 8fdb4dd. So it's a real liveness/deadlock bug in the transient-attach path on the shared current-thread runtime (server fails to deliver ATTACHED/TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT to a fresh transient client while an anchor + idle PTY sleep are live), NOT scheduling starvation. A nextest max-threads test-group CANNOT fix a test that deadlocks in isolation; dropping the quarantine as-written would turn the e2e lane RED. CORRECT SCOPE: (1) fix the actual hang first (instrument builder.rs:322 ATTACHED vs :348 SNAPSHOT recv), (2) THEN optionally add the test-group as hardening for the LATENT sibling reconnect_after_detach (which runs in the parallel default pool, masked today by the .config/nextest.toml retries=2 override), (3) drop ONLY the attach_detach_churn term from justfile:70 -E filter — LEAVE multi_mb_no_newline_burst quarantined (that's phux-fheq, not this bead).
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-06-06, supersedes both the bead's 'oversubscription' premise AND the flaky-e2e investigation's 'liveness deadlock' framing — it is NEITHER). Reproduced deterministically on current main (26437d0). Instrumented handle_attach + writer_task + stack-sampled the hung process:

- The server side is FAST and CORRECT: for the wedging transient client, handle_attach completes promptly (Attached SENT + SnapshotRequest sent + got snapshot reply ok=true at t=7s) and writer_task writes both frames (0x81 ATTACHED, 0x91 SNAPSHOT) to the socket. The runtime is HEALTHY — stack sample shows it parked in tokio::runtime::io::driver::Driver::turn (kqueue), not busy-looping, not blocked on a syscall. No deadlock.

- The panic is at builder.rs:491 (ClientHandle::wait_until), called from stress_attach_churn.rs:73 — NOT in ClientHandle::attach. The transient ATTACHES FINE; it then hangs in wait_until(|s| s.contains('CHURNMARKER')) for 15s and recv_framed's internal WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT .expect (common/mod.rs:258) fires.

- WHY: the transient's TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT does NOT reconstruct CHURNMARKER. Instrumented snap.bytes: 80x24, ~2149 bytes, has_marker=FALSE for BOTH the anchor and the transient. The anchor passes anyway because it saw CHURNMARKER as a LIVE broadcast delta (it attached before the marker was printed). The transient attaches AFTER the marker and must reconstruct it from the snapshot — but synthesize() yields a blank grid. The seed is 'printf CHURNMARKER; sleep 30' => a single line with NO trailing newline; synthesize()/libghostty grid export does not capture that current-row, no-newline content.

REAL FIX (server-side, in TerminalActor::synthesize / libghostty grid->VT export): ensure the snapshot reconstructs the live grid including the current cursor row written without a trailing newline. This is a fresh bounded sub-investigation in the synthesize path (terminal_actor/mod.rs synthesize + the libghostty export bridge). It is a genuine user-facing bug: any client re-attaching to a pane whose last output had no trailing newline (e.g. a shell prompt with no newline, a partial line) would see it missing from the reconstructed screen until the next live output.

NOT the fix: nextest max-threads test-group (the bead's suggestion) — would only mask it by changing scheduling; the snapshot is wrong regardless of parallelism. Do NOT de-quarantine until synthesize is fixed.

Also note: this same snapshot-content bug is why a flooding-seed contract test added for phux-7w1j (#63) flaked on CI and was removed.
FIXED + merged (#64, commit on main 214f60c). Root cause was the snapshot synthesizer reusing a RenderState whose libghostty per-row dirty-bit cache went stale across consumers (register_consumer's per-consumer reference consumed the Terminal dirty bits before the full snapshot ran), so synthesize() emitted stale/blank rows for a re-attach. Fix: synthesize() builds a fresh RenderState per call (full observation, immune to cross-consumer dirty consumption). attach_detach_churn de-quarantined; passes ~0.5s (was 15s hang); validated on the 2-core CI runner (e2e lane green in #64). NOT oversubscription, NOT a deadlock — both prior diagnoses were wrong; runtime parks healthily.
close_reason: Closed

title: e2e stress_resize_extremes::both_axes_shrink_storm_under_output hangs (pre-existing, blocks CI e2e lane)
description: PRE-EXISTING (not phux-jhv8/PR#48). both_axes_shrink_storm_under_output_does_not_panic in crates/phux-server/tests/stress_resize_extremes.rs hangs indefinitely: CI gave it >6000s then cancelled; reproduces locally on BOTH main and any branch (timeout rc=124 at 150s). main CI has been cancelled/failing on the e2e lane for many commits as a result. The sibling stress_output_extremes passes 10/10 and all non-stress attach e2e (attach_lifecycle, byc_6_1_attach_snapshot, attach_viewport_resize, concurrent_attach_no_lag, route_input_no_resize, concurrent_attach_l2 = 41 tests) pass, so the hang is specific to the resize-storm-under-output path. Test does a monotonic both-axes shrink to 1x1 + boundary churn while /bin/sh emits 'row-N' at 200/s, then resize(100,30) and wait_until(contains 'row-'); the wait never resolves => actor wedged or client never re-renders after the 1x1 clamp churn. Likely a server-side resize/reflow wedge at the 1x1 boundary, OR the harness client. Needs: bisect on main to find the introducing commit, then fix the wedge. Unblocks the CI e2e gate.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (not a deadlock, not a server bug, NOT related to phux-jhv8). The test harness ClientHandle::screenshot() (builder.rs) drains TERMINAL_OUTPUT 'until 20ms of quiet' (timeout(20ms, recv_typed) loop). The both_axes test's seed emits every 5ms forever (printf;sleep 0.005), so screenshot() at the end (cap.attach_screen(client.screenshot()...)) NEVER sees a 20ms gap and loops forever => the >6000s CI hang. Flaky because occasionally scheduler jitter yields a >20ms gap and it breaks. Confirmed by stack sample: runtime thread stuck 148 samples in ClientHandle::screenshot builder.rs:430; pty-reader blocked in PtyFd::read (seed throttled by the unread output, but that was a side effect). My earlier client-read/backpressure hypotheses were WRONG (draining the client did not help; the hang is purely the screenshot drain loop).

FIX: added ClientHandle::snapshot_text() (non-draining oracle read) + drain_output_bounded(max_frames) (count-bounded drain, safe vs infinite seeds). Replaced the final screenshot() in both both_axes_shrink_storm and resize_degenerate (same file, 20ms stty-size seed = same borderline hang) with drain_output_bounded(32)+snapshot_text(). Storm loops left untouched (they never deadlocked; resize_raw is send-only and always reached the final screenshot). Validation: both_axes 25/25 pass slowest 1s (was 100min hang).

FOLLOW-UP (separate, lower priority): the same screenshot()-on-a-fast-continuous-seed anti-pattern exists in other test files (stress_resize_storm.rs stty-size, stress_lifecycle_churn.rs tick loop). They are NOT currently failing CI (timing/seed cadence differs) but are latent. Consider either fixing each call site or making screenshot() itself count-bounded (it has 20 call sites incl perf_latency.rs, so a global change needs care).
RESOLVED — fix already on main, just never closed (fysb pattern). Landed as a1c6b18 'fix(test): stop stress_resize_extremes hanging CI forever (phux-s2iw) (#49)'. Live on main: builder.rs:445 snapshot_text() + builder.rs:459 drain_output_bounded(max_frames); stress_resize_extremes.rs both_axes_shrink_storm + resize_degenerate now use drain_output_bounded(32)+snapshot_text() instead of the infinite screenshot() 20ms-quiet drain. Verified: nextest --run-ignored ignored-only both_axes_shrink_storm PASS 0.351s (was >6000s hang). FOLLOW-UP latent siblings remain (screenshot()-on-fast-seed in stress_resize_storm.rs, stress_lifecycle_churn.rs) — not currently failing; track separately if they flake.

title: client freezes ~0.5s when opening neovim (alt-screen / full-paint burst)
description:
Client-side ~0.5s freeze when opening neovim in a phux attach. Diagnosis (code-read, not yet measured):

RANKED SUSPECTS:
1. Per-frame FULL repaint not coalesced. Each TERMINAL_OUTPUT/TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT triggers render_at_inner (render.rs:229-332) which walks every row/cell -> CUP+SGR+glyph then out.flush() (render.rs:330). nvim startup = burst of frames = N full repaints + N flushes. TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT forces Dirty::Full.
2. Synchronous scrollback replay: server_frame.rs:265-268 vt_write(scrollback_bytes)+vt_write(vt_replay_bytes) inline before render; up to 10k lines (driver.rs:432) = 100KB+ parsed on the hot path.
3. paint_full_frame (paint.rs:90-193) on SIGWINCH/alt-screen: ED2 clear + render_at_full (forced, ignores dirty bits) for every pane; not debounced (driver.rs:989-1047). Prime one-time-stall suspect on alt-screen enter.
4. predict reconcile (only if predictive-echo enabled): reconcile.rs:124-129 read_grapheme_string_at is O(row*col) per pending prediction.

Existing client tracing spans to confirm WHICH: handle_server_frame, vt_apply (bytes=N), paint_trigger (rows=N), paint_full_frame. 

CAPTURE (on a machine where it reproduces): RUST_LOG=phux=debug PHUX_LOG_FORMAT=json PHUX_LOG=/tmp/phux-client.jsonl phux attach <session>, open nvim, then: jq 'select(.fields."time.busy")|{span:.span.name,busy:.fields."time.busy"}' /tmp/phux-client.jsonl | sort — the span with ~500ms busy is the culprit. Fix follows the measurement (coalesce renders / debounce paint_full_frame / lazy scrollback). DO NOT fix blind.
notes: PR #48 opened: https://github.com/phall1/phux/pull/48 (branch fix/jhv8-output-coalesce). 2 commits: the coalescing fix + a pre-existing runtime.rs doc-link fix. just ci green locally.
close_reason: Fix landed on main via PR #48 (commit 624c305): per-pane frame coalescing in attach driver, FrameReader buffered try_recv, defer_paint seam. Measured -38% bytes / -66% paint+flush under the nvim startup burst. Tests included in the PR. e2e is green on main.

title: Separate FRAME_ACK semantics for raw broadcast vs synthesized tick output

Today this is mostly wasted bookkeeping, but if output modes become negotiable or switch mid-session, raw-pump ACKs can poison state-sync RTT/last_acked accounting. Fix by gating FRAME_ACK handling on output mode, or adding an emitter/source id so ACKs only update the matching emitter.

title: In-process session re-attach (switch-session effect)
description:
Wire the phux-4li.20 `switch-session` effect to an actual in-process re-attach so `<leader> a` can be bound.

CURRENT STATE (phux-4li.20):
- The client caches the server session graph from the ATTACHED SessionSnapshot (crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs: FrameOutcome.sessions, set in the Attached arm; cached in driver.rs main_loop as `sessions`/`focused_session`).
- `session-picker` action (crates/phux-client/src/attach/input_dispatch.rs run_action) opens a SelectList of peer sessions; selecting commits `switch-session { name }` through run_action — the single dispatch path.
- `switch-session` sets ActionEffects.switch_session = Some(name); apply_action_effects (input_dispatch.rs ~line 384) currently only logs + bells. `<leader> a` is LEFT UNBOUND in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml.

WHY RE-ATTACH WAS SCOPED OUT:
main_loop (crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:360+, run_with_stdout_predict at ~242) is single-session by construction. It constructs ~15 session-scoped locals up front: panes: HashMap<TerminalId,PaneSlot>, workspace, focused_pane, predict (PredictionState), pending_splits, pending_windows, layout_get_request_id, status_bar, overlays, session_name, sessions cache, etc. The ATTACH handshake (send_attach + wait_for_attached, driver.rs:301-339) runs once before main_loop. There is no entry point to re-run the handshake against a new AttachTarget without tearing down and rebuilding all of that state.

PLUMBING REQUIRED:
1. Detach from the current session: send FrameKind::Detach, await DETACHED (the detach path already exists via ActionEffects.detach in apply_action_effects, input_dispatch.rs ~365).
2. Re-run the ATTACH handshake against AttachTarget::ByName(name) (resolve_* in phux-server runtime.rs ~1249-1320 already supports ByName/ById). send_attach + wait_for_attached are reusable but currently private to run_with_stdout_predict.
3. Reset session-scoped state for the new SessionSnapshot: clear panes, rebuild workspace from the new bootstrap (handle_server_frame Attached arm already does Workspace::single + seeds focused_pane + session_name + sessions), drop the prediction queue, re-issue GET_METADATA/SUBSCRIBE_METADATA for the new collection's layout key, repaint.
4. Decide the control-flow shape: either (a) main_loop returns a 'switch to target X' signal up to run_with_stdout_predict which loops the handshake+main_loop, or (b) an in-loop re-attach helper that rebuilds the locals in place. Option (a) is cleaner — main_loop returns an enum { Detached, SwitchTo(AttachTarget) }; the outer fn loops while keeping the RawModeGuard installed (no flicker between sessions).
5. Once it works end-to-end, bind `a` = "session-picker" in crates/phux-config/src/default.toml prefix-table (the comment there documents this) and add an integration test that a client switches sessions and sees the new session's terminal.

TESTS: integration test under crates/phux-client (or the server integration harness) that two sessions exist, client attaches to one, commits switch-session, and observes the other session's snapshot/output.
close_reason: In-process re-attach: main_loop returns LoopExit{Detached,SwitchTo(name)}; outer loop reuses RawModeGuard+Connection, detach_and_drain frees server per-consumer state, re-ATTACH ByName rebuilds all session-scoped locals + flicker-free clear. Wire test phux_eb0_in_process_reattach proves same-connection re-attach. Landed 4c3dc26.

title: audit: snapshot/diff epilogue drops alt-screen modes 1049 and 1047 (only re-emits 47)
description:
CONFIRMED. grid.rs emit_epilogue() (crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs:937-942) re-emits only DEC mode 47 (ALT_SCREEN_LEGACY) when reproducing terminal state in TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT and in the per-tick reference diff. Real full-screen programs use mode 1049 (ALT_SCREEN_SAVE: vim, less, man, htop, tmux) or occasionally 1047 (ALT_SCREEN). libghostty tracks 47/1047/1049 as three independent mode bits (libghostty terminal.rs lines ~840-858; verified: after '?1049h', Mode::ALT_SCREEN_LEGACY reads false).

IMPACT: When a client attaches to (or a resize-resync fires for) a pane running vim/less, the synthesized snapshot paints the alt-screen CONTENT but the receiving mirror Terminal stays on the PRIMARY screen. Worse, because the live 47 bit is off, the epilogue actively emits '?47l', forcing the primary screen. The per-tick diff epilogue (synthesize_against_reference -> emit_epilogue) has the same defect, so the divergence persists for the whole attach. ReferenceCursorMode::capture (grid.rs:716-732) and LastAckedCursorMode::capture (terminal_actor.rs:107-124) likewise only track alt_screen_legacy, so a 47<->1049 transition mid-session may also be missed by the diff trigger.

REPRO: see pinning test crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs::audit_snapshot_drops_alt_screen_1049_mode (passes today, documenting the gap; flip its assertions when fixed).

FIX SKETCH: emit_mode for Mode::ALT_SCREEN (1047) and Mode::ALT_SCREEN_SAVE (1049) in emit_epilogue, and add both bits to ReferenceCursorMode + LastAckedCursorMode. Note ordering: 1049 also saves cursor/clears, so it should be emitted before the cursor-position re-establishment, not after. Parent: phux-ahk.
close_reason: Alt-screen modes 47/1047/1049 now emitted independently in the paint PROLOGUE (before row walk + cursor re-establishment, so 1049 clear-on-entry can't wipe content); per-consumer diff toggles only on actual transition. ReferenceCursorMode + LastAckedCursorMode track all 3 bits. Landed 38fe7a2.
