title: main CI red: spawn_terminal_inherits_focused_pane_live_cwd fails on Linux (exec of a shell builtin)
description:
main has been RED on the last 5+ consecutive CI runs (incl. commits unrelated to this test: 'blinking block cursor', beads syncs, docs/web #37). All fail on the SAME assertion: crates/phux-server/tests/spawn_terminal.rs:572 'expected ATTACHED' — the first frame after ATTACH is not TYPE_ATTACHED.

Evidence:
- Passes 5/5 locally on macOS /bin/sh.
- Fails deterministically on Linux CI (GitHub Actions, nix devshell) across multiple unrelated commits → NOT load flakiness; Linux-specific.

Leading hypothesis: the seed command is sh -c "cd '<dir>' && exec read _" (line 563). On Linux /bin/sh is dash, whose 'exec' rejects the 'read' builtin ('exec: read: not found'), so the seed shell dies, the pre-seeded 'focused' pane fails to spawn, and ATTACH ByName('focused') returns an ERROR frame instead of ATTACHED — tripping the line-572 assert. macOS /bin/sh tolerates it, hence green locally.

Suggested fix (to verify): drop 'exec' so the builtin runs in-shell: "cd '<dir>' && read _" (and ensure the pane stays alive without a tty stdin race). Confirm against dash before closing.

Impact: blocks merge on every PR (incl. phux-e0d / PR #38, whose own tests are green). This is the gating item for restoring a green main.
notes:
CORRECTION: the 'exec of read builtin' hypothesis is DISPROVEN. dash -c 'cd /tmp && exec read _' exits 0 — dash execs the builtin fine. Root cause is NOT shell portability of exec.

Verified facts only:
- Deterministic on Linux CI (GitHub Actions, nix devshell) across 5+ unrelated main commits.
- Green 5/5 on macOS /bin/sh locally.
- Failure is: first frame after ATTACH ByName('focused') != TYPE_ATTACHED (spawn_terminal.rs:572).
- Could not reproduce from macOS (platform=darwin); needs a Linux repro to identify what frame is actually received (likely an ERROR from a failed seed-pane spawn, but unconfirmed).

Root cause: UNKNOWN pending Linux repro. Do NOT apply a blind fix. Next step: reproduce on Linux (or add a one-shot CI debug commit logging the actual first frame type/payload) before changing the seed command or the spawn path.
close_reason: Fixed by commit 5a261db (#39): dropped 'exec' so the 'read' builtin blocks the seed/spawn shell on the PTY, keeping the focused pane alive past ATTACH. Main CI green for 2+ consecutive runs.

title: Extract phux-client-core (the no-refactor seam)
description: Extract the platform-agnostic client logic from phux-client into a new crate phux-client-core: per-pane libghostty Terminal mirror (driver.rs PaneSlot), binary-split layout tree (layout.rs/multi_pane.rs), input->wire encoding, output routing, focus. close_reason: DESCOPED. The web client (phux-web) is intentionally a lean, independent wire consumer (single terminal, canvas render) — its rendering and concerns differ entirely from the native multi-pane ratatui TUI, so a shared phux-client-core would de-duplicate little while coupling two very different consumers. The webasm stack works end-to-end without it. A future native+web shared core can be revisited if real duplication emerges; not required for the wasm client.

title: ghostty-vt.wasm rendering core + web-sys Rust driver
description: REFRAMED (no longer make-or-break): ghostty ships ghostty-vt as a STANDALONE wasm module (build.zig initWasm: addExecutable, rdynamic, no-entry, 'for embedders e.g. JS in a browser') — NOT a linkable archive. And libghostty-vt is FFI-deep (key.rs -> ffi::ghostty_key_encoder_*; lib.rs re-exports libghostty_vt_sys). DECISION: do NOT link zig into the Rust wasm binary. Build ghostty-vt.wasm from local ghostty (zig initWasm path), and write a Rust binding that loads+drives it via web-sys WebAssembly (Terminal::new/write/cells/dirty/resize). The Rust client stays pure Rust; ghostty-vt is a separate module. Eliminates the rust+zig shared-memory problem entirely.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build -p libghostty-vt --target wasm32-unknown-unknown succeeds; a smoke test feeds VT bytes to a Terminal and reads back grid state in wasm.

Canvas render verified in headless Chrome (1704dd4).

title: Splitting a pane blanks the original (source) pane's content
description: Repro (tmux-free, via crates/phux/examples/pty_screen.rs): attach, type 'echo MARKER' so the pane has content, then split (C-a | OR C-a -). The NEW pane shows a fresh shell prompt correctly, but the ORIGINAL pane you split from goes completely BLANK — its prior content (MARKER + prompt) disappears. Happens for both vertical (| , cols shrink) and horizontal (-, rows shrink) splits, so it is not cols-shrink-specific. PRE-EXISTING: reproduced on commit 706fc41 (before phux-tnh), so the phux-tnh pane-close reflow fix did not introduce it. Same family as phux-8v1 (libghostty reflow content-loss on the resized mirror + a state-sync gap), BUT notably phux-tnh's TerminalSpawned resync (which now emits TERMINAL_RESIZE for the shrunk original leaf on split) does NOT restore the content — so there is an additional mechanism beyond the resize resync: either the original pane's server Terminal loses content on its split reflow (so the resync snapshot is itself blank), or the split's SPAWN racing the original-pane resize leaves the resync capturing an empty grid. ONLY visible without tmux — tmux retains/reflows the byte stream and masks it. Verification rig: crates/phux/examples/pty_screen.rs (raw PTY + libghostty oracle, NO tmux). Investigate the local split action path (input_dispatch/actions split-pane), the original pane's client mirror reflow in paint_full_frame, and whether/what the server resyncs for the original leaf on split.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed tmux-free via pty_screen + focus-back experiment): the original pane's content is NOT lost permanently. Chain: (1) on split, paint_full_frame's safe_resize reflows the original pane's CLIENT mirror, which is lossy on shrink (same libghostty reflow issue as phux-8v1) so render_at_full paints it blank; (2) the server resync (phux-8v1/phux-tnh, ~50ms later) restores the mirror content via TERMINAL_OUTPUT vt_write, BUT non-focused panes are never repainted (server_frame.rs TerminalOutput/TerminalSnapshot handlers render only the FOCUSED pane), so the restored content is invisible; (3) focusing the pane (C-a h) triggers paint_full_frame which renders it via paint_focused_pane -> content reappears. PROOF: 'echo LEFTMARK999; C-a |; C-a h' shows LEFTMARK999 in the left pane. BIGGER BUG EXPOSED: non-focused panes are visually FROZEN — output to an unfocused pane updates its mirror but never repaints to screen until focus/full-repaint. FIX: repaint non-focused panes (cheap dirty-tracked render_at at their rect) when they receive TERMINAL_OUTPUT/SNAPSHOT, restoring the focused pane's cursor afterward. This fixes both the split-blank and the frozen-non-focused-pane class.
close_reason: Fixed in edb3c17. Root cause: non-focused panes were never repainted on TERMINAL_OUTPUT/SNAPSHOT (only the focused pane rendered), so the post-split resync that restores the original pane's mirror content was invisible until focus-switch. Fix: TERMINAL_OUTPUT handler now repaints non-focused panes at their rect (dirty-tracked render_at) + restores focused cursor. Also fixes the general frozen-non-focused-pane bug. Verified tmux-free via pty_screen for both | and - splits.

title: Client/server crash on terminal resize: libghostty PageList.resizeCols integer overflow when cols AND rows both shrink in one resize() call
description:
REPRO (verified via isolated tmux + resize-window): start phux attach at 100x30, resize terminal smaller in BOTH dimensions (e.g. 60x20) -> phux client panics with 'panic: integer overflow' inside libghostty Zig: PageList.resizeCols <- PageList.resize <- Terminal.resize <- ghostty_terminal_resize, called from phux_client::attach::paint::paint_full_frame (driver.rs:734 SIGWINCH branch). Process dies.

MATRIX (single pane, from 100x30):
- shrink cols only (->60x30): OK
- shrink rows only (->100x20): OK
- grow (->larger): OK
- shrink cols AND rows together (->60x20): CRASH
Splits crash the same way; not split-specific.

ROOT CAUSE: libghostty's PageList.resizeCols overflows when both dimensions decrease in a single resize() call (Zig integer-overflow safety check; debug build). phux depends on libghostty-vt as a pinned git rev, so the upstream Zig fix is out of this repo.

SERVER EXPOSURE: the same both-shrink hits the server too — on SIGWINCH the client sends TerminalResize(cols,rows) and terminal_actor.rs:1022 calls terminal.resize(cols,rows,...). A both-shrink there crashes the server.

FIX (phux-side workaround): a safe_resize(terminal, cols, rows) that, when both axes shrink vs the Terminal's current cols()/rows(), decomposes into two single-axis resize() calls (shrink rows first, then cols) — each individually safe. Apply at all libghostty resize call sites: client paint.rs (x2), client server_frame.rs:161, server terminal_actor.rs:1022. Long-term: fix/upstream PageList.resizeCols and drop the workaround.
close_reason: Fixed in 4afee05 via safe_resize decomposition (client paint.rs + server terminal_actor.rs): a both-axis shrink is split into two single-axis resize() calls, each safe. Verified single-pane + split both-shrink no longer crashes and redraws cleanly. Root cause is upstream ghostty PageList.resizeCols (self.rows - c.y - 1 underflow); fixing there separately. Workaround stays since phux pins a libghostty-vt git rev.

title: Auto-spawned server not daemonized: shares client controlling terminal, dies when terminal closes -> sessions vanish
notes: FIXED + verified. maybe_auto_spawn_server (crates/phux/src/main.rs) spawned the server as a plain child sharing the client's process group + controlling terminal (code even admitted 'good enough for demo'). Closing that terminal SIGHUP'd the server -> sessions vanished. FIX: auto-spawn now passes a hidden --daemonize flag; run_server calls rustix::process::setsid() before binding so the server lands in its own session with no controlling terminal (verified ps: PGID==PID, SESS=0). stderr redirected to phux-server.log beside the socket for debuggability. Added rustix 'process' feature to phux/Cargo.toml (same crate already used by phux-client; no new workspace dep). Verified: destroyed the originating terminal while attached -> server SURVIVED, session reattachable from a fresh terminal with content intact. Note: the zombie-client fix [[phux-bln]] also independently helped, but daemonization is the robust decoupling.

title: Detach never exits client: tokio::io::stdin reader thread hangs runtime teardown -> zombie steals first post-detach line (reattach 'does nothing')
notes: FIXED + verified. Root cause: detach returned Ok(()) and relied on unwinding, but tokio::io::stdin() (driver.rs) parks an UNCANCELLABLE blocking read on a helper thread; the RawModeGuard Drop restored termios fine, but the subsequent tokio runtime drop blocked forever waiting for that stuck read(). Result: a zombie client (confirmed alive 3s+ after detach) that kept a reader on the shared PTY and stole the FIRST line the user typed next -- typically the reattach command, so reattach appeared to do nothing. FIX: exit_after_detach() in driver.rs restores the terminal (mirrors terminal_reset_on_signal) and process::exit(0) at all three outcome.exit / detach-disconnect sites, bypassing the hung teardown. Verified via tmux harness: client gone <1s after detach, first post-detach command executes, reattach from the SAME shell works.

title: Split/resize leaves the surviving pane blank: paint_full_frame clears screen but render_at honors incremental dirty tracking
notes: paint_full_frame emits ED2 (\x1b[2J) then re-renders each pane via render_at. render_at early-returns on Dirty::Clean and only paints per-row-dirty rows. The pane that SURVIVES a split/resize has unchanged grid content, so libghostty reports it Clean -> render_at paints nothing -> the just-cleared screen leaves it BLANK. (Symptom looked like 'old pane shows stale content' but that stale content was actually the NEW pane's own fresh-shell zsh-init output; the original pane was simply empty.) FIX: added TerminalRenderer::render_at_full (forces Dirty::Full) and a force_full param on paint_focused_pane; paint_full_frame now forces a full redraw of every pane while the hot incremental TERMINAL_OUTPUT path stays dirty-tracked. Verified via tmux harness: SHORT-01..05 survive a '|' split into the left 40-col pane.
close_reason: Fixed: render_at_full + force_full on paint_focused_pane (committed b98a2c1, render.rs:174/paint.rs). paint_full_frame forces full redraw of every pane; hot incremental path stays dirty-tracked. Verified via tmux harness.

title: Split direction inverted: '|' produced stacked panes (horizontal divider) instead of side-by-side
notes: split_dir_arg in crates/phux-client/src/attach/input_dispatch.rs mapped the config 'direction' string straight to the same-named SplitDir variant. But the config string names the DIVIDER orientation (tmux model, documented in default.toml: '|' = vertical divider = side-by-side panes) while SplitDir names the SPLIT AXIS (Horizontal = splits width = side-by-side; Vertical = splits height = stacked, per layout::fill_rects). So 'vertical' was mapping to SplitDir::Vertical (stacked) when it should be SplitDir::Horizontal (side-by-side). FIX: crossed the mapping (horizontal->Vertical, vertical->Horizontal) + updated the unit test. Verified via scripts/tui-probe.sh: '|' now yields a vertical divider with side-by-side panes.
close_reason: Fixed: split_dir_arg mapping crossed in input_dispatch.rs:582-583 ('horizontal' divider->SplitDir::Vertical, 'vertical' divider->SplitDir::Horizontal) + unit test updated. '|' now yields side-by-side panes.

title: Live phux session: leader key inert, can't split, status bar shows only time, cursor stranded bottom-right
description:
Reported live by phall1 on main @ 2460eeb (2026-05-27 evening).

## Symptoms

- Cursor parks at bottom-right of host terminal for the entire session.
- Status bar shows only the time widget on the right; left (session-name) is blank.
- Prefix key (C-a) does nothing.
- Cannot split (C-a |, C-a -, all inert).

## Hypothesis (composite or single root?)

Two plausible root causes — possibly the same one, possibly two:

1. **Config path issue**: if phux_config::loader::load() degraded silently, both the resolver and status bar are disabled. Counter-evidence: time widget renders, so SOME status config is built — would expect a totally blank bar if config failed. Maybe only the session-name widget is failing (empty session_name string), in which case the resolver should still work.

2. **focused_pane is None when paint_full_frame runs**: see crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs:100-117. paint_bar_after_pane is called with fallback_origin=None, and the focused-pane render is skipped when focused is None. The cursor stays at the status bar's tail (bottom-right). This explains the cursor symptom, but not the leader-key symptom unless the resolver path is also gated on focused_pane being Some.

3. **Input not reaching resolver**: c0_or_ascii_to_key(0x01) does emit KeyEvent { mods: CTRL, key: A }, and the resolver build was verified to produce Feed::Partial → Feed::Resolved("split-pane") for "C-a |". So the resolver itself is fine. Either the parser path is not feeding bytes, or consume_chord is not being called.

## Repro capture needed

User to run:
  RUST_LOG=trace,phux_client=trace ./target/debug/phux attach 2>/tmp/phux.log
  # press C-a once
  # press |
  # press C-a d to detach
Then attach /tmp/phux.log to this issue.

## Refs

- Last code commit: 034f37e (fix clippy in input dispatch)
- Default config: crates/phux-config/src/default.toml (prefix=C-a, prefix-table |/-/h/j/k/l/x/n/p/d, [status] left=[session-name], right=[time])
- Resolver verified via smoke test: produces Partial then Resolved("split-pane") for C-a |.
- Paint cursor restoration: phux-9xn, phux-dca, phux-b9n landed restore-on-bar-repaint.

LABELS: area:client, area:input, area:tui, crate:phux-client, regression
notes: REOPENED 2026-05-28: prior 'fix' (CUP-restore band-aids in paint.rs) never worked live. Real root cause: every paint path computes the correct cursor-restore CUP but NEVER FLUSHES it. stdout is a LineWriter; the restore CUP has no trailing newline, and dropping the StdoutLock guard does not flush the global buffer. render_at() flushes mid-frame BEFORE the restore CUP is written; the bar paint + restore CUP that follow sit in the buffer until the next pane output. At an idle prompt no output arrives, so the host cursor strands at the bar's tail = bottom-right. The phux-gxy unit tests passed because they assert on the in-memory Vec buffer, which never exercises the flush. FIX: flush stdout after the final cursor write in paint_bar_after_pane() and paint_full_frame(). Verified empirically via new scripts/tui-probe.sh harness: cursor now lands at the shell prompt (2,22) instead of (80,23).
close_reason: Resolved by commits since the 2460eeb report. Verified end-to-end via scripts/tui-probe.sh (80x24): C-a | splits into side-by-side panes (leader live, k2a direction correct), both panes paint (d69 force-full redraw), cursor lands in the new right pane's prompt at 43,22 (NOT stranded bottom-right 79,23), status bar time widget renders. Residual: status-bar LEFT (session-name) still blank — that is phux-17u (session-name not wired through ATTACHED), tracked separately.

title: BUG: vim renders only half the screen — pane area smaller than host viewport
description:
User-reported: opening vim under phux shows the buffer occupying roughly half the host terminal's vertical space.

## Possible root causes (need investigation)
1. **Server PTY sized smaller than host viewport.** ATTACH carries `viewport: ViewportInfo` (driver.rs:300) but the server may apply only a default 80x24 to the spawned PTY on first attach, ignoring the ATTACH viewport. Confirm by reading the server-side ATTACH handler in crates/phux-server/ and the spawn-on-attach path.

2. **Pane area computed at half-viewport on the CLIENT.** If `multi_pane::compute_layout` returns a Rect with h=viewport.rows/2 for the single-pane case, the client-side libghostty mirror would be resized smaller than the server's PTY, so visible cells are only the top half. Check default LayoutState single-pane case + compute_layout in multi_pane.rs.

3. **Stale split.** User may have accidentally triggered a vertical/horizontal split via the new `|` or `-` chord (phux-9fu) and there's a hidden invisible second pane taking half. Check by attaching and inspecting layout state; if there are 2 leaves with one of dim 0 or one blank, the split-on-action path has a bug.

4. **Status bar reserves the wrong number of rows.** pane_viewport reserves 1 row (paint.rs:151-157). If it reserves N rows incorrectly, vim sees a shrunken viewport. Unlikely (subtraction is just 1) but worth checking when status bar wraps.

## Reproduction
`phux attach` then `vim` — observe buffer height vs host terminal height.

## Acceptance
- vim opens at the full available height (host_rows - 1 for status bar).
- The server's PTY for the focused pane matches the client's pane Rect dimensions.
- No invisible second pane in default single-pane attach.

References:
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:298-313 (send_attach)
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/multi_pane.rs (compute_layout)
- crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs (ATTACH handler)
- ADR-0013 (wire is VT bytes — server PTY size IS the canonical size)
close_reason: Landed on main as 248b5da (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-2lj-vim-half). Root cause: server's handle_attach in runtime.rs had _viewport prefixed with underscore — the ATTACH viewport was literally dropped on the floor. Panes spawned at hardcoded 80x24 and stayed there until first SIGWINCH. Fix: un-underscore + new apply_attach_viewport helper that mirrors handle_viewport_resize's per-actor resize fan-out. New regression test attach_viewport_resize.rs uses 'stty size' loop in PTY to verify post-ATTACH winsize; stash-verified to catch the bug (88 consecutive '24 80' readings without the fix).

title: BUG: cursor pinned at bottom-right of screen after fresh attach (paint sequence strands cursor when last_cursor is None)
description:
User-reported regression observed after phux-5ke + phux-b9n landed.

## Symptom
Cursor sits at the bottom-right corner of the host terminal after `phux attach`. Does not move with the focused pane's cursor.

## Hypothesised root cause (paint.rs:140-144)
`paint_bar_after_pane` only restores the cursor when `restore_cursor: Option<(u16,u16)>` is `Some`. `restore_cursor` traces back to `slot.renderer.last_cursor()` which returns `None` whenever libghostty's `Snapshot::cursor_viewport()` returns None — which happens on fresh attach (no PTY output yet), during alt-screen transitions, and any frame where the cursor sits outside the viewport.

In those None cases, the previous `StatusBarPainter::paint` writes to the bottom-row cells and naturally leaves the terminal cursor at the end of the bar (bottom-right). The phux-b9n fix made the cursor visible but did not give it a fallback landing position.

## Fix sketch
When `restore_cursor` is None, fall back to positioning at the focused pane's origin + (0,0) (or last known position). Two reasonable options:
1. Cache the last non-None cursor per slot; reuse when current is None.
2. Position cursor at focused pane's (rect.x, rect.y) — guaranteed to be inside the pane and away from the bar.

Option 2 is simpler and matches user expectation (cursor inside the visible pane).

## Acceptance
- `phux attach` shows the cursor inside the focused pane immediately, not at bottom-right.
- vim, less, htop, nvim cursor positioning still correct (they emit their own CUP).
- Regression test: extend an existing paint test or add a new one asserting cursor position is inside pane rect after `paint_full_frame` with a freshly-created pane (no PTY output).

References:
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs:116-145 (paint_bar_after_pane)
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs:73-74 (last_cursor doc)
- commit 138c772 (phux-b9n cursor-invisible fix)
close_reason: Landed on main as 78b316c (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-9xn-dca-cursor-bar). paint_bar_after_pane now plumbs the focused pane's Rect origin as a fallback; when last_cursor is None it emits CSI {y+1};{x+1}H + ESC[?25l so the cursor lands inside the pane area (hidden) rather than stranded at bottom-right after the bar paint. 3 new regression tests in attach/paint.rs::tests. 264 phux-client tests + integrated workspace 786/786 green.

title: Cursor invisible on fresh attach (status bar ?25l strands cursor)
description:
Surfaced immediately after phux-5ke landed on main (2026-05-27).
User reports cursor not visible on `phux attach`.

## Root cause

`render::chrome::status_bar::write_buffer` emitted `\x1b[?25l` (hide
cursor) at the start of every bar paint with the comment "Cursor stays
hidden — caller restores at the focused pane." The caller
(`attach::paint::paint_bar_after_pane`) only restored visibility when
`restore_cursor.is_some()`.

`restore_cursor` traces to `slot.renderer.last_cursor()`, which is
None whenever `libghostty_vt::Snapshot::cursor_viewport()` returns None
(per libghostty docs: "if it is currently visible within the viewport").
On a fresh attach with no PTY output yet, libghostty has no viewport
cursor and returns None — so the bar's `?25l` strands the cursor
invisible until the first pane render with a visible cursor.

Pre-existed wave-2 (the OLD hand-painted status_bar.rs also emitted
`?25l`), but went unnoticed because the older paint paths happened to
re-emit `?25h` more often. Wave-2's collapsed paint sequence
(`paint_full_frame` calls bar LAST with no following pane render) makes
the bug consistently visible on fresh attach.

## Fix landed

`crates/phux-client/src/render/chrome/status_bar.rs::write_buffer` no
longer emits `\x1b[?25l`. The flicker concern from the original comment
is sub-millisecond on modern terminals; the bug it created was visible
on every fresh attach.

`crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs::paint_full_frame` reordered:
focused pane now paints LAST (after dividers and status bar) so its

title: client: attach failure wedges terminal (alt-screen + cursor hidden); graceful failure UX
description:
Repro: \`phux attach <session>\` when no server is running, or when the session doesn't exist, or when the client gets signal-killed mid-attach. Terminal is left in alt-screen mode + cursor hidden + sometimes raw mode. User has to type \`reset\` blind.

Root causes:
1. \`attach::run\` installs RawModeGuard (alt-screen + raw mode + hide cursor) BEFORE the UDS connect + handshake. Any pre-handshake failure flickers the terminal through alt-screen for nothing.
2. RawModeGuard::Drop only runs on Rust unwinding. SIGTERM/SIGKILL/SIGHUP bypass it. The cleanup escapes (\\x1b[?1049l + \\x1b[?25h) never get written.
3. No signal handler installed to restore terminal state on signal exit.
4. Auto-spawn server always uses DEFAULT_SESSION_NAME ('default') but client asks for whatever was on the CLI. Mismatch causes attach to fail at handshake while client is already in alt-screen.
5. Connection errors surface as 'attach failed: connection refused' — actionable would be 'no phux server at <path>; start one with \`phux server\`' with the exact suggested command.
6. Stale socket files survive a crashed server (separate ticket — file follow-up).

Acceptance for THIS ticket:
- attach::run defers RawModeGuard installation until AFTER handshake + ATTACH succeeds (or skip alt-screen entirely on early failure).
- SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers installed that run terminal cleanup before exit.
- ConnectionRefused/NotFound socket errors produce a one-line clean error WITHOUT entering alt-screen.
- Auto-spawn passes the user's requested session name through to the spawned server.
- Test under the new \`Screen\` harness: a synthetic 'no server' scenario captures stdout and asserts NO alt-screen-enter byte sequence appears.

Out-of-scope: stale-socket cleanup (file follow-up bd if not already covered).

title: byc.8: server-side Terminal placement — spawn_local + LocalSet OR actor pattern
description:
Coming concern for byc.8 (server ATTACH handler). libghostty Terminal is !Send + !Sync (holds NonNull<TerminalImpl>, no unsafe impl Send/Sync in libghostty source).

runtime.rs:258 currently uses tokio::spawn (Send-required) for per-client handler tasks. Today the handler holds no Terminal — only logs unhandled frames. byc.8 will add real ATTACH handling that needs to own a Terminal per pane.

Three viable shapes — byc.8 must pick one:

1. spawn_local + LocalSet — keeps current_thread runtime per ADR-0003; Terminal stays on the runtime thread; preferred.
2. Dedicated pane-supervisor task that owns the Terminal; channels (mpsc) for input/output. The 'actor model' that was flagged earlier in the session as a possible refactor for ServerState shape. Cleaner separation but more plumbing.
3. RefCell<Terminal> behind Rc on a single-threaded executor. Discouraged — fights tokio's spawn conventions.

Do NOT try Arc<Mutex<Terminal>> — won't compile (Mutex requires Send for cross-thread sharing; Terminal isn't Send).

Decision needed at start of byc.8 work. ADR-worthy if the actor pattern is picked.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-0014 (per-terminal TerminalActor on LocalSet) + TerminalActor impl (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor.rs, 987 LOC, uses spawn_local + LocalSet per design 3 in original ticket). The ticket was filed when the actor pattern was still being chosen; ADR-0014 picked option 1 (spawn_local + LocalSet, one borrower, no RefCell) and shipped as TerminalActor in phux-byc.5. Unblocks phux-q0e.2.

title: Per-client capability downsampling: define ColorSupport + downsample fn + per-client storage
description:
SPEC §6.2 conformance: `crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs:121-122` unconditionally
emits `Color::Rgb` with a comment that says "the wire carries the final pixel
value" — directly violating SPEC §6.2: "a client advertising Indexed256 MUST
never receive truecolor RGB cells; the server must downsample."

## Design seam: per-pane capture vs per-client fanout

Three options were considered:

1. First-attach floor — capture in the lowest tier any current client
   advertises. Rejected: locks downsampling into the canonical state; a
   later-attaching TrueColor client cannot recover precision.
2. Per-tier cache — capture once in TrueColor, materialize one cached
   diff per active tier. Rejected as premature; complicates invalidation
   and is unnecessary until profiling shows it.
3. On-demand downsample at fanout — capture once in canonical TrueColor;
   each per-client fanout call downsamples to that client's advertised
   tier. Selected. Matches the existing "server owns canonical state,
   clients see derived views" model and keeps the diff-compute path tier-
   agnostic.

## Scope of THIS ticket (substrate only)

- `ColorSupport` enum (TrueColor | Indexed256 | Indexed16) in phux-protocol.
- `downsample(Color, ColorSupport) -> Color` (as helper fn, since `Color` is a
  re-export of libghostty-vt's StyleColor — no inherent impl possible).
- Per-client cap storage on `AttachedClient` in phux-server::state.
  Defaulted to `ColorSupport::TrueColor` (most-permissive; clients without
  advertised caps don't get downgraded).
- New `phux-server::downsample` module with `downsample_op` /
  `downsample_cell` for byc.5's fanout to plug into.
- Comprehensive unit + property tests.
- `diff_spike` MUST remain byte-identical — downsample is per-fanout, not
  per-capture; nothing in the capture path changes.

## Out of scope (follow-up tickets)

- HELLO ColorSupport wiring (SPEC §6.1 conformance — separate task).
- CIELAB perceptual color distance for downsample (better Indexed16 picks).
- Fanout layer itself (byc.5).
close_reason: Substrate landed in cc30ab5. ColorSupport enum + downsample_color + per-client color_support on AttachedClient + phux-server::downsample helper module + comprehensive tests (unit + proptest). diff_spike byte-identical. Follow-ups: phux-7lf (HELLO wiring), phux-i02 (CIELAB), phux-982 (Cow signature).

title: Server pane plumbing: PTY + per-pane diff loop
description:
Wire a real pane: spawn child PTY, feed bytes into libghostty_vt::Terminal, run grid::capture each frame, compute DiffOps, gate by FRAME_ACK/snapshot fallback per SPEC §6. Pools RenderState/RowIterator/CellIterator per pane (the spike allocates each call). Single-pane, no IPC yet — that's phux-byc.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `cargo run -p phux-server --example one_pane bash` spawns a real shell, accepts typed input from stdin, prints DiffOp summaries to stderr per frame.
- [ ] Steady-state capture loop allocates zero bytes (validated by criterion bench or dhat-rs heap trace).

title: Protocol foundation: input types + wire codec
description:
Translate SPEC §9 (input) and Appendix A (TLV framing) into Rust types and a length-prefixed codec. Closes the loop between phux_protocol and libghostty_vt by establishing the From<&Event> for libghostty_vt::*::Event boundary, with round-trip snapshot tests. ## Success Criteria

- [ ] Insta hex-dump snapshots committed for ≥8 representative diff frames (small change visible in PR diff).
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.

title: Document that fire-and-forget paste is per-event atomic only
description:
Closing phux-6b6t as option A leaves one real gap: nothing tells a consumer that splitting a single logical payload across multiple INPUT_PASTE / ROUTE_INPUT events is unsafe. L1 SPEC section 9 says a full mailbox drops the event and still acks Ok, and both drop sites now warn!/error! after PR #318, but the contract itself is only discoverable by reading the server source or hitting the corruption.

Document, in docs/spec/input.md and/or docs/consumers/: one INPUT_PASTE event is atomic (one contiguous buffer, one write_all), there is NO delivery or ordering guarantee ACROSS fire-and-forget events, and any payload too large for a single event must use APPLY_INPUT (ADR-0053, acknowledged and reconnect-safe) or PutFile (ADR-0059). Losing a keystroke is honest and recoverable; losing an interior fragment of a payload is undetectable and can hand a shell a truncated command, which is why this needs to be stated rather than inferred.

Clarification only -- no wire bytes change, so no CHANGELOG entry or version bump expected.

title: Copy-mode pane dims go stale on a peer's layout broadcast (no SIGWINCH)
description:
Found during self-review of PR #331 (phux-d26y, merged 2b4eadcb). Same root cause, same consequence, a trigger that PR did not cover.

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE
PR #331 refreshes copy-mode's cached pane_cols/pane_rows on the SIGWINCH edge. That is not the only way the focused pane's size changes.

A peer client's layout broadcast arrives as SET_METADATA on the session layout key and is handled in crates/phux-client/src/attach/server_frame.rs (the is_layout_key branch, ~1044-1067). It decodes the peer Workspace, reconciles it, REPLACES the local workspace wholesale, and returns FrameOutcome { layout_replaced: true, .. }. The driver consumes that flag at crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:2734 (fleet_dirty) and :2897 (the layout_replaced block) and repaints. No SIGWINCH is involved, so the on_viewport_resize fan-out PR #331 added to the SIGWINCH arm never runs.

If the replacement changes the focused pane's rect — a peer dragging a divider, splitting, or closing a sibling pane while you are mid-selection — copy-mode keeps clamping against the pane size it captured when it opened. That is exactly the pre-#331 state, with the same consequences:
- stale-large: the cursor sits outside the grid; the copy path resolves that corner via terminal.grid_ref(..).ok()? in crates/phux-client/src/attach/copy.rs, extract_selection_text returns None, and Enter dismisses copy-mode having SILENTLY copied nothing (no bell, no log, no clipboard write).
- stale-small: newly revealed rows/columns are unreachable and a Line-mode copy clips at the old right edge.

REPRODUCTION
1. Attach client A to a session with two panes split vertically.
2. In A, enter copy-mode on the focused pane and extend a selection to its bottom-right corner.
3. From client B (or the "phux resize" verb), shrink A's focused pane — drag the divider or resize the pane directly. A receives the layout broadcast; no SIGWINCH reaches A.
4. In A, press Enter to copy.
EXPECTED: the selection lands on the clipboard.
ACTUAL: nothing is copied, silently.

DEPENDENCY CONTEXT
- Builds directly on PR #331 (phux-d26y) and PR #319 (phux-fsb). The mechanism is already there: RenderOverlay::on_viewport_resize(pane_cols, pane_rows) with a no-op default, and OverlayState::on_viewport_resize fanning it across the stack. This bead is about CALLING it from a second site, not designing anything new.
- Call site: the layout_replaced branch in driver.rs:2897, after the workspace has been swapped and focus resolved, computing the pane rect the same way the SIGWINCH arm does — focused_pane_rect_for(&workspace, zoomed, focused_pane, viewport_dims, bar, sidebar), whose visibility was already widened to pub(super) in #331.
- Consider whether the same call belongs on any other path that can resize the focused pane without SIGWINCH: TerminalSpawned/TerminalClosed reflow (outcome.reflow_panes), toggle-zoom, and toggle-sidebar. Sidebar/zoom are unreachable while copy-mode is up (it captures all input and commits only copy/dismiss/scroll), but spawn/close driven by a PEER is not. Auditing those together is the point of this bead — a third one-off call site would be a smell; a single choke point where the focused pane rect is recomputed would be better.
- ADR-0045 owns the selection contract the fix must keep the renderer and the copy path agreeing on. ADR-0030: copy is a client-local projection, so no wire change.

VERIFICATION BAR
Failing-first, matching #319 and #331: a unit test driving the layout_replaced path (or the driver helper it calls) that shows the clamp stale before the fix. The live 2x2 harness from #331 is a good model but needs a second client to drive the broadcast — see that PR description for the pty-based approach that proved the SIGWINCH case.

title: Copy-mode clamps to stale pane dimensions after a terminal resize
description:
Sibling of phux-fsb (fixed in PR #319, merge 66ba8ae8), found while tracing that one. Same root shape — an overlay holding construction-time geometry across a resize — but a different overlay, a different consequence, and a different correct fix.

MECHANISM
CopyModeOverlay stores pane_cols/pane_rows at construction (crates/phux-client/src/render/overlay/copy_mode.rs:76-80, set in new() at :88) and never refreshes them. They are the clamp for every cursor movement (:174-175), the mouse-position quantizer (:132-133), Line mode's right edge (:165), and the page-scroll span (:210, :288). The SIGWINCH arm updates viewport_dims and resizes each PTY, and the server's resync snapshot re-sizes the client mirror — but nothing updates the overlay's copy of the pane size.

Unlike the context menu, copy-mode correctly takes the survives_resize() default of true: it is not a pinned box but a selection over the live pane, and dismissing it on resize would silently discard an in-progress selection. So the fix is REFRESH, not DISMISS.

REPRODUCTION A — shrink, silent no-op copy
1. Attach with a single pane in an 80x24 terminal.
2. Enter copy-mode (leader C-a [, or drag-select with the left button).
3. WITHOUT leaving copy-mode, shrink the terminal window to ~60x18.
4. Move the cursor down/right past the new bounds — the overlay still permits it (max_row/max_col are the old 23/79).
5. Press Enter to copy.
EXPECTED: the selected text lands on the clipboard.
ACTUAL: nothing is copied. The CopyRequest carries an out-of-range point; extract_selection_text's terminal.grid_ref(...).ok()? fails (crates/phux-client/src/attach/copy.rs:64-67), the function returns None, and copy_to_host_clipboard emits no OSC 52. The overlay dismisses as if it worked. Silent failure, no log, no bell.

REPRODUCTION B — grow, silently truncated selection
1. Same, but start at 60x20 and GROW the terminal to 100x30 while copy-mode is up.
2. Try to move the cursor into the newly revealed right/bottom region — it stops at the old 59/19.
3. Switch to Line mode (Tab) and copy a line that now runs past column 59.
EXPECTED: the whole line.
ACTUAL: clipped at column 59 — Line mode sets end_col = pane_cols-1 from the stale value (:165).

Both are non-destructive (a wrong or absent copy, never a destructive action), which is why this was split out of PR #319 rather than ridden along.

DEPENDENCY CONTEXT
- The hook point already exists. PR #319 added RenderOverlay::survives_resize() and OverlayState::dismiss_stale_on_resize(), swept from the SIGWINCH arm at crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:3469 (origin/main). A refresh hook belongs immediately beside it.
- Suggested shape: a trait method such as on_viewport_resize(&mut self, pane: Rect) defaulting to a no-op, implemented by CopyModeOverlay to re-derive pane_cols/pane_rows and re-clamp cursor + anchor into the new bounds. The driver already computes the focused pane rect via focused_pane_rect_for / content_rect, so the SIGWINCH arm can supply it.
- Decide explicitly what happens to a selection whose anchor falls outside the shrunken pane: clamp the anchor (keeps a smaller selection alive) or drop to a cursor-only state. Clamping is probably right; either way it must be a decision, not an accident.
- ADR-0045 owns the shared selection contract (SelectionRect / CopyRequest) that the fix must keep the renderer and the copy path agreeing on. ADR-0030: copy is a client-local projection, so no wire change is involved.
- Construction sites to keep consistent: crates/phux-client/src/attach/input_dispatch.rs:873 (drag-to-copy) and :2142 (the copy-mode action).

VERIFICATION BAR
A unit test per direction, each confirmed to fail before the fix (the discipline PR #319 used): shrink then commit still yields a resolvable CopyRequest, and grow then Line-mode copy reaches the new right edge. Plus a live pass — resize a real terminal with copy-mode up, both directions.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #331, merged as 2b4eadcb and verified present on origin/main (merge-base --is-ancestor, plus on_viewport_resize confirmed in main's copy_mode.rs tree).

FIX
RenderOverlay::on_viewport_resize(pane_cols, pane_rows) with a no-op default, plus an OverlayState fan-out, called from the SIGWINCH arm after phux-fsb's stale sweep so an overlay about to be dropped is never handed geometry it will not use. Copy-mode adopts the new dims and clamps BOTH corners.

Copy-mode keeps survives_resize() == true and is refreshed rather than dropped, unlike the context menu: it is a selection over the live pane, not a box pinned to the screen, and discarding an in-progress selection because the window changed size is worse than carrying a smaller one. The anchor is clamped rather than collapsed — this bead flagged that as a decision to make explicitly, and a partially preserved selection is still visible and still correct about the cells it names.

EVIDENCE — unit, failing-first
The trait hook landed as a no-op default FIRST, so the tests compiled and failed on assertions rather than on a missing method. Pre-fix failures: cursor (23,79) vs expected (17,59) after a shrink to 60x18; (19,59) vs (29,99) after a grow to 100x30. Seven tests total: shrink reclamp (both corners + the committed request naming only real cells), grow reach, Line-mode re-span, page-scroll span, an in-bounds-selection guard that passes on both sides, plus two stack-level tests proving the fan-out reaches copy-mode through Box<dyn RenderOverlay> and that sweep-then-refresh ordering holds.

EVIDENCE — local CI
just ci green, exit 0, 3133 tests passed.

EVIDENCE — live
Real client in a real PTY against a private server on its own socket (the live fleet was never touched), driving TIOCSWINSZ + SIGWINCH and asserting an actual OSC 52 clipboard write carrying a known marker:
  pre-fix  control (no resize) PASS | resize FAIL (no OSC 52 at all — the silent no-op)
  patched  control (no resize) PASS | resize PASS (marker on the clipboard)
The control is what made this trustworthy: the first harness selected blank cells, which phux deliberately declines to put on the clipboard (copy_to_host_clipboard_blank_span_writes_nothing), so it failed on BOTH binaries. Running the control located the fault in the harness rather than the fix.

EVIDENCE — required CI on the PR
check pass (2m35s), test pass (11m17s), commitlint pass, detect docs-only pass.

DOCS
docs/consumers/tui.md section 5 gains the copy-mode resize rule, contrasted against the context menu's opposite behavior (phux-fsb).

FOLLOW-UP FILED
phux-z6wt — the same stale-dims consequence via a peer's layout broadcast (SET_METADATA, layout_replaced), which reaches no SIGWINCH and so is not covered by this fix. Proven root cause and call site recorded there.

title: Large newline-free paste wedges canonical-mode PTY ingest permanently
description: Empirically reproduced on darwin: writing 4097 newline-free bytes to a pty master retains exactly 1024 (MAX_CANON) and silently discards 3073, with write() returning full success and zero BEL. Worse, the wedge is permanent: with 1800 newline-free bytes followed by a CR, the slave received 0 bytes in 6/6 trials -- once the canonical queue is at 1024 the terminating CR is itself discarded, so the line never completes. phux never sets termios on pane PTYs (openpty with NULL termios, spawn.rs:305-312) and never chunks or paces writes (spawn.rs:401-402, one unchunked write_all). This is the mechanism behind ADR-0059's 'canonical-mode PTY ingest was minutes-per-photo slow' and the reported 1.9 MiB JPEG stuck after 24s. It is a HANG, not corruption -- it does not explain the byte-level divergence in phux-6b6t. Split out of phux-6b6t.

title: Zero-drift reference docs: generate from the binary, truth-pass what stays curated
description:
Docs assert things the code disproves, in the documents new users read first:

- CONFIG.md:62-66 "There is no live-reload verb today" — phux config reload ships (commands/config.rs:340), reload-config is a bindable action. CONFIG.md:211 calls cwd/exit/exec widgets "design intent, not yet implemented" — all three are registered (widget/mod.rs:305-307). CONFIG.md never mentions phux config check and its schema overview (155-163) omits [sidebar]/[[remote]]/[[connector]]/status.position.
- docs/architecture/process-model.md:24-30 says the state dir is "design intent, not yet implemented" and "logs go to stderr by default" — both false (telemetry.rs:225-249; client NEVER writes stderr per telemetry.rs:16-20). tui.md:558-563 is correct.
- README.md:409-411 claims phux owns "literal search over scrollback" — no search action exists (ACTION_NAMES, input_dispatch.rs:1726-1762). Stated as shipped, is intent.
- README.md:337 "prefix-aware help hints" — help-hints is a static string (help_hints.rs:12-27); the prefix-aware surface is which-key, a different feature.
- tui.md:1914-1921 documents seven widget kinds that are not registered (window, pane, host, mode, key-indicator, text, spacer).
- vision.md:90-92 lists a tab strip as remaining work (it ships, default-on) while failure-state UI / log discovery / status verb — the actual gaps — go unnamed.
- README.md:91 pins "latest release v0.0.3" at v0.6.0.

Fix: one truth pass; where the doc promises something worth keeping (search, style tables), convert the claim to a tracked issue instead of prose. Consider a docs-check lint for registered-widget/action name references.
design:
---

**DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream F, 2026-08-01).** Rescoped from a one-shot truth pass to: (1) generate a docs/reference/ tree from the compiled binary's live inventories, (2) delete hand-maintained reference prose with a direct generated replacement, (3) truth-pass only what remains curated. Mechanism: the generator is a hidden clap subcommand `phux gen-reference-docs` (not a cargo xtask — would add a crate and a second compile of the dep graph; not a build script — build scripts must not write into the source tree), extending two in-tree precedents: phux completion renders from the live clap tree (completion.rs:39-45) and help_inventory.rs test-pins the command surface. Freshness: a unit test re-renders every page and byte-compares against docs/reference/ on disk, failing with the remedy `just docs-gen` — rides `just test` in `just ci` with zero new CI wiring. Any stream that changes the clap tree, config schema, actions, widgets, or hooks regenerates in its own PR; stream G's wrapup is a final regeneration + verify. Generated pages emit compliant frontmatter (fixed generator-owned date) + TL;DR + a GENERATED FILE marker so check-docs.sh needs no carve-out. No new deps: config reference derives from the embedded annotated default.toml (lib.rs:68) + a section-index const test-pinned against schema.rs — no schemars. Deletion list: tui.md §5.4 action table, §8.3 widget table incl. the seven never-registered kinds, §4.1 path block, CONFIG.md schema overview and widget/hook status prose. Curated + truth-passed only: README, process-model.md (state-dir rewrite owned by stream C's C1), vision.md, QUICKSTART, CONCEPTS, CONFIG.md layering material. Reconciler ordering: generation runs AFTER stream D finalizes the clap tree and help text (F1 depends on D6); action/widget/hook inventories consume stream A's phux-config vocab (F3 after A2/A9, F4 after A4). Decomposed into F1-F6; umbrella.

title: In-TUI discoverability: onboarding teaches detach, help-hints survive truncation, populate Hardcoded section
description:
The in-TUI teaching surfaces are the product's strongest asset (which-key, palette, help overlay, first-run toast) and each has one flaw at the exact moment it teaches:

1. First-run overlay (onboarding.rs:44-65) names config init and C-a ? but NOT the two most load-bearing multiplexer facts: how to leave (C-a d) and that `phux` comes back. Add detach/reattach to the body.
2. Help hints live in the status bar CENTER slot, which is truncated FIRST on overflow (status_bar.rs:152-177: "right wins first, then left, center yields last") — on narrow terminals the discoverability strip vanishes while the clock survives. Reconsider slot or truncation priority.
3. Help overlay "Hardcoded" section is always empty: help.rs:121 `let hardcoded_entries = Vec::new()`. Every driver-owned interaction is undiscoverable: copy-mode keys (copy_mode.rs:12-19), right-click context menu (menu.rs:26-41), drag-resize, sidebar clicks (sidebar.rs:47-73). Populate it.
4. Help overlay dismiss hint is wrong under default config: help.rs:129-134 scans cfg.global only; default binds ? in prefix-table (default.toml:237), so the footer says "Press Esc to close" and never echoes the chord. Resolve against both tables.
5. Banner at attach (attach.rs:64) prints to the primary screen then immediately alt-screens over itself — effectively never seen; drop or relocate.
design:
DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream B, 2026-08-01) — decomposed into B4/B5/B6/B7; umbrella. Resolved: (1) Onboarding adds two hint lines: `C-a d` detach ('your session keeps running') and naked `phux` to re-attach; hardcoding is safe by the module's own no-config-file argument (default.toml:216 binds d = detach). (2) print_banner removed from the three attach entry sites (attach.rs:68, 742, 838) where it is immediately alt-screened over; kept for server/relay. (3) StatusBar::render budget order flips from right-left-center to CENTER-LEFT-RIGHT so the teaching strip survives narrow terminals; the clock yields first. (4) The always-empty Hardcoded help section is populated from static &'static tables COLOCATED with the implementing modules (copy_mode, menu/context menu, dividers drag-resize, sidebar clicks), aggregated by help.rs into named sections; colocation + per-module adjacency tests is the anti-rot mechanism. (5) The help-overlay dismiss hint resolves show-help against cfg.global first, then cfg.prefix_table; for a prefix-table binding the footer echoes the BARE key and handle_key dismisses on it — truthful because the prefix resolver is bypassed while an overlay is active.

FINALIZER AMENDMENT (2026-08-01): phux-i0e8.7's punted sidebar/agent-dashboard discoverability finding lands here concretely — B6 additionally builds a 'Panels & dashboards' help-overlay section advertising the sidebar (off by default, schema.rs:40) via its toggle-sidebar binding resolved from the active config, and the agent-fleet dashboard chord (default C-a A, default.toml:190-199). The .7 punt is no longer dangling.

3. Eight commands' example blocks reflow into one mangled line (clap collapses doc-comment paragraphs): send-keys mod.rs:796, wait 864, run 1148, completion 1389 (three shell commands run together — copy-paste does damage), resize 607, signal 684, paste 831, ask 1093. The repo already knows the fix: rec/play use hand-written long_about (mod.rs:931-947, 1000-1023). Apply that pattern everywhere examples exist.
4. Repo-internal leakage: "pre-alpha; see docs/spec/" banner at v0.6.0 (main.rs:178); kill --help cites docs/consumers/tui.md §3 (mod.rs:504); config reload cites tui.md 4.3 (config_action.rs:104); root footer cites docs/operations.md (main.rs:143). Brew users have none of these paths. Extend the leak test (help_inventory.rs:201-220, currently bans ADR-/ticket tokens) to ban docs/ paths.
5. Exit codes 0/1/2/3/124/125 + passthrough are individually documented in doc comments (partial.rs:53-61 is an essay) and surfaced NOWHERE user-visible. Add an EXIT STATUS section next to the existing ENVIRONMENT section (main.rs:120-143).
design: DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream D, 2026-08-01). (1) Doubled --help fixed by keeping the curated categorized screen and suppressing clap's auto Commands block via a root-only help_template; -h gains a pointer to --help; subcommands stay visible in the tree so completions, `phux help <verb>`, and stream F's generated reference are unaffected. (2) The vacuous guard (help_inventory.rs:186-199) is fixed by extracting the curated screen to a named const asserted bidirectionally: every non-hidden subcommand appears in the const, root help contains no clap Commands: header, and no stale curated entries. spawn and launch are added. (3) The eight mangled example blocks (send-keys, wait, run, completion, resize, signal, paste, ask) become hand-written long_about per the rec/play pattern (mod.rs:931-947, 1000-1023). (4) EXIT STATUS section added to after_long_help documenting 0/1/2/3/124/125 and run's passthrough (partial.rs:53-62); reconciled later to render from stream F's canonical exit-code const (F4). (5) Internal docs/ path leaks (main.rs:142-143/178, mod.rs:504, config_action.rs:103-104) scrubbed; leak test extended to ban docs/ tokens; pre-alpha banner becomes a plain version banner. Decomposed into D5-D6; umbrella.

title: One CLI grammar: global --socket/--json, alias parity, unified split flags, JSON error contract
description:
89 invocation paths, per-command grammar. Verified inconsistencies:

- --socket copy-pasted 36 times, not global (only tag has global=true, mod.rs:1225). Live: `phux --socket /x ls` -> "error: unexpected argument". --json on ~32 verbs, no -j, global nowhere. 10 short flags total in the whole binary.
- --json is not honored on any error path: `phux ls --json` against a dead socket -> exit 1, 0 bytes stdout, prose on stderr (ls.rs:41, output_hygiene.rs:10-12 documents it as deliberate) — while spatial.rs:166 already has print_error(json,...); the CLI disagrees with itself. Agents need a machine-readable error shape.
- List/remove alias roulette across 8 registries (ls/list/rm/remove/kill/unlink/clear/--list flag; remote+worktree lack ls; tag lacks list and any --json). Split direction: spawn/launch/play take --split h|v while insert-pane/move-pane take boolean --horizontal/--vertical, and --horizontal is parsed then DISCARDED (main.rs:364,375).
- new --json requires -s enforced at runtime (new.rs:167) not via clap requires. service install --quic is Option<String> while server --quic is SocketAddr — same flag, two types.

Fix: one grammar pass — global --socket/--json (weigh against the --rec scoping rationale at mod.rs:48-54, which is the honest-help counterargument to global flags; decide deliberately), alias parity (ls+list, rm+remove everywhere), unified --split, a stable JSON error object on stderr or stdout for every --json verb, clap-level requires. Keep completions (already generated from the live tree) as the regression check.
design:
DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream D, 2026-08-01). Resolved asymmetrically on purpose: (1) --socket becomes a true clap global (36 of 41 verbs carry hand-copies — the copies are the drift risk; clap globals parse both positions, so `phux --socket X ls` works with zero teaching machinery; socketless verbs reject a provided --socket with a teaching error). The scoped-flag rationale is kept for --rec. (2) --json stays verb-scoped via one shared flattened Args struct (honest help by construction; clap-level `requires` expressible); misplaced `phux --json ls` gets a teaching hint via Cli::try_parse interception. (3) The JSON error contract codifies the shape spatial.rs:464-469 already emits, extended with remedy and exit_code: one line of JSON on stderr, stdout empty, exit codes unchanged (0/1/2/3/124/125 per partial.rs:53-62). (4) Alias policy: every list/remove registry gets ls+list and rm+remove visible aliases; plugin unlink gains rm/remove; tag gains --json; launch --list stays a flag. (5) insert-pane/move-pane adopt --split (value enum, h/v aliases) with hidden deprecated booleans for one release; service install --quic unifies to SocketAddr. All decisions recorded in ADR-0065 (written in D1). Decomposed into D1-D4; umbrella.

FINALIZER AMENDMENT (2026-08-01): two corrections. (a) The 'zero teaching machinery' claim is false while main.rs:66 sets args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true — clap 4.5 errors on any matched root arg followed by a subcommand with no global-arg exemption (clap_builder-4.5.44 parser.rs:480/:530). D1 removes that root setting and re-enforces the RecArgs-only-with-naked-phux rule explicitly (post-parse check or clap-level conflicts), keeping the --rec teaching error as a pinned regression. (b) ADR-0065 additionally records a deliberate short-flag policy decision for the audited '-j' finding (--json on ~32 verbs, 10 short flags total): adopt -j on the shared JsonOpt struct in D2 or document considered-and-rejected with rationale.

title: [umbrella] phux status verb, ls empty states, every error names its remedy
description:
Runtime visibility today is a 3-field ls and one-pane watch. Evidence:

- phux ls (ls.rs:46-68) prints NOTHING on an empty server (no "no sessions" line; --json emits zero bytes when no server runs). ls.rs:56 throws away attached_client_count that the wire already carries, to render a boolean.
- No phux status / info / server status verb exists (help_inventory.rs:87-176). operations.md:10-13 concedes it. vision.md:61-65 promises "observable in real time".
- The sidebar — the richest visibility surface (spaces + per-pane agent lifecycle) — is off by default (schema.rs:40) and discoverable only via "toggle sidebar" in the help overlay. agent-fleet dashboard (C-a A) is advertised only in a config comment (default.toml:190-199).
- Attach failure fallthrough (mod.rs:2076-2099): NotFound gets a copy-pasteable remedy (the bar), but Disconnected/Protocol/Terminal/Ghostty all collapse to "phux: attach failed: {other}" with no doctor pointer, no log path, no version comparison — even though doctor.rs:208-213 already knows how to print the protocol version. report_no_server (mod.rs:1989-2005) similarly fails the bar print_attach_error sets.
- ~10 sites print wire enums with {other:?} to users ("unexpected SPAWN_TERMINAL result: ...").

Fix: phux status (server pid, uptime, version, socket, client count, session/pane summary, log paths); ls empty state + real client counts; every terminal error path ends with its remedy (doctor, log path, or exact command); kill the {other:?} leaks. Empty-state bar is remote.rs:361-364.
design: DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream C, 2026-08-01). phux status needs NO wire change: sessions/windows/panes/attached_client_count from GET_STATE; server pid from UDS peer credentials (tokio UnixStream::peer_cred().pid(), Linux SO_PEERCRED and macOS LOCAL_PEEREPID both verified); negotiated protocol version by actually sending HELLO and reading HELLO_OK (frame.rs:1612-1641 — the one-shot CLI path skips HELLO today, purely a client-side probe); up-since from socket-file mtime (bind time; honest across ADR-0032 graceful upgrade); log paths from C1's canonical helper. ls fixes: empty snapshot prints 'No sessions.' plus exact spawn commands (remote.rs:361-364 precedent); human lines render the real client count; SessionJson gains additive attached_clients keeping `attached` and schema version. Error-remedy pass: report_no_server (mod.rs:1989-2005) and print_attach_error's fallthrough (mod.rs:2095-2098) end with log path + phux doctor; the {other:?} wire-enum leaks are enumerated exactly (14 sites in crates/phux: upgrade.rs:45, spatial.rs:246, detach.rs:70, play.rs:211, supervise.rs:73+117, spawn.rs:81/160/213/262/332, launch.rs:109, kill.rs:84+130; 7 in phux-client: state.rs:212, snapshot.rs:90, ask.rs:67, send_keys.rs:223/303/339, record.rs:188) and replaced by a shared explain_unexpected() helper that surfaces the server's own Error message. Sidebar/agent-dashboard discoverability lines belong to phux-i0e8.10. Decomposed into C4, C5, C6; umbrella. Cross-stream: status --json follows stream D's JSON error contract, so C5 depends on D2.

title: Ephemeral servers have no idle exit, so test harnesses leak daemons
description:
Observed on this machine during the recording/seams work: 69 live 'phux server --session gc-phux-bootstrap --socket /var/folders/.../gc-phux-<hex>.sock --daemonize' processes, all with the same start timestamp (a single burst) and still running hours later. They were still there while a full nextest run was going, and the resulting contention made sub-second tests time out at 80s -- that is how they were found.

phux is arguably behaving CORRECTLY: each was daemonized with a seeded session holding a live shell pane, and 'keep running until the panes are gone' is the tmux-like contract. server_self_exit.rs covers the no-panes case. So this is not a bug report against that behavior.

The gap is that there is no way for an EPHEMERAL caller to opt into a lifetime. A harness that bootstraps a server per test run on a unique temp socket has no lever except tracking the pid itself and killing it, and anything that dies before its cleanup step leaks a daemon with a live PTY child forever.

Possible shapes, needs a decision rather than a patch:
- '--exit-after-idle <dur>': exit once no client has been attached for the interval, regardless of live panes. Opt-in, so the default multiplexer contract is unchanged.
- '--exit-with-parent': tie the daemon's life to the spawning process.
- A documented reaping helper, if the answer is that this belongs to callers.

Cross-reference: scripts/demo-record.sh and crates/phux/tests/rec_e2e.rs both hand-roll exactly this cleanup (trap on exit / kill on drop), which is evidence the need is real and currently paid per-caller.
close_reason: Landed in PR #312 as phux server --exit-after-idle (ADR-0063).

title: Three more hand-rolled correlation loops can hang on a correlated ERROR
description:
Found during the phux-h5hj.1 audit but outside its named catalog, so deliberately not fixed there. Same bug class: a hand-rolled loop waits for one specific response frame and discards everything else, so a peer that legally answers with a correlated ERROR wedges the caller until timeout or forever.

Sites:
- crates/phux/src/commands/spawn.rs::dispatch_spawn_async -- SPAWN_TERMINAL / TERMINAL_SPAWNED. A satellite may legally answer with a correlated ERROR; relay.rs's own comment says so.
- crates/phux-client -- the remaining non-COMMAND request/response pairs identified in the audit report.

These are not COMMAND/COMMAND_RESULT pairs, so Connection::request does not directly apply. Either generalize the correlation helper over the response frame type, or give each pair its own typed round-trip. docs/spec/proto.md section 9 defines ERROR.request_id as present when the error is associated with a request, so the correlation is already specified -- the clients just do not honour it.
close_reason: Landed in PR #309 - the sweep found seven live wedge bugs, not the three catalogued.

title: Surface satellite degradation to the user, not just tracing::warn
description:
Follow-up from phux-h5hj.1. Connection::request now RETURNS the uncorrelated ERROR frames that handle_get_state_federated pushes ahead of a merged snapshot (one per unreachable satellite, commented 'Observable degradation, not silence'), and phux_client::state::get_state_on no longer discards them -- but it still only logs them via tracing::warn! and keeps its Result<SessionSnapshot, AttachError> signature.

So five phux-bin call sites still print nothing to the user when a satellite is unreachable and the listing is silently partial: commands/kill.rs:41, commands/rename.rs:40, commands/tag.rs:45, commands/new.rs:230, commands/agent/mod.rs::with_target_pane.

Work: widen the return type to carry the degradation alongside the snapshot, and decide per verb whether a partial answer is a warning on stderr, a non-zero exit, or a --json field. 'phux ls succeeded' and 'phux ls succeeded for the half of your fleet it could reach' should not be indistinguishable.
close_reason: Landed in PR #309.

title: Write down the rule: capabilities are the additive path, versions are the breaking one
description:
Since b7ffd459 the server rejects any client whose protocol major.minor differs -- a hard reject with no grace period (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs around lines 674-677 and 818-834). A minor bump is therefore a fleet-wide break: a 0.7.0 client cannot talk to a 0.6.0 server at all.

That constraint silently shaped the entire recording design. It is the reason phux rec had to be expressible over existing frames, and the reason a server-side recorder (which would have needed a new Command tag plus a ServerFeature bit plus a minor bump) was rejected -- see ADR-0060.

The repo already has ServerFeature bits, so the implied rule is: capabilities are negotiated and additive, versions are breaking and rare. Today that is tribal knowledge. It is arguably the single most consequential architectural fact in the project and a new contributor would have to reverse-engineer it from a commit message.

Work: state it normatively in docs/spec/proto.md alongside the version rules, cross-reference from CONTRIBUTING.md's wire-change checklist, and consider an ADR since it closes off 'just bump the version' as a design move.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Spec runs ahead of implementation with no gate proving it
description:
Two independent instances found during the recording work:

1. docs/consumers/tui.md section 10 specified 'phux capture --record TARGET --out FILE.cast' and 'phux play FILE.cast' as accepted design, and asserted recording should be a server-side PANE_OUTPUT tee. None of it was implemented, and it contradicted what actually shipped. Nothing caught the contradiction; only review did. (Superseded in PR #306.)
2. role_policy / TerminalRole (PRIMARY vs VIEWER) is specced at docs/spec/L1.md around lines 1031-1073 and unimplemented anywhere in phux-server -- the only workspace hit is a doc comment. The recorder is the natural first VIEWER consumer, and if role enforcement ever lands with the documented default { PRIMARY, NEVER }, every ATTACH_TERMINAL caller including the recorder starts failing against a live TUI.

The general problem: prose marked 'accepted' is indistinguishable from prose describing shipped behavior. Options: a machine-checkable status marker on spec sections, a gate cross-referencing spec sections to implementing symbols, or a convention that unimplemented design lives in ADR/ and never in docs/spec or docs/consumers. Pick one and apply it to the whole tree.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: stdout hygiene: verbs panic on SIGPIPE and it is not systematically enforced
description:
phux snapshot <target> | head -8 panics: 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)' plus a ~50-frame backtrace AND a misleading 'server panic' ERROR line from phux-server::telemetry's panic hook (the server is fine; it is the CLI). Source is the bare println! in print_screen_box, crates/phux/src/commands/snapshot.rs:192. Duplicate of phux-ngq2, tracked here as the systematic half.

Piping into head or less is an ordinary thing to do. Every verb that streams to stdout should exit 0 quietly on a closed pipe.

Work: a shared stdout writer that treats ErrorKind::BrokenPipe as a clean exit; migrate ls, snapshot, watch, and every --json path; extend crates/phux/tests/output_hygiene.rs to cover the broken-pipe case so this cannot regress. Also check whether the telemetry panic hook should stay quiet for CLI processes -- reporting 'server panic' from a client-side panic is actively misleading during triage.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: just ci does not run every gate CI runs (rustdoc)
description:
CI's rust-checks step runs fmt, clippy, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc, and deny. just ci runs fmt, lint, test, deny -- no rustdoc. A green local bar therefore does not predict a green CI, which it should.

Cost incurred: a red build on PR #306 for five rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links errors that a local just ci could not have caught.

Fix: add the doc gate to just ci. Then diff the justfile targets against .github/workflows/ci.yml step by step and make the local bar a superset, or state explicitly in CONTRIBUTING.md which gates are CI-only and why.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: Guard the generated bitmap font table against drift from its BDF source
description:
crates/phux-record/src/font/spleen_8x16.rs (112 KB) is generated from assets/spleen-8x16.bdf (149 KB) by scripts/gen-bitmap-font.py, run once by hand. Nothing references the generator: grep over every script, workflow, and the justfile returns zero hits. The committed table can be hand-edited, or the BDF bumped, with CI perfectly happy.

Preferred fix: a CI check that regenerates and diffs (python3 scripts/gen-bitmap-font.py | diff - src/font/spleen_8x16.rs). ~10 lines, keeps the committed artifact so there is no Python in the build path and no build-time codegen, and turns drift into a red build.

Rejected: a build.rs generating into OUT_DIR. It would put Python on every cargo build, which breaks the nix devshell hermeticity story and adds a build-script node to a 13-crate workspace. Note the repo does use build.rs where warranted (phux-server, clients/phux-vt-web); this is not one of those cases.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307.

title: phux snapshot panics on a broken pipe (SIGPIPE) instead of exiting quietly
description:
Found incidentally while building the recording demo.

Repro: phux snapshot <target> | head -8

Result: thread 'main' panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165: failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32), plus a ~50-frame backtrace AND a 'server panic' ERROR line from phux-server::telemetry's panic hook (misleading -- the server is fine, it is the CLI).

Source: the bare println! in print_screen_box, crates/phux/src/commands/snapshot.rs:192.

Piping a snapshot into head or less is an ordinary thing to do. It should exit 0 quietly. Likely fix: handle the ErrorKind::BrokenPipe write error explicitly on the stdout path rather than letting the println! panic, and check whether other verbs that stream to stdout (ls, watch) have the same hole.

Unrelated to recording; not fixed in PR #306 to keep that diff scoped.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #307 as part of phux-h5hj.8 (188 stdout write sites migrated; the misleading server-panic hook is gone).
