Needs wire pair + spec/CHANGELOG bump + registry reassignment + caller-side rollback. Serves agent-fleet use case. Medium.
close_reason: Merged in PR #350

title: ADR status hygiene + relay spec addendum (ADR-0057 open question 1)
description: Flip ADR-0055 (shipped in f2483ca/77451c0), ADR-0031, ADR-0034 from Proposed to Accepted — status lines drifted from reality. Same pass: write QUIC_RELAY_ALPN, relay tunnel shape, and close-code registry into docs/spec/ + docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md per the docs/spec-is-normative convention. Small, cheap credibility win.

title: relay end-to-end: route/SNI in phux://connect links and phux attach
description: ADR-0057 open question 2: connector dials out (crates/phux-server/src/connector.rs) but consumers cannot express 'attach to server X via relay Y' through pair.rs or attach.rs — relay unusable without hand-wiring. Add relay route/SNI parameter to phux://connect links and phux attach. Completes the flagship remote-attach thread. Medium.

title: verify: clipped context menu after resize may intercept input / commit kill-pane invisibly
description: Unverified research-team finding (verify agent stalled): crates/phux-client/src/render/overlay/menu.rs:186-204,372-378 — after a resize clips the menu away, it may still intercept input and commit destructive actions (kill pane) while invisible. Needs manual verification: trace resize path vs input_dispatch routing; if real, close/clamp menu on resize.
notes:
VERIFIED REAL (2026-08-01). Traced the SIGWINCH arm (driver.rs:3280) against overlay routing.

Mechanism: ContextMenu is the only overlay with construction-time geometry — bounds() returns a frozen self.rect and ignores the render area, while every other overlay (palette, pickers, help, prompt, which-key, toast) computes bounds from the area on each paint and reflows for free. The SIGWINCH arm updates viewport_dims and repaints but never touches the overlay stack, so after a shrink the menu's rect addresses cells that no longer exist.

Two distinct failures:
1. Fully clipped: render() bails, paint_clipped emits nothing, but is_active() stays true — the overlay keeps capturing EVERY key. Enter commits the selected row against a pane the user cannot see it pointing at; if the selection sat on 'Close pane' that is an invisible kill-pane. Reported symptom confirmed.
2. Partially clipped: the old render intersected with the buffer and painted a TRUNCATED box, while row_at kept hit-testing the full pinned rect — rows past the fold were clickable but never drawn.

Fix: RenderOverlay::survives_resize() (default true; false for ContextMenu) + OverlayState::dismiss_stale_on_resize() swept from the SIGWINCH arm before the repaint, so the resize frame is the one that erases it. Menu render is now whole-or-nothing, closing the partial-clip disagreement and the narrow race where a click lands between the resize and the sweep.

Not fixed here (separate, lower stakes): CopyModeOverlay stores pane_cols/pane_rows at construction for cursor clamping, so a resize can leave its clamp stale. Non-destructive (a copy of a wrong span, not a destructive action) and changing copy-mode's resize lifecycle is a visible behavior change — worth its own bead if it bites.
Recovered during JSONL/Dolt reconciliation from pre-session .beads/issues.jsonl sha256=49d185e9801b56e9f7e12e6d7548b2143a84803ffb46d01072fa9fa85ec5ccce. Prior differing fields (verbatim JSON): {"status":"open","updated_at":"2026-07-26T23:07:54Z"}
close_reason: Verified real and fixed in PR #319 (merge 66ba8ae8, all checks green). ContextMenu was the only overlay with construction-time geometry; the SIGWINCH arm never touched the overlay stack, so a clipped menu stayed active and invisible, with Enter committing its selected row (kill-pane if the selection sat there). Fix: RenderOverlay::survives_resize() + OverlayState::dismiss_stale_on_resize() swept from the SIGWINCH arm before the repaint, plus whole-or-nothing menu render closing the partial-clip hit-test disagreement. Four tests, each confirmed to fail without the fix. Adjacent copy-mode instance of the same shape split out as phux-d26y.

title: claude shim execs real claude on ANY nonzero phux exit, incl. mid-session failure
description: render_wrapper in crates/phux/src/commands/agent/shim.rs: wrapper runs phux new ... && exit 0, else exec real claude with original argv. phux new exits nonzero on attach errors long after launch (server crash), so users silently get a fresh unhooked claude with re-run flags. Fix: mktemp marker written by the inner branch once the session starts; on nonzero exit only fall back to real claude if marker is empty, else print 'phux session ended abnormally' and propagate status. Verified by research team.
notes: Fixed: wrapper passes a mktemp sentinel as first --phux-inner arg; inner stamps it before exec'ing Claude. On nonzero exit the outer only falls back to direct Claude if the sentinel is empty (launch never started); otherwise prints 'session ended abnormally' and propagates status. /dev/null fallback if mktemp fails degrades to old behavior.

title: protocol version negotiation bypassable by skipping HELLO
description: b7ffd45 put the version check only inside the Hello arm of handle_client (crates/phux-server/src/runtime/client.rs), but the dispatch loop tolerates clients that never send HELLO, and nothing records whether negotiation happened. An incompatible or malicious client can omit HELLO and issue Attach/Command frames (incl. PutFile) unversioned. Fix: hello_seen flag; reject non-Hello frames before successful HELLO with ErrorCode::VersionIncompatible and close. Verified by research team.
notes: Fixed scoped to threat model: server now requires HELLO before any other frame on network transports (QUIC/WS/WebTransport/SSH-tunnel) via hello_seen flag in handle_client; UDS/Localhost keep the documented same-uid leniency because the CLI control commands (ask/state/snapshot/spawn) never HELLO. Full §6.1 enforcement would need client-side hello-on-connect in Connection constructors first — follow-up if desired.

title: pane_kill_lets_foreground_process_flush_before_death flakes under full-suite load
description: Fails intermittently during a fully parallel 'just test' (1 failure in 2612), passes 10/10 in isolation and 2612/2612 on re-run. Two wall-clock waits on real subprocess scheduling: 2s for the foreground job to acquire a distinct process group after fork/exec of /bin/sh with 'set -m', and 5s for actor shutdown (SIGHUP + grace). Neither duration is part of what the test asserts. Raised to 20s/30s. If it still flakes, the cause is elsewhere and the panic message needs capturing - it was not recorded on the observed failure.
notes: Root cause found, and it was NOT a timeout. Failure message: 'foreground process must run its SIGHUP flush handler before the pane is killed; marker=""' in 0.684s — the final assertion, fast. Race: the test waits for a distinct process group (established at exec) before cancelling, but the shell's 'trap ... HUP' builtin runs AFTER exec. A SIGHUP landing in that window hits the DEFAULT disposition, killing the shell silently with no marker written. Fixed by making the script write an 'armed' file after installing the trap and having the test wait for it before token.cancel(). An earlier attempt widened the 2s/5s timeouts on a guess; that was wrong and has been reverted.
close_reason: Closed

title: l2_adversarial read_event ends a reader's loop on any non-Event frame
description: read_event() returned None for a non-Event frame, which every 'while let Some(..)' caller reads as end-of-stream. A subscriber handed an interleaved non-Event frame first stopped collecting with zero events while its peer collected normally, so test_concurrent_subscription_isolation failed 'A=0 B=1'. Load-sensitive: measured 6/10 red on f1a1306a (pre-branch main) under build load, 0/8 red on an idle machine. The helper's own comment said 'skip non-event frames'; the code returned. Fixed by looping until an Event or the deadline.

title: Cross-window and cross-session pane move without restarting the process
design:
Scoped 2026-07-25. There is no re-parent path today: Terminal.window is set at creation in phux-core/src/registry.rs and no wire command changes it. move-pane/swap-pane/insert-pane all go through spatial.rs::same_session(), which rejects cross-session with the 'cross_session' error code.

Doing this properly needs, in order:
1. ADR — moving a live Terminal between sessions changes who owns it; ADR-0050 settled ownership for NEW terminals only.
2. New wire command (MOVE_TERMINAL { terminal, target_window }), which per repo convention means docs/spec/*.md + docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md + a protocol version bump.
3. Server handler: re-parent in the registry, validate the target window exists and is local, reject satellites.
4. Layout edits on BOTH sessions (remove leaf from A, insert into B), each already expressible via LayoutOps.
5. Relax same_session() to permit exactly the move case, keeping swap/insert same-session.
6. Rollback semantics: if the layout write to B fails after the re-parent succeeds, the pane must not be orphaned — mirror the spawn-placement rollback in commands/spawn.rs.

Not started; a half-landed re-parent is worse than none.
close_reason: Implemented by another session as phux-p39: MOVE_TERMINAL cross-session pane moves landed on main (c2e003e1 + hardening b26a0d0b, released in v0.8.0). The ADR/spec/handler/rollback design steps this bead scoped were executed there.

title: Consolidate phux-server integration-test binaries to cut CI link time
description: Post-sccache measurement (train PR #255): the test lane's compile cost is now cached (321/323 hits) but wall time stayed ~15m43s because nextest links one binary per test file -- crates/phux-server/tests/ has ~40 files, and linking on the 2-core runner dominates. sccache cannot cache links. Lever: consolidate the integration tests into fewer binaries (e.g. one tests/integration.rs harness with 'mod' includes per current file, or grouped by subsystem), preserving nextest per-test granularity (nextest lists tests within a binary fine; per-binary parallelism becomes per-test threads). Watch for: (1) tests that assume process isolation via #[test]-per-binary side effects (env, cwd, signal handlers -- the PTY/UDS suites spawn real servers, should be fine since each test uses its own TempDir socket); (2) mod common sharing already exists, so include structure is amenable. Measure: test-lane wall before/after; target under 10m. Parent: phux-mmxz.

title: Experiment: sccache (GHA backend) to cache workspace-crate compiles in the CI test job
description: phux-mmxz established the test job's 8m54s is phux's own 11 workspace crates + ~40 test-binary links on a 2-core runner; Swatinem/rust-cache structurally cannot cache workspace crates. sccache with the GitHub Actions cache backend hashes crate inputs, so unchanged workspace crates hit cache across commits -- the one zero-cost lever left. Plan: (1) add mozilla-actions/sccache-action to the test (and check) jobs; (2) export RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache, SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED=true INTO the nix develop environment (verify the wrapper resolves inside 'nix develop -c'); (3) confirm cargo/nextest picks it up (sccache --show-stats step); (4) measure 3 runs vs baseline 13m22s; (5) revert if hit-rate is poor (incremental=false may be needed since sccache cannot cache incremental artifacts -- set CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 which CI should use anyway). Keep linking out of scope: sccache does not cache links; if link time dominates after this, the follow-on lever is consolidating integration-test binaries (nextest builds one per test file).
close_reason: Shipped via train PR #255 (commit 802e2f85) and measured: check job 380 hits/2 misses, test job 321 hits/2 misses -- compile caching near-perfect. title: ADR + spike: outbound dial-out (connector) mode -- server dials a relay endpoint and holds a persistent tunnel
description: Today every transport (UDS, wss, QUIC, ssh-stdio) requires the consumer to reach the server's address; ADR-0037 deliberately scoped relay/rendezvous out but preserved the door via the transport trait + URI-shaped identities. Open that door: a mode where the phux server dials OUT to a configured relay/rendezvous endpoint and holds a persistent QUIC tunnel over which consumers are bridged in -- outbound-only, so it works behind NAT/CGNAT with no overlay and no inbound port. Needs an ADR first (closes design space: enrollment/auth handshake shape, what the tunnel carries -- opaque frame relay per ADR-0007 hub semantics -- and how satellite identity tags compose with a relayed path). Spike: prove the existing quinn transport can run in dial-out+accept-bridged-streams shape against a stub relay binary in-tree (test-only).
acceptance_criteria: ADR accepted; spike demonstrates a consumer attaching through a stub relay to a NAT-simulated server with byte-identical frames
notes: ADR-0048 + spike in PR #238 (feat/dialout-connector-adr-spike). ADR Status: Proposed — flip to Accepted on merge, which satisfies acceptance criterion 1; criterion 2 (spike demonstrates attach-through-relay with byte-identical frames, NAT-simulated) is met by relay_connector_spike.rs (4 tests, all 7 ADR assertions, real pinned connector leg). Design input for the future implementation bead, discovered in the spike: quinn accept_bi() does not resolve until the peer sends bytes on the stream, so the connector's tunnel registration MUST carry a preamble on stream 0 or the relay deadlocks waiting — the production connector protocol needs an explicit registration message, not a silent open. Close on merge.
close_reason: ADR-0051 (renumbered from 0048 after collision) + relay connector spike merged as PR #238

title: Add canonical bracketed-paste CLI contract before host adapters expose paste
description: The Pi integration design wants a paste tool, but the current phux branch and canonical docs/consumers/agents.md expose no paste subcommand. Add a side-effect-free bracketed-paste CLI verb over the existing input projection if/when the core contract is approved, document its semantics (insert versus submit, trust policy, JSON/exit behavior), then let Pi/OpenCode adapters expose it. Do not simulate paste with character-by-character send-keys.
acceptance_criteria: phux paste is present on the shipped CLI, documented in the canonical agent contract, tested end-to-end, and host adapters can detect/support it without private wire access.
notes: Recovered context 2026-07-15: a full implementation existed 2026-06-11 on branch feat/agent-paste-verb (commit fc094fd) but never merged and is now unreachable from this clone. Design decisions from that session (bd memory agent-paste-bracketed-verb): (1) wire path already exists on main -- InputEvent::Paste -> FrameKind::InputPaste -> server PerTerminalPasteEncoder wrapping ESC[200~..201~ when DEC 2004 is on (see b9b9eb22); CLI/MCP projection only, no wire change. (2) Route ONE InputEvent::Paste over side-effect-free ROUTE_INPUT. (3) Trusted by DEFAULT (agent vouches for composed content, same trust as send-keys); --untrusted opts into the safety gate (untrusted multiline is_safe=false -> Reject policy silently drops, useless as a default). (4) Document the gotcha: bracketed paste INSERTS, does not SUBMIT -- paste-aware REPLs buffer awaiting a real Enter; agents must follow with send-keys Enter. title: CI test job: 8m54s is workspace compile, not cache
description:
Post-purge measurement corrects an earlier diagnosis.

Facts (run 29313337063 vs 29252506236):
- The Actions cache purge worked: compiled crates dropped 433 -> 21, and libghostty-vt-sys (the zig blob) no longer rebuilds at all (was 2x per run).
- The e2e filterset fix worked: redundant recompiles 37.41s + 49.25s -> 0.40s + 0.22s.
- But the test job only went 14m22s -> 13m22s, and 'Finished test profile in 8m54s' is UNCHANGED.

The 8m54s is NOT a cold dependency build. It is phux's own 11 workspace crates plus linking ~40 test binaries on a 2-core runner. Swatinem/rust-cache deliberately strips workspace crates before saving (own code changes every commit), so it structurally cannot cache this. mold is already in play via the nix devshell.

Levers actually available, none free:
1. 4-core larger runner — would roughly halve it, but larger runners are BILLED even on public repos. Today the repo's Actions bill is $0 (verified: timing API reports total_ms=0).
2. sccache, or rust-cache's cache-all-crates, to cache workspace crates too.
3. Reduce integration-test binary count (nextest builds one binary per test file; linking dominates on 2 cores).
4. Move more of the unit pool off the PR critical path.

Decide whether ~13 min is worth paying for. It costs $0 today.
notes: sccache experiment SHIPPED and measured (see closed child): compile caching near-perfect, check lane 3m43s, but test lane ~15m43s -- linking dominates. Remaining levers: consolidate test binaries (new child bead) or the paid 4-core runner (owner's call, human label stands).

title: phux split <target> [--horizontal|--vertical] [--ratio R] -- CLI verb
description:
Split a pane programmatically -- the thing the TUI has had all along (C-a double-quote / C-a percent) and the control surface has never had.

Pairs with the spawn-placement bug: 'split then run a command in the new pane' is the primitive an agent needs to build a workspace.
design:
layout_ops split() + SET_METADATA, plus a SPAWN_TERMINAL for the new pane's PTY. Study how the TUI already does exactly this asynchronously: attach/input_dispatch.rs:1568 sends SPAWN_TERMINAL and parks a PendingSplit (actions.rs:520); the TerminalSpawned reply arm applies the split to the client's tree (server_frame.rs:951). A headless CLI caller has no such event loop, so it must do the synchronous version -- spawn, await the reply, then write the layout. Get the ordering right or you will write a layout referencing a TerminalId that does not exist yet.

Same registry files / same conflict note as phux focus. Note SplitDir::Vertical is currently UNREACHABLE from any spawn path (registry.rs:139 hardcodes Horizontal) -- this verb is the first thing that can produce one, so exercise it.
acceptance_criteria: phux split . --vertical --ratio 0.3 produces a vertical split at 0.3 that an attached client renders correctly. Both directions tested. e2e test. Docs in all three places.

title: phux focus <target> -- CLI verb
description:
Move the attached client's focus to the pane a selector names. The verb that makes 'pop over to it' possible.

Semantics come from ADR-0044 -- this bead does NOT get to decide whether an agent can yank a human's viewport; read the ADR. If the ADR made directed focus opt-in, this verb must respect the config gate and must fail (or no-op with a clear message) when the gate is off, rather than silently doing nothing.
design:
Implementation is a layout_ops focus() + SET_METADATA. Files (from the verb-anatomy inventory):
  - crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs -- 'pub(crate) mod focus;' in the block at :39-63, and the Command::Focus variant (doc comment IS the help text)
  - crates/phux/src/commands/focus.rs -- NEW: pub(crate) fn run_focus(...) -> ExitCode
  - crates/phux/src/main.rs:199+ -- dispatch arm, AND a line in the curated long_about inventory at :48-113 (test top_level_help_lists_every_subcommand FAILS otherwise)
  - crates/phux/src/help_inventory.rs:83-139 -- add 'phux focus' to EXPECTED_INVENTORY, sorted (test command_inventory_matches_snapshot FAILS otherwise)
  - crates/phux/tests/ -- e2e test (pattern: run_wait_e2e.rs)
  - docs: docs/consumers/tui.md:92 verb block; docs/consumers/agents.md:85 verb catalog AND :693 exit-code table
Exit codes follow the house rule: 1 = phux could not reach/resolve; 2 = server refused.
CONFLICT: the three registry files above are shared with the sibling verb beads (split, move). Expect a trivial rebase.
acceptance_criteria: phux focus @7 moves an attached client's view to pane 7 (subject to the ADR-0044 gate). Selector grammar works including #tag. e2e test. Docs updated in all three places.
close_reason: Superseded by ADR-0049: focus is client-local, so a headless CLI subprocess cannot honestly mutate an attached TUI viewport. Explicit local next-attention/return navigation replaces it.

title: Nothing tells you to register the MCP adapter with a host -- document it
description:
phux-mcp is built, shipped in releases (scripts/dist.sh:23, release.yml:189), installed by scripts/install.sh:10 -- and there is no documentation anywhere telling a user to actually REGISTER it with an MCP host. Discovered the hard way: this repo's own maintainer had phux-mcp on PATH and a running server, and Claude Code had zero phux tools, because nothing ever ran the registration.

That is a complete adoption cliff for the flagship agent surface. It ships and it is invisible.
design: Add a 'Registering with a host' section near the top of docs/consumers/mcp.md with the concrete one-liners: Claude Code -> 'claude mcp add phux -- phux-mcp'; and the generic stdio JSON block ({command: 'phux-mcp'}) for other hosts, noting PHUX_SOCKET / --socket for a non-default socket (crates/phux-mcp/src/socket.rs). Mention the server must already be running (phux_new does not auto-spawn one -- tools.rs:132). Consider a 'phux mcp install' convenience verb as a follow-up bead if it feels warranted, but docs first.
acceptance_criteria: A reader who has just installed phux can go from zero to Claude Code calling phux_ls in one copy-pasted command. Cross-linked from README and docs/consumers/agents.md.
close_reason: Documented MCP host registration, socket configuration, server prerequisite, and cross-links.

title: De-duplicate GET_STATE: three hand-rolled copies of the same request loop
description:
The same 'send GET_STATE, loop recv() until the matching CommandResult, decode SessionSnapshot' dance is implemented three times:
  - CLI: crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs:1035 command_on() + :1057 request_command()
  - MCP: crates/phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:464 get_state() + :551 get_state_on()
  - MCP again: crates/phux-mcp/src/ask_tool.rs (its own third copy)

They have already drifted (the MCP copy never fetches the tag index -- see the #tag bug). Every bead in this epic that adds a verb or a tool needs this loop, so triplication becomes quadruplication unless it is fixed first. This is the highest-leverage cleanup in the epic.

Related: crates/phux-client/src/agent.rs (the typed Agent facade) is the OBVIOUS home and is DEAD -- see the sibling bead. Do not put this on Agent; put it in a free function module, which is the de-facto shared surface (selector.rs, snapshot.rs, send_keys.rs, run.rs, wait.rs, watch.rs, ask.rs all follow that pattern and ARE shared by both CLI and MCP).
design: Land one async fn in phux-client (e.g. crates/phux-client/src/state.rs: get_state(socket) -> SessionSnapshot, plus a get_state_on(&mut Connection) variant for callers already holding a connection), register in crates/phux-client/src/lib.rs:32-44, and delete all three copies. While you are there, fold in the tag-index fetch so #tag works uniformly.
acceptance_criteria: One implementation. CLI, MCP tools.rs, and ask_tool.rs all call it. No behavior change for existing verbs (verify with the e2e tests). Sets up the #tag fix.
close_reason: Implemented shared phux-client state/tag helpers, migrated CLI and MCP/ask, and added MCP #tag regression coverage

title: MCP: #tag selectors silently resolve to nothing
description:
crates/phux-mcp/src/tools.rs:608 resolve_one() calls selector::resolve(), NOT selector::resolve_with_tags(), and never fetches the L3 TagIndex. So any MCP tool given a '#tag' target resolves to zero candidates and returns 'no such target'.

The CLI does it correctly: crates/phux/src/commands/mod.rs:1136 resolve_targets() fetches the tag index via commands::tag::fetch_tag_index (see kill.rs:94).

This is a silent capability gap, not an error -- an agent using #tag through MCP just gets a confusing miss. Tags are how you would address a FLEET of agent panes, so this bites exactly the workflow this epic is about.
design: Fix in resolve_one (and required_target's callers) by fetching the tag index and using resolve_with_tags. Prefer landing the tag-index fetch as a shared fn in phux-client rather than a third copy -- coordinate with the get_state de-duplication bead.
acceptance_criteria: An MCP tool call with target='#foo' resolves the same panes as 'phux kill #foo'. Unit test in tools.rs covering a #tag selector against a fixture with a tag index.
close_reason: Implemented shared phux-client state/tag helpers, migrated CLI and MCP/ask, and added MCP #tag regression coverage

title: Verify Cachix caches for real (log-confirmed hits) + measure CI speedup
description: After the wiring merges, do NOT trust a green check — read the post-merge CI run logs and confirm: (a) NO 'HTTP error 401' / 'disabling binary cache' lines; (b) real Cachix activity: 'compressing and pushing <path> to <cache>' on first run, and 'copying path <...> from https://<cache>.cachix.org' (substituter HIT) on the SECOND run; (c) the zig libghostty blob + rustc devshell come from the cache instead of rebuilding. Record before/after CI wall-time (was ~13-18 min uncached). If it's still uploading to 'the GitHub Action Cache' or 401ing, it's not fixed — dig in. Depends on the wiring bead.
notes: Verified after PR #207 merge. Baseline run 29173202799: 00:06:58-00:21:33 (14m35s), check job 5m04s; logs show check rebuilt libghostty-vt-sys and magic-nix-cache used fallback GHAC after FlakeHub 401. First post-merge main run 29176991441 attempt 1: 02:35:28-02:49:39 (14m11s), check 2m41s. Warm attempt 2: 02:50:47-03:04:55 (14m08s), check 2m25s. Attempt 2 logs: 24 explicit copies from https://phux.cachix.org including rustc-1.90.0, rust-default-1.90.0 and nix-shell-env; both Swatinem rust-cache lanes exact-hit; zero libghostty-vt-sys compiles; zig-0.15.2 substituted from cache.nixos.org rather than built; zero HTTP 401, cache-disable, or 'the GitHub Action Cache' magic-cache lines. PR run 29176518648 authenticated and pushed rust-default plus the shell closure to phux. Overall wall improvement is modest (27s, 3%) because the parallel test lane remains the critical path (8m47s local workspace compilation + 136s tests), while the formerly rebuilding check lane improved 2m39s (52%).
close_reason: Two post-merge CI attempts log-confirm Cachix substituter hits, authenticated closure pushes, no 401/GHAC fallback, and no libghostty rebuild; before/after timings recorded

title: Wire cachix/cachix-action into ci/stress/publish-crate/release + flake.nix substituter

Config the action with name=<cache> + authToken=secrets.CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN + pushFilter to skip the libghostty source. Add the cache as a substituter so builds PULL from it: flake.nix nixConfig { extra-substituters = 'https://<cache>.cachix.org'; extra-trusted-public-keys = '<cache>.cachix.org-1:...'; } OR set it in the workflow via cachix use. After the devshell/build, push the closure (cachix push <cache> or the action's post-hook). Remove the now-unused id-token: write if desired (or leave; harmless). Depends on the human-prereq bead. Branch + PR + gate; do NOT merge red.
close_reason: PR #207 rebase-merged as 6bf2257 after full local and GitHub CI gates; merge state explicitly verified MERGED

title: Swap CI Nix caching: magic-nix-cache (FlakeHub 401/paid) -> Cachix (free OSS)
description: PROBLEM (verified in run 29173202799 logs): magic-nix-cache tries FlakeHub Cache but gets HTTP 401 ('unable to download https://cache.flakehub.com/nix-cache-info'), because FlakeHub Cache is a PAID Determinate feature — the free tier phall1 is on covers flake publishing, not the binary cache. It falls back to the GitHub Actions Cache (GHAC), which has a 10GB/repo cap shared with Swatinem/rust-cache, so the big Nix devshell closure + Rust artifacts + the zig-built libghostty blob evict each other -> partial hits -> 13-18 min CI runs. PR #206 already added 'id-token: write' to ci/stress/publish-crate/release (harmless, correct config, live if FlakeHub Cache is ever purchased) but the 401 proves the permission alone can't fix a paid-feature wall. GOAL: migrate to Cachix, which is genuinely free for open source (public repo), has no size cap, and no 401. GHOST NOTE: the zig libghostty blob (libghostty-vt-sys build) is the expensive artifact; Swatinem/rust-cache should STAY for Cargo artifacts, Cachix handles the Nix store/devshell closure. ACCEPTANCE: CI logs show real Cachix push+pull (not GHAC uploads, not a 401), CI wall-time drops materially on a warm cache, all 4 workflows migrated, no functional regression.
close_reason: Cachix migration merged in PR #207 and verified from raw CI logs across push and warm pull runs

title: Move input encode onto the dedicated input lane (Send mode snapshot)
description:
Follow-up to phux-51n6.2 / ADR-0044. The dedicated input lane routes input off the main thread, but ENCODE (wire event -> PTY bytes) stays on the actor thread because the per-pane encoders read the pane's live DEC-mode state from the !Send Terminal (cursor-key/keypad application mode, mouse tracking/format, DEC 1004 focus, DEC 2004 bracketed paste) via set_options_from_terminal.

To move encode onto the lane: publish a Send snapshot of those encoder-relevant modes from the actor after each output batch (modes only change from PTY output), and have the lane's encoders consume it via the explicit setters (set_cursor_key_application, set_keypad_key_application, set_tracking_mode, set_format, focus/paste mode flags) instead of set_options_from_terminal. Needs an equivalence test: snapshot-driven encode must be byte-identical to live-terminal encode across representative mode states (a missed mode silently mis-encodes input). Then the whole route+encode path runs off the actor thread and hands encoded bytes to the Send pty_tx.
close_reason: Implemented dedicated-lane snapshot-driven input encoding with exact pinned libghostty capture/apply API

title: Auto-activate loss-tolerant state-sync for forwarded/lossy-leg consumers
description: ADR-0042 landed the advance-on-ack loss-tolerant reference model (phux-v45.8), fully wired end-to-end via ConsumerAttachRequest.loss_tolerant and enable_loss_tolerance, and proven by actor-level tests. Production attach currently sets loss_tolerant=false: a satellite cannot see the hub's downstream fan-out drop from its own reliable link. Wire real activation for a forwarded consumer — either the hub requesting loss-tolerant state-sync from the satellite (the hub attaches as a StateSync consumer and signals loss-tolerance), or a QUIC-datagram transport signal. See ADR-0042 Tradeoffs (Auto-activation is deferred) and runtime/attach.rs / runtime/commands.rs loss_tolerant:false sites.
design: Design read 2026-07-15, round 2 (verified to main 87382fa7): (1) Production loss_tolerant:false sites: runtime/attach.rs ~1123 (local ATTACH) and runtime/commands.rs ~701 (ATTACH_TERMINAL incl. hub-relayed). (2) No loss-tolerance bit on the wire; ConsumerAttachRequest.loss_tolerant is server-internal. (3) The caps blob in HELLO is PREFIX-EXTENSIBLE (decode.rs ~338: shorter blob leaves trailing caps at defaults), so a trailing loss-tolerant byte is an ADDITIVE spec change -- but note the optional palette block is currently omitted-when-None, so the encoder must start always-writing the palette present-byte once any field follows it (safe both directions: the TLV field is length-delimited, old decoders ignore unread tail). (4) OPEN QUESTION discovered: the hub->satellite link authenticates via bearer preamble (hub/link.rs) and does NOT appear to send FrameKind::Hello at all -- so a HELLO-caps bit may never reach the satellite for link clients. Before implementing, read hub/link.rs's post-connect send path and the satellite's client task for link connections to determine (a) whether the link HELLOs (then caps-bit works, set once per link = loss-tolerance for all relayed consumers, defensible per ADR-0018 addendum), or (b) the link skips HELLO (then the carrier must be a link-level frame or a new field on the relayed ATTACH_TERMINAL command instead). (5) Local direct attaches stay loss_tolerant:false. Satellite-side activation plumbing (enable_loss_tolerance, terminal_actor/mod.rs ~1165-1190) exists and is tested.

title: launch executor for integration [launch] command templates

There is no 'phux launch' subcommand and launch-bench.sh runs 'phux new -s <session>' with no command, so installing agent-tools/herdr does NOT auto-run phux-agent-wrap.sh and no phux.agent/v1 record is written automatically. Implement an executor that resolves a template's [launch] command (expanding ${PHUX_PLUGIN_ROOT}, honoring working_directory) and spawns it as a pane's program, threading the pane target so the wrapper self-identifies. Until then, README documents manual/alias activation.

title: server: inject PHUX_TERMINAL_ID into spawned pane processes

To let a pane's foreground process (e.g. the agent wrapper examples/plugins/agent-tools/scripts/phux-agent-wrap.sh) self-target its own pane, the server should inject PHUX_TERMINAL_ID=<wire local id> into the CommandBuilder at spawn time. The wire id is idempotently internable (registry::intern_terminal_wire) before the actor build in runtime/commands.rs seed_session_with_pty_and_colors / spawn_pane_with_pty_and_colors, so the value is knowable pre-spawn. New always-on pane env surface likely warrants an ADR + docs/spec note. Without this, the wrapper only writes a phux.agent/v1 record when a launcher passes PHUX_AGENT_TARGET/--target.

title: Attach relay across the hub: two-hop output/input/ack path
description: Thread TERMINAL_OUTPUT, input, FRAME_ACK through hub->satellite; verify predictive echo and snapshot-on-attach survive per ADR-0007 s4 invariants. Size: M.

title: Render Kitty graphics on the client (ADR-0034)
description: The client ingests TERMINAL_OUTPUT via vt_write then re-renders CELLS ONLY (crates/phux-client/src/attach/render.rs), so out-of-band Kitty graphics images are silently dropped. The server already forwards APC _G bytes verbatim (crates/phux-server/src/downsample.rs) and libghostty-vt exposes the needed APIs (kitty_graphics()/PlacementIterator/is_virtual in crates/libghostty-vt/src/kitty/graphics.rs) but phux never calls them. The pixel-size probe blocker was fixed in PR #138; this is the remaining graphics-rendering work.
design: Per ADR-0034: prefer the Kitty Unicode-placeholder protocol (placements become cell content, fitting the existing cell-walker) with a client-side APC placement re-emit as fallback. The TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT synthesizer (crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs) must replay live image state so images survive detach/reattach.
acceptance_criteria: kitty +kitten icat renders an image inside a phux pane; the image survives detach/reattach; works with the cell renderer (no raw-byte passthrough that corrupts cursor/coords).
notes: User visual smoke found first-live-render bug: docs/assets/payload.sh showed the image only after detach/reattach. Root cause: client-side libghostty mirrors had 0x0 cell pixel geometry, so classic Kitty placements without explicit c/r dimensions could not infer their grid footprint during live render; snapshot replay later supplied c/r, making it appear on reattach. Fixed PaneSlot construction and safe_resize to seed 8x16 fallback cell pixels, matching server actor behavior. Added regression pane_slot_initializes_nonzero_cell_pixels_for_live_kitty_render. just ci passed: 1581 tests / 30 skipped plus fmt, clippy, docs, deny, rustdoc.

title: [epic] Swarm batch — parallel backlog map-reduce
description:
ENTRY POINT for a fresh-session swarm. Goal: map-reduce the phux backlog across parallel agents.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (learned 2026-06-10/11): client changes funnel through driver.rs / server_frame.rs / input_dispatch.rs / paint.rs / render.rs. Agents editing these in parallel collide in the REDUCE (merge) phase. So: parallelize ACROSS disjoint lanes; SERIALIZE within the client lane (rebase + just ci between each). origin/main moves under you (multiple concurrent agents in this workspace — main checkout is on other branches; NEVER touch it, always use your own worktree off origin/main).

WORKFLOW per item: worktree off origin/main -> implement -> nix develop --command just ci GREEN -> clippy+fmt preflight (backtick doc identifiers; map_or not map().unwrap_or()) -> push (gh auth switch --user phall1 first) -> PR -> watch CI -> rebase onto moving main if needed + re-run just ci -> merge -> close bead. Verify TUI render changes via emulator where possible (snapshot --cells); assembled-frame render is the one thing CI can't prove.

LANE A — Client render/UX (SERIALIZE; shared hub). Order matters:
  A1 phux-jow6 mouse-while-zoomed (quick) [turnkey: bead has fix]
  A2 phux-l5xa snapshot --rendered HARNESS [turnkey] -- DO EARLY: unblocks verified render for A3+
  A3 phux-4h5a sidebar 2/2 [turnkey: foundation merged #98/#99, integration plan on bead] -- verify with A2
  A4 phux-7143 copy-mode word/line/semantic select [scoped by agent]
  A5 phux-7ubw letterbox/mirror [scoped by agent]

LANE B — Server/transport (PARALLEL to A; disjoint files):
  B0 phux-fak5 graceful upgrade -- IN PROGRESS by another agent (feat/portable-pty-adopt); COORDINATE, do not duplicate
  B1 phux-ign + phux-0o8 per-Terminal TERM=ghostty SPAWN field + KIP round-trip [scoped by agent] -- protocol+server, disjoint
  B2 phux-84yt QUIC transport (P0) -- LARGE, needs its own sub-decomposition before swarming

LANE C — Predict (PARALLEL; predict/ module + light server_frame hook):
  C1 phux-pxaj adaptive auto-back-off slice [scoped by agent]

DEFERRED/BLOCKED: phux-97w (upstream libghostty pin) blocks phux-3sy scrollback search; epics phux-klxy/phux-0wmf/phux-yx6y/phux-nol/phux-51n6 need decomposition first.
EXCLUDED (not phux): gc/mol beads phux-887dj/9fq0j/jiesq/u02uj/zklq4.

REDUCE: merge in dep order (A1->A2->A3; B/C parallel); each rebases onto current origin/main + re-verifies just ci before merge. Keep PRs small. Done beads this lineage: phux-7ry0, phux-v9zw, phux-efj7, phux-9ydy, phux-5pyx, phux-ac14, phux-jy4t, phux-x2hm (all merged).

title: Cursor lags a frame on a pure cursor move (Clean render skips cursor)
description: Moving the cursor without changing cells (left/right arrow within a command line, accepting a zsh autosuggestion, vi-mode motions) leaves libghostty's rows Dirty::Clean. render_at_inner early-returned on Clean BEFORE its cursor block, so it neither emitted a CUP nor updated last_cursor — the on-screen cursor stayed put until the next keystroke dirtied a cell (e.g. Esc changing cursor shape). Most visible in vi-mode shells. Fix: on Clean, reposition the cursor + refresh last_cursor/last_cursor_local when it moved; emit nothing when unchanged (idle no-op preserved).
close_reason: Merged in #105

title: New session inherits the previous session's layout (group-scoped layout metadata)
description: Layout is persisted as L3 metadata at Scope::Group(DEFAULT_GROUP_ID) — ONE shared group across all sessions (driver.rs:1559 LAYOUT_KEY const + DEFAULT_GROUP_ID). So a new session (C-a C) reads the previous session's multi-pane tree but only owns one spawned terminal → dead/empty panes; and splitting in one session clobbers another's saved layout. Immediate fix (this bug): reconcile_loaded_layout discards a loaded tree whose leaves don't include the session's ATTACHED focused pane (foreign layout) → clean single pane. PROPER fix (follow-up): key the layout metadata per-session (LAYOUT_KEY + session id) at all 5 sites (GetMetadata/SubscribeMetadata driver.rs:955/960, SetMetadata input_dispatch.rs:413 + driver.rs:1229, is_layout_key match server_frame.rs:995) so each session remembers its OWN layout with no cross-session clobbering. focused_session is available (driver.rs:941).
close_reason: Merged in #107 (per-session layout keys)

title: [epic] Perfect predictive echo
description: Predictive (Mosh-class) local echo is experimental and currently being flipped OFF by default because it mispredicts in common real-world cases. Make it robust enough to re-enable by default. Known issues: (1) vi-mode shells (bindkey -v / set -o vi): normal-mode keys h/j/k/l/i/x/dd are COMMANDS not inserts, so every keystroke mispredicts an insert glyph the server then contradicts — the client can't detect vi mode without shell integration; (2) top-left ghost after fast split/focus-change (FIXED phux-cdvr: suspend until authoritative cursor); (3) general fragility under fast layout/screen transitions and alt-screen apps. Direction to evaluate: adaptive auto-back-off (stop predicting after N consecutive reconcile contradictions, resume when typing normalizes); only predict at/after a known prompt boundary; OSC-133 shell-integration signal for prompt + mode; RTT-adaptive enable. Re-enable default only once vi-mode + modal apps are clean. See phux-7ry0, phux-cdvr, phux-9gw.* lineage.
notes:
SCOPED (adaptive-backoff slice): First shippable slice of self-healing predictive echo. GOAL: when the server keeps CONTRADICTING predictions (vi-mode, modal apps, fast transitions), auto-suspend predicting; resume when reconciles confirm cleanly again. Reuses the existing suspend/is_suspended/set_cursor-rearm machinery (phux-cdvr) — no new overlay/render work.

CONTRADICTION-TRACKING DESIGN (all internal, no config knob this slice; thresholds hardcoded const in state.rs, doc as future-tunable like PredictiveConfig note at state.rs:24):
- Add to PredictionState (state.rs:130 struct, after the suspended field): contradiction_streak:u32 (consecutive reconcile passes that contradicted), clean_confirm_streak:u32 (consecutive clean productive passes since auto-suspend), and auto_backed_off:bool to distinguish a BACKOFF suspend from the existing re-anchor suspend so set_cursor unconditional re-arm (state.rs:262) does NOT prematurely clear a backoff.
- New method note_reconcile(&mut self, stats: ReconcileStats) on PredictionState: if stats.contradicted>0 then contradiction_streak+=1, clean_confirm_streak=0, and when streak>=BACKOFF_THRESHOLD (const 3) call internal auto_suspend (sets suspended=true + auto_backed_off=true, drops queue like suspend). If stats.contradicted==0 AND stats.confirmed>0 (clean PRODUCTIVE pass) then clean_confirm_streak+=1, contradiction_streak=0, and when auto_backed_off && clean_confirm_streak>=REARM_THRESHOLD (const 2) clear auto_backed_off + suspended=false. Empty passes (confirmed==0 && contradicted==0) are NEUTRAL — leave streaks alone.
- ReconcileStats already has confirmed/contradicted/pending (reconcile.rs:49) and is computed by reconcile_terminal_output_per_cell. PREFER: reconcile fn calls state.note_reconcile(summary) just before return (reconcile.rs:161) so all callers get backoff free; the contradicted-suffix clear() (reconcile.rs:149) stays untouched. IMPORTANT: streak fields must NOT be reset by clear() or suspend() (clear runs on every contradiction) — keep them out of those resets.
- set_cursor guard (state.rs:262): only clear suspended when !auto_backed_off, so a backoff survives cursor/snapshot syncs and only the clean-confirm path re-arms. Existing re-anchor suspend() (state.rs:201, from reanchor_predict_to_pane) leaves auto_backed_off untouched.

DRIVER HOOK (light): server_frame.rs:528 already discards _stats from reconcile_terminal_output_per_cell. Internal approach = ZERO driver diff (keep the call). Alt: rename _stats to stats and add predict.note_reconcile(stats). Chosen: internal. The wholesale-drain reconcile_terminal_output (reconcile.rs:67) does NOT feed backoff (not a per-cell verdict) — leave it.

CONFIG: no new knob. predictive-echo (phux-config ExperimentalCfg, default false) stays the only surface; backoff is internal and only runs when echo is opted-in. Thresholds = hardcoded consts doc-earmarked for a future PredictiveConfig field. Default stays OFF; this slice makes opt-in self-healing, a later slice flips default once vi-mode clean.

TESTS (mirror reconcile.rs per-cell + state.rs unit module):
- state.rs: 3 contradictions in a row via note_reconcile then is_suspended true & predict_key Skipped; backed-off state survives set_cursor (still suspended); 2 clean productive confirms after backoff then re-armed (predict_key Predicted); empty passes do not move streaks; re-anchor suspend() independent of auto_backed_off.
- reconcile.rs: integration — predict_key inserts then reconcile with contradicting cells 3x via row_reader, assert is_suspended; then confirming cells, eventually re-armed. Reuse row_reader/key_text helpers.

FILES TOUCHED (swarm conflict map): predict/state.rs (struct fields + note_reconcile + auto_suspend + set_cursor guard + tests); predict/reconcile.rs (call note_reconcile before return + integration tests); attach/server_frame.rs (NONE if internal; else 1 line at :528). No config-crate change.

PHASING: P1 state.rs fields + note_reconcile + auto_suspend + set_cursor guard + unit tests. P2 wire into reconcile_terminal_output_per_cell + integration tests. P3 verify zero/one-line driver hook at server_frame.rs:528. P4 docs: predict/mod.rs backoff paragraph + consts as future-tunable. OUT OF SCOPE: OSC-133, RTT-adaptive, flipping default ON.

Verified now with: nix develop -c env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/phux-ultrawork-target cargo test -p phux-client-core predict:: (91 predict tests passed). Remaining predictive/latency ideas stay tracked in phux-51n6.

title: Predictive echo ghosts a glyph at top-left after a fast split/focus change
description: After a split (or any focus change to a not-yet-rendered pane), a quick keystroke echoes a predicted underlined glyph at screen top-left that the real pane never overwrites, so it lingers. Cause: reanchor_predict_to_pane fell back to set_cursor(0,0) when the pane had no authoritative cursor yet (last_cursor_local None). Fix: suspend prediction until the next authoritative cursor sync (set_cursor) re-arms it, instead of guessing (0,0). Follow-up to phux-7ry0.
close_reason: Merged in #102

title: Pane zoom (tmux prefix-z): temporarily maximize the focused pane
description: Toggle the focused pane to fill the whole pane-viewport (others hidden, no dividers) and back — tmux's beloved prefix-z. Cleanest design: a driver-local zoomed: Option<TerminalId>; when Some, render/reflow against a synthetic LayoutState::single(zoomed) instead of workspace.active_window(), so the existing paint + reflow handshake resizes the pane's PTY to full size and back with no paint-code changes. Add zoom-pane action (ACTION_NAMES + run_action + action_registry REGISTRY) + default keybind; show a Z flag in the status bar when zoomed. Edge cases: single-pane no-op, zoom+split, zoom+close. Needs live verification of the resize handshake (memory: see-rendering-via-emulator).
notes: SCOPED (session 2026-06-10): Design CONFIRMED sound. Add Workspace::render_window(zoomed: Option<&TerminalId>) -> Cow<LayoutState> in phux-client-core/src/layout/mod.rs (~:304): Some(id)+id-still-a-live-leaf => Cow::Owned(LayoutState::single(id)); else Cow::Borrowed(active_window). Folding the liveness guard in makes zoom self-healing on close/window-switch. NOT a single chokepoint: ~20 active_window() reads split into RENDER/REFLOW reads (swap to render_window when zoomed: driver.rs 997,1101,1170-1178,1252-1261,1284,1416-1428,1462,219,246; server_frame.rs 249,362,466,487,509,744) vs MUTATION/INPUT reads (stay real). Driver-local zoomed:Option<TerminalId> near driver.rs:827; thread into handle_server_frame + DispatchCtx. Action: toggle-zoom in ACTION_NAMES + run_action (mirror next-pane arm) + ActionEffects.toggle_zoom + action_registry REGISTRY (drift test) + default.toml 'z'. Single-pane => bell no-op. Resize handshake (crux): reuse compute_reflow with prev=pre-toggle rects, new=post-toggle; emit TERMINAL_RESIZE BEFORE repaint (mirror close path driver.rs:1248). Status Z flag: WindowInfo.zoomed + window_infos(zoomed). Auto-clear zoom on split + window-switch (tmux semantics). RISKIEST: mouse routing input_dispatch.rs:249 must hit-test the SYNTHETIC layout when zoomed (click anywhere -> zoomed pane). Unit-testable: render_window truth table, run_action arm, compute_reflow diff, window_infos. title: Warp-style session/window sidebar + pluggable chrome regions
description: Toggleable vertical sidebar (default left, ~20 cols) listing windows as tabs, each titled from its OSC title (now available via window_infos, #95) with the focused tab highlighted; click/select to focus. Delivers the 'chrome modular and pluggable' ask via a ChromeRegion reservation abstraction (sidebar = just another region alongside status bar + dividers). Default-off to keep the main path snapshot-stable.
design:
PHASED (each independently shippable):

P1 Chrome-region reservation + viewport offset. Today reservation is 1-D: pane_viewport() only shrinks height for the status bar; pane rects tile from (0,0). compute_layout/pane_rects walk_layout from Rect{0,0,w,h} — passing a non-zero-origin Rect offsets all leaf rects AND divider cells automatically (no separate offset pass). Risk = the ~8 viewport->pane-area sites that must all consume the same reservation or panes/dividers/reflow(TERMINAL_RESIZE)/mouse/predict disagree: paint.rs pane_viewport+2 compute_layout calls+single-pane fallback; server_frame.rs snapshot+output paint origins+fallbacks; driver.rs SIGWINCH reflow prev/new dims; reflow.rs pane_rects; mouse.rs route_mouse_event+clamp; actions.rs min-cell gate. Predict follows for free (it reads slot.renderer.last_origin from the rect). rasterize() takes (cols,rows) for edge-junction math — must take the content rect so sidebar-boundary junctions are right. Introduce ChromeRegion{reserve(Edge,thickness); paint(rect,ctx)} + ChromeLayout folding regions off the outer rect to a residual content Rect; re-express pane_viewport in terms of it (status-bar-only residual is byte-identical => snapshots stable).

P2 Sidebar painter (render/chrome/sidebar.rs impl ChromeRegion): one row per window 'N title', active row themed (new slots sidebar_active/inactive/border, default to accent/dim/border). Feed from window_infos(&workspace,&panes) (already title-aware). Cache like StatusBarPainter (unchanged input => zero-byte repaint). Reserve Edge::Left when [sidebar].enabled.

P3 already partly done: titles come from window_infos (#95, phux-efj7).

P4 Mouse+keys: route_mouse_event sidebar pre-check (x<width => window index => switch_window); new actions toggle-sidebar (driver-held bool, layout_mutated=true to reflow) + focus-window(index), added to ACTION_NAMES + run_action + action_registry REGISTRY (drift test enforces).

P5 Config: [sidebar] enabled(false)/width(20)/position(Left|Right) in schema.rs; theme slots.

No wire/L3/ADR change (client-only chrome; titles from the client's own libghostty mirror; sidebar visibility is per-client render state like focus, ADR-0019 dec 6). Default-off keeps every existing snapshot/test green; the enabled path gets its own tests. Full design + file:line anchors captured in session 2026-06-10.
notes: INTEGRATION (2/2) turnkey site list — thread a content-rect reservation (sidebar inset by width+position; full pane area when disabled, so default-off == compute_layout, snapshot-stable). Replace compute_layout(ls, pane_dims) with compute_layout_in(ls, content_rect, viewport_dims) and pane_rects with pane_rects_in at: paint.rs:62 (paint_focused_pane), paint.rs:159 (paint_full_frame); server_frame.rs:253,364,469,557,585; driver.rs:1166,1417,1495 (SIGWINCH reflow + repaint); reflow.rs:112 (compute_reflow); actions.rs:358 (min-cell gate). Also: route_mouse_event (mouse.rs) needs the content offset + a sidebar hit-zone; driver builds SidebarPainter from cfg.sidebar + paints it into the reserved rect after panes; add toggle-sidebar + focus-window actions (ACTION_NAMES + run_action + action_registry REGISTRY drift test). Foundation merged: #98 (compute_layout_in/pane_rects_in), #99 (SidebarCfg + SidebarPainter). Verify the resize handshake live (memory: see-rendering-via-emulator) since reflow timing is involved.
close_reason: Merged as PR #124: window sidebar 2/2 — chrome-region reservation (content_rect) threaded through paint/server-frame/reflow/resize/min-cell/rendered-compositor; SidebarPainter strip + toggle-sidebar action; default-off byte-identical; enabled path verified via snapshot --rendered harness. Mouse click-to-focus + focus-window-by-index deferred (marked in-code).

title: Modal overlays float over live panes instead of full-screen takeover
description: Command palette, rename prompts (window/session), help, and pickers cleared the whole screen (\x1b[2J) and painted a blank full-viewport buffer, so the live panes vanished behind the modal. Make them true floating modals: repaint the panes as the base frame, then emit only the modal's bounded rect on top.
design: RenderOverlay::bounds(area)->Option<Rect> reports the painted region (None = full-screen). OverlayState::active_bounds unions the stack; paint_clipped emits only those cells via emit_buffer_clipped. Driver paint_active_overlay floats: paint_full_frame base then paint_clipped.

title: Predictive echo ghosts mid-screen after split
description: After creating a split, the first keystrokes into the newly focused pane render as a predictive-echo 'ghost' in the middle of the screen (the upper pane) instead of at the prompt. Root cause: the predict layer is pane-local internally, but the driver fed it outer-viewport-absolute cursor coordinates (renderer last_cursor) while bounding it with the pane's grid size. set_cursor's clamp (row.min(rows-1)) then dragged a lower pane's absolute cursor up into the wrong region, and the overlay painted at the absolute coordinate. Only correct when the focused pane sits at viewport origin (0,0).
design: Keep predict pane-local end-to-end; translate to outer only at the paint boundary. Renderer caches last_cursor_local (pre-origin) + last_origin; overlay::render takes a pane origin and shifts each CUP; snapshot/output-reconcile feed pane-local cursor; reanchor predict to the focused pane on every focus change (click, keybinding nav, split).
close_reason: Fixed in #93 (merge 3cdaf83): predictive echo anchored pane-local; overlay shifts by pane origin.

title: pixel geometry + XTWINOPS replies: kitten icat preflight fails inside phux
description: kitten icat refused to run inside phux: TIOCGWINSZ reported 0x0 pixels (server hardcoded PtySize pixel fields to zero, discarding the client's ViewportInfo pixel_w/pixel_h) and the CSI 14t fallback was mute (no libghostty on_size/on_pty_write effect handlers, so ALL terminal-generated replies — XTWINOPS, DECRQM, CSI 21t — were dropped). Fix: resolve per-cell px from most recent usable subscriber report, plumb through ResizeRequest to term.resize + PTY winsize, install on_size + on_pty_write (weak sender to avoid shutdown deadlock).

title: State-sync tick path may serve stale rows after resize (same class as GET_SCREEN flake)
description: Root cause found while fixing the route_input_no_resize CI flake: the SnapshotSynthesizer's POOLED render_state can serve stale row bodies after a TERMINAL_RESIZE interleaves with fresh-RenderState snapshot walks (attach / resize-resync). GET_SCREEN was fixed by switching to a fresh RenderState per call (low-frequency agent path). The TICK path (prepare_tick / synthesize_incremental / mark_synced) still reads through the shared pooled render_state and may have the same post-resize staleness exposure for OutputMode::StateSync consumers. No repro today (the TUI is Raw mode; tick gate skips raw-only panes). Before any real StateSync consumer ships (browser client, satellites), either prove the pooled path is resize-safe or rebuild the pooled objects on dims change. Evidence trail: /tmp phux-repro dumps from 2026-06-10, fresh-RS resync saw has_z=true while shared-RS walks read 0 chars for 5s.

title: flaky test: route_input_no_resize fails under 2-core CI contention (tight 1s echo poll + transient dims read)
description: route_input_delivers_keys_without_resizing_the_pane intermittently FAILS on the 2-core GitHub CI runner under full-parallel nextest (passed on the 3ns5 CI run, failed on the ahk.2 run -- same code path, different run = timing flake, NOT a regression; the dims assert at L244 fails after a fast 1.2s). Cause: poll_for_echo has only a 40x25ms=1s budget; under saturation the routed key's PTY echo doesn't arrive in 1s, so it returns the last (transient) snapshot and the dims assert fires on it. FIX: poll until BOTH the echo is present AND dims==(120,40), with a generous deadline (poll-until-condition per the emdv flake-fix pattern). Local: passes consistently.
close_reason: Fixed in a001ea9: poll_for_echo now polls until BOTH echo present AND dims==(120,40) (dims optional), with a 5s budget (was 1s). Test-only; passes 9/9 locally. Addresses the 2-core CI timing flake (echo lag -> transient snapshot -> dims assert).

comments.author: phall1
comments.text: Root cause finally pinned (2026-06-10): NOT echo timing. The Terminal received the echoed bytes fine; GET_SCREEN's shared pooled RenderState served stale (empty) row bodies forever after the TERMINAL_RESIZE raced the debounced resize-resync's fresh-RenderState walk. A fresh-RS resync snapshot saw the 'z' (has_z=true) microseconds before a shared-RS GET_SCREEN walk read 0 chars. Fixed by giving screen_state_with_scrollback a fresh RenderState+iterators per call (phux-uow0 pattern). Follow-up for the tick path: phux-5pyx.

title: Agent-native composited-view introspection: snapshot --rendered (structured cells of the assembled multi-pane frame)
description: phux exposes server grid state per-pane (snapshot --cells, side-effect-free GET_SCREEN) but has NO surface that emits the CLIENT's COMPOSITED view -- the assembled multi-pane frame (layout tiling + dividers + status bar) as the human's glass actually shows it. This gap is why client-composition/render bugs (e.g. phux-3ns5 mirror-resize: server grid was correct 120x39 while the client painted a stranded ~22-row survivor) are invisible to server snapshots and force an EXTERNAL emulator (pyte) to verify the human-facing render. Proposal: a control-plane surface (e.g. phux snapshot --rendered TARGET) that drives the client's existing headless render path (RenderSink -> Vec<u8>, the attach render path already sink-injectable, phux-549) and returns the composited view as STRUCTURED CELLS (grapheme/style/cursor per cell of the assembled frame) -- NOT VT bytes (bytes would need re-parsing by an emulator, reintroducing the symmetric-blindspot/round-trip problem). Net: an agent (or a test, or an assistant debugging) can ask 'what does the assembled screen look like right now' and get cells back, with no external emulator -- closing the loop and making phux self-verifying. Squarely on the 'best terminal for agents' arc (see bd memory agent-terminal-design-signal-...). Open Qs: where composition happens for a headless query (server has grids+layout-in-metadata but layout/tiling is client-side today; either render client-side headless on demand, or teach the server to composite from grids+layout); per-pane focus/cursor semantics in the composited cell stream; relation to the structured GET_GRID idea in the design-signal memory.
notes: SCOPED (session 2026-06-10): Composite CLIENT-SIDE (server has no ratatui/layout/dividers/bar; porting violates ADR-0020). Phase1 phux-core/src/screen.rs: add RenderedFrame{schema_version,cols,rows,cursor:Option<CursorState>,cells:Vec<RenderedCell>} dense row-major, RenderedCell{grapheme:String,style:CellStyle}; reuse CellStyle/CellColor/CursorState. Phase2 (core work) phux-client render.rs: factor render_at_inner cell walk (render.rs:387-447) so a new render_at_cells writes grapheme+style into a caller dense grid (no VT, no re-parse) reading the SAME RowIterator/CellIterator+cursor_viewport/cursor_visible; mirror wide-cell SpacerTail from synthesizer.rs:454-478. compose_full_frame_cells mirrors paint_full_frame (paint.rs:137): compute_layout, fill panes, overlay divider cells (read from dividers.rs compose_buffer ratatui Buffer directly), overlay status bar cells (status_bar.rs:173 Buffer), composited cursor per end_of_frame_cursor policy. Phase3 driver.rs run_headless_rendered alongside run_with_stdout(:450): handshake+snapshot ingest then ONE compose, return RenderedFrame. Phase4 CLI --rendered on Command::Snapshot (commands/mod.rs:190), mutually exclusive with --cells. RISKS: R2 attaches (NOT side-effect-free like GET_SCREEN) - needs --cols/--rows since no TTY; R3 settle timing (wait for all pane mirrors + layout metadata before compose, not a sleep); R4 ratatui Style->CellStyle inverse of to_ratatui_style(status_bar.rs:110), Color lossy for named/indexed. THIS DOUBLES AS THE RENDER-VERIFY HARNESS for x2hm + 4h5a (assert frame.cells[r*cols+c].grapheme/style + cursor).
close_reason: Merged as PR #115: snapshot --rendered composited multi-pane view as dense cells; doubles as the render-verify harness

title: Latency follow-ups after the input-scheduling trio (predictive echo, dedicated input lane, state-diff mode, cheap copies)
description:
The interactive-latency trio landed (commit 284fcbd): fair input scheduling (input arm before output, bounded both ways), 48KB coalesce cap + mid-burst yield, FrameAck gated on negotiated OutputMode. Verified by input_interleaves_with_a_large_pty_output_burst (red->green). This bead tracks the REMAINING ranked items from the verified latency-architecture map (workflow wbdtdk7ch), so they aren't lost:

DEEP (high effort, high value):
- PREDICTIVE ECHO ON AT THE PROMPT (#7): near-free shell-typing win — it's a flag (schema.rs ~407 default + attach.rs). Makes cooked/shell typing competitive with mosh over local UDS. Does ~nothing for full-screen app mode (Claude Code/nvim) — set expectations. Field-prove then flip default-true.
- DEDICATED INPUT LANE / MULTI-THREAD (#8): the single new_current_thread LocalSet (runtime/mod.rs ~226) is the ROOT of input/output contention. libghostty Terminal is !Send (ADR-0003/0014) so it can't move, but input route+encode could get its own runtime/thread so it preempts output broadcast. Big change; addresses contention at the root rather than per-select!.
- STATE-DIFF / FRAMERATE-CAPPED OUTPUT MODE (#9, mosh-style): forwarding raw VT (ADR-0013) re-parses+re-renders every wasteful app repaint byte-for-byte on the client. An RTT-paced server-side delta would bound the re-parse/re-render RATE under runaway output. The dormant StateSync/SnapshotSynthesizer machinery is the seed.

CHEAP HYGIENE (low felt impact, do opportunistically):
- Kill COPY #1: PTY reader buf[..n].to_vec() (spawn.rs ~232) -> reuse a BytesMut, split_to(n).freeze().
- Collapse the per-consumer pump -> Outbound mpsc -> separate writer_task hop (attach.rs ~910 + client.rs ~1078) for the single-consumer case + make write_frame take (header, Bytes body) and write_all_vectored to drop COPY #3 (encode flatten, encode.rs ~140). NOTE: the earlier 'terminal_id String clone' was a MISDIAGNOSIS — TerminalId::Local{id:u32} is an 8-byte copy; don't intern it.
- Memoize set_options_from_terminal (input/key.rs ~76) when grid modes unchanged + send Bytes not to_vec on the input encode (mod.rs ~1057).

FLOOR — do NOT chase: client mirror parse + render_at (load-bearing for ADR-0013 client-owned grid); the single IPC round trip for authoritative echo (can't predict away in app mode — mosh can't either); TLV scratch allocs (negligible). The felt win for the Claude-Code-in-phux case was the trio (anti-starvation); the rest is shell-mode polish + throughput hygiene.
notes: Split 2026-07-10 into four concrete children per the ranked list; this bead stays open as tracker until children close. FLOOR items documented as do-not-chase.
close_reason: Latency-follow-ups tracker complete: 51n6.1 (predictive-echo alt-screen gate) merged, 51n6.2 (dedicated input lane, ADR-0044) merged, 51n6.3 (state-diff output mode convergence proof, ADR-0043) merged, 51n6.4 (copy hygiene) closed as investigated-no-safe-win, 51n6.5 (predict-test drives real dispatch) merged. Residual edges tracked as 51n6.7. FLOOR items intentionally not chased per the latency map.

title: Authenticated, encrypted transport for remote consumers (no SSH tunnel)
description: phux is reachable today only locally (UDS) or via SSH-tunneled stdio. A remote, non-SSH consumer (e.g. a native/GUI consumer per the ADR-0017 consumer model, or any program over a network) needs an authenticated, encrypted path that is not an SSH tunnel. The WebSocket transport exists (crates/phux-server/src/transport.rs: TCP + RFC 6455, PHUX_WS_ADDR) but is plaintext and unauthenticated. Scope: a self-contained, transport-agnostic auth/pairing protocol (phux issues and verifies its own device token; pair via a code/QR from the desktop) plus encryption for the remote path. Needs an ADR.
design: No homegrown crypto: lean on TLS (rustls) and/or an overlay's encryption; do not invent a handshake. The wire codec is already transport-agnostic, so auth/encryption is a transport-layer concern. SEQUENCING: wss+TLS+token is Phase 1, chosen on reachability merit — a consumer is usually behind NAT/CGNAT, so assume the user runs an overlay (Tailscale/Headscale/WireGuard) or LAN; the overlay then provides reachability + encryption and the server just needs the token. Relaying TCP+TLS/:443 is the commodity no-overlay fallback (relay bead). Phase 2 QUIC (phux-84yt) only on the no-overlay path. Pair with OutputMode::StateSync (ADR-0018) for TCP HOL. GUARDRAIL (no lock-in): auth MUST be self-contained and overlay-agnostic — verify our own token, treat any overlay as a dumb encrypted pipe, never couple to overlay identity APIs; reachability stays swappable (overlay -> Headscale -> WireGuard -> LAN -> first-party relay).
acceptance_criteria: An ADR records the auth+encryption approach and trust boundary; the transport can require the token; a remote consumer attaches over a network with auth+encryption and no SSH tunnel; auth is self-contained (no overlay-API coupling); OutputMode guidance documented.

title: flaky test: eof_detach::pty_eof_drives_terminal_closed_to_attached_client fails under full-parallel nextest
description:
OBSERVED: phux-server::eof_detach pty_eof_drives_terminal_closed_to_attached_client intermittently FAILS during 'cargo nextest run --workspace' (full ~1380-test parallel run, observed twice this cycle) but PASSES reliably in isolation (5/5 across separate runs). Classic timing flake under CPU contention: the PTY EOF -> TERMINAL_CLOSED -> attached-client notification has a race/timeout that only loses when the machine is saturated by 200+ concurrent tests. On the 2-core CI runner this will intermittently red the suite.

LIKELY CAUSE: a fixed sleep/timeout or an ordering assumption between the PTY reader thread seeing EOF, the actor emitting TERMINAL_CLOSED, and the test draining the client mailbox. FIX DIRECTION: replace any fixed-duration wait with a poll-until-condition (bounded retry), or raise the timeout generously, or make the test await the specific frame rather than a deadline. Find the test in crates/phux-server/tests/ (eof_detach integration) and the EOF->close path in terminal_actor. SEVERITY: medium (CI flake, not a product bug) — but it will waste CI cycles and erode trust in green.
notes:
THIRD flake observed 2026-06-07: phux::bin/phux commands::run::tests::run_nonce_is_unique_across_invocations fails under full-parallel nextest, passes 3/3 isolated. NOTE: different mechanism from the PTY-timing flakes (eof_detach, route_input_no_resize) — this is a NONCE-COLLISION: run_nonce likely derives from a coarse clock (seconds/millis) or a non-atomic counter, so two invocations within the same tick collide when the suite runs them back-to-back. Real (if minor) robustness bug, not just a test-harness issue: the run nonce should use a monotonic atomic counter or higher-resolution+random source so production 'phux run' calls in tight succession can't collide either. Worth a small dedicated fix separate from the timing-flake test-grouping.
FIXED on branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity (unmerged). (1) EOF-watcher/attach TOCTOU race: gather subscribers + intern wire id + reap pane in ONE with_mut before the off-lock TERMINAL_CLOSED fanout, so no ATTACH can subscribe to an already-EOF'd pane (commit 21b5ce8). eof_detach green 3x + lifecycle suite 41/41. (2) run_nonce collision: added a process-global AtomicU64 to both phux + phux-mcp copies so two calls in one clock tick can't collide; the unique-across-invocations test is now deterministic (commit 0fb45f8).
close_reason: Verified fixed: EOF ReapAndNotify single-with_mut (runtime/client.rs) + run_nonce AtomicU64 (phux + phux-mcp) are in main; eof_detach uses poll-until-condition not fixed sleep. pty_eof_drives_terminal_closed_to_attached_client PASSED in full-parallel nextest (1400/1400) this run -- the exact flake condition the bead described.

title: audit: terminal_inputs per-pane log grows unbounded (write-only in production)
description:
CONFIRMED (audit phux-ahk, verified by skeptic + maintainer read). ServerState.terminal_inputs (HashMap<TerminalId, Vec<TerminalInput>>, crates/phux-server/src/state/registry.rs:31, appended in record_terminal_input ~765) accumulates every keystroke/mouse/focus/paste recorded against a pane and is only cleared on reap (forget_terminal_bookkeeping -> remove, ~708). For a long-lived pane it grows without bound.

Aggravating: in SHIPPED code the log has NO production reader. The only reader is the #[cfg(test)] terminal_input_log_for (~880). The state/mod.rs module doc claims 'the PTY writer task reads from this log (phux-byc.4)', but that path never landed — keystroke->PTY writes happen via a different path, so the log is effectively append-only/inspection-only in production.

DECISION NEEDED (why this is a bead not a blind fix): either (a) cap it (ring-buffer / VecDeque, keep last N, or TTL-evict) preserving the multi-client merge-point semantics the doc describes, or (b) if byc.4's PTY-writer consumer is dead, feature-gate or delete the log entirely. (a) bounds memory cheaply; (b) removes dead state. Pick one with the byc.4 owner. Tests push 3 entries so any cap >= a few thousand keeps them green.

SEVERITY: medium (slow leak, only for very long-lived high-input panes).
notes: FIXED on branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity (unmerged), commit 4a70200. Per audit reframe (it was never WRITTEN in prod, not just unread -> no leak), DELETED the dead scaffolding: terminal_inputs field, record_terminal_input, terminal_input_log_for, the forget_terminal_bookkeeping cleanup, and the test of the dead log. Corrected the false module doc. TerminalInput type kept (live mailbox event). Maintainer decision was delete, not bound.
close_reason: Done: terminal_inputs field/record_terminal_input/terminal_input_log_for all deleted from phux-server state; grep finds no production references.

title: audit: per-consumer snapshot+cursor/mode recomputed every tick (scales with consumer count)
description:
CONFIRMED (audit phux-ahk). The actor holds ONE shared SnapshotSynthesizer (terminal_actor/mod.rs:88 synth: RefCell<...>), but synthesize_against_reference is called once PER CONSUMER PER TICK (each consumer has its own ConsumerReference). Inside it, two terminal-only (consumer-independent) computations are redone N times for N consumers on a shared pane:
1. self.render_state.update(terminal) (synthesizer.rs:654) — re-snapshots the whole terminal per consumer.
2. ReferenceCursorMode::capture(&snapshot, terminal) (synthesizer.rs:718) — 5x terminal.mode() FFI calls + cursor queries (reference.rs:95-99), per consumer.
Both depend only on the shared terminal state within a tick, so with N consumers it is 5N mode-FFI calls and N full snapshots where 5 and 1 would do.

FIX SKETCH: hoist the per-tick terminal snapshot + cursor/mode capture to once per tick in tick_emit, compute the shared bits once, and pass them into each consumer's diff (synthesize_against_reference takes the precomputed snapshot/live_cm instead of recomputing). Care: RefCell borrow of synth, snapshot lifetime, and consumers attaching mid-tick. The auditor flagged only the mode FFI; the render_state.update redundancy is the bigger cost.

SEVERITY: medium (idle/steady-state CPU on multi-consumer panes; harmless for single-consumer).
notes:
RISK REFINEMENT (for the implementer): the hoist is semantically identical, not just an optimization — tick_emit runs synchronously on the actor thread and the Terminal is NOT mutated during the per-consumer loop, so every consumer already observes the same terminal state this tick. Capturing render_state.update(terminal) + ReferenceCursorMode::capture ONCE before the loop and reusing across consumers cannot change output. Shape: split synthesize_against_reference(&mut self, terminal, reference) into (a) a once-per-tick snapshot+cursor/mode capture borrowing self.render_state mut, then (b) a per-consumer diff_against_reference(&self, &snapshot, &live_cm, &mut reference). Watch the borrow split (update is &mut self.render_state once; the diffs are & + &mut per-reference) and keep reset_geometry driven off the shared snapshot dims. Existing multi-consumer tick tests (tick_emit_serves_every_consumer_on_a_shared_pane, tick_emit_mixed_mode_*) guard rendering parity. Low correctness risk, moderate mechanical effort; deserves its own focused PR.
AUDIT REFRAME + partial fix on branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity. KEY FINDING: the per-consumer tick/SnapshotSynthesizer path is DORMANT in production — the shipping client never negotiates OutputMode::StateSync, so tick_emit early-returns (no consumer wants state sync) and synthesize_against_reference's per-consumer recompute never runs for a human attach. So ahk.2's 5N-mode-FFI/N-snapshot cost is NOT the felt lag. The CONCRETE attach cost it/ahk.4 pointed at — register_consumer priming a full per-consumer reference + cursor/mode capture on EVERY attach — IS real and is FIXED (commit c345b49): both gated behind tick_managed, so a Raw attach is O(1) instead of O(rows*cols). The StateSync-path hoist (compute render_state.update + ReferenceCursorMode::capture once/tick) remains valid future work for WHEN StateSync ships, but is not worth doing against dead code now.
close_reason: Fixed in e5f52fc: split synthesize_against_reference into prepare_tick (render grid ONCE per tick into shared tick_* buffers + 1 cursor/mode capture + precomputed epilogue/screen-toggle) and diff_consumer (per-consumer compare+emit). tick_emit renders once for N consumers instead of N times (and 1 mode-FFI batch vs 5N). Wrapper preserves the single-consumer API. Verified: 27/27 state-sync tick tests + full workspace nextest 1400 pass.

title: agent-tool MCP gap: expose phux_watch (events) + phux_kill
