title: copy-mode: engine-driven word/line/all/semantic-output select on client
description: Wire copy-mode's word/line/all and semantic-prompt select-output to the client's own libghostty engine via select_word/select_line/select_all/select_output (SelectLineOptions::with_semantic_prompt_boundary), on slot.terminal. Client-local per ADR-0030. Builds on the client-local copy bead. Parent: phux-abi.
notes:
SCOPED (read-only investigation, 2026-06-11):

ARCHITECTURE / BOUNDARY: Selection is a client-local projection (ADR-0030). The overlay (render/overlay/copy_mode.rs) holds NO terminal ref — only pane-local row/col + SelectionMode, and emits a coordinate-only CopyRequest {start/end row/col, rectangle}. Engine resolution lives entirely in attach/copy.rs (copy_to_host_clipboard -> extract_selection_text -> Terminal::grid_ref + Selection::new + format_selection_alloc), invoked from the input_dispatch.rs copy-mode arm (OverlayOutcome::Copy at line ~184-194) against slot.terminal. render/ never imports libghostty_vt (CI boundary guard) — keep it that way.

NOT BLOCKED ON phux-97w. 97w's dangling-pointer bug is ONLY in the Formatter{selection:Some(_)} path (Formatter::new_inner). The one-shot format_selection_alloc + FormatOptions::with_selection path is SOUND at the current pin 6d49dfd and is already what copy.rs uses (confirmed in phux-server/src/search.rs lines 39-60). select_word/select_line/select_all/select_output ALL have safe Rust wrappers on Terminal at this pin (selection.rs:201-336): select_all(), select_line(SelectLineOptions::new(ref).with_semantic_prompt_boundary(true)), select_output(grid_ref), select_word(SelectWordOptions::new(ref)). Selection exposes start()/end()/is_rectangle(). All option types public under libghostty_vt::selection::*. EVERYTHING is doable NOW.

PLAN (phased, client-only, NO wire/protocol change):
P1 verbs that DON'T need cursor grid_ref: extend SelectionMode -> add a SelectionGrab enum carried on CopyRequest (or a new OverlayCommand::Copy variant param). 'A'=select-all maps to Terminal::select_all(); engine derives Selection directly, format via existing format_selection_alloc. Add key 'A' in copy_mode.rs handle_key.
P2 verbs that NEED the cursor grid_ref (resolved in copy.rs, not overlay): 'w'=word -> select_word(SelectWordOptions::new(grid_ref(Point::Viewport{cursor_col,cursor_row}))); 'V'=line -> select_line(SelectLineOptions::new(ref)); semantic 'V' variant -> .with_semantic_prompt_boundary(true). For these the overlay must pass its cursor (row,col) through CopyRequest so copy.rs can build grid_ref(Point::Viewport) and call the derive helper instead of building a linear Selection from two corners.
P3 select-semantic-output: ']' or similar -> select_output(grid_ref at cursor). Requires OSC-133 zones in the pane's mirror; degrade to None (no-op, best-effort) when absent — matches existing blank-span no-op contract.

KEY DESIGN CHOICE: add an enum (e.g. SelectionGrab { Rect, Word, Line, LineSemantic, All, Output }) to CopyRequest replacing/augmenting the bool . copy.rs::extract_selection_text matches on it: Rect/Char keep the two-corner Selection::new path; the rest call the derive helpers with a grid_ref at (cursor_row,cursor_col) and format the returned Selection. Overlay must carry cursor coords in CopyRequest (it already has cursor_row/col).

FILES TOUCHED (stays within render/overlay/ + input_dispatch copy-mode arm + attach/copy.rs — low swarm-conflict surface):
- crates/phux-client/src/render/overlay/copy_mode.rs (add key bindings w/V/A/], extend copy_request())
- crates/phux-client/src/render/overlay/mod.rs (extend CopyRequest with grab enum + cursor coords)
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/copy.rs (match grab enum -> derive helper vs two-corner Selection)
- crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs (optional: status strip text per grab mode)
- input_dispatch.rs copy-mode arm unchanged structurally (already routes OverlayOutcome::Copy)

TEST STRATEGY: unit tests in copy.rs (extract via select_word/line/all/output using fresh Terminal + vt_write fixtures, incl. OSC-133 \x1b]133;A/B/C\x07 fixtures for semantic line + select_output — see synthesizer.rs:1680 for the fixture pattern); key-binding tests in copy_mode.rs (w/V/A produce CopyRequest with correct grab). No protocol/wire tests needed (client-local). cargo nextest run -p phux-client; clippy -D warnings.
CORRECTION (shell ate one line above): the SelectionGrab enum AUGMENTS rather than replaces the existing rectangle bool — Rect path keeps using the two-corner Selection::new(start,end,true); the new grab variants (Word/Line/LineSemantic/All/Output) instead call the derive helpers with a grid_ref at the overlay cursor and format the RETURNED Selection. Net: copy.rs::extract_selection_text branches on grab; everything else unchanged.
close_reason: Merged as PR #119: engine-driven word/line/all/output copy-mode select via libghostty one-shot wrappers (client-local, ADR-0030)

title: 9q5f follow-up: styled (SGR) scrollback in ATTACH snapshot
description: phux-9q5f ships plain-text scrollback in TERMINAL_SNAPSHOT.scrollback_bytes (history rows as text + CSI S into client scrollback). The live viewport keeps full SGR; history does not. Reproduce per-cell SGR styling for history rows too (walk Point::History GridRefs emitting emit_cell-style SGR deltas, mirroring the viewport path) so scrolled-back content matches its original colors. Bounded; additive; no wire change.
notes: DEFER PLAN (assessed 2026-06-09): feasible but needs a small libghostty-rs fork addition. The history walk uses Terminal::grid_ref(Point::History) -> GridRef, which exposes style() (Style with unresolved StyleColor fg/bg) and cell() (Cell has bg_color_rgb/bg_color_palette but NO fg equivalent). The viewport path's resolved colors come from CellIteration::fg_color/bg_color (render.rs), which read RenderStateRowCellsData FFI -- NOT reachable from a history GridRef. So styled scrollback needs: (1) fork: add Cell::fg_color_rgb()/fg_color_palette() mirroring the existing bg_color_* in crates/libghostty-vt/src/screen.rs + the FFI binding; (2) phux: a styled scrollback_bytes walk that, per history cell, reads grid_ref.style() + resolves fg/bg (palette -> Terminal palette, rgb direct, default) and emits via phux_protocol::sgr::write_reset_and_sgr, mirroring emit_cell. Additive, no wire change. Plain-text scrollback already works; this only adds color to scrolled-back history (quality, not a release blocker).
close_reason: Implemented in e684f86: write_reset_and_sgr_unresolved (emits fg/bg from StyleColor directly -- palette stays 38;5;n, no fork/resolution needed) + scrollback_styled_bytes walks Point::History cells emitting SGR deltas. Shared attr/underline emitters prevent drift from the resolved encoder (regression test). No wire-format change. Verified: SGR unit tests + 9q5f scrollback round-trip + full nextest 1404 pass.

title: Client mirroring/letterbox: render a referenced Terminal letterboxed when view size differs
description:
ADR-0027 (decision points 1-2). When multiple views reference one Terminal and a view's slot is larger than the Terminal's authoritative (cols, rows), render the Terminal mirrored and LETTERBOXED in that view rather than reflowing the shared grid (a Terminal has one PTY winsize / one grid width). When the chosen size is larger than a view, the view clamps. Honest, documented behavior per ADR-0027, matching tmux.

DEPENDS ON: phux-xjgs (window-size config key) — the letterbox path needs the resolved policy to know WHICH size is authoritative before it can render the others letterboxed/clamped. Also relates to phux-nk07 (multi-client viewport ownership) for the server-side geometry pick.

v1 mirrors share scroll (per-view scroll is deferred in ADR-0027).

LANE NOTE: client letterbox/mirroring rendering code — kept out of the window-size config PR by design.

Source: ADR/0027-terminal-references-and-l3-links.md, decision points 1, 2, 3 (deferred scroll).
notes:
SCOPE ASSESSMENT (2026-06-07, after landing the nk07/xjgs server policy in PR #76). Two findings make this a dedicated, real-TUI-verified PR rather than a quick follow-up:

1. MIRRORING IS STRUCTURALLY UNBUILT. The headline premise ('multiple views reference one Terminal') has no consumer: crates/phux-client-core/src/multi_pane/layout.rs pane_rects() returns HashMap<TerminalId, Rect> — one slot per Terminal. The layout tree's leaves map uniquely to TerminalIds; the same Terminal cannot occupy two slots. Mirroring needs a layout-model change (allow a Terminal in N leaves) first.

2. THE REACHABLE SLICE (single-view letterbox when the policy-chosen grid < the client's slot, now possible post-nk07) requires UNWINDING the client-drives-geometry model. Today crates/phux-client/src/attach/paint.rs paint_focused_pane() calls safe_resize(slot.terminal, rect.w, rect.h) — it forces the LOCAL libghostty mirror to the slot size and renders at the rect origin, and the reflow pipeline (attach/reflow.rs) emits RESIZE to drive the PTY to that slot (rasterize.rs:64-67: 'the rect a pane is painted into always equals the rect pane_rects tells the server to size the PTY to'). To letterbox, the client must instead size its mirror to the SERVER's authoritative grid (the snapshot cols/rows the nk07 policy picked), compute a centered offset within the rect, render_at that offset, and clear the margins — i.e. defer to the server's geometry instead of owning it. That touches paint + reflow + the RESIZE-emission loop together and must be verified in a real multi-client TUI (two clients of different sizes on one session), which a headless test can't fully cover.

RECOMMEND: split into (a) single-view letterbox under the nk07 policy [reachable now, the valuable 80%], and (b) true mirroring [needs the layout-model multi-leaf change first]. (a) is the next bead to take; (b) waits on a layout-model bead. The server half it depended on (phux-xjgs/nk07) is shipped.
SCOPED (2026-06-11, render plan): Single-view letterbox is render-only, NO wire/protocol/driver-hub changes. The mirror is ALREADY server-authoritative (server_frame.rs:271-278 is the ONE resize site; paint_focused_pane/paint_full_frame already DO NOT resize the mirror to the rect — phux-wurs landed that). Today render_at_inner (render.rs:325-481) CLIPS via rows_total=min(mirror,clip), cols_total=min(mirror,clip) (render.rs:385-386) at origin (rect.x,rect.y). Letterbox = change clip->center: when mirror dims < rect, compute centered sub-rect (pad_x=(rect.w-mirror_cols)/2, pad_y=(rect.h-mirror_rows)/2), shift CUP origin by the pad, and paint blank-fill bars in the 4 margins; when mirror > rect keep today's clip (clamp). PLAN: (P1) add a pure helper letterbox_rect(rect, mirror_cols, mirror_rows)->(inner_origin, inner_clip, margins) — unit-testable, no I/O. (P2) thread an effective_origin/effective_clip + margin-fill into render_at_inner OR add render_at_letterboxed wrapper that emits margin bars then calls the existing core at the centered origin; keep render_at(min-clip) as the clamp path. (P3) call it from paint.rs paint_focused_pane (render.rs:80-86) and paint_full_frame non-focused loop (paint.rs:178-184) using slot.terminal.cols()/rows() vs rect.w/h. (P4) margin fill: emit ' ' runs (or theme bg) for the pad rows/cols, each a CUP+blank-run; reset SGR. FILES: render.rs (+ helper +letterbox path), paint.rs (call sites, pass mirror dims). STAYS WITHIN render.rs+paint.rs — does NOT touch driver hub, reflow.rs, server_frame.rs, or layout/rasterize. TESTS (headless, in render.rs #[cfg(test)]): mirror smaller than rect -> centered (CUP offset by pad), correct N margin rows/cols blanked; mirror == rect -> no padding (byte-identical to today); mirror larger than rect -> clamps (existing clip tests stay green); odd-diff centering (floor split, extra pad on bottom/right); cursor last_cursor includes pad offset. DEPENDS-ON note unchanged: true multi-leaf mirroring (same Terminal in N slots) still needs the layout-model change (client-core multi_pane/layout.rs pane_rects HashMap<TerminalId,Rect> is 1 slot/Terminal) — OUT OF SCOPE for this render-only cut; this delivers the reachable single-view letterbox under the nk07/xjgs policy.
close_reason: Merged as PR #120: single-view letterbox renders an undersized mirror centered with blank margins; mirror>=rect clamps as before. Multi-leaf mirroring (one Terminal in N slots) tracked separately (needs layout-model change).

title: L3 tag/link metadata schema (ADR-0027): normative wire spec for terminal tags + link edges
description:
ADR-0027 follow-up (foundation). Spec the normative L3 metadata schema for terminal tags and cross-terminal link edges, keyed on TerminalId, carried over the existing SET_METADATA / SUBSCRIBE_METADATA verbs (ADR-0015 L3). No new wire tag.

Scope:
- Freeform string tags on a TerminalId.
- 'link' edge as a metadata record with a spec'd shape: { target: TerminalId, kind } where kind is an OPEN enum (v1 defines 'group'; future kinds additive).
- Server stores opaque bytes; the *schema* is normative so tag/link meaning cannot drift between clients.

Deliverables per CONTRIBUTING.md for normative wire changes:
- Add/extend the relevant docs/spec/*.md (likely docs/spec/L3.md) with the tag + link record shapes and the key namespace.
- Add a docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md entry.
- Bump the spec version per CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Decide whether this warrants its own ADR (open enum + key namespace is a design-space close-off; likely yes).

This is the FOUNDATION: the #tag selector (separate bead) and L3 links build on it. No code change strictly required beyond the schema doc, but it must land before consumers interpret the bytes.

Source: ADR/0027-terminal-references-and-l3-links.md, decision points 4 and 5.
close_reason: Done via PR #75 (merged, CI green): L3 tag/link schema in docs/spec/L3.md §3.6 + TERMINAL_TAGS_KEY/TERMINAL_LINK_KEY + CHANGELOG 0.4.0-draft.1. No wire-format change.

title: stress_output_extremes::multi_mb_no_newline_burst fails on CI runner (server EOF on 2MB no-newline burst)
description: QUARANTINED from the e2e lane (justfile e2e -E filter). Fails 3/3 on the 2-core GitHub runner with UnexpectedEof 'early eof' at common/mod.rs:248 (server closed the connection mid-read) around 31s into the 2MB burst, OR builds.rs:212 attach failure. Passes 10/10 LOCALLY under the same serial config, so it is environment-specific to the constrained runner, not a deterministic logic bug. Hypotheses to investigate: (1) a 2MB single line with NO newline can't be chunked on newline boundaries -> a PANE_OUTPUT frame approaches/exceeds MAX_FRAME_LEN and the server errors+closes; (2) memory pressure on the runner processing a 2MB grid line in libghostty; (3) a write/flush timeout under slow CI I/O. The test asserts the server does-not-panic on the burst -- if the server genuinely dies on 2MB no-newline input that is a real robustness bug worth fixing (a user piping a huge no-newline blob would hit it). Repro on a constrained env (e.g. cgroup-limited 2 cpu / low mem, or the CI runner). Re-enable by dropping it from the e2e -E filter once fixed. Found while consolidating CI (PR #50).
notes:
FIX IN PROGRESS (PR pending). Confirmed harness-only (not a server robustness bug; frame-size hypothesis disproven). Root cause: the seed's fixed sleep 30 let the server self-exit and close the socket mid-drain on the 2-core runner -> UnexpectedEof panic in wait_until's recv_typed. Fix: (1) wait_until uses EOF-tolerant try_recv_typed (clean self-exit close -> graceful break, not panic); (2) multi_mb seed sleep 30 -> sleep 100000 (decouple from wall clock). De-quarantined from justfile e2e -E (now ZERO quarantined tests). Local: 18/18 + full e2e lane validating.
CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-07, after de-quarantine #65 failed on CI): the EOF/self-exit race was real and is FIXED (long-lived seed + EOF-tolerant wait_until, on main), but it was NOT the whole story. On the 2-core runner multi_mb still fails 3/3 at the marker assert (stress_output_extremes.rs:64), ~33s/try — a CLEAN assert-fail now (no more UnexpectedEof panic). Root cause #2: the 2MB no-newline drain through the single-thread runtime legitimately exceeds wait_until's 15s WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT on two cores, so NONLDONE never arrives in time. Re-quarantined in PR #67 to green main. REAL FIX NEEDED: give this test a longer per-test wait budget (e.g. a wait_until_with_timeout variant, or bump WIRE_RECV_TIMEOUT for the e2e lane) OR shrink the burst (2MB->smaller) while keeping the no-newline shape. The harness improvements (EOF-tolerance, long seed) stay on main and are correct. Lesson: validate constrained-env-specific tests against actual CI, not just locally (local is too fast to reproduce the drain timeout).

title: audit: dropped consumer_detach (full mailbox) leaks ConsumerReference + wastes tick work until pane dies
description:
CONFIRMED (low-probability, real). detach_and_release_consumer_state (crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs:633-658) sends ConsumerDetachRequest via try_send. On TrySendError::Full it DROPS the request (runtime.rs:644-649) with a comment claiming the entry is 'freed on actor teardown'. But for a long-lived pane (NOT being torn down), the per-consumer entry in TerminalActor.consumer_states is then never removed: unregister_consumer (terminal_actor.rs:1057-1061) only runs when a ConsumerDetachRequest is actually received.

Consequence: the orphaned ConsumerSyncState (which owns a ConsumerReference = Vec<Vec<u8>> of  row bodies, terminal_actor.rs:160 / grid.rs:670) lives until the whole pane actor dies. Worse, tick_emit (terminal_actor.rs:1734-1790) keeps iterating that dead consumer EVERY tick: synthesize_against_reference does a full grid render for it (compounding phux-4l0), then try_send hits TrySendError::Closed (terminal_actor.rs:1781) which only logs 'entry will be reaped on detach' and continues — it does NOT remove the entry. So the dead consumer is re-rendered 33x/sec forever.

TRIGGER: consumer_detach mailbox (DEFAULT_INPUT_MAILBOX=64) saturates while the actor is slow draining it (e.g. mid huge PTY burst) during a storm of attach/detach across many clients on one pane. Rare today (panes ~1:1 with sessions) but a real correctness/resource bug.

FIX SKETCH: (a) in tick_emit, on TrySendError::Closed actually mark the entry for removal (collect closed client_ids and remove after the loop), making the tick self-healing; and/or (b) make detach_and_release_consumer_state await a bounded send (or retry) rather than best-effort try_send. Option (a) is the robust fix — it reaps any orphaned entry regardless of why detach was missed. Parent: phux-ahk.
close_reason: tick_emit self-heals: a Closed outbound mailbox reaps the ConsumerReference entry. Dead consumers cost nothing (short-circuit skips them). Landed 38fe7a2.

title: audit: state-sync tick walks+renders every row each tick with no dirty short-circuit (idle CPU)
description:
CONFIRMED. SnapshotSynthesizer::synthesize_against_reference (crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs:531-615) renders EVERY viewport row into a fresh Vec<u8> (line 560: 'let mut body: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(...)') and byte-compares against the per-consumer reference, on EVERY call, with NO dirty short-circuit. tick_emit (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor.rs:1717-1791) calls it per attached consumer every DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL (30ms = 33Hz, terminal_actor.rs:337), and consumer_tick_emits defaults ON (terminal_actor.rs:946).

COST: an idle pane with N consumers still pays N*rows row renders + N*rows transient Vec allocations per tick (33 * N * rows allocs/sec) to discover 'nothing changed'. For a 50-row pane with 3 consumers that's ~5000 throwaway Vec allocs/sec while completely idle. The libghostty RenderState already computes Snapshot::dirty() (Clean/Partial/Full) cheaply; synthesize_against_reference ignores it entirely.

NOTE: dirty-isolation across consumers (the reason ConsumerReference exists, phux-ia4) means we cannot simply consult the shared dirty bits per-consumer (RenderState::update consumes them on first read). But a single per-tick 'is the shared terminal Clean since last tick?' probe BEFORE the per-consumer loop could skip the entire walk for all consumers when the terminal hasn't changed at all — the common idle case. Only when Dirty != Clean do we fall into the per-consumer row diff. That preserves correctness (a Clean terminal cannot have diverged from any consumer's last-emitted reference) while eliminating the idle walk.

REPRO/pin: crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs::audit_reference_diff_returns_empty_when_unchanged_but_still_walks (pins the empty-return correctness half). Parent: phux-ahk.
close_reason: tick_emit short-circuits the per-consumer row walk when terminal_dirty_since_tick is clean AND no consumer needs_initial_emit; freshly-attached consumers still get a first pass (preserves phux-ia4 guarantee). Landed 38fe7a2.

title: Edge-case + scroll + memory/efficiency hardening pass
description: Audit and add coverage: (1) scrollback/scrolling correctness under resize, wide glyphs, huge output, alt-screen toggles; (2) memory: scrollback mirror growth bounds, per-consumer reference grid footprint, predictive-echo buffers; (3) efficiency: hot-path allocations on the tick/emit path, diff cost. Add edge-case tests (resize storms, rapid attach/detach, multi-consumer). Identify and file concrete sub-issues for any real problems found rather than fixing blindly.
notes:
AUDIT PASS 2026-06-07 (multi-agent, adversarially verified): ran 3 parallel auditors (scroll/resize correctness, memory bounds, hot-path efficiency) + per-finding skeptic verification (default-to-refuted). 6 findings, all survived verification. FIXED + landed (PR #80, merged): (1) emit_instants RTT map unbounded growth for never-acking consumers -> MAX_EMIT_INSTANTS=256 oldest-evicted cap + regression test; (2) format!-alloc in scrollback SU synth -> write! inline. FILED as children for design-decision/lower-priority remediation: phux-ahk.1 (terminal_inputs per-pane log unbounded, write-only in prod), phux-ahk.2 (per-consumer snapshot+cursor/mode recomputed every tick, scales with consumer count), phux-ahk.3 (WS write_frame per-frame Vec), phux-ahk.4 (prime_reference per-row alloc at attach). Audit mandate (identify + file sub-issues) fulfilled; parent stays open until ahk.1-4 remediation lands.
AUDIT 2026-06-08 (adversarial, 17 findings all verified) — NEW high-value color-fidelity bugs found beyond the filed children, FIXED on branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity (commit 607dd22): (1) underline + overline were never emitted by the server snapshot synth OR the client pane renderer -> all neovim undercurls/cursorline + p10k underlines flattened; (2) the server's emit_sgr_delta gate keyed only on attribute flags (styles_equal ignored fg/bg), so adjacent same-attribute cells differing only in COLOR dropped the second color (multi-color ls / syntax highlighting reverted to the prior run's color on the synthesized snapshot); (3) emit_cell pushed the blank-cell space BEFORE reading style, dropping the background of colored-but-blank regions. All three surfaced only after attach/re-attach/resize (steady-state is raw byte-faithful PTV) — matching the maintainer's 'color glitch on attach'. Fixed via a shared phux-protocol::sgr encoder (single source of truth, prevents re-drift) + per-cell full-pen (Style+fg+bg) tracking + emit-before-blank reorder, with round-trip color tests. See branch for the lag work too (ahk.2/ahk.4 reframe, chunk coalescing, Bytes forward).

Subtasks resolved: ahk.1 (terminal_inputs deleted), ahk.2 (per-tick render hoisted, e5f52fc), ahk.3 (WS frame copy deferred -- needs tungstenite 0.26 Bytes migration; UDS path already zero-copy), ahk.4 (won't-fix: prime row allocs are irreducible + once-per-attach). title: Per-consumer dirty isolation: enable consumer_tick_emits for multi-consumer panes
description: Blocker surfaced in phux-3uv. RenderState::update CONSUMES the Terminal's shared dirty state (libghostty-rs render.rs:304-308). With N consumers sharing one pane, the first consumer's synthesize_incremental->update in a tick clears the dirty bits, starving every other consumer (Dirty::Clean -> empty emit). multi_client_scenario / byc_6_5 (multi-client same-pane attach) break if the flag is flipped. phux-3uv landed the other two prerequisites (client FRAME_ACK loop; per-tick-managed-consumer broadcast suppression via ConsumerAttachOutcome.tick_managed) and the single-consumer tick path is correct (unit test tick_emit_emits_once_when_gate_is_on). To flip consumer_tick_emits to true safely, the SnapshotSynthesizer needs per-consumer dirty isolation: either snapshot the dirty row set ONCE per tick before any consumer walks (and feed each consumer's diff from that snapshot), or diff each consumer against its own reference grid rather than the shared terminal dirty bits. ADR-0018 assumes this isolation; reconcile with the renderstate-as-cache memory which overstated what RenderState provides. See memory phux-3uv-renderstate-update-consumes-dirty.
close_reason: Per-consumer dirty isolation via per-consumer reference grid (option 2): each consumer diffs against its own last-synced rows, never the shared Terminal dirty bits that RenderState::update consumes. Reference advances on emit (emit-once). Landed 6196adf.

title: Flip consumer_tick_emits on: drive client FRAME_ACK + suppress broadcast per tick-managed consumer
description: phux-0q8 wired the per-consumer state-sync LIFECYCLE live (register on ATTACH, free on DETACH) but gated tick emission OFF behind consumer_tick_emits (default false). Enabling the actual lazy-state-sync emission (ADR-0018) requires two things first, or the consumer double-paints: (1) the phux-client must drive the FRAME_ACK loop (it sends none today), else the unacked delta is re-diffed forever; (2) the live broadcast pump (runtime.rs handle_attach) must be SUPPRESSED per tick-managed consumer so exactly one emitter serves each consumer (else two independent seq streams violate SPEC 12.2 monotonic-per-consumer). Then flip the flag and confirm via the existing tests/phux_0q8_no_double_emit.rs (which currently asserts exactly-once under the gated-off path) plus an acked-incremental path test.

title: Surviving pane does not reflow to full viewport after sibling pane closes
description: Repro: in an attached phux session, split a pane (e.g. horizontal split via prefix C-a), then quit/exit the shell in one of the two panes. The surviving pane stays at its small split size instead of growing to fill the freed space. Expected: when a pane closes and the layout collapses to a single pane, the survivor should be resized to the full viewport (its Terminal + PTY winsize grown) and repainted. Symptom suggests the client never sends a resize for the survivor's new larger dims after kill_pane collapses the tree, so the survivor's PTY/Terminal stays at the split dimensions. Related render path: crates/phux-client/src/attach/{driver.rs (TerminalClosed handling), layout.rs (kill_pane), multi_pane.rs (compute_layout), reflow.rs}. Reported live by user 2026-05-29. Verify via scripts/tui-probe.sh: split, exit one pane, assert survivor content fills full height/width.
close_reason: Fixed in e4d0d43. Root cause: on pane close (TERMINAL_CLOSED/EOF) the client folded the layout + resized its local mirror but never sent a TERMINAL_RESIZE for the survivor's grown dims, so the survivor's server PTY stayed at the split size and the shell kept rendering small. Fix: FrameOutcome.reflow_panes (set by TerminalClosed/TerminalSpawned arms) -> driver diffs folded layout vs pre-frame rects and emits per-leaf TERMINAL_RESIZE (same path as SIGWINCH). Verified: split 80x40 -> survivor stty size 19 80; after exit -> 39 80. Also fixes latent split-side sibling-shrink gap.

title: q0e per-consumer state-sync is implemented but not wired into runtime
description: The ADR-0018 lazy state-sync machinery in TerminalActor (consumer_states, register_consumer, tick_emit, synthesize_incremental, ConsumerSyncState, FRAME_ACK handling) is fully implemented but DEAD: runtime.rs constructs the consumer_attach channel with the receiver dropped (let (consumer_attach_tx, _consumer_attach_rx), ~runtime.rs:2512 and 2616), so register_consumer is never invoked and consumer_states is always empty. The live output path is instead the raw PTY-byte broadcast (output_tx) fanned out by per-attach output pumps in runtime.rs (~1548). Net effect: incremental state-sync is not active in production despite phux-q0e being closed; the FRAME_ACK loop is dormant; clients receive raw PTY bytes + full snapshots (attach, and post phux-8v1, live resize) only. Discovered while fixing phux-8v1. Decide: (a) wire register_consumer/tick_emit into handle_attach and switch the output path to the per-consumer tick, or (b) if the raw broadcast is the intended v0.1 path, mark the q0e tick code dead/experimental and update ADR-0018 status + the q0e close note to reflect that it is staged-but-not-active.
close_reason: Lifecycle wired live (register/detach per-consumer RenderState), tick emission gated off (consumer_tick_emits=false) to avoid double-emit vs the live broadcast pump since v0.1 client sends no FRAME_ACK. Regression-locked by tests/phux_0q8_no_double_emit.rs (exactly-once). Production switch deferred to the new follow-up. main cbc7c30, just ci green.

title: Repeating/duplicated characters on real-terminal resize (redraw artifact, post-resize repaint)
description:
REPORTED by phall1 (live, real terminal): resizing the actual host terminal phux runs in leaves repeating/duplicated characters on screen. Distinct from phux-y06 (the resize CRASH, now fixed) — this is a redraw/repaint artifact that was previously masked by the crash and is now visible since resize survives.

KNOWN: SIGWINCH path is crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs:~700-742 -> paint_full_frame (paint.rs). paint_full_frame writes ED2 (\x1b[2J\x1b[H) then re-renders each pane via render_at_full + dividers + bar. Reflow on resize (libghostty) may duplicate lines, or the host terminal's own reflow of pre-repaint content duplicates before phux paints, or scrollback/vt_replay double-emits.

NOT YET INVESTIGATED. Hypotheses to check: (1) host terminal reflows old content on resize before phux's ED2+repaint, and phux only clears the viewport not scrollback; (2) render_at_full emits content that overlaps an un-cleared region; (3) snapshot/scrollback replay on a resized pane double-writes.

VERIFICATION (NOT tmux — that's circular for a tmux replacement): build a direct PTY harness — allocate a pty (portable_pty), run 'phux attach' in it, write known content, TIOCSWINSZ to resize, read master output, assert no duplicated lines / single coherent frame. Or reason from the repaint code first.
notes: FOLLOW-UP 2026-05-29: the original close (commit 5d80ecb, immediate snapshot on every live resize) fixed discrete resize but introduced a DRAG regime bug — a window drag fires a SIGWINCH storm so the server flooded the client with full snapshots, and a stale-width snapshot corrupts the mirror (duplicated chars while dragging). Fixed in 706fc41 by debouncing the resync (RESIZE_RESYNC_DEBOUNCE=50ms) so a drag coalesces to one snapshot at the settled size. Guard: rapid_resizes_coalesce_into_one_resync_snapshot.
close_reason: Fixed in 831acbb. Root cause: resize reflows server + client mirrors independently; libghostty cols-shrink reflow loses client-mirror content and the live output path never re-sends the historical grid -> lost/duplicated rows. Fix: TerminalActor re-broadcasts a full snapshot (DECSTR+ED2+home reset preamble) on live resize via the output broadcast; ATTACH-time resize suppressed to avoid reordering the handshake. Verified with new raw-PTY harness (crates/phux/examples/pty_resize_probe.rs) + unit regression test resize_rebroadcasts_grid_snapshot_for_phux_8v1. just ci green.

title: [design decided: tmux model] Server lifecycle: pane-close -> remove empty session -> exit server when no sessions remain; add kill-session + phux ls
notes: FOLLOW-UP FIX (auto-spawn grace): a server now only self-exits after it has served >=1 client (ServerState::has_served_client, set on attach; checked in the exit watcher alongside !root_token.is_cancelled()). Without this, an auto-spawned server whose seed pane died before any client attached would self-exit mid-handshake -> user saw "no server". Also silences the spurious "self-exit" log on Ctrl-C shutdown. Tests: server_self_exit.rs now has both served-then-exit and never-served-stays-up cases.

title: Slim README.md to a router
description:
README.md is BOTH the router and the landing page (the repo page + future docs site index). Two jobs:

1. Draw people in tastefully — phux is pre-alpha but the thesis is real and the prose should land it. Tight hook, a 'why does this matter' beat, status honesty, then the door.
2. Route — once they're in, they need to know exactly which doc answers their next question (concept, spec, contributor, consumer).

Final shape:
- Hook (1 short paragraph + the Hashimoto pull-quote, or replace if there's a better one)
- 'What this is' — 3 bullets max, written like a product page, not a changelog
- 'Why it looks different from tmux' — kept short, links into docs/CONCEPTS.md for depth
- Status — pre-alpha honesty + what works today
- Quickstart — nix develop / just ci / one-line attach
- 'Where to go next' table — small, links into docs/{CONCEPTS, spec, architecture, consumers, vision} + ADR/
- Non-goals (terse) — links to CONTRIBUTING for full list
- License

Target <150 lines. No duplicate prose with CONCEPTS — link instead. Stability: stable; this is the most-read file in the repo and shouldn't churn every wave.

title: [epic] Full docs restructure: 3-layer + discipline
description:
Restructure the entire doc surface into Orientation / Reference / Decision layers + a Discipline layer (frontmatter, TL;DR, CI checks). Replaces the current 4 overlapping preambles (README/VISION/ARCH/DESIGN) with one canonical CONCEPTS doc; splits SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md per concept; normalizes ADR statuses; archives ratified research/. Final wave flips warn(missing_docs) -> deny across all crates and fills item-level intent docs.

Rationale: today the same fact lives in 4+ places and drifts independently. The structural fix is one-fact-one-home + machine-checkable freshness signals. See conversation 2026-05-27 with phall for the full spec.

Lands as one big PR on phux-swarm branch.
design:

Orientation: README.md (router), docs/CONCEPTS.md (canonical 'what is phux'), docs/QUICKSTART.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md+CLAUDE.md.
