title: server: PTY EOF (shell 'exit') doesn't notify client — client freezes in alt-screen
description:
User repro: typed 'exit' in the pane's shell. Shell exits. Client TUI froze; no path back to the outer shell except Ctrl-b d (detach) or kill.

Current behavior: pane_actor.rs:598 handles PtyEvent::Eof by detaching the PTY-read branch (self.pty_rx = None) and reaping the child, then keeping the actor alive 'for snapshot/input drain'. The server never broadcasts a state change. runtime.rs only emits FrameKind::Detached when the *client* requests detach (line 590).

Desired behavior options:
(a) On last-pane-EOF in the attached session, server sends FrameKind::Detached so the client unwinds its alt-screen guard cleanly.
(b) Server sends a new PaneClosed frame; client picks another pane to focus, or sends Detach if none remain.
(c) Server keeps the empty pane in place but allows the user to respawn via a re-seed command.

(a) is the minimum viable behavior — matches tmux/screen 'session closed' UX. (b) is the long-term shape once windows/panes have richer lifecycle ops; tracks SPEC §10. Pick one as the immediate fix and file (b) follow-on if (a) ships first.

Also: confirm the PaneActor's 'keep alive for snapshot/input drain' comment still makes sense once we notify clients on EOF — a closed pane shouldn't accept new input, and snapshots of a dead pane have unclear semantics.
close_reason: Fixed in commit ad93cd7 on fix/phux-it8-eof-detach: PaneActor now fires an internal exit_notify oneshot on PTY EOF; the runtime's per-pane EOF watcher broadcasts FrameKind::Detached to attached clients and detaches them. Test: crates/phux-server/tests/eof_detach.rs (pty_eof_drives_detached_frame_to_attached_client). Multi-pane (phux-9gw) deferred via TODO.

title: client/server: app inside pane doesn't receive expected keys (e.g. htop 'q' to quit)
description:
User repro: ran phux attach demo, ran htop inside, pressed 'q' to quit — no effect. Likely root cause: phux advertises TERM=ghostty to the inner shell (pane_actor.rs:271). Ghostty's terminfo declares kitty keyboard protocol support, so apps that detect this can flip into CSI-u mode where every keypress (including 'q') becomes a CSI-u escape like \x1b[113;1u. Apps that don't natively understand kitty protocol (htop, less, many old TUIs) won't recognize the quit key.

Investigation needed:
- Trace the exact bytes phux's per-pane key encoder writes when 'q' is pressed inside htop (instrument crates/phux-server/src/input/key.rs around the Event::encode call).
- Check whether htop's terminal-init turns on kitty modes (CSI > 1 u). If so, the encoder will produce CSI-u bytes; if not, plain ASCII.
- Decide policy: (a) advertise TERM=xterm-256color until ghostty's kitty support is mature in phux's path; (b) make ghostty terminfo correct for our path; (c) downgrade kitty protocol when the inner app hasn't requested it (which should already be the case — confirm).

Related: phux-19e (smarter client stdin parsing) is about the opposite direction. This ticket is about server-side encoding mismatching the inner app's expectations.
close_reason: 3120f40 — fix(server): default TERM=xterm-256color to unbreak htop quit

title: RenderState::update second-call diagnosis (deferred from 460faeb)
description:
Wave-2 agent's regression test (call render() twice in a row, assert Dirty::Clean on second) hit Error::InvalidValue from libghostty. Agent dropped the test rather than diagnose. Production paths (server SnapshotSynthesizer + client PaneRenderer) work fine — they each call snapshot.set_dirty(Dirty::Clean) between updates. The contract IS clear from libghostty source: Snapshot holds &mut RenderState; you can update again after Snapshot drops.

InvalidValue comes from .dirty().and_then(|v| v.try_into().map_err(|_| Error::InvalidValue)) — FFI returned a Dirty value outside {Clean, Partial, Full}. Likely the test was missing the set_dirty(Clean) reset between updates, OR libghostty returns an out-of-band Dirty value in a specific scenario the agent didn't characterize.

Tiny investigation: reconstruct the failing test scenario, find the actual cause, either fix the test or file a libghostty upstream issue if the FFI is returning an unmodeled value.
notes: Re-prioritized 2026-05-26 from P3 → P2: this becomes load-bearing for state-sync per ADR-0018 addendum. State-sync's tick driver calls snapshot.dirty() per consumer per tick on the same RenderState across many updates. The FFI InvalidValue case the deferred test hit (Dirty value outside {Clean, Partial, Full}) must be either characterized (so the synthesizer can guard against it) or fixed upstream before phux-q0e.A ships. See phux-q0e (epic) for the dependent work.
close_reason: Diagnosed via PR #5: Outcome B (upstream FFI bug in libghostty-vt rev 31d1f70 at Snapshot::set — passes *const *const T to C instead of *const T). Calling Snapshot::set_dirty(_) poisons the next update's dirty() read with InvalidValue, value-agnostic. Diagnostic test in crates/phux-server/tests/phux_l0t_dirty_diagnosis.rs pins the contract. Existing .unwrap_or(Dirty::Full) workarounds in client renderer and server synthesize_incremental implement strict over-emission, preserving ADR-0018 loss-tolerance. Dirty::Clean/Partial fast paths are dead code in any pipeline that calls mark_synced until upstream is fixed. Upstream issue to file as follow-up.

title: phux-server::downsample: handle image protocols + keyboard protocol gating + OSC 8 stripping
description:
Follow-up to ADR-0013 byte-stream rewriter landing. The v0 rewrite_bytes() in phux-server::downsample handles truecolor SGR -> indexed256/16 only. SPEC §6.2 requires additional gating per client caps:

- Image protocols: drop or transform sixel (DCS) / kitty graphics (APC G) / iTerm2 (OSC 1337) when the client did not advertise the matching ImageProtocol bit. The OSC/DCS/APC passthrough is permissive today; needs a capability-gated drop path.
- Kitty keyboard protocol: APC keyboard-reply sequences must be stripped from the outbound stream for clients that did not negotiate the matching kbd_protocols bit. The canonical Terminal still processes them locally.
- OSC 8 hyperlinks: strip when ClientCapabilities.hyperlinks == false.
- ITU-style colon separators: the rewriter currently only recognises ';'. tmux handles both 'CSI 38;2;R;G;B m' and 'CSI 38:2::R:G:B m'; add the colon variant for parity.

Scope: code only (crates/phux-server/src/downsample.rs + tests). No SPEC changes needed — §6.2 already mandates the behavior; this is implementation catch-up.
notes: Follow-up filed as phux-4rj (ClientCapabilities wiring).

title: phux-server: handle ATTACH frame and respond with ATTACHED + PANE_SNAPSHOT
description:
The server's per-client task in crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs::handle_client today only handles FrameKind::Ping. The match arm for FrameKind::Attach / FrameKind::Detach / FrameKind::Input* falls through to a debug log and the connection sits idle. byc.6 (the integration tests) is blocked on this handler existing.

Under ADR-0013 the response sequence to ATTACH is bytes-on-wire:

1. Resolve target -> SessionId via ServerState.
2. Allocate per-client mpsc + spawn writer task draining into the UnixStream.
3. Build SessionSnapshot from the registry; send FrameKind::Attached { snapshot, initial_client_id }.
4. For each pane in the focused window: call phux_server::grid::SnapshotSynthesizer::synthesize(&terminal) to produce { cols, rows, vt_replay_bytes }, then send FrameKind::PaneSnapshot { pane_id, cols, rows, vt_replay_bytes, scrollback_bytes: None } per SPEC §8.4 / §13.
5. Subsequent live output flows as FrameKind::PaneOutput { pane_id, seq, bytes } -- the per-pane PTY pump + downsample::rewrite_bytes path that byc.5 covers.

On FrameKind::Detach: send Detached and drop the writer.

On AttachError::UnknownSession: send an ERROR frame with code SESSION_NOT_FOUND (102 per SPEC §14). Requires the ERROR variant — see follow-up phux-byc.9.

Acceptance: byc.6 tests #1, #2, #5 must pass once this and the ERROR-variant ticket land.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,ipc,libghostty
design:
On receiving FrameKind::Attach { target, viewport, request_scrollback, scrollback_limit_lines }:
1. Resolve target → SessionId via ServerState (AttachTarget::ByName lookup is implemented; ById / Last / CreateIfMissing per SPEC §13).
2. Allocate a per-client mpsc channel and call ServerState::attach(client_id, name, tx).
3. Spawn a writer task draining the mpsc into the UnixStream's write half.
4. Build a SessionSnapshot from the registry and send FrameKind::Attached { snapshot, initial_client_id }.
5. For each pane in the session's active window, send FrameKind::PaneSnapshot per SPEC §13 attach sequence.

On FrameKind::Detach: send FrameKind::Detached, then drop the writer (which closes the socket on the server side).

On AttachError::UnknownSession: send an ERROR frame with code SESSION_NOT_FOUND (102 per SPEC §14). Requires the ERROR variant — see follow-up ticket.

Acceptance: byc.6 tests #1, #2, #5 must pass once this and the ERROR-variant ticket land.

title: Conform DiffOp to SPEC §8.1/§8.5: cursor + modes as PANE_DIFF fields, not ops
description:
SPEC §8.1 defines `PANE_DIFF` as carrying `cursor: CursorState`, `modes: PaneModes`, and `base_frame_id`/`revision` as **struct fields**, not as entries in the `ops` list. SPEC §8.5 is explicit on the rationale: "pulling them out into separate messages would increase wire chatter for no benefit." The current implementation models cursor as `DiffOp::CursorMove { row, col }` (op-byte 0x03) and `DiffOp::CursorStyle { visible, shape, blink }` (op-byte 0x04), and the `PaneDiff` frame body has no cursor / modes / base_frame_id / revision fields.

Why now: scope is small (one server example, one client mirror, a handful of tests). As more compute/apply/render code lands, the op-stream shape will calcify and the migration will be harder. Wire format is breaking — no external consumer yet — so do it before anyone latches.

Surgical edit list:
- crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/op.rs: delete `DiffOp::CursorMove` and `DiffOp::CursorStyle` variants
- crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/cursor.rs (new): re-home `CursorState`, `CursorShape`, add `PaneModes` bitset
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/diff.rs: delete op-byte 0x03/0x04 encode/decode + proptest strategy entries
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/frame.rs: `PaneDiff` gains `base_frame_id: u64`, `cursor: CursorState`, `modes: PaneModes`, `revision: u8`
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/decode.rs: decode the new fields
- crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/field.rs: add field-ID constants for new PaneDiff fields
- crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/compute.rs: stop emitting cursor ops; return cursor + modes alongside ops
- crates/phux-client/src/mirror/apply.rs: drop CursorMove/CursorStyle match arms; consume cursor+modes from PaneDiff
- crates/phux-client/src/mirror/state.rs: track modes (or pipe through)
- crates/phux-server/examples/diff_spike.rs and one_pane.rs: update to new compute_diff signature
- Tests: regenerate snapshots, append new cursor-field + modes round-trip tests, replace existing CursorMove/CursorStyle tests
close_reason: Landed in fd89d93dc712c4d46aee8f5066ffaa846f59e7d8. CursorState + PaneModes + base_frame_id + revision fields added to PaneDiff per SPEC §8.5; op-stream cursor ops deleted. New diff_spike md5: b84a5890eda2277734faad33b7411c74. Follow-up phux-bxa filed for MouseProtocol/MouseEncoding enums.

title: Wire ColorSupport through HELLO/ClientCapabilities per SPEC §6.1/§6.2

title: Add constructors + non_exhaustive to public structs in phux-protocol
description:
Follow-up to the enum non_exhaustive pass. Six public wire types (SessionInfo, WindowInfo, PaneInfo, SessionSnapshot, ViewportInfo, PaneSnapshotPayload) currently allow struct-literal construction from external crates. For a published crate, adding any field is a breaking change.

## Approach
1. Add a `new(...)` constructor or builder for each type taking the load-bearing fields, with sensible defaults for the rest.
2. Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to each struct.
3. Refactor crates/phux-protocol/tests/{frame_wire_snapshots,wire_roundtrip}.rs to use the constructors (currently 20+ struct-literal sites).
4. Verify cargo nextest + clippy stay green.

## Why
Pairs with the enum non_exhaustive landed alongside (AttachTarget, LayoutNode, SplitDir). Together they make additive evolution of phux-protocol non-breaking for third-party clients — which is the whole point of the published-crate stance per ADR-0008/0010.

## Cascade
Blocks: nothing currently. Should land before the first crates.io publish (phux-protocol 0.1.0).
close_reason: Already implemented on main in commit 3d7335b — six structs (SessionInfo/WindowInfo/TerminalInfo/SessionSnapshot/ViewportInfo) have non_exhaustive + new() + with_* setters; bd state was stale. Verified via grep + git log. Wave-2 fan-out agent C confirmed no-op.

title: Migrate wire encoder to TLV (SPEC Appendix A)
description:
Migrate the phux-protocol wire encoder from positional field encoding to TLV per SPEC.md Appendix A: {field_id: varint, wire_type: u8, value}.

## Why
The current encoder in crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/encode.rs writes fields positionally. This makes ANY extension to an existing frame body a wire-breaking change: e.g., adding a field to PaneSnapshotPayload, SessionInfo, or ATTACH requires a major-version bump because decoders cannot skip unknown trailing fields without TLV envelopes.

SPEC.md Appendix A mandates TLV precisely to make additive evolution backwards-compatible:
- Field IDs in crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/field.rs are ALREADY defined but unused by the encoder/decoder — they were laid down anticipating this migration.
- §6 obliges decoders to skip unknown fields by length, which TLV's self-delimiting structure makes mechanical.

## Cascade
This commit's spec-conformance pass for ATTACH/ATTACHED/PANE_SNAPSHOT/SessionInfo/WindowInfo/PaneInfo (followup to phux-4az) papers over the issue: it matches SPEC §13 shapes exactly but keeps the positional encoder. Any future field addition to those shapes is a breaking wire change today.

## Scope
- Replace primitive writes in Encoder/Decoder with field-tagged writes consuming field.rs constants.
- Define varint and tagged-union (wire_type=7) encoding per Appendix A.
- Maintain MAX_FRAME_LEN, big-endian, and existing decode-error semantics.
- Update all FrameKind variants to emit TLV bodies.
- Regenerate all wire snapshots.
- Add round-trip tests for unknown-field skipping (forward-compat invariant).

## Out of scope
- Schema versioning beyond what SPEC §6 already prescribes.
- Removing positional helpers used by sub-records (DiffOp encoding is unchanged unless we choose to TLV-ify it; that's a separate decision).
notes: REBASE ASSESSMENT 2026-05-29: wave5-tlv (commit ebb8770) is 21 commits BEHIND main, 1 ahead. The TLV commit is 2305 insertions / 67 files (encode.rs+decode.rs rewrite, ~40 .snap fixtures, wire_roundtrip.rs +738, spec). Since the branch point (merge-base 2460eeb), main added +310 lines to frame.rs (the 4li frame set: GetMetadata/ListMetadata/SpawnTerminal/TerminalResize/etc.) and +31 to decode.rs. So a git rebase is NOT viable as a fast-forward: it conflicts in frame.rs/decode.rs AND the ~15 newer frame variants would have no TLV encoding. Treat as a FRESH re-migration on current main using ebb8770 as the design reference, not a cherry-pick/rebase. Estimate: large (multi-hour), high snapshot churn. Defer behind the small additive wire items (4r1, ign).
close_reason: Closed

title: phux-client attach loop: connect, render mirror, propagate input
description:
The base attach loop that 9gw.1 (predictive echo) was implicitly waiting on. Connects to a phux-server over UDS, sends HELLO + ATTACH, accumulates diff frames into a DiffMirror (9gw.2), forwards local keypress/mouse/focus/paste events upstream, and renders the mirror to the outer terminal (crossterm or direct VT writes). This is what makes 'phux attach <session>' a working command.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,tui,vt-rendering
design:
Module: crates/phux-client/src/attach/
  connection.rs  — UDS connect, framed read/write halves
  loop.rs        — main attach loop (tokio select! over: server frames, stdin bytes from outer terminal, resize signals)
  render.rs      — VT emission from DiffMirror to stdout (crossterm or raw escapes; pick simplest first)
  input.rs       — read raw VT bytes from stdin, parse via libghostty's input layer, encode as INPUT_KEY/INPUT_MOUSE/etc, send upstream

Lifecycle:
  - parse args (server socket path, session name)
  - enter raw mode + alt screen on outer terminal
  - connect UDS, exchange HELLO, send ATTACH
  - on receive ATTACHED { snapshot }: ingest_snapshot into DiffMirror, full render
  - loop:
      tokio::select! {
        frame = framed_reader.next() => apply ops to mirror; redraw changed region
        stdin_bytes = stdin.read() => parse to InputEvent[]; send each upstream
        sigwinch = signal::unix::signal(SIGWINCH).recv() => send RESIZE to server
        ctrl+b d (or whatever the detach key is) => send DETACH; exit cleanly
      }
  - on exit: restore outer terminal (leave alt screen, disable raw mode)

Scope guard: does NOT implement predictive echo (that's 9gw.1, layers on top of this).

Depends on:
  - phux-9gw.2 (DiffMirror) ✓
  - phux-byc.3 (server runtime + UDS listener)
  - phux-byc.4 (ATTACH/DETACH lifecycle)
  - phux-6yl.* (wire codec, input event encoding)

Verify:
  cargo nextest run -p phux-client
  Manual: terminal A runs `phux serve`, terminal B runs `phux attach default`,
    typed keys appear in the inner shell and inner shell output renders.
acceptance_criteria: phux attach <session> connects, renders the active pane, propagates input, and detaches cleanly. cargo nextest run -p phux-client green. Manual test in two terminals works.
close_reason: Landed in b237eba. Code: 4-module attach module (connection.rs/driver.rs/input.rs/render.rs ~1400 LOC + tests) + phux attach <session> CLI subcommand. just ci green (workspace nextest 278 passing, +18 new tests in phux-client). Manual two-terminal smoke test deferred until phux-byc.8 (server ATTACH handler) lands — handle_client only handles PING today. Three follow-ups filed: phux-4hp (VIEWPORT_RESIZE wire frame + SIGWINCH wiring), phux-631 (configurable detach key), phux-19e (smarter VT input parser).

title: phux-client: diff mirror — accumulate incoming Grid diffs into local state
description:
phux-client needs a local Grid mirror that consumes incoming diff frames from the server (CellRun/Clear/CursorMove/CursorStyle per phux-6yl.5) and produces a current-state Grid the renderer reads. Prerequisite for both attach-loop rendering AND predictive echo (9gw.1).

## Required Skills
rust,vt-rendering,libghostty
design:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:407-440 §8 hot-path frame model
  SPEC.md:487-535 §8.3 Diff operations
  SPEC.md:536-567 §8.4 Snapshots
  ADR/0002-diff-based-protocol.md

Module: crates/phux-client/src/mirror/
  state.rs    — DiffMirror { grid: libghostty Grid, cursor: Cursor, frame_id: u64 }
  apply.rs    — fn apply(state: &mut DiffMirror, ops: &[DiffOp])
                  per-op: CellRun → write cells at (row, col),
                          Clear → blank N cells from (row, col),
                          CursorMove → update cursor,
                          CursorStyle → update cursor attrs.
  snapshot.rs — fn ingest_snapshot(state: &mut DiffMirror, snap: &Snapshot)
                  full-state reset (used on first ATTACH or recovery).

Replay invariant test (mirrors diff_spike from the server side):
  Given a starting Grid G0, a server-produced diff D such that G0.apply(D) = G1,
  the client's DiffMirror starting at G0 applies D and produces a Grid
  byte-identical to G1.

  Reuse the server's diff_spike example output as a fixture if practical.

Tests in crates/phux-client/src/mirror/tests.rs (or tests/mirror_replay.rs):
  - apply CellRun + read back exact bytes
  - apply Clear over a populated row, assert blanked
  - CursorMove updates cursor; CursorStyle propagates attrs
  - Random-walk proptest: arbitrary sequence of DiffOps applied to an
    empty Grid produces the same Grid as applying them via the server's
    capture+diff path (round-trip with the server-side replay invariant)
acceptance_criteria: DiffMirror::apply is invariant w.r.t. server-side replay (client mirror after applying diff bytes == server Grid that produced them). Proptest passes. cargo nextest run -p phux-client green.

title: Integration test: server + synthetic client message exchange
description:
End-to-end harness that spins up a phux-server process (or in-process runtime), drives it with a synthetic client over the wire codec, and asserts the full HELLO → ATTACH → INPUT → diff-stream → DETACH lifecycle. Captures the byc epic's overall acceptance criteria.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,integration-testing
design:
New: crates/phux-server/tests/end_to_end.rs

Harness approach (in-process, no subprocess fork):
  let socket = tempdir().path().join('phux.sock');
  let server = tokio::spawn(phux_server::runtime::run_with_shutdown(socket.clone(), shutdown_rx));
  // give it a moment to bind
  let client = UnixStream::connect(&socket).await?;
  let (mut reader, mut writer) = phux_protocol::codec::framed(client);

Scenarios to assert (one #[tokio::test] each, or one parameterized):

1. handshake_roundtrip:
   - Client sends HELLO with proto version
   - Server responds HELLO_ACK with negotiated capabilities (SPEC §6)
2. attach_returns_snapshot:
   - Client sends ATTACH(session='default')
   - Receives ATTACHED with SessionId + a pane snapshot frame
3. input_routes_to_pane:
   - After ATTACH, send INPUT_KEY('a')
   - Assert the pane's input log contains the encoded byte (stub from byc.4)
4. detach_clean_shutdown:
   - Send DETACH; receive DETACHED; the connection drains; no panics.
5. server_survives_mid_frame_disconnect:
   - Client writes a partial frame (half a length prefix) then drops the
     stream. Server must NOT panic; the per-client task exits cleanly.

Then shutdown_tx.send(()).await; server.await??; assert socket file unlinked.

Note: this test depends on byc.3 (runtime+socket) and byc.4 (ATTACH/DETACH).
Should be the LAST byc task to land.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 scenarios pass. cargo nextest run -p phux-server --test end_to_end green. No flakes under --test-threads=1.

Each under 0.2s. Full phux-server crate 779/779 green.

title: phux-server: ATTACH/DETACH lifecycle + multi-client keystroke merge
description:
Implement the ATTACH/DETACH message handlers and the multi-client merge semantics: multiple clients attached to the same session see the same pane, with their keystrokes interleaved in arrival order at the PTY.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,ipc
design:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:238-282 §7.1/7.2 Client/Server message catalog (ATTACH, ATTACHED)
  SPEC.md:283-308 §7.3 DETACH/DETACHED
  SPEC.md:955-1015 §10.1-10.2 Sessions/Panes

Builds on byc.3's per-client task and byc.1's Registry.

Server-side state:
  pub struct AttachedClient {
      id: ClientId,
      session: SessionId,
      tx: mpsc::Sender<ServerFrame>,  // server → client outbound frames
  }
  pub struct ServerState {
      registry: phux_core::Registry,
      attached: HashMap<ClientId, AttachedClient>,
      pane_subscribers: HashMap<PaneId, Vec<ClientId>>,
  }

ATTACH handler:
  - On ATTACH(session_name), look up SessionId (or create if not found and
    allowed by attach flags), register the AttachedClient in pane_subscribers
    for the active pane.
  - Send ATTACHED response with SessionId + initial pane snapshot.

DETACH handler:
  - Remove ClientId from pane_subscribers; close mpsc tx; respond DETACHED.

INPUT_KEY / INPUT_MOUSE / INPUT_FOCUS / INPUT_PASTE handlers:
  - For each input message from an attached client, route it to the
    server-side per-pane channel that ultimately writes to the PTY (PTY
    wiring lives in phux-bc1.2; for now route to a stub Pane::ingest_key
    method that just records the event).
  - Order: a SINGLE mpsc per pane consumes inputs from all attached
    clients. Whatever ordering the tokio scheduler delivers IS the
    arrival order — this is the multi-client merge contract.

Test (crates/phux-server/tests/multi_client_merge.rs):
  - Spin up server with one session/window/pane
  - Connect two synthetic UnixStream clients, both ATTACH same session
  - Each client sends a sequence of distinct INPUT_KEY events
  - Assert: the per-pane input log contains every key from both clients
    exactly once, in some interleaving (not strictly deterministic, but
    every key appears).
acceptance_criteria: ATTACH/DETACH round-trips. Two attached clients on the same session both see the same active pane. Per-pane input log records every keystroke from both clients exactly once. Integration test green.
close_reason: wave 6 swarm (byc.4 state scaffold + mdBook + crates.io). Wire integration deferred to phux-byc.6 pending phux-4az.

title: phux-server: tokio current-thread runtime + Unix socket listener
description:
Wire phux-server's main loop on a tokio current-thread runtime. Bind a Unix domain socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/phux/phux.sock (or fallback), accept client connections, hand each off to a per-client task that speaks the wire codec from phux-6yl.4.

## Required Skills
rust,tokio,unix-sockets
design:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:96-116 §4 Transport (UDS, framing assumptions)
  SPEC.md:117-149 §5 Framing (length-prefixed TLV from phux-6yl.4/5)

New: crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs
  pub struct ServerRuntime { registry: phux_core::Registry, socket_path: PathBuf, ... }
  pub fn run(socket_path: PathBuf) -> Result<(), ServerError>:
    - Build tokio Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build()
    - block_on(async move { serve_loop(...).await })

serve_loop:
  - Bind UnixListener::bind(socket_path)
  - Loop: accept().await → spawn client task
  - On SIGINT/SIGTERM (use tokio::signal): drain accept loop, drop listener,
    unlink socket file. Existing client tasks get a cancellation token.

Per-client task:
  - Frame reader: phux_protocol::codec::FrameReader<UnixStream read half>
  - Frame writer: phux_protocol::codec::FrameWriter<UnixStream write half>
  - For byc.3 specifically: just LOG every incoming frame and respond with
    PONG to PING. Full message routing comes in byc.4.

Socket path resolution: \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/phux/phux.sock if set,
else /tmp/phux-\$UID/phux.sock. Create the parent dir with 0700 perms.

Refuse to run if the socket file already exists AND a process holds it
(connect-probe). If stale, unlink and proceed.

Tests:
  - integration test in crates/phux-server/tests/socket_lifecycle.rs:
    spawn server in a temp dir, connect a tokio UnixStream, send a PING,
    read PONG, shut server down via the cancellation token, assert socket
    file is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Server binds UDS, accepts a connection, round-trips PING→PONG. Clean shutdown unlinks socket. Integration test in tests/socket_lifecycle.rs green.

title: Selection / copy-mode protocol + libghostty selection APIs
description:
tmux copy-mode is one of its defining features; we need a peer. libghostty PR #12794 (merged 2026-05-24) adds selection APIs to libghostty-vt's C surface: select_word, select_line, select_all, select_output, format_buf, selection_adjust, selection_order, selection_contains, selection_equal. Wire these through phux's protocol so clients can drive copy-mode against the canonical server-side selection state.

Defer until libghostty-rs wraps the new C APIs (track via libghostty-rs commits — they were already integrating at the time of phux's wave 1).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Wire format additions in SPEC.md: SELECTION_BEGIN, SELECTION_ADJUST, SELECTION_FORMAT_REQUEST, SELECTION_FORMAT_RESPONSE, SELECTION_CLEAR. Per-pane, per-client (each client has its own selection).
- [ ] phux-server bridges to libghostty_vt::selection::* (once libghostty-rs wraps them).
- [ ] phux-client renders selection as a visual overlay on the diff mirror.
- [ ] Copy-mode keybind (default `Ctrl-b [`) enters selection mode; arrows adjust; Enter copies to clipboard via libghostty_vt clipboard OSC.
- [ ] Rectangular selection (Mosh's `RECT` order from PR #12794) supported.
- [ ] Semantic-prompt-aware select-output (jump from prompt to prompt) works.
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; clippy -D warnings clean.

## Out of scope for this epic

- Search-in-buffer (different feature, file separately later).
- Vim-style motion commands inside copy-mode (post-v0.1 UX polish).
- Yank-buffer history (tmux's `paste-buffer` list).

## Watch / unblock signal

libghostty-rs adds a 'selection' module wrapping the PR #12794 C surface. Until then this epic stays deferred.
notes:
COPY-MODE DESIGN DECISION (ADR-0030 reconciliation, 2026-06-07)

DEPENDENCY BLOCKER RESOLVED. The epic's "watch/unblock signal" (libghostty-rs
wraps the PR #12794 selection C surface) is MET. The pinned fork
phall1/libghostty-rs@6d49dfd ALREADY exposes a safe Rust `selection` module:
Selection::new(start,end,rectangle), adjust(Adjustment), contains/equals/order/
to_ordered, and on Terminal: select_word/select_line/select_all/select_output/
select_word_between/set_selection, format_selection_buf/format_selection_alloc,
SelectLineOptions::with_semantic_prompt_boundary. No pin bump, no C-surface
wrapping needed. (Closes the libghostty side of phux-3sy/phux-97w too.)

CURRENT STATE ON MAIN (measured by code-read):
- Client overlay render/overlay/copy_mode.rs computes a visual CellRange
  selection (char/line/rect), and on arrow/Enter emits
  OverlayCommand::SendSelection(SelectionEvent).
- input_dispatch.rs:187 sends that as an INPUT_SELECTION wire frame to the
  server; the server stores per-client/per-Terminal selection state
  (state/registry.rs::set_selection).
- THERE IS NO COPY. "Enter to copy" is a no-op end-to-end: no
  SELECTION_FORMAT_REQUEST is sent, no extraction runs, nothing reaches a
  clipboard. The server's extract.rs (format_selection_alloc) exists but is
  wired only to scrollback search, not to copy-mode.

ARCH CONFLICT: the INPUT_SELECTION frame + SelectionEvent/SelectionMode wire
types + server-side selection storage are a PRE-ADR-0030 design. ADR-0030
(decision 1-2) makes selection a CLIENT-SIDE PROJECTION: both ends run
libghostty (ADR-0013), so the client selects on its OWN engine copy, extracts
locally, and copies to the LOCAL clipboard — NO wire state. The current
server-stored/shared selection is exactly the "structured view on the wire"
ADR-0030 rejects.

DECISION:
1. copy-mode is CLIENT-LOCAL. On commit (Enter), the client maps its overlay
   CellRange -> libghostty GridRefs on the focused pane's own slot.terminal
   (Point::Viewport grid coords; the overlay already moves in grid columns, so
   libghostty owns wide-cell semantics — no char-offset remap needed),
   builds a Selection (rectangle flag from mode), format_selection_buf -> text,
   and writes it to the clipboard via OSC 52 to the host terminal. Purely
   local; no wire.
2. word/line/all/semantic-output adjust run on the client engine via the
   now-available select_* APIs.
3. Removing the INPUT_SELECTION wire frame + SelectionEvent/SelectionMode wire
   types + server-side selection state is WIRE-BREAKING + architectural ->
   PROTOCOL_VERSION bump + docs/spec/CHANGELOG.md + STOP FOR REVIEW. Not done
   unilaterally.

SUPERSEDED BEADS (pre-ADR-0030, now anti-goals): phux-dh4 (server-side
selection state), phux-bli phase-1 (INPUT_SELECTION wire frame). Reconcile/close.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: client-local copy (Enter copies), wire-surface removal
(review-gated), engine-driven word/line/semantic select.
PROGRESS 2026-06-07 (ADR-0030 copy-mode client-local migration): phux-v6jw DONE (PR #82, merged) — copy-mode is now a client-side projection: Enter resolves the selection against the focused pane's own libghostty engine (format_selection_alloc) and copies via OSC 52 to the host clipboard; new attach::copy module + hand-rolled base64; copy actually works now (the old INPUT_SELECTION path sent a coordinate-free frame the server dropped). phux-q1ni DONE (PR #83, merged, wire-breaking, PROTOCOL_VERSION 0.5.0) — removed INPUT_SELECTION frame + Selection input-event + input/selection.rs + all server selection state; zero selection structure remains on the wire. REMAINING: phux-7143 (engine-driven word/line/all/semantic-prompt select on the client) — additive UX enhancement; needs the dispatcher to call select_word/line/all/output on slot.terminal and feed the resulting Selection endpoints back into the overlay's anchor/cursor (engine->overlay coordinate feedback). Rectangular selection already supported via the overlay's Rect mode + Selection::new rectangle flag. Success criteria largely met except the engine-driven select (7143) and copy-mode mode-cycling UI.
close_reason: Copy-mode/selection epic COMPLETE via PR #203 + ADR-0045: client-side copy-mode over the consumer's own libghostty engine (superseding the epic's original server-side-wire design per ADR-0030). Char/Line/Block selection modes (Tab-cycle), sound with_selection extraction (unblocked by the phall1/libghostty-rs fork fix), OSC-52 clipboard, no wire change. Follow-ups: phux-p9m5, phux-pzwd.

title: Predictive local echo (Mosh-class UX), client-side
description: Implement Mosh-style predictive local echo in phux-client: client maintains a prediction overlay against its diff mirror, dim-renders predicted cells, reconciles on server FRAME_ACK (SPEC §6). Transport-agnostic — Unix socket today, QUIC later. Mandated by ADR-0007.
design:
Module: crates/phux-client/src/predict/
  state.rs    — PredictionState { pending: VecDeque<Prediction>, mirror: Grid }
  overlay.rs  — render predictions over the diff mirror (dim attribute)
  reconcile.rs — on FRAME_ACK, walk pending predictions and drop confirmed ones; on mismatch, snap mirror to authoritative state

Algorithm (Mosh-style, on our cell diffs):
  1. User key event K arrives client-side.
  2. Send K upstream; locally apply guess(K) to a copy of the mirror.
  3. Render guess cells with PREDICTION attribute (dim).
  4. On FRAME_ACK from server (matched by frame_id), compare server cells
     in the affected range with our prediction.
       match → drop prediction, render normally
       mismatch → drop prediction, render authoritative
  5. On timeout (no ACK within N ms) → drop prediction.

PredictionPolicy enum: Always, Adaptive (RTT-based), Never. Configurable via TOML (phux-nz4).

Reference: Mosh SSP paper, section on prediction.
acceptance_criteria: Typing over a 200ms-RTT simulated link feels instant. Predictions render dim, reconcile within one FRAME_ACK. Snapshot test for the prediction overlay state machine. cargo nextest run -p phux-client passes; clippy -D warnings clean.
notes:
Spec refs:
  SPEC.md:150-161 — §6 FRAME_ACK (the reconciliation signal)
  ADR/0007-mosh-class-transport-and-satellites.md — load-bearing rationale

Verify:
  cargo nextest run -p phux-client predict::
  cargo clippy -p phux-client -- -D warnings
  Manual: `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms` then type rapidly

Predicts printable ASCII + EOL-backspace only; reconciles cumulatively on TERMINAL_OUTPUT. Underline decoration (SGR 4). Off by default behind PredictiveConfig::enabled; new run_with_predict entry point. ~970 LOC including tests; 26 new tests. Follow-ups: phux-9gw.1.1 (widen safe set), phux-9gw.1.2 (TOML config knob).

title: Wire codec scaffold: TLV framing per SPEC Appendix A
description: Big-endian, length-prefixed frames with custom TLV. Field IDs per Appendix A. Encoder writes into &mut Vec<u8> (or bytes::BytesMut); decoder takes &[u8] and returns Result<(Frame, &[u8] remaining), DecodeError>. Module: crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/.
design:
New module: crates/phux-protocol/src/wire/
  frame.rs       — Frame header (length-prefixed, big-endian per SPEC Appendix A)
  field.rs       — TLV field ID constants matching SPEC §7
  encode.rs      — Encoder writes into &mut bytes::BytesMut
  decode.rs      — Decoder takes &[u8], returns Result<(FrameKind, &[u8] tail), DecodeError>
  error.rs       — thiserror DecodeError enum
  mod.rs         — public surface

Add `bytes = "1"` to workspace dependencies. Use BytesMut for the encoder buffer.

Decoder must never panic on malformed input — every length read is bounds-checked. The proptest in acceptance criteria validates this.

This task scaffolds the codec. Per-frame variants (HELLO, INPUT_KEY, DIFF_FRAME, etc.) land in follow-ups — but the FrameKind enum should be declared (with at least HELLO + PING as proofs of concept) so the boundary is exercised end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: Proptest: encode→decode roundtrip for every Frame variant. Malformed input never panics (fuzz-style assertions).

title: Umbrella: `phux host` namespace consolidation + concept-pair help disambiguation
description:
Four near-duplicate concept pairs force users to learn distinctions the product should absorb (decision bead — needs a naming/IA design pass, likely an ADR since it closes a design space):

- phux enroll HOST vs phux satellite enroll HOST (mod.rs:1324-1355 vs 1841-1874): same positional, same five flags, differ only in --session vs --json.
- phux remote vs phux satellite (mod.rs:1431-1472 vs 1826-1922): both add/list/remove registries of other phux servers with --token-file/--cert-fingerprint.
- phux pair vs phux relay pair (mod.rs:1277 vs relay.rs:59): same verb, unrelated objects (device token vs route token).
- phux workspace vs phux worktree (mod.rs:1200 vs 1426): one letter apart, both git-checkout-shaped, workspace inspect vs worktree list overlap.

Also in scope: stdio-bridge is a machine-only verb in the human namespace (consider hiding); agent install-claude/uninstall-claude hard-code a vendor into a generic namespace (agent/mod.rs — also the only subcommand family with zero doc comments on its args; fix those regardless). Attach name-shadowing (remote registry shadows local session, attach.rs:524-529) must at minimum be documented in attach --help.

Constraint: renames are breaking; keep old names as hidden aliases for one release, per the deprecation pattern.
design:
---

DESIGN RESOLUTION (stream E, 2026-08-01) — decided, do not relitigate. (1) remote + satellite + top-level enroll consolidate under `phux host` (`host add|ls|list|rm|remove|enroll`) with a --role remote|satellite axis (default remote); the old three verbs become HIDDEN aliases for one release cycle printing a one-line stderr deprecation note; completions follow the visible tree only. (2) Config stays SPLIT: [[remote]] and [[satellites]] encode deliberately opposite trust directions (phux-config/src/remote.rs:7-12 — collapsing would let phux enroll edit federation topology); no [[hosts]] array, no migration. (3) pair / relay pair / workspace / worktree KEEP their names and get cross-referencing help text only. (4) Enroll asymmetry: --json valid on both roles (remote-role enroll gains JSON output — local, no wire change); --session rejected under --role satellite with a remedy-naming error. (5) Adjacent fixes: agent subcommand arg docs (agent/mod.rs:26-90), attach name-shadowing documented in attach --help (attach.rs:524-529), stdio-bridge hidden (mod.rs:1240-1245); install-claude/uninstall-claude keep their names. Recorded in ADR-0066 (renumbered from the planner's 0065 — stream D's grammar ADR owns 0065). Decomposed into E1-E6; umbrella.

title: eof_detach test is load-sensitive: 2s deadline fails under parallel load
description:
phux-server::eof_detach pty_eof_drives_terminal_closed_to_attached_client failed at 79.9s during a full-workspace nextest run on a machine also running seven agents and a 12-minute compile. Re-run in isolation on the same tree: PASS in 0.847s.

The test seeds a shell with 'sleep 0.2; exit 0' and asserts TERMINAL_CLOSED arrives within a 'generous two-second deadline'. Two seconds is generous on an idle laptop and not generous on a saturated one, and CI runners are frequently saturated.

Not a correctness bug and not a regression -- the contract it pins is right. But a wall-clock deadline in a test that gates every PR is a future flake. Options: raise the deadline substantially (it costs nothing when the path works), or drive it off an event rather than a timer. Same audit applies to the other two tests nextest reported as 'slow' in that run.

scripts/check-release-version.sh carries a hand-maintained packages=() array. It was already stale before the recording work -- missing phux-dial, phux-plugin, and phux-relay -- so the check silently verified less than it claimed.

Fix: derive the list from cargo metadata (jq over .packages[] filtered to workspace members) so a new crate is covered the moment it exists. Then audit the tree for other hand-maintained lists with the same failure mode: the justfile e2e filterset is an explicit binary_id list where a missing entry means tests never run in CI and rot green.
close_reason: Landed in PR #307 (check-release-version.sh now derives from cargo metadata; 13 crates).

title: rec: playback verb (phux play FILE.cast) - deferred from the recording epic
description:
Deferred out of the built-in recording epic (phux-e7ez) on purpose, not forgotten.

Recording ships write-only: phux rec / phux --rec produce asciicast v2 plus natively-rendered GIF/APNG. Playback is deliberately NOT shipped because 'asciinema play FILE.cast' already reads our output, and the smol manifesto argues against growing a second surface we then have to keep honest.

Revisit if either becomes true:
- users are round-tripping casts and want playback INSIDE a phux pane (a pane whose PTY is fed from a cast is a genuinely different thing from asciinema play in a shell, and is the real argument for building it);
- we ship cast v3 by default and want a reader that does not depend on the user's asciinema version.

Note when picking this up: docs/consumers/tui.md section 10 previously specified 'phux capture --record' and 'phux play' as accepted design. ADR-0060 supersedes that section and retires the 'capture' name; a future playback verb should be called 'play' and read the same cast the recorder writes.
close_reason: Landed in PR #312 as phux play (ADR-0064) - playback as a live pane, not a shell-level viewer.

title: per-consumer link sub-identities on federation link (ADR-0038 deferral)
description: All hub consumers collapse to one identity on the satellite: no per-consumer audit/authz, and link redial frees the satellite-side input lease while hub-side exclusion persists (documented flaw, spec draft.15). Prerequisite for multi-tenant/team (enterprise) deployments. Wire change: sub-identity tagging on relayed frames. Deserves its own ADR extending 0038. Large.

title: federate APPLY_INPUT: route acknowledged idempotent input to satellites
description: ADR-0053 built reconnect-safe input for unreliable remote consumers but scoped it local-only — APPLY_INPUT rejects SATELLITE TerminalIds, so the guarantee is missing exactly where transports fail. Extend over hub relay: operation-id cache on owning satellite, hub passes through verbatim like PUT_FILE (ADR-0059). Care: server_id incarnation semantics across the hop. Medium.

title: agent-detection manifests: gemini-cli (then cursor-agent, aider, goose)
description: Detection framework proven (ADR-0046, crates/phux-server/rules/*.toml, 5 manifests). gemini-cli ships a plugin integration (examples/plugins/agent-tools/integrations/gemini-cli.toml) but no rules manifest — users hit the inconsistency. Each agent = TOML manifest + identify fixtures/tests per verified-manifest pattern (47c039a, 9b2d8a2). Small, high leverage.

title: service.rs hardening: systemd %/$ escaping and HOME-unset launchd path
description: Two unverified low findings in crates/phux/src/commands/service.rs: (1) systemd unit does not escape % specifiers or $ expansion in ExecStart/Environment (lines ~831-845) — paths containing % or $ generate broken units; (2) with HOME unset, launchd unit files are written into the current directory (lines 66-77, 862-864). Verify and fix both.

title: phux enroll writes bearer token to disk before name/endpoint validation
description: run_enroll (crates/phux/src/commands/enroll.rs:224) calls write_token before NewRemote validation. Scenarios: --name '../../x' writes token outside <state>/remotes via unsanitized join before name rejection; quic endpoint without fingerprint fails AFTER token write, leaving orphaned 0600 bearer-token files. Fix: construct/validate NewRemote first (validate_token_file permits not-yet-existing file), then write_token, then add_or_update. Verified by research team.
notes: Fixed: NewRemote validated before write_token in run_enroll (both ssh-only and paired paths); finish() now takes the pre-built NewRemote so validation happens exactly once, before any disk write.

title: relay ensure_self_signed silently rotates cert when one of the pair is missing
description: crates/phux-relay/src/tls.rs ensure_self_signed guard is cert.exists() && key.exists(); with exactly one file missing it regenerates BOTH, silently rotating the pinned fingerprint and breaking every connector/consumer pin with opaque TLS failures. Fix: three-way match — both=ok, neither=generate, one=error naming the missing file and warning that deleting both rotates the fingerprint. Verified by research team.
notes: Fixed in BOTH sites (relay tls.rs and phux-server transport/tls.rs — same pattern existed server-side): three-way match, partial pair now errors with PartialTlsPair naming present/missing file instead of silently regenerating. Tests added in both modules.

title: CI runner disk pressure: test job died with 'No space left on device' before running tests
description: Run 29443995632 (PR #256, 2026-07-15): the test job's runner hit ENOSPC writing its own worker log after the cache-restore steps (nix store via cachix + Swatinem/rust-cache + the new sccache GHA restores), before the tests step started -- every step after rust-cache concluded null and the job failed at runner level. A rerun was issued (may pass on a fresh runner). Standard ubuntu-latest runners have ~14GB free; the restore stack now sits near that edge and will recur as caches grow. Mitigations, cheapest first: (1) add the free-disk preamble (rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc /usr/local/lib/android etc., frees ~25GB, costs ~30s); (2) prune rust-cache's cached target (its cache key already splits check/test profiles -- check sizes via the Actions cache UI); (3) cap what sccache stores. Evidence lives in the run's annotation (System.IO.IOException: No space left on device).
close_reason: Merged as PR #259: disk-headroom preamble (drops dotnet/Android/GHC, ~25GB back) in both compile jobs, with df lines for observability

title: [bug] overlay stub_tailscale_binary_round_trips test is flaky under parallel load
description: commands::overlay::tests::stub_tailscale_binary_round_trips (crates/phux/src/commands/overlay.rs, landed with phux-zndc / PR #237) failed once under full-parallel nextest load in two independent sessions on 2026-07-15, passing in isolation and on clean re-runs both times. It execs a stub tailscale binary, so it is likely sensitive to spawn latency or PATH/tempdir contention under load. Same class as the attach_last flake (phux-mn3b, fixed by polling an observable instead of assuming timing): find the timing assumption and replace it with a bounded poll or generous deadline. It will produce random red CI until fixed.
close_reason: Landed on main via integration train PR #255 (rebase-merge, commits 8a4097e4..b5f72d15)

title: CI never runs the examples/agents smoke test (just placed-fleet-smoke exists but no workflow calls it)
description: justfile:162 has a recipe smoke-testing examples/agents/ scripts against a throwaway server (bash examples/agents/tests/placed-fleet-smoke.sh), but no .github/workflows job invokes it, so the agent-facing example scripts can silently rot (this was flagged as a deferred gap when the agent-surface wave landed 2026-05-29). Add a CI job (or fold into the test job) that runs the smoke variant; keep the live variant out of CI if it needs a real TTY. Verify the smoke script is CI-safe (no interactive TTY assumptions) first.
close_reason: Landed on main via train #258 (commit 87382fa7): hermetic 3.6s agents smoke wired into the CI test lane with a timeout guard

title: phux fails with a raw 'path must be shorter than SUN_LEN' when PHUX_SOCKET is a long path
description: Setting PHUX_SOCKET to a deep path (e.g. a per-session scratch dir) fails with 'phux: attach failed: attach loop io error: path must be shorter than SUN_LEN' after a confusing 2s auto-spawn timeout ('auto-spawn skipped (auto-spawned server did not bind ... within 2s)'). The real cause -- the UNIX domain socket path limit, ~104 bytes on macOS -- is never named, and the suggested remedy ('Start a server manually with phux server') does not help since a manual server hits the same limit. Validate the socket path length up front and fail with a message that names the limit and the offending path length. Hit while scripting phux against an isolated socket.
close_reason: Landed on main via integration train PR #255 (rebase-merge, commits 8a4097e4..b5f72d15)

title: attach_last integration test is flaky under parallel CI load
description: crates/phux-server/tests/attach_last.rs::last_resolves_to_most_recently_focused_not_last_attached failed once during a full 'just ci' run (assertion 'focused session name' at attach_last.rs:79), then passed 10/10 when run in isolation. Uses its own TempDir socket, so it is not cross-test socket contention -- looks like a timing/ordering race in what the server reports as focused_session, only surfacing under parallel load. Not a product bug as far as observed, but it will produce red CI at random.
notes: Close-reason correction: PR #250 went green but was BLOCKED by the strict up-to-date ruleset after main moved (Pi commits cb99f188/127a8d22 landed mid-flight). The fix lands via the integration train branch train/wave-2026-07-15 (cherry-picked commit, rebase-merge). Same change, different vehicle.
close_reason: Merged as PR #250: replaced the ping-as-flush assumption (broken by ADR-0044's input lane) with a GET_STATE poll of the touched-session order

title: Worked example: orchestrate a fleet
description:
examples/agents/ has 01-ls-and-snapshot, 02-run-and-exit-codes, 03-send-keys-and-wait, 04-read-act-wait-loop, agent_loop.py. Add the one this epic makes possible: launch N agents into placed panes, watch them concurrently, surface the blocked ones, and jump to the first one that needs a human.

This is the executable proof that the epic worked, and it is the thing to run before closing the epic.
design: Follow the house style of the existing numbered scripts. Prefer the CLI (per ADR-0022 the CLI is the stable contract) but ALSO include the MCP-flavored equivalent so both surfaces are demonstrated at parity -- the parity bead should have made that possible, and if it is awkward to write, that is a signal parity is not actually done.
acceptance_criteria: The script runs green against a live server. It launches, places, watches, and jumps. It is referenced from examples/agents/README.md's loop table.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed. Remaining dependency beads track broader/general follow-up, not this delivered scope.

title: Config: focus-follows-agent (opt-in directed focus)
description:
The escape hatch for people who DO want the viewport to move on its own -- explicitly opt-in, default off, per ADR-0044.

Gated behind the ADR because an agent silently moving a human's view mid-keystroke is a genuinely bad default: you are typing in pane 3, an agent finishes in pane 7, your cursor is now somewhere else and your next keystroke went to the wrong process. That is a data-loss-shaped bug, not just an annoyance -- which is also why this should probably never apply while the target pane is not idle.
design: Config lives in phux-config (TOML + widgets). Read ADR-0044 for the exact gate semantics before implementing; if the spike found that an agent can ALREADY move a viewport by writing layout metadata, then this bead is not adding a capability -- it is adding the gate that should have been there, and the default-off path needs to actively ignore a remote focused_terminal change.
acceptance_criteria: focus-follows-agent = false by default. When true, an attention event moves the attached client's focus. Documented in docs/consumers/tui.md config section. Off-by-default behavior is tested, not just asserted.
close_reason: Superseded by ADR-0049 and phux-oih5.16: explicit advisory next/return navigation avoids automatic keystroke misdirection.

title: phux move-pane / swap-pane -- CLI verbs for reorganizing
description:
Rearrange an existing workspace: move a pane elsewhere in the tree, or swap two panes. The 'reorganize' half of the ask -- lower priority than focus and split, because those two plus placement-on-launch already cover the main agent-orchestration loop.

Consider whether these are one verb with a flag or two verbs; the TUI has no equivalent action today, so there is no existing naming to match -- pick something and put it in the docs.
design: layout_ops move()/swap() + SET_METADATA. Same registry-file conflict note as the sibling verb beads. If the tree operations get hairy (moving a leaf between subtrees requires collapsing the vacated split), keep the hard logic in layout_ops with unit tests over fixtures rather than in the verb handler.
acceptance_criteria: A pane can be moved and two panes can be swapped, with the attached client re-rendering correctly. Unit tests on the tree ops. e2e test. Docs.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Delete the dead phux_client::Agent facade (or fill it) -- it is all stubs and nothing imports it
description:
crates/phux-client/src/agent.rs, 359 lines, exported at lib.rs:46. Status:
  - connect_uds() and get_state() work.
  - run() returns Err('run not yet implemented; use phux_client::run directly')
  - subscribe_events(), send_signal(), attach_or_create() are stubs.
  - wait_for_prompt() is a half-stub (polls once, never checks shell_state).
  - EventType has a single __Placeholder variant.

NEITHER the CLI NOR the MCP adapter imports it. docs/consumers/sdk.md:53-55 already admits it is incomplete. It is a decoy: it is the thing a new contributor (or a swarm agent) will naturally reach for, and it will waste their time or -- worse -- they will 'helpfully' extend it and split the surface in two.

The real shared surface is the free functions in phux-client (selector, snapshot, send_keys, run, wait, watch, ask), which both consumers actually use.
design: Recommend DELETE, and make docs/consumers/sdk.md name the free-function modules as the surface. If you instead choose to fill it, that is a bigger commitment than it looks -- it becomes the thing every new verb in this epic must also land a method on, and nothing in the epic needs it. Deleting is the honest move; sdk.md already says as much.
acceptance_criteria: Either agent.rs is gone and sdk.md documents the free-function surface, or Agent is complete and both CLI and MCP are migrated onto it. Not the current halfway state.
close_reason: Removed dead Agent facade and documented the free-function SDK surface

title: The '=' (last-focused) selector is a lie -- aliased to '.', no MRU tracking exists anywhere
description:
crates/phux-client/src/selector.rs:221: 'Selector::Current | Selector::Last => snapshot.focused_session' -- one arm, both variants. Same aliasing at :175. The module doc admits it at :17 ('same as . here'), but docs/consumers/tui.md:249 advertises '=' as 'last (most recently focused)' to users.

There is NO last-focused / MRU tracking anywhere in the codebase, client or server. No previous-pane pointer, no MRU stack.

Either implement it or remove it from the grammar and the docs. Shipping a documented selector that silently means something else is worse than not having it. This epic makes it matter: 'jump back to where I was' is exactly the move a human wants after being pulled to an agent pane.
design: If implementing: MRU is per-client (focus is client-local, ADR-0019), so it belongs in the client's driver state next to focused_pane (attach/driver.rs:1516), and '=' resolution needs access to it. Note that selector resolution is currently a pure function of the server's GET_STATE snapshot (selector.rs), so a client-local MRU does not fit that signature cleanly -- that is the real design question. For headless CLI/MCP callers there is no meaningful 'last focused' at all, which argues for scoping '=' to the attached TUI and making it an explicit error elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Either '=' resolves to a genuinely different pane than '.' in the attached TUI (with a test), or it is gone from selector.rs, tui.md:249, and the grammar docs. No third option.
close_reason: Merged in reviewed green orchestration train PR #246; combined local just ci and GitHub check/test passed.

title: Copy-mode: add reverse-column-drag block EXTRACTION test in copy.rs
description: From #203 integration review: the block highlight side has a reverse-column test (contains_block_normalizes_inverted_column_corners), but the copy/EXTRACTION side (resolve_and_copy in copy.rs) has no test for a down-and-left block drag (CopyRequest arrives start_col>end_col). Correctness relies on the pinned fork's FFI per-axis column normalization (confirmed at 130d9e5). Add a copy.rs test extracting a reverse-column block to lock in the highlight/copy cross-boundary agreement the whole design rests on.
close_reason: Landed on main via integration train PR #255 (rebase-merge, commits 8a4097e4..b5f72d15)

title: Copy-mode: remove dead copy-mode-cycle-mode global action + plumbing (Tab is the real path)
description: From #203 integration review: the global copy-mode-cycle-mode action + OverlayState::cycle_copy_mode/cycle_selection_mode plumbing is unreachable — the input dispatcher resets+bypasses the resolver while an overlay captures keys (input_dispatch.rs:324-328), so a keybind resolving to it never fires against a live copy-mode overlay. The working cycle is the in-overlay Tab key. Its tests exercise the accessor directly, not real keybind reachability. Delete the dead action + plumbing, or document why retained.
close_reason: Landed on main via integration train PR #255 (rebase-merge, commits 8a4097e4..b5f72d15)

title: Relay roll_back Regated arm clobbers a Retained snapshot (residual L1 9.1 edge on triple-coincidence path)
description: From v45.15 review: roll_back_subscription's Regated arm unconditionally sets the gate to Open, clobbering a SnapshotGate::Retained(snapshot) a return-leg snapshot established between the sync re-gate and the async error reply. Path: B event-subscribed to term 9 upgrades to attach (AwaitingFirst); consumer C attached so a resync snapshot fans to B while B mailbox full -> B.gate=Retained; B's upgrade attach returns transient error -> roll_back forces Open, discarding retained snapshot -> next delta delivered with no snapshot (L1 9.1 violation). Self-heals on next resync; rare triple-coincidence. Fix: roll_back Regated should only reopen when gate is still AwaitingFirst, leave Retained intact. Also the ~1 RTT EVENT-frame suppression during the upgrade AwaitingFirst window (best-effort, bounded).
close_reason: Closed

title: Input lane: ROUTE_INPUT stays inline while INPUT_* routes via lane — mixed frames to one pane lose ordering; interleave test doesn't evidence preemption
description: From 51n6.2 review: (1) handle_route_input (ROUTE_INPUT) still try_sends to the pane mailbox inline on the main thread while INPUT_* frames route via the input lane, so a single client mixing INPUT_* and ROUTE_INPUT to one pane loses wire ordering (not covered by the ADR-0044 INPUT-vs-ACQUIRE/RELEASE timing shift). Route ROUTE_INPUT through the lane too, or document the ordering constraint. (2) lane_routed_input_interleaves_with_a_large_pty_output_burst mirrors the inline test and would pass with inline routing — it exercises the actor's biased-select fairness, not the lane's off-thread preemption; add a test that honestly evidences the root-fix property. Also: a full accept-loop + real-clients shutdown regression test (the class the input_lane drop-hang bug slipped through).
close_reason: Routed local ROUTE_INPUT through dedicated input lane with mixed FIFO, off-thread, lease, satellite, and live-client shutdown regression coverage

title: Wire base_seq on TERMINAL_OUTPUT to close the loss-tolerant residual bound (full Mosh SSP)
description: ADR-0042's loss-tolerant advance-on-ack model heals the dominant loss mode (a frame the relay never delivered) exactly, because the consumer stays at the last-acked state. The residual: a row that flips A->B->A across a DELIVERED-but-unacked frame within one RTT can be missed (the acked->live diff sees A->A). Closing it needs the wire to carry the delta's base seq and the client to apply a delta only when its mirror state matches that base (the Mosh fragment/datagram layer). This is a wire-versioned change (new TERMINAL_OUTPUT field + client base-match apply). See ADR-0042 Tradeoffs and Alternatives (Port Mosh's SSP wire).
notes: Scoping note 2026-07-15: this is a wire change in the same state-sync family as phux-kztd (loss-tolerance activation bit). If both proceed, do them in ONE spec bump/PR wave -- each alone requires docs/spec + CHANGELOG + version bump, and they land on adjacent frames (TERMINAL_OUTPUT here, ATTACH_TERMINAL/caps there). See phux-kztd's design field for the activation-topology decision that this residual-bound work builds on.

title: Relay: SubscribeEvents->Attach upgrade on same terminal leaves snapshot gate Open; Bell dropped for gated subscriber
description: From v45.14 review: (1) register_subscriber's idempotent branch ignores awaits_snapshot, so a same-client upgrade from SubscribeTerminalEvents (gate Open) to AttachTerminal keeps the gate Open and that attach's deltas aren't gated ahead of its snapshot. Pre-existing (event subs already receive fanned TerminalOutput). (2) Bell frames route through fan_out and are suppressed-then-dropped for an AwaitingFirst gated subscriber (only TerminalClosed was routed past the gate via fan_out_close) — acceptable but undocumented intentional drop.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #201 (dedicated input lane ADR-0044 + relay SnapshotGate upgrade edge). Residual follow-ups: phux-51n6.7, phux-v45.16.

title: Relay: second concurrent subscriber can see a delta before its own snapshot
description: From v45.12 review: register_subscriber inits pending_snapshot=None and fan_out delivers deltas unconditionally to a subscriber with no pending snapshot. When hub consumer B attaches to a satellite terminal already streaming to consumer A, B is added to subscribers immediately and the next inbound TERMINAL_OUTPUT (A's stream) reaches B before B's own return-leg snapshot (~1 RTT later) — the L1 9.1 violation v45.12's spec text claims to hold. Pre-existing v45.7, outside v45.12's briefly-full-mailbox scope. Fix: mark a newly-registered subscriber as awaiting-first-snapshot and suppress its deltas until that snapshot lands (reuse pending_snapshot machinery). Also: TerminalClosed/Bell suppressed-then-dropped when a pending-snapshot subscriber is reaped (best-effort close delivery); Seized event hardcodes Running lifecycle.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #198 (SnapshotGate: gate second-subscriber deltas until its own snapshot lands; best-effort TerminalClosed delivery)

title: Predictive-echo alt-screen gate test bypasses the real dispatch path
description: From 51n6.1 review: key_predicted_at_prompt_but_gated_in_app_mode re-implements the dispatch-site condition (predict.is_enabled() && !terminal_in_alt_screen()) inline rather than driving dispatch_input_events, so a refactor silently dropping the gate clause would not be caught. Make the test exercise the real dispatch path.

title: Takeover ACQUIRE_INPUT over a satellite bypasses hub lease ledger, does not notify evicted holder
description: From v45.7 review: Cooperative lease aliasing is handled correctly hub-side, but SEIZE/takeover-mode ACQUIRE_INPUT over a satellite overwrites satellite_leases without the ledger check and without notifying the evicted hub consumer — the prior holder keeps believing it holds the wheel while its relayed INPUT_* is silently dropped. Document or fix takeover semantics across federation.

title: Overlay modals size against full viewport, overlapping the sidebar strip
description: From foz.10 review: centered modals (palette etc.) are sized/positioned against the full viewport rather than the content rect inset by the sidebar — box edge lands inside the strip; a wider modal or narrower viewport could occlude the chrome the foz.10 fix preserves. Size/center overlays against the content rect.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #194 (CLI help reconcile + overlay modal content-rect sizing)

title: Attach stream: foreign-session pane topology + agent records for one-step cross-session fleet focus
description: From foz.7: the attach stream describes foreign sessions only as name + window count; agent records and asked flags are per-attached-pane subscriptions, so the fleet dashboard (and window picker) render foreign sessions as a switch-session hop instead of one-step pane focus. Only the CLI projection enumerates all terminals. Extending the attach stream (or a lazy per-overlay query) is a wire/projection decision — likely wants ADR review against ADR-0018/0030.

title: Copy hygiene: PTY reader BytesMut reuse, vectored write_frame, key-options memoization
description: From the latency map (51n6 CHEAP): (1) PTY reader buf[..n].to_vec() (spawn.rs ~232) -> BytesMut split_to(n).freeze(); (2) collapse per-consumer pump->Outbound mpsc->writer_task hop for single-consumer + write_frame(header, Bytes) with write_all_vectored (attach.rs ~910, client.rs ~1078, encode.rs ~140); (3) memoize set_options_from_terminal (input/key.rs ~76) when grid modes unchanged + send Bytes on input encode. NOTE: TerminalId clone was a misdiagnosis — do not intern. Do NOT chase the FLOOR items (client mirror parse, echo round-trip, TLV scratch).
close_reason: Investigated all three micro-optimizations; landed 0/3 — each fails the clean-win/no-regression bar: (1) PTY-reader uninit BytesMut read is unsound per Read contract and safe alternatives realloc (worse than to_vec for sub-4KB reads); (2) vectored write_frame is a cross-cutting wire-core change (QUIC/WT gain nothing, tokio lacks write_all_vectored) with real correctness risk; (3) encoders already return borrowed slices from reused buffers, Bytes would add allocation. Documented so this isn't re-attempted. FLOOR items correctly left alone.

title: Unify cwd validation/precedence between attach CreateIfMissing and create_named_session seed paths
description: Follow-ups from phux-3mtf review: (1) create_named_session (SESSION_CREATE_KEY path, runtime/commands.rs ~653) passes wire cwd through unvalidated, so a stale path can still fail a seed; (2) precedence diverges — attach path applies wire cwd on top of a cwd-less override command, create_named_session applies it only when no override exists; (3) is_dir() gate does not check enterability (mode-700 foreign dir passes validation then fails spawn, contradicting fallback docstring). Treat spawn-blocking cwd defects uniformly across both paths.

title: Upstream follow-up: Formatter::new with selection Some(_) still unsound at libghostty-rs 8e1b0f7
description: The one-shot Terminal::format_selection_alloc path is sound and is what phux uses (extract.rs, client attach/copy.rs). But the Formatter::new selection path remains unsound at pin 8e1b0f7: new_inner stores &s.inner where s is the Selection moved out of the by-value Option in the match arm, so the borrow dangles before opts.into() runs (documented in phux-server/src/search.rs module notes). Either fix upstream in libghostty-rs and bump the pin, or keep the standing rule that phux never uses Formatter with selection: Some(_). Parent epic: phux-abi.
notes: Upstream issue filed 2026-07-11: https://github.com/phall1/libghostty-rs/issues/8 (enabled issues on the fork to do so). Documents the Formatter::new_inner dangling-pointer unsoundness with mechanism + suggested fix. Confirmed still present at the current phux pin 81b776c6 (upstream head 0006e130 is only a build tweak, no Formatter fix — so bumping the pin does NOT resolve this). Bead stays deferred until the fork/upstream fixes it and phux repins; phux's format_selection_alloc workaround remains the standing rule.
close_reason: RESOLVED: user fixed the Formatter::new selection unsoundness in their fork (phall1/libghostty-rs@130d9e5) with a borrowed lifetime-tracked with_selection(&Selection) API; phux repinned to the fork via PR #202 (merge e86eeb6, full just ci green, 2239 tests). The dangling-pointer path is gone. Issue filed at phall1/libghostty-rs#8 for the upstream PR. The copy-mode swarm (ADR-0045) can now use with_selection and drop the format_selection_alloc-only workaround.

title: Timing flake: continuum autosave archive-override test fails under full parallel nextest load
description: phux-plugin::action_runtime checked_in_continuum_autosave_honors_archive_override failed once under full parallel load during wave-2 integration CI, passes in isolation and on rerun. Pre-existing timing sensitivity in the action-runtime archive override path; deflake (unique temp dirs / longer deadline / serial marker).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: phall
comments.text: Root cause: the test gave the action a 2s timeout while spawning a three-deep process chain (sh -c -> autosave.sh -> stub phux). Under parallel nextest load the chain is scheduler-starved past 2s; run_command_spec then reports TimedOut (empty output) and the assert_eq!(outcome, Completed) at action_runtime.rs:250 fails. No shared state: TempDirs are per-test, nextest is process-per-test, and no test writes the checked-in examples/plugins/continuum tree. Repro before fix: 5/20 loaded runs failed, failures at 2.08-2.11s wall. Fix: generous 60s HANG_GUARD const for both continuum completion tests (timeout semantics still covered by action_runtime_times_out_and_reports_cancellation). After fix: 0/20 loaded runs failed under harsher stress; observed action wall time up to 4.5s under load, confirming 2s was structurally too tight.

title: Pane Kill sends group-SIGKILL, gives foreground claude no chance to flush
description: Secondary/lower-priority companion to phux-0db. TerminalSignal::Kill sends a group-SIGKILL via killpg (phux-server/src/terminal_actor/mod.rs:1324-1344, :1340-1343). Killing a pane from the client while claude is the foreground process (instead of exiting claude first) gives claude no chance to flush its transcript. The clean shell-exit path (handle_pty_eof, mod.rs:1749-1756) reaps gracefully and sends no signal, so 'quit claude, then exit the shell' is fine. Consider a graceful SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL with a grace window for pane kills.
notes: Recovered during JSONL/Dolt reconciliation from pre-session .beads/issues.jsonl sha256=49d185e9801b56e9f7e12e6d7548b2143a84803ffb46d01072fa9fa85ec5ccce. Prior differing fields (verbatim JSON): {"close_reason":"Closed","closed_at":"2026-07-04T13:52:13Z","dependencies":[{"created_at":"2026-07-03T15:00:31Z","created_by":"jamesponwith","depends_on_id":"phux-0db","issue_id":"phux-sw1","metadata":"{}","type":"related"}],"dependent_count":0,"notes":"Implemented on branch claude-persistence. Root cause was more precise than the bead's pointer: the killpg-SIGKILL at deliver_signal (mod.rs:1324) is the DELIBERATE ADR-0033 TerminalSignal::Kill control (left as-is on purpose). The actual pane-CLOSE path (kill-pane action -> SPAWN_KILL / phux kill -> handle_kill_terminals -> detach_terminal_actor -> token cancel -> shutdown_pty) hard-killed via std Child::kill (SIGKILL of the shell pid, no grace). Fix: shutdown_pty now async; when the child is still alive it calls new terminate_child_group which SIGHUPs the process group (natural terminal-hangup; interactive shells act on it promptly, so idle-pane close stays snappy), polls try_wait up to PANE_KILL_GRACE (500ms), then SIGKILLs the group as backstop. Master stays open during grace so a foreground claude can still write its transcript flush. Added regression test pane_kill_lets_foreground_process_flush_before_death (traps SIGHUP, writes marker, asserts marker present) - verified it FAILS if the graceful signal is swapped to SIGKILL. fmt+clippy clean; full phux-server suite 596 passed.","started_at":"2026-07-03T20:25:00Z","updated_at":"2026-07-04T13:52:13Z"}

Bead predates the landing and was never closed.

title: WebTransport (HTTP/3 over QUIC) for the browser client
description: The browser-flavored QUIC upgrade (cf phux-84yt). Browsers cannot open raw QUIC/UDP sockets; WebTransport (over HTTP/3 = QUIC) is their only door to QUIC-class transport (multiplexed streams, no HOL blocking, connection migration, datagrams). Scope: when phux wants the QUIC experience in clients/phux-web, add a WebTransport path on the server (quinn + h3 + webtransport) sharing the same QUIC server as native QUIC. NOTE: phux-web only — a native consumer uses raw QUIC via quinn directly and does not need WebTransport. Still inherits QUIC UDP reachability constraints (relay bead). Lower priority; after native QUIC. Relates: phux-84yt, ADR-0025.
close_reason: Merged via PR #190 (WebTransport listener + phux-web fallback)

title: Relay/rendezvous so a phone can reach a NAT'd phux server
description: For reaching a NAT'd phux server when the user is NOT on an overlay/LAN. A server behind NAT/CGNAT cannot accept an inbound connection from a remote client. Solution: a relay with a public IP that both the server and the client dial OUTBOUND, which bridges them (Cloudflare Tunnel / Tailscale DERP / ngrok / VS Code tunnels style). Server side: phux dials OUT to a configured relay and accepts consumers routed back over the wss transport (phux-5vsr). Easiest over TCP+TLS/:443 (commodity L7 proxying) — a reason wss is Phase 1. This is the long-term own-the-whole-stack reachability option, independent of any overlay vendor. ADR alternatives: STUN/ICE hole-punching (fails on symmetric NAT -> TURN), or requiring an overlay.
notes: P3/later: not needed when the user runs an overlay (Tailscale/Headscale/WireGuard) or LAN — the overlay handles NAT traversal + encryption and the server only needs the pairing token. Build only for no-overlay users, after the auth protocol (phux-5vsr), if there is demand. Also the long-term escape from depending on any overlay vendor.
close_reason: ADR-0037 explicitly defers NAT relay/rendezvous to a WireGuard-class overlay network (Tailscale/Headscale) below the wire, and to an enterprise platform — phux stays overlay-agnostic and dials routable IPs with zero new code. Out of scope for phux core by decision.

title: audit: WebSocket write_frame allocates a Vec per frame via to_vec()
description:
CONFIRMED (audit phux-ahk). WsWriter::write_frame (crates/phux-server/src/transport.rs:216) calls frame.to_vec() to own the borrowed frame slice for Message::Binary. Every TERMINAL_OUTPUT frame to a WebSocket client (phux-web) allocates+copies the full frame, per-consumer per-tick on the WS path. The UDS path (UdsWriter::write_frame ~91) writes the borrowed slice directly with no copy.

FIX SKETCH: check whether tokio-tungstenite's Message::Binary can take Bytes/Arc<[u8]> to avoid the copy; if not, pool/reuse a frame buffer at the WsWriter level. Needs a small library-capability investigation (hence a bead). SEVERITY: low (only the WS transport; UDS unaffected).
notes: Still open. Confirmed by audit (WsWriter::write_frame copies the encoded frame per send). Investigated during branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity work: tokio-tungstenite/tungstenite pinned at 0.24 in Cargo.lock, whose Message::Binary takes Vec<u8>; the Bytes-payload API landed in tungstenite 0.26. The caller also hands write_frame a &[u8] borrowed from a reused encode buffer, so a copy is needed to own it for the async send regardless. UNBLOCK: bump tungstenite to >=0.26 then switch to Message::Binary(Bytes). WS path is the browser consumer, not the UDS/TUI path.
close_reason: Deferred (low value for v0.1, needs a wire-stack change to do right): the WS write_frame copy (frame.to_vec() into Message::Binary) is structural under the pinned tokio-tungstenite 0.24, whose Message::Binary owns a Vec<u8>. Avoiding it requires changing FrameWriter::write_frame from &[u8] to an owned Vec<u8>/Bytes so the WS path MOVES into Message::Binary -- a core Transport-trait signature change that only benefits the secondary browser/WS path (the primary UDS path is already zero-copy: write_all(&frame)). The clean version composes with a future tungstenite 0.26 bump (Bytes-based Message), which also lets the already-Bytes TerminalOutput payload flow through with no copy at all. Not worth the trait churn for the WS path pre-1.0.

title: audit: prime_reference allocates a fresh Vec per row at attach (reuse reset_geometry buffers)
description:
CONFIRMED (audit phux-ahk). SnapshotSynthesizer::prime_reference allocates a fresh Vec<u8> per viewport row at consumer registration (crates/phux-server/src/grid/synthesizer.rs:803) — 24 allocations for an 80x24 grid per attach. reset_geometry (grid/reference.rs:47) already pre-sizes rows_body to empty Vecs; prime could populate those in place by swap (same pattern as synthesize_against_reference ~707) instead of allocating fresh.

Not on the hot tick path (attach-time only), so low priority. FIX SKETCH: iterate the preallocated empty row bodies and fill in place via a single scratch buffer + swap. SEVERITY: low.
notes: SUPERSEDED by commit c345b49 (branch hardening/snapshot-sgr-fidelity). Rather than pool the per-row Vec allocs in prime_reference, register_consumer now SKIPS prime_reference entirely for raw (human) consumers — the reference it builds is never read on that path. So the per-row alloc cost is gone in the dominant mode without the pooling rework. The pooling optimization still applies if/when a tick-managed (StateSync) consumer attaches frequently, but is low priority.
close_reason: Won't-fix (premise doesn't hold): the per-row Vec<u8> bodies prime_reference allocates ARE the consumer's reference grid — N row bodies must be materialized once and retained, so N content allocations are irreducible. reset_geometry's rows_body = vec![Vec::new(); rows] are zero-capacity empties (no heap to reuse), and prime runs ONCE per consumer attach (not per tick). The per-TICK hot path already reuses capacity via mem::swap (synthesize_against_reference). 24 one-time allocs/attach is negligible and irreducible; no real win available.
