title: phux-ign Part 1: prove kitty-KIP round-trip for real TUIs, then maybe restore TERM=ghostty
description:
Follow-up to phux-ign (Part 2 landed in commit feat(server): per-Terminal TERM as a phux-config default).

GOAL: prove phux input/output round-trips the kitty keyboard protocol (KIP) for representative TUIs (htop, less, vim, neovim, fzf, btop), then EITHER restore TERM=ghostty as the default (revert 9734d42 swap, with a regression test) OR keep TERM=xterm-256color if a real gap persists.

WHY IT IS NOT DONE:
1. The representative TUIs are NOT nix-pinned. On this host htop/nvim/btop/fzf resolve to /opt/homebrew or /usr/bin (host-provided), and flake.nix declares none of them. The only spawn fixtures the test suite uses are /bin/sh and cat (POSIX-guaranteed). A test depending on host-installed TUIs is non-reproducible and would skip/flake in CI and other contributors sandboxes, so it cannot be the robust proof Part 1 requires.
2. The phux-7vx root cause is that TERM=ghostty terminfo advertises fullkbd, ncurses pushes CSI>Nu, libghostty pivots the per-pane encoder to CSI-u, and htop does NOT parse incoming CSI-u for the keys it owns -> q quit is dropped. That lack of CSI-u parsing is in htop, external to phux. Existing tests (crates/phux-server/tests/htop_keys.rs) already prove: (a) under xterm-256color plain q round-trips as 0x71; (b) the encoder DOES emit CSI-u once an app pushes kitty flags. Restoring TERM=ghostty would re-break htop unless a real KIP round-trip with these apps is demonstrated.

REMAINING MANUAL SMOKE (must be run on a machine that actually has the apps, or after pinning them in flake.nix):
- Build phux, set defaults.term="ghostty" (now a config knob, no code change needed thanks to Part 2).
- phux attach demo; run htop; press q -> must quit. Repeat for F-keys.
- Run nvim/vim: enter/exit insert mode, :q -> must work; arrow keys, function keys.
- Run btop: q to quit, function keys.
- Run less: q to quit, navigation keys.
- Run fzf: type-to-filter, Enter/Esc.
If ALL round-trip cleanly under TERM=ghostty, flip defaults.term default to "ghostty" in phux-config schema + default.toml and add a regression test (ideally after pinning at least one KIP-aware TUI in flake.nix so the test is reproducible). If htop (or any) still drops keys, keep xterm-256color; the per-spawn env override and the new defaults.term knob already let a user opt into ghostty deliberately.

title: audit: search Match.col is a char offset, not a grid column — diverges past wide glyphs
description:
CONFIRMED (latent). search::Match.col/len (crates/phux-server/src/search.rs:86-96) are char offsets into the right-trimmed projected row String, NOT grid columns. For any row containing a wide (CJK/emoji) glyph before the match, char offset != grid column (off by one column per preceding wide glyph). The module doc (search.rs:25-57) already flags that match coordinates are meant to be handed to a libghostty Selection (which is grid-COLUMN based) for extraction. So when the upstream extraction bridge unblocks (the dangling-pointer pin in Formatter::new_inner, search.rs safe_api_selection_formatter_bridge_is_broken_at_pin), naively passing Match.col as a grid column will mis-locate selections.

SEVERITY: low/latent — extraction is currently blocked upstream so nothing consumes these coords as grid columns yet, but the trap will bite whoever wires the bridge. Also affects any UI that highlights a match by grid column.

REPRO/pin: crates/phux-server/src/grid.rs::audit_line_char_offset_diverges_from_grid_column_past_wide_glyph (shows X at char offset 1 but grid column 2 after a wide glyph).

FIX SKETCH: either (a) report a second grid-column coordinate alongside the char offset, computed during find_in_row by walking the row's cells with display widths, or (b) document on Match.col that callers must remap char->grid-col via the row walk before building a Selection, and provide a helper. Parent: phux-ahk.
close_reason: Already resolved on main. Fix-sketch (b) is fully implemented: crates/phux-server/src/extract.rs provides char_col_to_grid_x() — the row cell-walk that inverts char-offset->grid-column, skipping SpacerTail and advancing by display width — and extract_match()/extract_match_in_scope() are the real in-tree consumers that remap before building a libghostty Selection. The search::Match docstring (search.rs) documents the char-offset-vs-grid-column trap at both type and field level and points callers at the helper. Tests prove it: extract::wide_glyph_before_match_shifts_grid_column and scrollback_match_with_wide_glyph_round_trips. Sketch (a) (redundant grid-col field on Match) was deliberately rejected and documented as such (dead weight to keep in sync; add only if a consumer needs the raw column without the walk). No grid-column-highlighting UI consumer exists yet; when one appears it uses the same helper.

title: Wire up libghostty Selection+Formatter extraction bridge once upstream pin fixes Formatter::new_inner
description: phux-3sy shipped find-in-scrollback but could not ship the extraction wrapper (Match coords -> libghostty Selection -> Formatter -> text/VT/HTML). Root cause: at libghostty-rs pin acc4b87, the safe crate's Formatter::new_inner takes &raw const of a match-arm-local copy of the Copy ffi::Selection, so the selection-restricted format path passes a dangling pointer and libghostty returns InvalidValue. The types are all public (screen::Selection, Terminal::grid_ref, fmt::Formatter) — only the upstream pointer bug blocks it. The test safe_api_selection_formatter_bridge_is_broken_at_pin in crates/phux-server/src/search.rs pins the gap and will fail when the pin moves. When it does: bump the libghostty-vt rev, implement extract(terminal, Match, Scope, Format) building a linear Selection from two grid_ref endpoints (note the char-offset vs grid-column mapping caveat for wide glyphs), and flip the pin test into a passing extraction round-trip.
close_reason: Bridge complete: pin 8e1b0f7 fixed the upstream Formatter::new_inner dangling-pointer bug via the sound one-shot format_selection_alloc API (pin test already flipped to safe_api_selection_formatter_bridge_round_trips_at_pin). This wave adds the remaining Format dimension: extract(terminal, Match, Scope, Format) -> Vec<u8> for text/VT/HTML in phux-server/src/extract.rs, String helpers delegate to it, stale blocked-upstream docs removed from search.rs. Note: Formatter::new with selection: Some(_) is STILL unsound at 8e1b0f7 (new_inner stores &s.inner of a moved local); phux uses only the one-shot API. Commit 90f9e10 on wave25/97w-selection-bridge.

title: Scrollback search primitive + safe wrappers for libghostty selection helpers
description: libghostty_vt (pin Uzaaft/libghostty-rs acc4b87) exposes cell/scrollback access (Point::History, total_rows, scrollback_rows), selection helpers (select_word/select_line/select_output OSC-133-aware, in libghostty-vt-sys C API, NOT yet wrapped in the safe Rust API), and a Formatter (fmt.rs) to extract selection text/VT/HTML. It exposes NO search/regex. Verdict from audit: selection+extraction = delegate (write thin safe wrappers over the FFI helpers); search = build a thin find-in-scrollback over the server's existing scrollback mirror (src/grid.rs), handing match coords to libghostty Selection+Formatter for extraction. Update the CONTRIBUTING no-list 'no copy-mode reinvention' item to say precisely: selection/copy delegates to host terminal + libghostty; phux owns only find-in-scrollback.
notes:
SEARCH (build) = DONE: find-in-scrollback primitive shipped in crates/phux-server/src/search.rs with full test coverage. CONTRIBUTING no-list updated. SELECTION/EXTRACTION (delegate) = PARTIAL/BLOCKED upstream: verified against pin acc4b87 — the safe Selection+Formatter types are public, but Formatter::new_inner passes a dangling pointer for the selection (Copy ffi::Selection addressed as a match-arm temporary), so selection-restricted formatting returns InvalidValue. Extraction wrapper deferred to phux-97w; gap pinned by a regression test. OSC-133 boundary helpers intentionally not wrapped (that is the engine we refuse to reimplement).
UNBLOCKED (per phux-7143 scoping): the one-shot libghostty select_* API (select_word/select_line/select_all/select_output, safe Terminal wrappers at libghostty selection.rs:201-247; sound per search.rs:39-60) works at the pinned rev 6d49dfd. Only Formatter{selection:Some(_)} (phux-97w) is buggy — search can use the one-shot path. Swarm-able as its own group (server/core search primitive).

title: Gate ROUTE_INPUT on a PRIMARY role policy (reject viewers with PERMISSION_DENIED)
description: phux-3j3 added Command::RouteInput (tag 0x08), a side-effect-free input route. SPEC input.md §7 documents it as primary-only, but the server (handle_route_input in runtime.rs) does not yet enforce a RolePolicy/PRIMARY gate — no role machinery is wired for control commands today. When role enforcement lands for input, ROUTE_INPUT must reject non-primary/viewer connections with PERMISSION_DENIED to match the spec.
design: DESIGN (wave-10 read-only pass, go=WAIT-FOR-TRANSPORT): No materialized role state today — roles are per-TERMINAL (not per-connection), defaulting to PRIMARY on ATTACH (L1.md §7.1). PRIMARY is implicit: a client in terminal_subscribers[tid] has an active subscription. Gate site: runtime.rs:2158 handle_route_input. PermissionDenied error code ALREADY EXISTS. Option 1 (interim, cheap): add client_id to handle_route_input, reject unattached/unsubscribed clients with PermissionDenied — no role map needed. Option 3: full terminal_roles: HashMap<TerminalId,HashMap<ClientId,TerminalRole>>. WHY WAIT: connection identity (ClientId, attached/client_layers/terminal_subscribers) is exactly what the phux-web Transport-trait extraction (phux-486.4) is reshaping; building role enforcement on it now risks a one-way-door rework. Revisit once 486.4 lands; the call-site signature should stay stable (internal lookup changes only).
close_reason: Interim PRIMARY-role gate for ROUTE_INPUT (Option 1): handle_route_input rejects unsubscribed/viewer with existing PermissionDenied; PRIMARY approximated by active subscription. client_id threaded so the full role-map swap is a no-caller-change later. Landed 88477b1.

Fix: ignore designated/changing rows or hash a normalized view; clamp/log sub-interval dwell; document effective resolution. Found by harden-wait-run workflow (HIGH/MED).

title: Split phux-client into core+render crates to enforce ratatui boundary natively
description:
Follow-up surfaced during phux-5ke implementation. Today the ratatui
boundary (ratatui imports allowed only under
`crates/phux-client/src/render/`) is enforced by a grep script
(`scripts/check-ratatui-boundary.sh`, wired into `just ci`). This is
load-bearing for ADR-0020.

The grep is intentionally a placeholder because no native Rust mechanism
restricts imports per-module within a single crate:
- `clippy::disallowed_types`/`disallowed_methods` apply crate-wide, not
  per-module. Banning all of ratatui crate-wide and unbanning per-module
  is not possible.
- Module visibility (`pub`/`pub(crate)`) restricts exports, not imports.
- There is no `#[restricted_to(path)]` attribute.
- Custom lint plugins require nightly.

The native solution is a **crate split**: extract everything under
`crates/phux-client/src/render/` into a new `phux-client-render` crate
that has `ratatui = { workspace = true }` in its Cargo.toml. The
remaining `phux-client-core` (attach loop, pane mirror, predict, layout
math) does NOT depend on ratatui. The boundary becomes
compiler-enforced for free; the grep script can be deleted.

## Why this is deferred today

Per the design discussion that motivated phux-5ke, we agreed:
"module isolation now, sub-crate when a second consumer shows up."
Currently only the TUI consumes `phux-client`. The crate split adds
ceremony with no immediate payoff. The trigger for revisiting this
bead is one of:

1. A second consumer materializes (headless test client, a recording
   tool, a GUI client, etc.). The crate split unblocks them.
2. Compile times in `phux-client` become painful and incremental
   compilation isolation matters.
3. The boundary script catches a real violation and we want stronger
   guarantees.

## Scope when this lands

- New crate `phux-client-render` (publishable? probably not for v1;
  match the other internal crates).
- Move `crates/phux-client/src/render/` → new crate root.
- Rewire `phux-client` to depend on `phux-client-render` (only callable
  through a small re-export surface).
- Delete `scripts/check-ratatui-boundary.sh` and remove the `just ci`
  hook.
- Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` to reflect the new crate graph.
- Update `ADR/0020-layered-render.md` to note the boundary is now
  compiler-enforced.

## Not in scope today

This bead exists as a marker. Do not implement until a trigger above
fires.
close_reason: Already done on main (phux-5ke / ADR-0020). The crate split landed: phux-client-core exists as the ratatui-free pane-interior substrate (layout math, multi-pane composition, predictive echo) with NO ratatui dependency (verified: no 'use ratatui' in src, no ratatui in Cargo.toml — the textual mentions are 'ratatui-free' comments/description). phux-client (chrome + attach loop) depends on phux-client-core and holds 'ratatui = { workspace = true }'; never the reverse. The boundary is now compiler-enforced: a stray 'use ratatui' in phux-client-core fails to build. The grep guard scripts/check-ratatui-boundary.sh is deleted and 'just ci' no longer invokes it (only retirement comments remain in justfile:144). All three goals met: native enforcement, grep retired, big mechanical diff landed.

title: ADR-0020: layered render (ratatui chrome over libghostty pane interiors)
description:
Write ADR-0014 documenting the layered-render decision. Captures the
design discussion from 2026-05-27 so future contributors don't re-litigate
"why not ratatui-ghostty for panes" or "why not rmux-style structured
snapshots".

## Required sections (per ADR template in ADR/)

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Client paints VT bytes directly to stdout today. Multi-pane
  composition and chrome (status bar, dividers) is hand-rolled cell
  positioning. Need to ship overlays (help, command palette, session
  picker) and richer status bar without rewriting cell-positioning every
  time. ADR-0013 fixed wire as bytes; this is a CLIENT INTERNAL decision
  about render layering.
- **Decision**: Hybrid layered render. ratatui owns chrome (status bar,
  dividers, overlays); libghostty owns pane interiors via VT bytes to
  stdout. Boundary: ratatui `Cell::skip` carve-outs over pane rects.
  Two renderers, disjoint regions, layered (not interleaved).
- **Consequences**:
  - + libghostty feature parity automatic on pane hot path.
  - + ratatui layout system + widget ecosystem for chrome velocity.
  - + ADR-0013 untouched (no wire change).
  - − Two renderers in one process; SGR + cursor handoff invariants
    required at the chrome/pane boundary.
  - − ratatui dep weight (~30k LOC + crossterm).
- **Rejected alternatives**:
  - **ratatui-ghostty (lossy widget) for pane interiors** — loses kitty
    graphics, sixel, OSC 8, modern keys. Fine for thumbnails only.
  - **rmux-style structured cell snapshots on the wire** — directly
    contradicts ADR-0013; would require re-modeling every libghostty
    feature in protocol types.
  - **All-ratatui with libghostty as a buffer source** — same loss as
    ratatui-ghostty; loses the dirty-row local rendering of
    `RenderState`.
  - **Status quo (all hand-rolled)** — overlay velocity is the
    motivating problem; status quo doesn't solve it.
- **Boundary invariants** (paste from epic):
  - ratatui imports live ONLY in `crates/phux-client/src/render/`.
    Enforced by `scripts/check-ratatui-boundary.sh` in `just ci`.
  - Chrome and pane regions are disjoint in any given frame.
  - SGR reset at every chrome ↔ pane transition.
  - Cursor ownership is single-renderer per frame; chrome layer parks
    cursor at end-of-frame; pane layer positions it for focused pane.

## Acceptance

- `ADR/0014-layered-render.md` exists, follows template.
- Linked from ARCHITECTURE.md client section.
- Linked from epic phux-5ke when closed.
notes: Landed in #25 (ADR-0020).

title: Predict multi-codepoint graphemes (ZWJ sequences, combining marks)
description:
Deferred from phux-9gw.1.4. The current predict layer accepts single Unicode scalar values only; multi-codepoint graphemes (e.g. flag emoji \🇺🇸\ = U+1F1FA + U+1F1F8, ZWJ family emoji, accented characters typed as base + combining mark) are rejected by the 'two-chars-in-text' guard in predict_key_with_grid.

To predict them safely we need: (1) cluster awareness via unicode-segmentation::Graphemes, (2) cell-width computation across the whole cluster (which may exceed UnicodeWidthChar::width on its base), (3) reconcile-side comparison that compares the full base cluster string against the cell's graphemes vec (read_grapheme_at currently returns only Option<char>).

Out of scope for phux-9gw.1.3+4+5 because it touches the reconcile read API and adds a new dep. File when there is appetite for the cell-grapheme-string plumbing.
close_reason: Predict multi-codepoint graphemes (flag/ZWJ/combining) via unicode-segmentation; reconcile reads full cluster string. Landed 3f23726.

title: Server: most-recently-focused session tracking (richer Last)
description: AttachTarget::Last today resolves against ServerState::last_attached_session — "last client attach," not "last focused session." Per phux-k61.1 issue spec, the ideal semantic for naked `phux` is "most-recently-FOCUSED" session (i.e. respects in-session activity, not just attach timestamp). Wire a per-Session last-touched timestamp (updated on input, focus, or attach) and have Last resolve against that. Until this lands the current behavior is good enough: last attach is a sensible proxy on single-session days.
close_reason: Closed

title: Server: implement AttachTarget::CreateIfMissing
description: phux-k61.1 shipped naked `phux` with the Last → ByName("default") fallback cascade. The remaining edge case — "server is running but every session has been killed" — would be cleanly handled by AttachTarget::CreateIfMissing, which is currently stubbed in crates/phux-server/src/runtime.rs:848 with a "not yet implemented" SessionNotFound error. Wiring it up requires server-side session creation + initial pane spawn at attach time, which overlaps with the SPAWN frame work. Pick this up alongside any phux-byc.* session-creation IPC pass.
close_reason: Landed in e9242fe. Server resolve_create_if_missing reuses seed_session_with_actor/seed_session_with_pty helpers; root_token threaded through accept_loop -> handle_client -> handle_attach -> resolve_attach_target. Three wire integration tests in attach_create_if_missing.rs. Wire schema: CreateIfMissing {name: String, command: Option<Vec<String>>, cwd: Option<String>} — name is required; client (naked phux) uses DEFAULT_SESSION_NAME = 'default'.

title: Align `just ci` with GitHub Actions CI — add cargo doc check
description:
GitHub Actions CI runs five gates: fmt, clippy, test, deny, **doc** (`cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`). The local `just ci` recipe runs only fmt + clippy + test + deny — `cargo doc` is missing. This causes agent PRs that pass `just ci` locally to fail CI on doc lints (e.g. `private_intra_doc_links` on a doc comment that references a private item).

Fix: add a `doc` recipe to the justfile and chain it into `ci`. Mirror the CI invocation: `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features`.

Surfaced on phux-0wx/phux-jes (PR #12) where a doc comment linked to a private `State::X10Mouse` enum variant; `just ci` green, GH `doc` check red. Fixed in PR #12 by de-linking the reference, but the underlying gap remains.

LABELS: area:dx, crate:phux
close_reason: Landed in commit f3f6b40 via PR #16. justfile 'doc' recipe + ci target chain now includes cargo doc with RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings'. Aligns local just ci with CI's doc gate. Verified by break test.

title: Predict full-line backspace from a known prompt column
description: Deferred from phux-9gw.1.1. To predict erasing back to the prompt (Ctrl-U / repeated Backspace), we need to know where the prompt ends. Requires OSC 133 shell integration or a server-side prompt-column tracker. Without it, full-line backspace risks erasing the prompt itself.
notes: Explicitly deferred during phux-9gw.1.3+4 fan-out (PR for that work shipped without this sub-ticket). Implementation path requires either OSC 133 (FinalTerm) shell-integration plumbing through the server-side libghostty parser into the protocol, OR a client-side heuristic (first non-space column on attach + watch for prompt-repaint signals). Neither is a 30-line change. Keep open for a dedicated PR once OSC 133 lands or a heuristic is designed.

title: Predict UTF-8 single codepoints with grapheme width
description: Deferred from phux-9gw.1.1. Currently predict_key only accepts ASCII printable (0x20..=0x7E). Widen to any single Unicode scalar value with cell width 1 or 2 (use unicode-width crate). Multi-codepoint graphemes (ZWJ sequences, combining marks) stay deferred. For width 2 (CJK / emoji): the prediction must occupy two cells; the overlay paints the base grapheme at col, advances cursor by 2; reconcile reads cell at col.
close_reason: Landed in PR (this branch). predict_key now accepts any single Unicode scalar value; uses unicode-width crate (added with PR-body justification). Width 1 → 1-col advance; width 2 (CJK / wide emoji) → 2-col advance with right-edge guard. Width 0 (combining marks) and multi-codepoint graphemes (ZWJ) still deferred — filed as follow-up.

title: Predict cursor-motion arrows over a known line
description: Deferred from phux-9gw.1.1. Implement left/right arrow predictions within the text region of the current line. Requires reading the renderer's cell grid for the current row to know the text extent — TerminalRenderer::read_grapheme_at (added in phux-9gw.1.1) gives us a clean read path. PredictionKind::CursorLeft / CursorRight would update the predict cursor without painting a cell; reconcile confirms via cursor_after.col == pred_col.
close_reason: Landed in PR (this branch). CursorLeft/CursorRight predictions over a known cell, with width-aware advance/retreat. Reconcile classifier added (confirmed/pending/contradicted). Overlay paints no cell. Tests: arrow_left_over_known_cell, arrow_right_over_wide_grapheme, arrow_left_at_col_zero, arrow_right_at_right_edge, per_cell_cursor_left_*, per_cell_cursor_right_*.

title: client: kitty CSI u — KIP levels 3-5 (alternates, base layout, text reports)
description: phux-1kf targets KIP levels 1+2 (disambiguate + event types). Higher levels are absorbed and their sub-params dropped: level 3 (REPORT_ALTERNATES, shifted_key + base_layout_key), level 4 (REPORT_ALL_KEYS_AS_ESCAPE_CODES — already implicit in the parser via the keycode path), level 5 (REPORT_ASSOCIATED_TEXT). Implementing 3 requires plumbing the alternate codepoint through to KeyEvent (probably via unshifted_codepoint or a new field), and 5 requires deciding whether the text payload from the kitty side overrides our locally-derived text (server-side encoder concern).
close_reason: Landed in commit 0150b9d via PR #17. KIP level 5 text payload populates KeyEvent.text when group-1 sub-params ≥ 2 present. Level 3 alternates/base-layout dropped with tracing.

title: client: kitty CSI u — distinct repeat-event handling
description: phux-1kf parses kitty CSI u at KIP level 1+2 but drops event_type=2 (repeat). Re-emitting as KeyAction::Repeat would duplicate Press semantics until downstream encoders model repeat distinctly; revisit once libghostty's key::Encoder grows repeat-aware bytes or once a phux feature (e.g. hold-to-repeat heuristics) needs the signal.
close_reason: Landed in commit 0150b9d via PR #17. event_type=2 maps to KeyAction::Repeat (libghostty variant verified at rev 31d1f70).

title: Wire [experimental] predictive-echo TOML flag in phux-config
description:
phux-9gw.1 landed predictive local echo gated behind PredictiveConfig at the Rust API level. The TOML side ([experimental] predictive-echo = true in config.toml) was deferred to avoid colliding with concurrent phux-nz4 status-bar config work on phux-config/schema.rs.

Add an ExperimentalCfg section to phux-config/src/schema.rs with predictive-echo: bool, default false. Plumb it through to the CLI's attach call so that run_with_predict gets the user's config.
close_reason: Landed in commit 557a7f6 via PR #13. New [experimental] section in phux-config schema; predictive-echo: bool default false. CLI dispatches to run_with_predict when set. DESIGN.md §4.2 documents the flag and the 'experimental knobs may rename without SemVer bump' caveat. 3 config parser tests.

title: Widen predictive echo: cursor-motion arrows + Enter + UTF-8 + per-cell match
description:
Follow-up to phux-9gw.1. v0 reconciliation drops the entire pending queue on any TERMINAL_OUTPUT; v0 predict-set is printable ASCII + EOL backspace only. Widen:

1. Predict Enter at end-of-line (newline + CR + cursor to col 0).
2. Predict cursor-motion arrows over a single known line (left/right within text region).
3. Predict full-line backspace from a known prompt (track prompt column).
4. Predict UTF-8 single codepoints (currently ASCII only).
5. Per-cell match game in reconcile: instead of draining everything, walk the prediction queue against the freshly-rendered authoritative cells; keep predictions that are still ahead of confirmed state, drop only the ones that have been resolved.

Acceptance: a Mosh-class typing experience over a 200ms-RTT link including arrow editing of just-typed input.
close_reason: Landed in commit db106e6 via PR #15. Per-cell match reconcile (option b: read_grapheme_at via RenderState snapshot, avoids second !Send Terminal) eliminates v0 drain-on-every-frame flicker. Predict Enter at EOL. 12 new unit tests. Deferred: phux-9gw.1.3 (cursor-motion arrows), phux-9gw.1.4 (UTF-8 codepoints), phux-9gw.1.5 (full-line backspace from prompt column).

title: client: full kitty CSI u keyboard protocol parsing
description: phux-19e absorbs but drops kitty CSI u sequences (e.g. CSI 97;5u for Ctrl-a in KIP). To round-trip the kitty keyboard protocol end-to-end the client parser needs to decode these into KeyEvent. Decisions: which KIP level to target (basic vs. progressive enhancement), and how to handle alternates/text reports.
close_reason: Landed in commit 2bf3634 via PR #14. Kitty CSI u parser targeting KIP level 1 (disambiguate) + level 2 (event types). 12 unit tests. Levels 3-5 (alternates, base layout, text codepoints) absorbed-and-dropped; follow-ups filed: phux-9z0 (repeat events), phux-y5p (KIP 3-5), phux-6ri (hyper/meta mods missing in libghostty Mods).

title: client: urxvt-1015 decimal mouse parser
description: Niche mouse format CSI <btn>;<col>;<row>M (no leading <). Similar to SGR but without the < marker. Dispatcher already exists in input.rs; add a branch that recognises 'M' final with numeric-only params.
close_reason: Landed in commit 5f4fbc0 via PR #12. urxvt-1015 decimal mouse (CSI <btn>;<col>;<row>M, no leading <). 4 unit tests (click/release/wheel). Shipped together with phux-0wx.

title: client: legacy X10 mouse parser (CSI M Cb Cx Cy)
description: phux-19e covered SGR (DEC mode 1006) only. X10 legacy format encodes mouse reports as the literal 3 bytes after CSI M (button | 32, col + 32, row + 32). Needed for terminals that don't enable SGR mouse extensions. Implement in crates/phux-client/src/attach/input.rs (new CSI consumer-state for the 3 trailing bytes after 'M' final).
close_reason: Landed in commit 5f4fbc0 via PR #12. X10 legacy mouse (CSI M Cb Cx Cy) — new 3-byte consumer state in input.rs. 5 unit tests (click/release/shift). Shipped together with phux-jes.

title: RTT-adaptive tick interval (Mosh-style, clamp [20ms, 200ms])
description:
Replace fixed 33 Hz tick (phux-q0e.C) with per-consumer RTT-adaptive interval per ADR-0018 / Mosh §3.

Measure RTT via PING/PONG timestamps (we have these per spec-anchors) or piggybacked timestamps on FRAME_ACK. Per-consumer tick interval ≈ RTT/2 clamped to [20 ms, 200 ms]. Adjust slowly (EMA, factor TBD).

Defer until phux-q0e.A/B/C/D are operational and we have real-traffic data to tune against. Fixed 33 Hz is fine for local UDS.
close_reason: Already shipped on main (crates/phux-server/src/terminal_actor/tick.rs). Full Mosh-style RTT-adaptive tick: MIN_TICK_INTERVAL=20ms / MAX_TICK_INTERVAL=200ms clamp band; RttEstimator with TCP-RTO-style EMA (RTT_EMA_ALPHA=0.125, observe() folds samples); desired_tick_interval() = clamp(srtt/2, MIN, MAX); RTT sampled by piggyback on FRAME_ACK (emit_instants emit-Instant -> on_frame_ack duration -> EMA), with the server taking the min desired interval across consumers in adaptive_tick_interval(). Replaces the fixed 33Hz (DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL=30ms cold-start). Tests: adaptive_tick_interval_for_test, ack_without_emit_instant_produces_no_sample. Dependency q0e.4 + parent epic q0e both closed; this was just left open. (NB: the RTT emit-Instant map it relies on was hardened against unbounded growth in PR #80 / phux-ahk.)

title: phux-roz follow-up: tighten terminal reset on signal — held Termios + consumer-owned guard
description:
Today's phux-roz fix installs SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers + a panic hook that run terminal_reset_on_signal before exit. The reset is BEST-EFFORT: it re-cooks the terminal (forces ICANON + ECHO + ISIG flags on) rather than restoring the user's original Termios, because the saved Termios lives in the RawModeGuard which the signal handler can't safely reach.

Acceptable today (the user's outer shell still works after; user can 'reset' if anything sticks), but a cleaner shape:

1. Move saved Termios into a process-global Mutex<Option<Termios>> that:
   - RawModeGuard::install_with_stdout populates on entry.
   - terminal_reset_on_signal reads on signal/panic.
   - RawModeGuard::Drop reads + clears on normal unwind.
   The signal-safety of accessing a Mutex from a tokio signal arm is fine (the arm runs on the runtime thread, not in raw signal-handler context).

2. Consider whether ALT_SCREEN_ACTIVE (currently a SeqCst AtomicBool) should also live alongside, or whether the Termios's presence is itself the signal.

3. The 'libghostty renderer still writes to real stdout because its iterators aren't generic over Write' note in the wave-5 agent's design call could be revisited if a future test or alternate consumer surface needs the renderer to write into a captured buffer.

Naturally cascades with the L1 rename and the consumer-side detach policy (phux-it8 follow-up): if 'detach' becomes a consumer choice rather than a server-driven event, the consumer's RawModeGuard cleanup becomes the only place the reset story matters.

Commit reference: 63dc6ff.
close_reason: Landed on main as 00288fc (cherry-picked from fanout/phux-2r7-rawmode). Process-global SAVED_TERMIOS: Mutex<Option<Termios>> populated by RawModeGuard::install_with_stdout; signal arms + panic hook now read it to restore the user's ORIGINAL termios (not just re-cook ICANON+ECHO+ISIG). ALT_SCREEN_ACTIVE kept separate (decision documented inline) because alt-screen ENTER and termios flip happen at distinct points. 722 tests pass + 1 #[ignore]'d manual SIGINT repro.

title: phux-7vx follow-up: per-Terminal TERM as L1 SPAWN field; restore TERM=ghostty when round-trip is proven
description:
Today's phux-7vx fix swaps the default TERM=ghostty -> TERM=xterm-256color on the server-spawned PTY (pane_actor.rs:default_shell_command). Reason: TERM=ghostty's terminfo advertises 'fullkbd' which newer ncurses interprets as 'kitty keyboard protocol safe', so htop/less/vim/etc. push CSI > N u, libghostty pivots to CSI-u for every keypress, and TUIs that don't speak kitty (like htop) drop quit/F-keys.

Two follow-on tasks live under this:

1. PROVE THE ROUND-TRIP. Validate phux's input/output layer round-trips kitty KIP correctly for at least: htop, less, vim, neovim, fzf, btop. Integration tests using the wave-4 Screen harness (Screen helper at crates/phux-server/tests/common/screen.rs) where possible, manual smoke tests where not. Once this is green, restore TERM=ghostty default and the user gets ghostty's full terminfo capabilities.

2. EXPOSE TERM AS L1 SPAWN CONFIG. Under ADR-0015 the L1 SPAWN message creates a Terminal. The PTY env (TERM, LANG, PHUX_*, etc.) is part of that spawn. Today the server hardcodes TERM in default_shell_command. Move to a per-Terminal env-map field in the SPAWN request so a consumer (TUI or agent) can override it. Default value lives in phux-config (when that crate gets fleshed out). Blocked by L1 cascade for the wire-message shape.

Commit reference: 9734d42 (the current hardcoded swap).

Per-spawn TERM is reachable TODAY via SPAWN_TERMINAL.env TERM entry (attach.rs:499-503, precedence doc attach.rs:478-486). REMAINING for phux-ign: first-class optional TERM field on SPAWN (additive). PHASE A wire (DISJOINT from client render): add field::spawn_terminal::TERM=6 (field.rs:239-250); add term: Option<String> to FrameKind::SpawnTerminal (frame.rs:1522-1536, enc frame.rs:1970-1997 write_field id 6 when Some, dec decode.rs:849-885 new arm, default None — _=>{} loop already forward-compat). FrameKind is #[non_exhaustive] (frame.rs:1066) but struct-variant add breaks exhaustive matches: update constructors input_dispatch.rs:715/763 (env stays None, term None), decode.rs:878, tests frame_wire_snapshots.rs:747/761, wire_roundtrip.rs:1570/1936/1955, server tests. PHASE B server: attach.rs handle_spawn_terminal signature (432-439) take term:Option<String>; apply precedence compiled-in -> s.term() (488) -> wire term field -> wire env TERM; thread through runtime/client.rs:717. PHASE C tests: new wire snapshot w/ term field, roundtrip, server spawn test asserting cmd.get_env(TERM). phux-0o8 round-trip proof is ORTHOGONAL and BLOCKED: encoder already pivots correctly (htop_keys.rs proves legacy q=0x71 default + CSI-u after CSI>31u; client decodes inbound CSI u input.rs:55-66; downsample.rs:236-250 gates kbd replies on caps). title: phux-it8 follow-up: reshape EOF as L1 TERMINAL_CLOSED + consumer-side detach policy
description:
Today's phux-it8 fix has the server send FrameKind::Detached when a pane's PTY EOFs. Under ADR-0015's L1 substrate, the more honest shape is:
- Server emits TERMINAL_CLOSED { terminal_id, reason, exit_status } (an L1 lifecycle event)
- The CONSUMER decides what to do:
  - A TUI with no remaining terminals in its attached Collection may choose to detach itself
  - An agent SDK consumer just notes the exit code and continues subscribing/observing
  - A recorder consumer logs the close and keeps going

Currently the server bakes the TUI's 'no terminals left -> detach' policy in. Behaviorally identical for v0.1 single-pane sessions; only matters once Collections support multi-Terminal lifecycles and non-TUI consumers exist.

Implementation when this gets picked up:
- Rename FrameKind::Detached's role: detach as a state change owned by the client request, separate from terminal lifecycle.
- Add FrameKind::TerminalClosed { terminal_id, reason, exit_status } per ADR-0015 §L1 lifecycle.
- Move the 'no panes -> detach client' policy out of server runtime; into TUI consumer code (likely crates/phux-client/src/attach/driver.rs main_loop).
- Update phux-server/tests/eof_detach.rs to assert TerminalClosed arrives; add a separate TUI-consumer test that asserts the TUI detaches in response.

Blocked by: L1 vocabulary cascade (PaneId -> TerminalId rename; see phux-byc.5 / ADR-0015 §Doc impact / ADR-0016).

Commit reference: b5b7617 (the current shape).
notes: DEFERRED 2026-05-29 (campaign triage): P3, and the ticket itself states it is behaviorally identical for v0.1 single-pane sessions — the 'consumer-owned detach policy' only matters once Collections support multi-Terminal lifecycles and non-TUI consumers exist. Moving the 'no panes -> detach' policy from server (on_terminal_exited) to the client touches the lifecycle suite (eof_detach, reconnect, server_self_exit) for zero v0.1 behavioral gain. The 'reason' field is a clean additive wire change but low value alone. Revisit alongside Collections multi-Terminal work or the q0e wiring (phux-0q8).
close_reason: Done: server emits TERMINAL_CLOSED (not server-baked Detached); consumer-owned detach policy in attach/server_frame.rs L850-866 (detach only when LAST pane folds out; closing one of several keeps attach alive); regression tests L1709/1746/1775. The optional 'reason' field is deferred per CHANGELOG 0.2.0-draft.2 (exit_status is the compact subset); core consumer-decides behavior is implemented + tested.

title: ADR cleanup: refresh 0004/0006/0007/0008/0010/0012 references to diff-based architecture (post-ADR-0013)

Update the bet to ADR-0013 and the location to 'phux-protocol::wire::frame::PaneOutput'. Recommend an ADR-0008-style 'What this ADR replaces' amendment pattern.
- ADR-0008 §1: 'what stays phux-defined' lists Cell, Grid, DiffOp, CursorState, CursorShape — most are going away. Update to reflect that wire-side definitions shrink to envelopes + PANE_OUTPUT + PANE_SNAPSHOT bytes payload.

- ADR-0012 line 202: layout snapshots flow through diff frames — minor; the snapshot mechanism changes but layout-on-wire is still structured (lifecycle concern, not pane content).

title: phux-server::downsample: switch to Cow if benchmarks justify
description:
Follow-up to phux-2li. The downsample helper API in `phux-server::downsample`
takes `&DiffOp` and returns an owned `DiffOp`. The TrueColor fast path
therefore unnecessarily clones. Caller is currently expected to skip the fn
when the cap is TrueColor; this leaves the optimization at the call site,
not in the helper.

If profiling on the fanout layer ever shows clone overhead is measurable,
switch the signature to `Cow<'a, DiffOp>`. API is stable today specifically
because byc.5 hasn't built fanout yet.
close_reason: STALE per triage: ADR-0013 (bytes-on-the-wire, commit 460faeb) superseded the DiffOp-based architecture this bead targeted. downsample now operates on byte streams (rewrite_bytes/rewrite_bytes_with_caps), not &DiffOp; the Cow optimization is moot. No code change.

title: Perceptual color distance (CIELAB) for downsample — better Indexed16 picks
description:
Follow-up to phux-2li. The downsample helper currently uses naive squared
Euclidean distance in RGB space for nearest-palette lookup. This is the
standard "good enough" baseline but well-known to mispick on the 16-color
tier in particular (e.g., dark blue often loses to magenta because R is
weighted equally with G).

Migrate to a perceptual metric:

- Convert RGB → CIELAB (sRGB gamma decode + linear transform).
- Distance = Euclidean in Lab (or CIEDE2000 if we want to be fancy).

Out of scope for the substrate ticket because (a) it would expand the test
matrix significantly, and (b) the choice is reversible — the API
(`downsample(Color, ColorSupport)`) is stable; only the internals change.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stress-test 'frontend-agnostic' claim (ADR-0010): non-TUI client or soften ADR
description:
## Goal

Validate that phux's wire protocol is **genuinely** frontend-agnostic, not nominally so. ADR-0010 makes "frontend-agnostic" a load-bearing identity claim, but the reference implementation has only ever served a TUI client. No non-TUI consumer has exercised the wire format, so subtle TUI-coupling could exist in the protocol that nobody will notice until someone tries to build a non-TUI client.

This ticket forces the question before v0.1 tags.

## Two paths (pick one)

1. **Build a minimal non-TUI reference client.** Stress-test what breaks; fix gaps in the protocol. Candidates, cheapest first:
   - **Structured-output exporter** — a CLI that subscribes to PANE_SNAPSHOT + diffs and emits JSON/JSONL of cell state. Tests whether the protocol carries enough information to reconstruct a pane without VT semantics.
   - **Recording/replay viewer** — captures wire traffic and replays it offline. Tests `FrameId` ordering and `FRAME_ACK` semantics in isolation from a live PTY.
   - **egui/wgpu GUI client** — most expensive, most thorough. Probably overkill for validation alone.

2. **Soften ADR-0010's central decision to "TUI-first, non-TUI not precluded."** Honest if (1) is too expensive. Keeps the must-not-preclude invariants; drops the implication that we've validated them.

## Decision criteria

Pick (2) unless someone is going to actually build the client. (1) without follow-through is theater. P3 because this is a pre-v0.1 concern, not a current blocker — but it MUST be resolved before v0.1 tags or the ADR is misleading.

## Risk list to investigate during (1) if pursued

- **`RenderingMode::VtReplay` path (SPEC §6.2).** SPEC splits `Diff` and `VtReplay` modes; the VtReplay path is probably under-specified for non-VT renderers. What does a non-VT consumer do with VtReplay frames — refuse the session? Translate via libghostty-vt in the client? Spec needs an answer.
- **`PaneDiff::ops` assume 2D grid consumers.** `PUT_CELL`/`RUN`/`COPY_RECT`/`CLEAR_RECT` are grid ops. A structured-output / accessibility viewer would need a different abstraction layer. Is the right answer "consumers project ops onto whatever model they want," or does the protocol need a higher-level abstraction?
- **Input atoms re-exported from libghostty (ADR-0006/0008) are TUI-shaped at their core.** KEY/MOUSE/FOCUS/PASTE atoms reflect terminal-input semantics. A GUI consumer would translate at the boundary — that's fine, but is the translation lossy or lossless? Worth proving with a working translator.
- **Status-bar widgets (DESIGN.md) emit ANSI sequences for clients to render.** A GUI client wants structured data — does a `StatusFrame` wire type need to exist? Currently the answer is "TUI-only widget output," which is exactly the kind of TUI-coupling ADR-0010 forbids in principle but permits in practice.

## Cross-refs

- ADR-0010 (this ticket exists because of its validation-status section)
- ADR-0006 / ADR-0008 (libghostty atom re-export — the load-bearing TUI dependency)
- SPEC §6.2 (`RenderingMode`, `ServerFeature`)
- SPEC §8 (cell-diff protocol — the surface a non-TUI client must consume)
- DESIGN §14 (out-of-scope GUI client mention)
close_reason: ADR-0010 softened to 'TUI-first, non-TUI not precluded'; must-not-preclude marked structural not validated. Landed be99a28.

title: Migrate Cell::text from Vec<char> to SmallVec for inline storage
description:
**Problem**

`Cell::text` is currently `Vec<char>` per cell (`crates/phux-protocol/src/diff/cell.rs:32`). For an 80x24 grid that's 1920 cells x 24-byte Vec headers = ~46KB pointer overhead alone, plus a heap allocation per non-empty cell. At 200x60 it's ~12000 headers. The common case (ASCII, single-grapheme) doesn't need a heap allocation.

**Fix**

Swap to `SmallVec<[char; 2]>`: one base codepoint + one common combining char inline. Empty cells and ASCII use zero heap.

**Why now**

Cheap pre-renderer. Once 9gw.3 lands and the renderer assumes `Vec<char>`, this becomes intrusive.

**Wire format**

Unaffected. The hand-written wire codec encodes length-prefix + chars; the in-memory collection type is invisible to the wire. Verified via diff_spike byte-identical output.
close_reason: Landed in 5c5c1d6. Cell::text now stack-allocates for grapheme clusters of length <= 2 (covers empty cells, ASCII, and base+single-combining — the common case). Wire format unchanged; verified via diff_spike byte-identical output (md5 004fe6c4a8f2ad4e61ee8054fb459fbd). smallvec gated behind the protocol's `server` feature, so the publish-clean default build is unaffected.

title: Publish phux-protocol v0.0.1 placeholder to crates.io for docs.rs
description:

## Required Skills
rust,cargo-publish,docs.rs
design:
Sub-steps:

1. Decide libghostty-vt handling:
   - Option A: Make libghostty-vt an OPTIONAL dep behind a 'server' feature.
     phux-protocol public API uses re-exported types only when 'server' is
     enabled. Default features OMIT libghostty-vt. docs.rs builds default
     features → no git dep → publishable.
   - Option B: Wait for libghostty-vt to land on crates.io upstream.
   - Option C: Carve a no-libghostty subset of phux-protocol (likely too
     invasive given ADR-0008's 'use libghostty types directly').
   Recommend A.

2. crates/phux-protocol/Cargo.toml:
   - Remove publish = false
   - Bump version = '0.0.1' (override workspace.package.version locally,
     or bump workspace.package.version and let phux-protocol inherit while
     other private crates keep publish = false).
   - Add [features] section: server = ['libghostty-vt']
   - Move libghostty-vt from dependencies to optional dep with no default
     feature, or under [target.'cfg(...)'.dependencies].

3. Cargo.toml workspace: add docs.rs metadata to phux-protocol:
   [package.metadata.docs.rs]
   all-features = true

4. Local verify:
   cargo publish -p phux-protocol --dry-run
   cargo doc --no-deps -p phux-protocol
   (with and without --features server)

5. cargo publish -p phux-protocol (live, requires CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN).

6. Confirm https://docs.rs/phux-protocol/0.0.1 renders.

Caveat: this is the first place we'd hit the consequence of phux-protocol
re-exporting libghostty types in its PUBLIC api (ADR-0008). The 'server'
feature gating is the standard escape hatch. Document this in ADR-0008.

title: Satellite / federation v0.2 — hub-and-spoke across hosts
description:
Multi-host phux: one phux-server acts as hub, exposes sessions from peer phux-servers (satellites) over QUIC and SSH-stdio transports. Killer use case: AI-agent sandboxes — spin up disposable VMs, attach to all of them from one local hub.

Deferred to v0.2. ADR-0007 captures the design and the v0.1 must-not-preclude invariants so this stays additive.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `phux satellite add devbox ssh://devbox` registers a satellite via SSH-stdio.
- [ ] `phux ls` from the hub shows local and satellite sessions, namespaced as `local://name` and `sat://devbox/name`.
- [ ] Attaching to a satellite session works transparently — same input, diff, FRAME_ACK semantics as a local pane.
- [ ] Satellite disconnect mid-frame: hub buffers input, pane goes amber, reattach within 30s replays via snapshot fallback.
- [ ] QUIC transport (quinn) implemented and exercised in CI integration tests.
- [ ] Hub does NOT re-encode VT bytes; encoders stay per-satellite per ADR-0006.
- [ ] No regressions to single-host v0.1 ergonomics (Unix socket transport remains default).

## Out of scope for this epic

- Mesh topology (rejected in ADR-0007).
- Mosh wire-compatibility (rejected in ADR-0007).
- Direct client → satellite shortcuts (NAT-punching, discovery, etc.).
- Central registry / OIDC auth.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] github.com/phall1/phux is public with green CI on main.
- [ ] Every PR runs fmt, clippy -D warnings, nextest, cargo-deny, cargo doc — and merging is blocked on all five.
- [ ] CI wall time under 5min on cold cache.
- [ ] docs.rs builds successfully for phux-protocol once a 0.0.1 placeholder is published.
- [ ] mdBook deploys SPEC + ADRs to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
- [ ] Repo has topics: rust, tmux, libghostty, terminal-multiplexer, kip, kitty-keyboard-protocol.
close_reason: All 5 children complete (a38.1-.5): public repo, gated CI, mdBook deploy, phux-protocol 0.0.1 on crates.io, repo topics. Closed as eligible.

title: Config (TOML) + widget-first status bar
description:
TOML config loader with schema (per DESIGN.md), keybind resolver, status-bar architected as a widget/plugin system from day one (default config is just one composition of widgets). Validates the 'agents read/write the config' premise.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `~/.config/phux/phux.toml` loads at startup. Missing file → sensible defaults. Malformed file → clear error pointing to line:col.
- [ ] An agent can programmatically generate a valid phux.toml from a JSON spec (round-trip test in tests/).
- [ ] Status bar is composed from a `[[status.widgets]]` list. ≥2 widgets ship in-tree (`time`, `session-name`) as examples of the WidgetSpec contract.
- [ ] Keybinds resolve correctly under modifier combinations matching libghostty key-encode (snapshot test).
- [ ] `cargo nextest run -p phux-config` green; clippy -D warnings clean.
close_reason: EPIC complete: all 5 children (nz4.1-5) landed — TOML loader w/ XDG + line:col errors, StatusWidget/WidgetRegistry, time+session-name widgets, keybind resolver, status bar in client render path. 90 tests green. Audited 2026-05-28.

title: CI rot risk: integrations/pi + integrations/opencode npm suites and clients/ wasm builds run in no lane
description: Audit evidence (2026-08-02): integrations/pi (404K) and integrations/opencode (144K) carry real npm test suites with zero CI/justfile invocation; clients/phux-web + phux-vt-web have no CI lane building the wasm; scripts/ci/*.sh (734 lines) escapes the shellcheck glob scripts/*.sh in the justfile. Decide: add lanes or accept documented rot risk.

title: Policy engine is permissive-only scaffolding; decide activate-or-prune
description: Audit evidence (2026-08-02): PolicyEngine has exactly one impl (PermissivePolicy allow-all); ServerConfig::policy_bundle is written None at both writers so authorize_hello is statically Ok and the deny/ERROR path is unreachable; AuditSink/NoopAuditSink/InputProvenance/4 authorize_* methods have zero callers (~350 LOC in phux-server, ~250 stranded pub types in published phux-protocol::policy). Backing: ADR-0031. Either wire a real policy source or prune to the vocabulary the wire actually uses; protocol-side removal is a semver decision.

title: client: kitty CSI u — hyper/meta modifier bits dropped
description: phux-1kf maps KIP modifier bits into libghostty::Mods. KIP defines hyper=16 and meta=32 as distinct modifiers, but libghostty's Mods has no bits for them — we drop both silently. If/when libghostty grows hyper/meta (or if we add a phux-side wrapper), surface them through. Caps_lock and num_lock are already mapped.
close_reason: Landed in commit 0150b9d via PR #17. Hyper→SUPER, meta→ALT (refined option c). Preserves user intent over silent drop. Distinct bits when libghostty grows them is deferred.
